areas.text: A great wooden balance beside the barn door, where the reeve weighs goods and settles quarrels.

locations.name: Basalt Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-10 · Danger: Low]

A quarry in the hills behind the coast where black basalt is cut and crushed for the roads.

areas.name: Quarry Crusher House
areas.text: The noisy shed where the stone is broken down.

areas.name: Quarry Pit
areas.text: The deep pit of black stone and loose scree.

locations.name: Battera's Castle
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An old castle on high ground above walls and cliffs, the property of the billionaire Battera, who has spent fortunes buying every copy of the game Greed Island. Players he hires come by train, sign his contract and go down to the basement, where thirty-two consoles run the game.

areas.name: Castle Gatehouse
areas.text:
The gatehouse where the train passengers are met and checked in by armed guards.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Yorknew City (about 2000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Castle Upper Halls
areas.text: The ornate upper floors where Battera receives his players.

areas.name: Console Room
areas.text: The basement room of thirty-two consoles, each with a monitor showing a player's status.

locations.name: Beach Girl's Cottage
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A whitewashed cottage in the dunes outside Soufrabi, home of a young woman with her hair tied back who watches the harbour from her door. She speaks to players only when they come in numbers.

areas.name: Beach Cottage Dune Path
areas.text: The sandy path through marram grass to the cottage.

areas.name: Beach Cottage Porch
areas.text: A porch of bleached boards facing the harbour.

locations.name: Beans's Briefing Room
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 8-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A plain room near the hall where the new Hunters are seated, given their cards and told what they can do with them. The talk is short; the card in the hand is what everyone remembers.

areas.name: Briefing Room Lectern
areas.text: The lectern where the briefing is read to the new Hunters.

areas.name: Briefing Room Licence Box
areas.text: The locked case that holds the new cards until they are handed out.

locations.name: Beauty Springs Valley
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

A steaming valley of hot pools in terraces, with a bamboo rail for towels. Bathers swear their skin is softer after half an hour in the water.

areas.name: Beauty Springs Terraces
areas.text: Terraces of steaming pools down the valley side.

areas.name: Beauty Springs Towel Rail
areas.text: A bamboo rail and a bench at the path's end.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small city in the Kukan'yu Kingdom with a railway station, a few streets of shops and nothing to say about itself. Applicants who come here in January have usually been told what to buy and where.

areas.name: Beeskafmarro Station
areas.text:
The station with its platforms and the ticket windows where trains leave for the coast.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Dolle Harbor (about 2000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Station Street
areas.text: The short street outside the station, with its cafe and its store.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro Bus Terminal
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The terminal beside the station where buses leave for the villages along the coast and inland. A noodle stand under the canopy feeds the drivers.

areas.name: Beeskafmarro Bus Bays
areas.text: Six numbered bays under a concrete canopy.

areas.name: Bus Terminal Noodle Stand
areas.text: The stand where the drivers eat between runs.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-7 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small white chapel on the hill above the city with a bell, a few pews and a graveyard of fishermen.

areas.name: Beeskafmarro Chapel Graveyard
areas.text: The graveyard of fishermen's stones behind the chapel.

areas.name: Chapel Pews
areas.text: A few wooden pews before a plain altar.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro Fish Cannery
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-9 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The cannery on the quay that takes the catch from the coast boats and puts it in tins for the trains. It employs half the families in the lower town.

areas.name: Cannery Floor
areas.text: The noisy floor of belts and sealing machines.

areas.name: Cannery Quay
areas.text: The quay where the boats unload into crates of ice.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro Freight Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The rail yard behind the station, where wagons of timber, fish and machinery are shunted between the coast line and the inland routes. It works through the night.

areas.name: Beeskafmarro Sidings
areas.text: Rows of wagons on sidings, some of them unlocked.

areas.name: Freight Yard Office
areas.text: The office where the clerk keeps the manifests.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro Middle School
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-7 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The city's middle school, a plain concrete building with a sports ground and a gym. Its pupils know every shortcut in the city.

areas.name: School Gymnasium
areas.text: The wooden-floored gym with its climbing ropes.

areas.name: School Sports Ground
areas.text: The dirt ground with goals and a running track.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro Pawnshop
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A narrow pawnshop on a back street with watches, cameras and the odd sword in its windows. The owner buys anything with a story.

areas.name: Pawnshop Back Room
areas.text: The back room of things not for sale in the window.

areas.name: Pawnshop Counter
areas.text: The grilled counter where goods are weighed and haggled over.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro Police Box
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A one-room police post on the corner of the main street, with a constable, a bicycle and a map of every lane in the city.

areas.name: Police Box Desk
areas.text: The desk with its logbook and telephone.

areas.name: Police Box Map Wall
areas.text: A wall map of the city with pins for every reported theft.

locations.name: Beeskafmarro Ward Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-8 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The city's clinic, run by an elderly doctor and two nurses, which treats colds, cuts and the occasional broken arm from the freight yard.

areas.name: Ward Clinic Surgery
areas.text: The doctor's room with its couch and lamp.

areas.name: Ward Clinic Waiting Room
areas.text: Plastic chairs, a ticket machine and a television on mute.

locations.name: Beyond's Detention Room
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

A small holding cell on Tier 1 where the expedition's leader, Beyond Netero, is kept under watch for the whole voyage.

areas.name: Holding Cell
areas.text: The cell with its bed, its manacle and its quiet prisoner.

locations.name: Bilgai Desert
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A desert in the Republic of Rokario, near its border with the Republic of Hass.

areas.name: Bilgai Dunes
areas.text: The dunes away from the road.

locations.name: Bilgai Gypsum Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A great white quarry cut into the edge of the Bilgai Desert, where gypsum is blasted out, broken and trucked to the railway for plaster and cement. The dust is so fine it gets into the workers' food.

areas.name: Bilgai Blasting Shed
areas.text: A low concrete shed with a heavy door and a lock that does not catch.

areas.name: Bilgai Quarry Face
areas.text: A tall white wall of stone, drilled and stepped, glaring in the sun.

locations.name: Bilgai Rest House
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 18-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A whitewashed rest house halfway across the Bilgai Desert on the road to Hass, with a water tank, a few beds and a radio to call the city if a vehicle breaks down. Herders water their camels here; drivers fill their radiators.

areas.name: Bilgai Rest House Tank
areas.text: A steel tank on stilts and the trough below it where camels and lorries both drink.

areas.name: Bilgai Shade Porch
areas.text: A deep porch of rugs and cushions where travellers wait out the heat.

locations.name: Binolt's Clearing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A hollow in the badlands on the way to Masadora, closed in by walls of eroded rock, where the ground is trampled flat and the stone is scarred at head height. Players say a man with scissors lives near it and that it is wiser to walk around.

areas.name: Clearing Fire Ring
areas.text: A ring of stones blackened by many fires, with bones in the ashes.

areas.name: Clearing Thrown Rocks
areas.text: The open ground strewn with rocks thrown in a long fight.

locations.name: Biscuit's Stone-Breaking Ground
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

A rocky field at the badlands' edge where the ground is covered in broken stones, as if someone had made a game of smashing a whole heap of rocks with one. Players camping nearby hear the cracks from dawn to dark.

areas.name: Stone-Breaking Field
areas.text: The field of broken rock, shards everywhere underfoot.

areas.name: Stone-Breaking Teacher's Boulder
areas.text: A round boulder where a teacher sits to watch and count.

locations.name: Black Lantern Gambling Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A gambling hall reached through the kitchen of a noodle shop in the back lanes of Zaban City, with card tables, a roulette wheel and a cashier's cage behind bars. Most nights its tables are full of people who should know better.

areas.name: Black Lantern Cage
areas.text: The cashier's cage, barred, with a guard on a stool.

areas.name: Black Lantern Noodle Kitchen
areas.text: The noodle shop's kitchen, the only way in or out.

areas.name: Black Lantern Tables
areas.text: Card tables and a roulette wheel under low red lamps.

locations.name: Black Whale 1
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The first of the Black Whale class, built for Kakin's expedition to the New Continent: 1,500 metres long, 800 high and 800 wide, carrying 200,000 passengers, its eyes serving as searchlights. Too large to dock, it is served by ferries and airships. It sails under the Royal Army's martial law, its five tiers dividing the passengers by wealth.

areas.name: Central Connecting Passage
areas.text: The guarded throughways between tiers, where a ticket from the Royal Army, or from a Mafia ticket-puncher, is needed to pass.

areas.name: Hull Springs
areas.text: The great springs that hold the tiers inside the hull.

areas.name: Top Dome
areas.text: The dome over the ship's top, closed in bad waters.

locations.name: Black Whale Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The command bridge of the Black Whale 1, high in the hull behind the great eyes that serve as its searchlights. From here the Royal Army runs the ship under martial law.

areas.name: Bridge Chart Room
areas.text: A room of chart tables where the voyage's route is plotted day by day.

areas.name: Bridge Helm Deck
areas.text: The main deck of the bridge with the helm, radar and a wall of windows.

locations.name: Black Whale Cargo Holds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-36 · Danger: Deadly]

The holds below the tiers, where luggage, provisions and stores for two months at sea are stacked in caged bays. Every royal household's allowance is weighed and stowed here.

areas.name: Cargo Hold Drone Bay
areas.text: A bay open to the air where delivery drones land their loads.

areas.name: Cargo Hold Luggage Cages
areas.text: Caged bays of trunks and crates, each tagged with a household's seal.

locations.name: Black Whale Propeller Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-34 · Danger: Severe]

The machinery hall at the stern of the hull, beside the lowest tier, where the propeller shaft turns day and night. The noise reaches every cabin on Tier 5.

areas.name: Propeller Hall Control Room
areas.text: A glassed room of gauges where the engineers watch the drive.

areas.name: Propeller Shaft Gallery
areas.text: A long gallery beside the turning shaft, slick with oil.

locations.name: Black Whale Shipyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-32 · Danger: Severe]

A shipyard on the far side of the bay with a dry dock big enough to swallow a town and gantries that can be seen from the capital. Thousands work in shifts around the clock, and its lights never go out.

areas.name: Shipyard Building Dock
areas.text: The dry dock itself, where the black hull rises in scaffolding.

areas.name: Shipyard Spring Foundry
areas.text: A furnace hall where springs taller than houses are cast and tempered.

locations.name: Black Whale Switchboard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-38 · Danger: Deadly]

The telephone exchange of the ship, run by the Royal Army, which manages every phone line aboard and keeps a log of every call put through.

areas.name: Switchboard Line-Cutting Panel
areas.text: A locked panel where a line can be cut off for good with a key.

areas.name: Switchboard Operator Bank
areas.text: Rows of operators at their boards, plugging and unplugging calls.

locations.name: Blackpeat Moor
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

Open moor south of the villages where peat is cut, stacked and dried for winter fuel. In the long hollows the mist lies until noon, and the peat-cutters tie themselves together with rope in bad weather.

areas.name: Blackpeat Cutter's Bothy
areas.text: A stone shelter with a turf roof, where cutters sleep through the season.

areas.name: Blackpeat Cutting Banks
areas.text: Long black banks where the peat is sliced out with spades and stacked to dry.

locations.name: Bottle Glass Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

A ridge made almost entirely of bottles and window glass, glittering for miles on a sunny day. Nobody crosses it barefoot, and nobody crosses it fast.

areas.name: Glass Ridge Bottle Picks
areas.text: Patches where whole bottles lie stacked by colour, ready to be sacked.

areas.name: Glass Ridge Shard Slope
areas.text: A long slope of shards that slides and rings under any weight.

locations.name: Bourbon's Snake Cave
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A deep cave on Zevil Island, reached through ferns on a slope above the sea. The floor moves with snakes, and they do not like anyone who tries to leave.

areas.name: Snake Cave Den
areas.text: The inner chamber where the snakes coil around their master.

areas.name: Snake Cave Mouth
areas.text: The fern-hung mouth of the cave, where the snakes let anyone in.

locations.name: Bull Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The cheap end of Yorknew's auction season: stalls where every lot carries a paper tag, and whoever has written the biggest number on it when time runs out takes it home, unless the seller likes an offer before then.

areas.name: Haggling Corner
areas.text: A corner where sellers and buyers settle early.

areas.name: Tag Stalls
areas.text: The rows of stalls where every item carries a bidding tag.

locations.name: Bunkhouse Eighty-Eight
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A cheap hostel near the central station, sixteen bunks to a room, packed in auction season with backpackers, students and small dealers hoping one lucky find will pay for the trip. The kettle never cools.

areas.name: Bunkhouse Common Room
areas.text: A common room of a sagging sofa, a television and a kettle.

areas.name: Bunkhouse Dormitory
areas.text: A room of steel bunks and padlocked lockers.

locations.name: Bunzen
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A town of the game, busy with townsfolk and players, with a forest nearby.

areas.name: Bunzen Forest Edge
areas.text: The edge of the forest beside the town.

locations.name: Bunzen Exorcism Glade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

A small glade in the forest by Bunzen's gate, ringed by trees hung with paper charms. Townsfolk keep away from it when someone is chanting there.

areas.name: Exorcism Glade Fire Pit
areas.text: A blackened fire pit in the centre where the ritual is done.

areas.name: Exorcism Glade Ring
areas.text: The circle of trees with charms on strings between them.

locations.name: Bunzen Woodcutters' Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A yard at Bunzen's edge where woodcutters stack logs and saw planks. The townsfolk here work steadily and say the same things about the weather every day.

areas.name: Woodcutters' Log Stacks
areas.text: Rows of stacked logs drying under rough roofs.

areas.name: Woodcutters' Saw-Pit
areas.text: A long pit with a two-man saw over it.

locations.name: Buor Toll Passage
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

The one passage that leads to the central dining hall of Tier 5, where three men of the Buor Family have set up a turnstile and charge passengers to pass.

areas.name: Buor Instant Food Stall
areas.text: A trestle table of instant noodles and a kettle.

areas.name: Toll Passage Turnstile
areas.text: A turnstile bolted across the passage, with a cash box beside it.

locations.name: Butlers' Firing Range
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

A long range scraped into the slope below the butlers' house, where the staff practise with pistols and rifles and with whatever else they throw. One steel plate at the end is dented all over by coins.

areas.name: Firing Range Armoury Hut
areas.text: A hut of racked guns and ammunition crates under a padlock.

areas.name: Firing Range Lanes
areas.text: Ten lanes of packed earth with paper targets on wooden frames.

locations.name: Butlers' Quarters
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-26 · Danger: High]

The grounds and house where the Zoldyck butlers live, train and are schooled, halfway up the mountain. A young butler with a cane stands guard at a line on the path and stops anyone who crosses it.

areas.name: Butlers' Hall
areas.text: The hall where the butlers eat, study and play their games.

areas.name: Canary's Line
areas.text: The line drawn across the path where a girl with a cane stands guard.

locations.name: Butlers' Schoolhouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The school where the estate raises its future butlers. Most of its pupils were taken in as orphans; they learn manners, languages, driving and fighting in the same building and are expected to open the first door of the Testing Gate before they are trusted with anything.

areas.name: Butlers' Schoolhouse Classroom
areas.text: A classroom of scrubbed desks and a blackboard of etiquette rules.

areas.name: Schoolhouse Dormitory
areas.text: Long rooms of narrow beds made with hospital corners.

areas.name: Schoolhouse Weight Gym
areas.text: The gym where children lift and push iron until the gate becomes possible.

locations.name: Camp Tiger Uplands
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-34 · Danger: Severe]

Open uplands beyond the survey forest where summer storms walk the ridges and lightning strikes the same trees year after year. Herders keep away from the high ground at night and tell stories about fires that nobody lit.

areas.name: Uplands Ash Hollow
areas.text: A sheltered hollow ringed with old fire pits and gnawed bones.

areas.name: Uplands Lightning Ridge
areas.text: A bare ridge of split and blackened trees where the storms strike most often.

locations.name: Captain's Ship
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A small passenger ship that carries hopefuls from the islands to the exam's landing port at Dolle Harbor. Its captain smokes a pipe, drinks, calls seasick passengers pathetic and reads the weather hours ahead. He chooses whom to take the rest of the way.

areas.name: Passenger Hold
areas.text: The hold below where the applicants sit out the storm and size each other up.

areas.name: Storm Deck
areas.text: The open deck, slick with spray, where the crew fight the rigging in the wind.

areas.name: Wheelhouse
areas.text: The captain's wheelhouse, with the wheel, the charts and the smell of pipe smoke.

locations.name: Caretakers' House
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A long house of salvaged boards where orphans of the heaps are fed, counted and put to bed by caretakers chosen by the neighbours. A child here needs a caretaker's leave to go further than the end of the street.

areas.name: Caretakers' Bed Hall
areas.text: Rows of cots and hammocks, each with a name chalked on the post above it.

areas.name: Caretakers' Soup Kitchen
areas.text: A lean-to with a great pot over a drum fire and a bench along the wall.

locations.name: Casino King's Salon
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A private room above the casino floor in Dorias where the Casino King plays poker with any player who dares. A rope keeps the watching crowd back from the table.

areas.name: Salon Baize Table
areas.text: The green table under a low lamp.

areas.name: Salon Rope Line
areas.text: The rope where onlookers crowd.

locations.name: Casino Spade Royale
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A casino off Auction Avenue where the winners of the day's sales come at night to give some of it back. The drinks are free to anyone holding chips, the clocks have all been taken down, and the doormen can tell a card counter from across the room.

areas.name: Spade Royale Counting Room
areas.text: A locked room of counting machines, paper bands and canvas bags.

areas.name: Spade Royale Gaming Floor
areas.text: Tables of roulette, dice and cards under three chandeliers.

areas.name: Spade Royale High-Stakes Salon
areas.text: A curtained salon where the minimum bet keeps the room empty.

locations.name: Castle Hill Village
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The village at the foot of the castle cliff, a few streets of stone houses that lived on fishing until the billionaire bought the hill. Now it lives on him: the cooks, cleaners, drivers and guards' families rent its rooms, and its one bar shows the news from Yorknew every night.

areas.name: Castle Hill Bar
areas.text: A low bar with a television on a bracket and fishermen's photos on the walls.

areas.name: Castle Hill Bus Turn
areas.text: The turning circle where the delivery vans and the evening bus wait.

areas.name: Castle Hill Grocer
areas.text: A cramped grocer's shop with crates on the pavement and an order book on the counter.

locations.name: Castor Line
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A train line through Yorknew City, one of whose branches runs downtown. Its carriages are crowded at all hours during the auctions.

areas.name: Castor Carriage
areas.text: A crowded carriage where a passenger can read a book and listen.

locations.name: Cathedral of the Nine Bells
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

An old stone cathedral in the middle of the glass towers, older than most of the city. Its nine bells ring the hours, its side door feeds the hungry at noon, and its confessionals hear more than the police do.

areas.name: Nine Bells Belfry
areas.text: The belfry stair and the bells above it.

areas.name: Nine Bells Nave
areas.text: The long candlelit nave under a ribbed roof.

areas.name: Nine Bells Soup Door
areas.text: The side door where the noon meal is served from steel pots.

locations.name: Caveau de Riquewihr
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A restaurant in Antokiba run by cats, which gives a card to anyone who eats a huge plate of spaghetti in half an hour.

areas.name: Spaghetti Table
areas.text: The table where the challenge is eaten.

locations.name: Cedar Gorge Sawmill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A sawmill in a wooded gorge west of the town, cutting timber from the hill forests into boards and beams for the lowland towns.

areas.name: Cedar Gorge Log Pond
areas.text: A pond of floating logs waiting for the saw.

areas.name: Sawmill Saw Floor
areas.text: The open floor of the main saw.

locations.name: Cemetery Building
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-28 · Danger: Severe]

A huge building in Yorknew City that hosts the Mafia's own Underground Auction every September. The Mafia families send their high-ranking men, and some bosses come themselves to show off their wealth; whole families have gone bankrupt in its bidding wars.

areas.name: Auction Hall
areas.text: The hall of tiered seats facing the stage and its lots.

areas.name: Cemetery Vault
areas.text: The strongroom below where the lots wait.

areas.name: Cordon Line
areas.text: The ring of cars and armed men a kilometre out when the auction sits.

locations.name: Cha-R Bonded Warehouses
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

A row of bonded warehouses on the harbour's east side where goods sit under customs seal until their duty is paid. Half the trade of the port passes through them sooner or later.

areas.name: Cha-R Cold Store
areas.text: A refrigerated shed with heavy doors and frost on the walls.

areas.name: Cha-R Weighing Floor
areas.text: A concrete floor of platform scales where every load is weighed and logged.

locations.name: Charcoal Burners' Clearing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-28 · Danger: Severe]

A clearing where charcoal is burned in earth mounds, the fuel the smiths and the salt-boilers live on. The burners live beside their mounds for days, watching the smoke colour.

areas.name: Charcoal Clearing Cordwood Stacks
areas.text: Walls of split wood stacked to season at the clearing's edge.

areas.name: Charcoal Clearing Mounds
areas.text: Rounded earth mounds leaking blue smoke, each with its watcher.

locations.name: Chongso Radar Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-38 · Danger: Deadly]

A military radar station on a hilltop in the north-east, its white domes watching the sky and the sea for anything approaching the country. The road up passes three checkpoints.

areas.name: Radar Station Domes
areas.text: White domes on the crest, humming in the wind.

areas.name: Radar Station Operations Room
areas.text: A dark room of green screens and operators in headphones.

locations.name: Church Screening Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The nave of the big church, turned into a picture house on screening days. A bedsheet is hung for a screen, a projector clatters at the back, and every child in the inner zones crowds in for a cartoon dubbed by the city's own voices.

areas.name: Screening Hall Backstage
areas.text: A curtained corner behind the sheet, with a microphone on a cable and scripts on the floor.

areas.name: Screening Hall Pews
areas.text: Pews and chairs from a dozen dumps, packed shoulder to shoulder on screening days.

locations.name: Church Video Cellar
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A low room under the big church, fitted with a salvaged television and a tape player, where children who find videotapes in the heaps are allowed to sit and watch them. The priest keeps the key on his belt and rarely says no.

areas.name: Video Cellar Tape Shelves
areas.text: Shelves of tapes sorted by a child's handwriting: works, broken, cartoons, news.

areas.name: Video Cellar Viewing Bench
areas.text: A bench of planks facing the television, worn smooth by small knees.

locations.name: Cloudline Restaurant
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A restaurant on one of the high hundreds floors, where spectators with money eat above the weather and fighters with rooms on the same floor eat for a fraction. The dishes are named for great fights of the past.

areas.name: Cloudline Private Room
areas.text: A screened room for diners who want to talk unheard.

areas.name: Cloudline Window Tables
areas.text: Tables pressed against the glass with the cloud tops below.

locations.name: Club Velours
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

A members' club down a flight of steps from a quiet street, where a jazz quartet plays to booths of red velvet. It serves good whisky and bad food, and nobody comes for the food.

areas.name: Velours Bandstand
areas.text: A small raised stage with a piano and a double bass.

areas.name: Velours Velvet Booths
areas.text: Horseshoe booths of red velvet with a lamp on every table.

locations.name: Commission Airfield
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 5-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A headland airfield where the Association's exam airship is moored, fuelled and serviced between phases. It has a mast, a hangar and a crew who answer to the commission.

areas.name: Airfield Flight Office
areas.text: The office with the flight log and the radio.

areas.name: Airfield Hangar
areas.text: The hangar of tools, spare envelopes and engines.

areas.name: Airfield Mooring Mast
areas.text: The steel mast the airship ties to, with a lift to the gondola.

locations.name: Commission Proving Range
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A fenced range of rough hills where the commission tries out the phases it means to set, from chases to traps, on its own staff before the applicants ever see them.

areas.name: Proving Range Observation Hut
areas.text: A hut on a rise where examiners watch and take notes.

areas.name: Proving Range Trap Lines
areas.text: Rows of trial traps, some still armed.

locations.name: Compost Terraces
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Stepped beds dug into the rotting heaps and planted with greens, beans and mushrooms. The rot keeps them warm through winter, and the smell is part of the bargain.

areas.name: Terraces Green Beds
areas.text: The open beds of greens and beans, watered by can.

areas.name: Terraces Mushroom Sheds
areas.text: Dark sheds of plastic sheeting full of mushroom logs.

locations.name: Continental Street
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A broad street in Yorknew City lined with office buildings, running west from downtown.

areas.name: Continental Pavement
areas.text: The wide pavement past the office towers.

locations.name: Cyclops Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A ridge among the badlands where a pack of one-eyed giants keeps its ground. They attack anyone they find there on sight, swinging tree trunks as clubs.

areas.name: Cyclops Ridge Crest
areas.text: The broken crest of the ridge, where the giants stand to watch.

areas.name: Cyclops Ridge Gully
areas.text: A narrow gully below the crest, too tight for a giant to follow.

locations.name: Dalmont Boxing Gym
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A gym in an old warehouse on gym row, where an ageing coach trains boxers for the tower's lower floors. He is honest about what he can teach, which is rare on this street.

areas.name: Dalmont Coach's Office
areas.text: A glass box of an office with a desk of old fight records.

areas.name: Dalmont Warehouse Ring
areas.text: A canvas ring under a skylight with tape on the ropes.

locations.name: Dayroad Park
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: High]

A large municipal park in Yorknew City, with lawns, paths and food stands, where people come to rest away from the auctions.

areas.name: Food Stands
areas.text: The stands along the main path.

areas.name: Park Lawns
areas.text: The wide lawns where people picnic.

locations.name: Dead Set Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

A hill of dead televisions, radios and tape players, where the city's tinkerers come for parts. Anything with a screen in the city was probably built from pieces of this hill.

areas.name: Dead Set Summit
areas.text: The top of the hill, screens facing every way like a crowd of blind faces.

areas.name: Dead Set Tinker Bench
areas.text: A bench of doors on crates, covered in valves, solder and screws.

locations.name: Dentora Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A whitewashed chapel on a rise above the market town, its bell rung for weddings and funerals. The graveyard behind it is larger than the town would need.

areas.name: Chapel Graveyard
areas.text: A sloping graveyard of small stones, many without a body under them.

areas.name: Chapel Nave
areas.text: Rows of pews and a candle stand.

locations.name: Dentora Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The town's only clinic: a doctor, two nurses, a pharmacy counter and an ambulance that rarely leaves the car park. It sees broken ankles from the mountain paths and food poisoning from the market.

areas.name: Clinic Pharmacy Counter
areas.text: A counter of medicines behind glass.

areas.name: Clinic Waiting Room
areas.text: Plastic chairs, a magazine rack and a ticket machine.

locations.name: Dentora Highway
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-20 · Danger: High]

The highway from the Dentora Region down through forests to the town of Parasta and its airport. It is quiet at night and patrolled by nobody.

areas.name: Forest Lay-by
areas.text: A lay-by among the trees where drivers rest.

areas.name: Highway Bridge
areas.text: A bridge over a gorge on the way down.

locations.name: Dentora Hot Springs
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A bathhouse built around natural hot springs on the slope below the gate road, its outdoor pools facing Kukuroo Mountain. Tourists come for the view; locals come for their backs.

areas.name: Hot Springs Bathhouse Hall
areas.text: A timber hall with changing rooms and a tea counter.

areas.name: Hot Springs Outdoor Pools
areas.text: Stone pools steaming in the open air.

locations.name: Dentora Mountain Rescue Hut
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A mountain rescue hut on the slopes outside the wall, crewed by volunteers who bring down hikers who fall on the region's trails.

areas.name: Rescue Hut Gear Store
areas.text: A store of stretchers, ropes and lamps.

areas.name: Rescue Hut Radio Room
areas.text: A cramped room of radios and maps.

locations.name: Dentora Orchards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The terraced orchards on the low hills west of town that fill the fruit stalls in the market. Picking season brings in workers from the lowlands.

areas.name: Orchard Packing Shed
areas.text: A shed where the fruit is sorted and crated.

areas.name: Orchard Terraces
areas.text: Steps of fruit trees cut into the hill.

locations.name: Dentora Police Post
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small police station by the market with two officers and one patrol car. They deal with pickpockets, lost tourists and drunks.

areas.name: Police Post Cell
areas.text: A single cell with a bench and a drunk asleep on it.

areas.name: Police Post Front Desk
areas.text: The desk where complaints are taken, a bell on the counter.

locations.name: Dentora Pumice Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A quarry outside the wall where light volcanic stone is dug and crushed for building blocks and garden gravel. The quarry works close to the family's land, but never closer.

areas.name: Pumice Quarry Crusher
areas.text: The crusher and conveyor that grind the stone.

areas.name: Pumice Quarry Face
areas.text: The terraced face of pale stone.

locations.name: Dentora Region
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A region of the Republic of Padokea, a country anyone may enter without papers. Its market town lives off the tourists who come to ride a bus up into the mountains and look at the gate of the Zoldyck Family, the most famous assassins in the world, whose home is the whole of Kukuroo Mountain.

areas.name: Dentora Bus Terminal
areas.text:
The terminal where the tour bus and the long-distance coaches leave, plastered with tour posters of the mountain.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Dolle Harbor (about 30000 Jenny), Heavens Arena (about 15000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Dentora Market
areas.text: The open market of fruit stalls and souvenir sellers.

areas.name: Mountain View Inn
areas.text: A cheap inn with a view of the clouded peak, popular with bounty hunters on their way up.

locations.name: Dentora Reservoir Dam
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A concrete dam east of the town that holds a reservoir and makes the region's electricity. Engineers in a turbine house keep the lights on in the market town.

areas.name: Dam Crest Road
areas.text: The road across the top of the dam.

areas.name: Dam Turbine House
areas.text: The humming turbine hall.

locations.name: Dentora Souvenir Arcade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A covered row of souvenir shops off the market, selling anything that can be printed with a mountain or a silhouette: mugs, shirts, keyrings, toy hounds and postcards of the gate.

areas.name: Souvenir Arcade Print Shop
areas.text: A back room with a printing press for shirts and mugs.

areas.name: Souvenir Arcade Shopfronts
areas.text: The row of narrow shops with their goods on the pavement.

locations.name: Dentora Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The railway station of the Dentora market town, where long-distance trains from the lowlands end. Half the arrivals are tourists and the other half look like they are carrying weapons in their luggage.

areas.name: Dentora Station Platforms
areas.text: Two platforms under an iron canopy.

areas.name: Dentora Station Ticket Hall
areas.text: The ticket hall, its walls papered with tour posters.

locations.name: Desert Highway
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The highway across the Gordeau Desert between Lingon Airport and Yorknew City, straight and fast, with nowhere to turn off.

areas.name: City Limits
areas.text: The point where the desert gives way to the first buildings of the city.

areas.name: Highway Shoulder
areas.text: The dusty shoulder where a broken-down car waits.

locations.name: Desert Roadhouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A roadhouse on the desert highway with a gas pump, a counter and a radio, the only stop between the airport and the city.

areas.name: Roadhouse Counter
areas.text: The counter with its stools and its radio.

locations.name: Desert Tow Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

A garage and wrecking yard off the highway, owned by the only mechanic willing to drive into the desert for a broken-down car. He tows anything for anyone and asks very little.

areas.name: Tow Yard Workshop
areas.text: An open-fronted workshop of hoists, tools and a radio on a nail.

areas.name: Tow Yard Wreck Rows
areas.text: Lines of stripped cars rusting under the sun.

locations.name: Diamond Row
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

One short street where the city's diamond and gold trade lives: cutters upstairs, dealers on the pavement, showrooms with doors that buzz open only for a known face. A stone can change hands three times between one end and the other.

areas.name: Diamond Row Cutting Lofts
areas.text: Upstairs lofts of wheels and lamps where the stones are cut.

areas.name: Diamond Row Showrooms
areas.text: Showrooms of velvet trays behind buzzer doors.

locations.name: Dictator's Camp Ruins
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: Severe]

The bones of the internment camp the city is said to have begun as, fifteen centuries ago, surfacing here and there where the rubbish has been dug away. Few residents come; fewer stay after dark.

areas.name: Camp Ruins Watchtower Stump
areas.text: The top of an ancient tower poking out of the heap like a chimney.

areas.name: Camp Ruins Wire Trench
areas.text: A trench dug along an old fence line, rusted wire coiling out of the walls.

locations.name: Diksakura
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A store beside the station in Beeskafmarro that sells the usual things. A customer who pays with the right card is shown, without comment, to a door at the back.

areas.name: Back Storeroom
areas.text: The storeroom behind the door, much larger than the store should hold.

areas.name: Checkout Counter
areas.text: The counter where the special card is shown and the clerk nods to the back.

locations.name: Disused Castor Tunnels
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

The tunnels of an old branch of the Castor Line, closed when the new line was dug. Maintenance crews go down once a year; the city's homeless, its smugglers and its bored teenagers go more often.

areas.name: Castor Brick Vaults
areas.text: Arched brick vaults where water drips from the roof.

areas.name: Old Castor Platform
areas.text: A tiled platform under dust, its station sign half fallen.

locations.name: Doli Border Truck Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A gravel yard on the western edge of Doli City where lorries wait to run travellers out to the border stop of NGL. Drivers sleep in their cabs, drink tea at the stall and take whoever comes with a reason and a fare.

areas.name: Doli Truck Yard Departure Board
areas.text: A board of chalked names and times that nobody keeps to.

areas.name: Doli Truck Yard Tea Stall
areas.text: A tin-roofed stall with a kettle on a gas ring and stools made of crates.

locations.name: Doli Boxing Gym
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A basement gym under a hardware shop, open from dawn to midnight to anyone who pays the month. The owner was a middleweight once and still shouts the rounds himself.

areas.name: Doli Gym Bag Row
areas.text: A row of heavy bags hanging on chains, split and taped many times over.

areas.name: Doli Gym Ring
areas.text: A canvas ring with grey ropes, patched where the corner posts have rubbed it through.

locations.name: Doli Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small whitewashed chapel at the top of a stepped street, its bell rung by hand for services and funerals. Its priest lets travellers sleep on the pews when the hotels are full.

areas.name: Doli Chapel Bell Steps
areas.text: The stepped street below the chapel, where the bell can be heard across the city.

areas.name: Doli Chapel Pews
areas.text: Plain wooden pews under a beamed roof, a blanket folded on the end of each.

locations.name: Doli City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small, densely packed city in the Republic of Rokario and one of the nearest modern towns to the NGL border. Trains run to the rest of the country and buses to the border stop.

areas.name: Chalkboard Square
areas.text: The square with a public chalkboard where messages are left.

areas.name: Doli Back Streets
areas.text: The packed streets of flats and shops behind the station.

areas.name: Doli Station
areas.text:
The railway station, with its trains to the cities and its buses to the border.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to NGL Border Stop (about 800 Jenny), Peijin (about 6000 Jenny); ferries sail to Yorknew City (about 20000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Doli Covered Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An iron-framed market hall in the middle of Doli City, glazed overhead and loud underneath. Fish come up from the estuary before light, vegetables from the farms around Quen City by mid-morning, and the bargaining never stops.

areas.name: Doli Market Fish Aisle
areas.text: Wet stone and ice, eels in tubs and crabs climbing over each other.

areas.name: Doli Market Green Stalls
areas.text: Long tables of greens, roots and fruit from the farms upcountry.

areas.name: Doli Market Noodle Counter
areas.text: A steaming counter against the end wall that feeds the porters standing up.

locations.name: Doli Estuary Wharf
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The fishing wharf where the river below Doli City meets the sea in a wide brown estuary. Small diesel boats go out on the tide and come back with eel, flatfish and crab for the market.

areas.name: Doli Wharf Customs Shed
areas.text: A tin shed with a desk, a stamp and a harbourmaster who is rarely at it.

areas.name: Doli Wharf Fuel Pump
areas.text: A single pump at the end of the jetty where the boats wait their turn.

areas.name: Doli Wharf Net Poles
areas.text: A field of tall poles hung with drying nets, mended by old women on stools.

locations.name: Doli Firefly Marsh
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

A wide salt-edged marsh south of Doli City where the tide creeps up the creeks and the reeds stand head-high. One old tree grows alone on a hump in the middle; on summer nights its branches fill with small green lights.

areas.name: Doli Marsh Lone Tree
areas.text: The hump of firm ground and its single tree, the only dry seat in the marsh.

areas.name: Doli Marsh Reed Creeks
areas.text: Winding channels through the reeds, ankle-deep at low tide and waist-deep at high.

areas.name: Doli Marsh Sap Thicket
areas.text: A tangle of low shrubs on the marsh's edge with sticky, sweet-smelling stems.

locations.name: Doli Municipal Park
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A scrap of grass, gravel paths and plane trees between two blocks of flats in Doli City. Old men play cards here in the afternoon; after dark it belongs to the stray dogs and to anyone feeding them.

areas.name: Doli Park Gravel Circle
areas.text: An open ring of gravel in the middle of the park, wide enough for a fight.

areas.name: Doli Park Lamp Bench
areas.text: The one bench the lamp reaches, worn smooth by the card players.

locations.name: Doli Night Bar
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A low-ceilinged bar a street back from the station, where railwaymen drink after the last train and nobody asks a stranger his business. The landlord keeps a shogi board for regulars and a bat under the counter for the rest.

areas.name: Doli Bar Back Booth
areas.text: A booth behind a pillar where two people can talk without being heard.

areas.name: Doli Bar Counter
areas.text: The long counter, its brass rail kicked bright along the bottom.

locations.name: Doli Night Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A two-room clinic over a pharmacy that keeps its light on after the hospitals of Doli City close their doors. The doctor stitches, sets and bandages, and asks how only when the answer might matter.

areas.name: Doli Clinic Surgery
areas.text: A narrow room with a couch, a lamp on an arm and a locked drug cabinet.

areas.name: Doli Clinic Waiting Room
areas.text: A row of plastic chairs, a ticking clock and a rack of old magazines.

locations.name: Doli Woods
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

A forest outside Doli City where small, timid eight-legged dogs live in the bushes.

areas.name: Bush Paths
areas.text: The paths through the bushes where the dogs hide.

locations.name: Dolle Coast Guard Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

The kingdom's coast guard post for the harbour approaches: a two-storey block, a radio mast and one white cutter at its own jetty. The officers inspect cargo, fish drowned tourists out of the strait and, every January, try to keep the incoming applicants from stabbing each other on the quay.

areas.name: Coast Guard Cells
areas.text: Two barred cells at the back, meant for drunks and smugglers.

areas.name: Coast Guard Jetty
areas.text: A short jetty with the patrol cutter tied up and fuelled.

areas.name: Coast Guard Radio Room
areas.text: A room of receivers and charts where the night watch listens to the strait.

locations.name: Dolle Fish Auction Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A shed the length of a football pitch on the working end of the waterfront, where the night's catch goes under the hammer before sunrise. Buyers from the restaurants of Zaban City shout over each other in a dialect the applicants stepping off the ferries cannot follow.

areas.name: Dolle Auction Floor
areas.text: Rows of crates on the hosed concrete, ice melting into the drains, buyers tagging lots with coloured chits.

areas.name: Dolle Ice House
areas.text: A cold block of a building where the ice is crushed and shovelled into barrows.

areas.name: Dolle Porters' Bench
areas.text: A bench by the shed's back door where the porters smoke between lots and watch the ferries come in.

locations.name: Dolle Harbor
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A large port town where hopefuls for the Hunter Exam land every winter and set out to find the exam site. Its streets fill with fighters, cheats and guides selling directions, and a bus leaves for Zaban City every day. On a hill outside town stands a single enormous pine.

areas.name: Applicants' Row
areas.text: The lane of cheap inns and food stalls where applicants sleep, eat and spy on each other.

areas.name: Dolle Bus Stop
areas.text: The stop at the edge of town where the bus for Zaban City waits, its driver smiling too much.

areas.name: Dolle Pier
areas.text:
The long piers where the ships tie up and the ticket clerks sell passage on.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Beeskafmarro (about 2000 Jenny), Dentora Region (about 30000 Jenny); ferries sail to Whale Island (about 3000 Jenny), Yorknew City (about 20000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Dolle Pinewood
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

The dark pine forest that runs from the back of Dolle Harbor up to the hill of the lone pine. It is a few hours on foot by the right path and a night of going round in circles by any other, and the sounds it makes after dark send most applicants back to the bus.

areas.name: Pinewood Canopy Walk
areas.text: High branches where the trees grow close enough for something quick to cross from one to the next.

areas.name: Pinewood Fork Stones
areas.text: A clearing where three paths meet beside a heap of mossy boulders.

areas.name: Pinewood Ravine
areas.text: A cleft in the forest floor with a stream at the bottom and a fallen trunk across it.

locations.name: Dolle Seafarers' Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 1-5 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small whitewashed chapel built into the sea wall by fishermen's wives three generations back. Sailors leave model ships in the rafters for luck, and in exam season the pews hold as many nervous applicants as widows.

areas.name: Seafarers' Chapel Nave
areas.text: Plain pews under a ceiling of hanging ships, each one a little votive in wood and string.

areas.name: Sexton's Vestry
areas.text: A cramped side room with the candle stock, a kettle and the sexton's book.

locations.name: Dolle Shipyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-7 · Danger: Low]

Two slipways, a dry dock and a gantry crane at the eastern end of the port, where trawlers and the ferries that carry applicants from the islands are scraped, welded and painted. The yard works all hours and smells of hot metal and paint.

areas.name: Shipyard Dry Dock
areas.text: The drained dock where a hull sits on blocks, weeping rust onto the floor.

areas.name: Shipyard Gantry
areas.text: The crane's walkway high over the yard, open to the wind off the sea.

areas.name: Shipyard Welding Shed
areas.text: A tin shed full of blue light and the hiss of torches.

locations.name: Dons' Retreat
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

The top floors of a private tower that the heads of the Mafia take every September, one office for each Don and a round room where they meet. No name is on the building and no lift reaches those floors without a key.

areas.name: Dons' Guarded Landing
areas.text: A landing with armed men, a metal detector and a single lift door.

areas.name: Dons' Round Room
areas.text: A round room under a skylight, ten chairs at one table.

locations.name: Dorias
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The gambling city, built round its casino, which anyone may enter, children included. Some cards come only from a triple seven on the slots or from beating the casino's king at poker.

areas.name: Casino Floor
areas.text: The floor of slot machines and tables.

locations.name: Dorias Pawnshop
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A pawnshop across the street from the casino with three gold balls over its door and a cage over its counter. Players who lose at the tables come here to sell what they have left.

areas.name: Pawnshop Back Shelves
areas.text: Shelves of unclaimed goods in the dim back room.

areas.name: Pawnshop Cage Counter
areas.text: A counter behind a wire cage, a book beside the window.

locations.name: Dross Street Tenements
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

A poor quarter of brick tenements on the west side, crowded with families who came for factory work that has since left. The streets are narrow, the boilers fail every winter, and the Sengi Guild's unmarked door is somewhere in these blocks for those who know how to look.

areas.name: Dross Street Back Courts
areas.text: Courtyards of washing lines, bins and a broken swing.

areas.name: Dross Street Stoops
areas.text: Front steps where neighbours sit, smoke and watch the street.

locations.name: Drum Barrens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-34 · Danger: Severe]

A stretch of ground where foreign barges and lorries tip their chemical drums. Nothing grows, and the puddles shine in colours no water has.

areas.name: Barrens Dead Pond
areas.text: A hollow full of shining liquid, ringed by white crust.

areas.name: Barrens Drum Rows
areas.text: Rows of rusted drums, some upright, some split open on their sides.

locations.name: Dry Salt Pan
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: Severe]

A white salt pan deep in the desert, flat and blinding, where the ground cracks under the sun.

areas.name: Salt Flat
areas.text: The white open flat.

locations.name: Dumping Shore
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

The shore where barges from other countries tip their waste, and the sea carries back what floats.

areas.name: Barge Landing
areas.text: The landing where the barges unload.

areas.name: Rusting Hulls
areas.text: The hulls of dead ships beached and stripped.

locations.name: Duranti's Lunch Counter
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A narrow lunch counter near the Bull Market, all chrome and steam, where traders eat standing and settle deals with ketchup on their fingers. Its plate of the day is large and its coffee is bad.

areas.name: Duranti Back Booth
areas.text: One booth at the back where the noise covers a quiet talk.

areas.name: Duranti Counter Stools
areas.text: Red stools along the counter, with a view of the griddle.

locations.name: Eastbank Power Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

Four brick chimneys on the east bank mark the station that lights the downtown towers. Coal comes in by the trainload, steam goes up day and night, and the turbine hall is loud enough that the men inside talk with their hands.

areas.name: Eastbank Coal Siding
areas.text: A siding where wagons tip coal into the hoppers.

areas.name: Eastbank Switching Yard
areas.text: A fenced yard of transformers and breakers behind razor wire.

areas.name: Eastbank Turbine Hall
areas.text: A long hall of humming turbines and steel walkways.

locations.name: Estate Airship Mast
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A mooring mast on a shoulder of the mountain where the family's own airship ties up. Jobs take the family to every continent, and they do not queue at public airports.

areas.name: Airship Mast Fuel Store
areas.text: Fenced fuel tanks and a pump shed.

areas.name: Airship Mast Platform
areas.text: The top of the mast, where the ship's nose is clamped.

locations.name: Estate Infirmary
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The estate's own clinic, a long white building between the butlers' grounds and the kennels. Its doctor has set more broken bones than most hospitals see.

areas.name: Infirmary Antidote Cabinet
areas.text: A locked glass cabinet of antidotes and the notebook beside it.

areas.name: Infirmary Ward
areas.text: A ward of white beds with curtains on rails.

locations.name: Estate Jungle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-26 · Danger: High]

The dense jungle that covers the foot of Kukuroo Mountain inside the walls, under thick cloud. Paths run from the gate toward the butlers' grounds and the peak; anything off them belongs to the hound.

areas.name: Hound's Path
areas.text: The trodden path from the gate through the trees.

areas.name: Mike's Lair
areas.text: The clearing where the great hound sleeps on bones.

locations.name: Estate Motor Pool
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

The garage near the gate where the estate keeps its cars: limousines for the family, vans for supplies and plain sedans for jobs that should not look like anything. Butlers learn to drive here, and to drive badly on purpose when it matters.

areas.name: Motor Pool Garage Bays
areas.text: Rows of black cars under dust sheets, each with its keys in a locked box.

areas.name: Motor Pool Inspection Pit
areas.text: A pit lit by a hanging lamp, with a mechanic's legs sticking out of it.

locations.name: Estate Supply Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A yard just inside the wall where deliveries for the estate are unloaded: food for a house of hundreds, fuel, cloth, medicine and a great deal of meat. The drivers never come in; butlers meet them at the gate.

areas.name: Supply Yard Loading Dock
areas.text: The dock where crates come off the trucks.

areas.name: Supply Yard Weighbridge
areas.text: A weighbridge and a hut where every load is logged.

locations.name: Exam Airship
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The Hunter Association's airship that carries the applicants from one far site to the next. It has a lounge, sleeping corners and a view of the clouds, and the examiners ride in their own room.

areas.name: Airship Lounge
areas.text: The long lounge where the applicants rest and eye one another.

areas.name: Examiners' Room
areas.text: The private room where the examiners eat and talk.

locations.name: Exam Tunnel
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A tunnel more than eighty kilometres long a hundred storeys under Zaban City, where hundreds of applicants with numbered badges wait for the exam to start. It runs mostly flat, then turns into a long climb of stairs, and it ends in the fog of the wetlands.

areas.name: Badge Hall
areas.text: The hall at the bottom of the lift where a little man hands out numbered badges.

areas.name: Long Run
areas.text: The flat stretch of tunnel where the examiner sets the pace.

areas.name: Tunnel Stairs
areas.text: The long stairs at the end that climb to daylight.

locations.name: Far Coast Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-10 · Danger: Low]

The road that runs along the cliffs from Beeskafmarro to the tower's strait, with one filling station and long stretches of nothing.

areas.name: Coast Road Cliff Bend
areas.text: A sharp bend over the sea with a broken guard rail.

areas.name: Coast Road Filling Station
areas.text: A lone filling station with two pumps and a shop.

locations.name: Far Forage Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-34 · Danger: Severe]

A long ridge at the far edge of the country's forests, where game is plentiful and people are few.

areas.name: Far Forage Game Trails
areas.text: Trails worn by deer and boar along the ridge's spine.

areas.name: Far Forage Shepherd's Hut
areas.text: An empty stone hut on the ridge, its roof half fallen in.

locations.name: Ferrin Creek Sawmill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low]

A sawmill on a creek where the farmland east of Nancha City gives out to forest. Its loggers fell the outer woods and haul the timber to the city by lorry; past a certain ridge they will not cut, and they will not quite say why.

areas.name: Sawmill Bunkhouse
areas.text: A long hut of bunks, a stove and wet boots in rows.

areas.name: Sawmill Floor
areas.text: A roofed floor of band saws, sawdust ankle-deep and a conveyor of planks.

areas.name: Sawmill Log Pond
areas.text: A dammed pond where the logs float before they go to the saw.

locations.name: Feverwort Infirmary
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The country's largest house of healing, run by herbalists and bone-setters. No modern medicine may cross the border, so fevers are fought with willow bark and steam, and wounds with honey and clean linen.

areas.name: Feverwort Burial Garden
areas.text: A quiet garden behind the ward, its rows of wooden markers close together.

areas.name: Feverwort Drying Loft
areas.text: The loft where herbs hang upside down in bunches to dry.

areas.name: Feverwort Long Ward
areas.text: A ward of rope beds under open windows, smelling of steam and bitter herbs.

locations.name: Final Phase Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The hall where the exam's last phase is fought: a one-on-one tournament in which one loss is enough to fail and one win is enough to pass. The chairman draws up the bracket after talking to each applicant.

areas.name: Interview Room
areas.text: The small room where the chairman talks to each applicant alone.

areas.name: Tournament Floor
areas.text: The open floor where the fights are held.

locations.name: Finalists' Rest Hotel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A quiet seaside hotel owned by the exam's selection committee, where the airship brings the last applicants for the final phase. Each of them has a room and a few hours to wait before the bracket is posted.

areas.name: Rest Hotel Gravel Garden
areas.text: A raked garden where someone has been practising footwork.

areas.name: Rest Hotel Guest Rooms
areas.text: A corridor of single rooms, each with a sea view and a lock.

areas.name: Rest Hotel Lobby
areas.text: The lobby where guards watch the door and the finalists pass one another.

locations.name: First King's Temple
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

The oldest temple of the capital, raised to the First King who made a small, threatened warlord state into the root of the present empire. Pilgrims climb the hill steps on his feast days and leave paper offerings at his statue.

areas.name: Temple Hill Steps
areas.text: A long flight of worn stone steps lined with offerings and incense burners.

areas.name: Temple Manuscript Library
areas.text: A dim library of locked cases, where monks copy and recopy brittle scrolls.

locations.name: Floor Master Floors
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

The floors from the 230th to the 250th, each the home of one of the twenty-one Floor Masters, the arena's highest ranked fighters. A Floor Master's floor is taken only by beating its owner.

areas.name: Challenge Lift
areas.text: The lift that rises to the Floor Masters' floors only for a challenger.

areas.name: Master's Hall
areas.text: A floor-wide hall kept for one fighter.

locations.name: Forest Warden Lodge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

The lodge of the forest wardens, who keep the country's woods, mark trees for felling and turn travellers back from the forbidden forests. Visitors who stray are brought here first.

areas.name: Warden Lodge Armoury Nook
areas.text: A curtained corner where a rack of rifles stands oiled and ready.

areas.name: Warden Lodge Front Room
areas.text: A room of maps on hide and a book of travellers turned back.

areas.name: Warden Lodge Horse Line
areas.text: A covered line where the wardens' horses wait saddled for patrol.

locations.name: Founder's Longhouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 22-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The seat of the country's government: a long timber hall where the founder of the movement and his council hear petitions, pass judgements and write the laws that keep the machines out. Petitioners queue for days to be heard.

areas.name: Longhouse Council Room
areas.text: A closed room behind the hall, its door guarded day and night.

areas.name: Longhouse Petition Hall
areas.text: The long hall itself, with the council's benches at the far end and the petitioners at the near.

areas.name: Longhouse Waiting Mound
areas.text: The grassy mound before the doors where petitioners camp under blankets.

locations.name: Foundlings' Doorstep
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A sheltered shelf beside a shrine door where babies are left, and a bell to ring when one is. Whoever answers it takes the child in, and the city counts the child as its own.

areas.name: Doorstep Bell Shelf
areas.text: The covered shelf, its boards padded and a bell rope hanging beside it.

areas.name: Doorstep Night Bench
areas.text: A bench inside the door where a volunteer sleeps sitting up, within reach of the bell.

locations.name: Fountain Corner Plaza
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A wide paved corner where the shopping streets meet, with a dry fountain at its middle and buskers on its edges. Street acts set up here in auction season because the foot traffic never stops.

areas.name: Fountain Corner Pitch
areas.text: The open paving where a table and a crowd fit.

areas.name: Fountain Corner Rim
areas.text: The dry fountain's stone rim, where performers stand.

locations.name: Foxbear Glade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A small clearing in the forest, half grown over with bracken. Three years ago a boy who ignored the claw marks was caught here by a foxbear mother, and a tall, white-haired stranger in a blue cap stepped in between them.

areas.name: Foxbear Glade Bracken
areas.text: Waist-high bracken over soft ground, broken by old paths.

areas.name: Foxbear Glade Fallen Trunk
areas.text: A mossed trunk across the glade's edge, a good seat for a long story.

locations.name: Gannet Stack
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low]

A sheer rock out of the sea off the island's east coast, white with the droppings of thousands of nesting seabirds. The islanders row out in spring to take eggs from its lower ledges, and they come back smelling of it for days.

areas.name: Gannet Stack Egg Ledges
areas.text: The crowded lower ledges where the eggs are taken in spring.

areas.name: Gannet Stack Landing
areas.text: A slippery rock shelf where a boat can just about get a person ashore.

locations.name: Gasworks Wasteland
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

Where the old gasworks stood on the west edge there is now only rubble, tall weeds and the iron skeleton of a gasholder. Children dare each other to climb it, stray dogs run in packs, and a few homeless men have built shacks under the embankment.

areas.name: Gasholder Skeleton
areas.text: The rusted iron frame of the gasholder, open to the sky.

areas.name: Gasworks Embankment Shacks
areas.text: Shacks of board and tarpaulin against the rail embankment.

areas.name: Gasworks Rubble Field
areas.text: Acres of broken brick, weeds and snapped pipes.

locations.name: Gatekeeper's Booth
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A sentry box no bigger than a bus shelter, standing in the shadow of the Testing Gate. A balding old man in a guard's cap sits in it with a telephone that rings straight through to the butlers on the mountain.

areas.name: Gatekeeper's Booth Telephone
areas.text: The wall phone, its line running up the mountain to the butlers' house.

areas.name: Gatekeeper's Booth Window
areas.text: The sliding window where tourists ask silly questions and get patient answers.

locations.name: Gemmo Marshes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-36 · Danger: Deadly]

A wide stretch of marsh in the north-east, half water and half reed, crossed by duckboard paths that only the reed cutters trust. A watchtower from an older war leans over it.

areas.name: Gemmo Marsh Duckboards
areas.text: Narrow board paths over black water, rotten in places.

areas.name: Gemmo Marsh Watchtower
areas.text: A leaning concrete tower half sunk in the marsh.

locations.name: Gilder Lane Pawnbrokers
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A short lane off the main street lined with pawnshops, each window crammed with watches, cameras, knives and medals. In exam season they buy applicants' gear cheap from those who have given up and sell it dear to those who have not.

areas.name: Gilder Lane Back Room
areas.text: A back room behind one of the counters where the better goods are kept.

areas.name: Gilder Lane Windows
areas.text: The barred shop windows along the lane, crowded with other people's belongings.

locations.name: Gittarackur's Burrow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A hole in the forest floor of Zevil Island, filled back in so neatly that the ground barely shows it. Anyone who walks over it is being watched from below.

areas.name: Burrow Needle Tree
areas.text: The tree beside it with a few needles still in its bark.

areas.name: Burrow Turned Earth
areas.text: The square of loose soil over the hole, scattered with leaves.

locations.name: Gold Dust Girl's Mansion
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A shuttered mansion in its own grounds whose guard, a calm man in a suit, turns every visitor away with a warning about the traps inside. Gold glints in the gutter by the drains.

areas.name: Gold Dust Mansion Bath Room
areas.text: A hidden room far below, with a tiled bath glittering with gold.

areas.name: Gold Dust Mansion Steps
areas.text: The front steps where the guard stands.

areas.name: Gold Dust Mansion Trap Stair
areas.text: A stair down through floor after floor of traps.

locations.name: Gordeau Arroyo
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A deep canyon cut through red rock by flash floods, dry most of the year and roaring for an hour after a storm. The only trees in the desert grow along its floor.

areas.name: Arroyo Flood Line
areas.text: A tide mark of driftwood and rubbish high up the canyon wall.

areas.name: Arroyo Floor
areas.text: A sandy floor between red walls, with cottonwoods leaning in the shade.

locations.name: Gordeau Balloon Ledge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

A high, flat ledge of rock above the open desert, with a long view of the road and a sheer face below. A hot-air balloon would have to fall a long way to land anywhere else.

areas.name: Balloon Ledge Cliff Face
areas.text: The face below the ledge, steep enough to climb down only by sliding.

areas.name: Balloon Ledge Rim
areas.text: The edge of the ledge, where a person can sit with their feet over the drop.

locations.name: Gordeau Cement Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A working cement plant whose silos are the first thing a driver sees of the city from the desert. The kiln burns day and night and coats the whole works in fine grey dust.

areas.name: Cement Works Kiln House
areas.text: The long rotating kiln inside a shed that glows at the far end.

areas.name: Cement Works Silo Gallery
areas.text: A catwalk running along the tops of the silos, high above the yard.

locations.name: Gordeau Date Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate]

An irrigated farm of date palms and vegetable plots, green against the sand, that sells its fruit at the city markets. The palms are older than the airport.

areas.name: Date Farm Palm Rows
areas.text: Long shaded avenues of palms with ditches of water running between them.

areas.name: Date Farm Porch
areas.text: A wide farmhouse porch with a rocking chair and a crate of fruit.

locations.name: Gordeau Desert
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-30 · Danger: Severe]

A large, dry wasteland on the outskirts of Yorknew City, crossed by the road to Lingon Airport. Off the road there is nothing but rock, sand and heat, and nobody to see what happens.

areas.name: Open Sand
areas.text: The flat open sand where a fight can be seen for miles and heard by nobody.

areas.name: Rock Outcrop
areas.text: A spine of rock rising from the sand, the only shade.

locations.name: Gordeau Drive-In Cinema
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

An open-air cinema on the edge of town, its screen facing away from the city so the lights do not wash it out. Teenagers from the outskirts fill it at the end of every week.

areas.name: Drive-In Back Row
areas.text: The last row of speaker posts, where the cars park dark and close.

areas.name: Drive-In Projection Hut
areas.text: A hut of whirring projectors at the back of the lot.

locations.name: Gordeau Dune Sea
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

Deep in the desert, beyond the last road, the sand rises into dunes that roll on to the horizon. Cars stall here and people on foot lose their way within an hour.

areas.name: Dune Sea High Crest
areas.text: The top of the tallest dune, where the wind blows sand off the edge.

areas.name: Dune Sea Trough
areas.text: A long trough between dunes, quiet and baking.

locations.name: Gordeau Footpath Wash
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A dry streambed that winds out of the western sands toward the city, easier walking than the dunes on either side. Walkers who have no business on the highway use it.

areas.name: Footpath Wash Bend
areas.text: A sharp bend where the bed cuts deep and the banks give shade.
