areas.name: Footpath Wash Thorn Thicket
areas.text: A tangle of thorn bushes where the wash widens.

locations.name: Gordeau Gun Club
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A private shooting club out in the scrub, with a pistol range, a rifle range and a clubhouse bar. Members only, and the membership is very particular.

areas.name: Gun Club Clubhouse
areas.text: A bar of dark wood under mounted trophies and a ceiling fan.

areas.name: Gun Club Pistol Range
areas.text: A line of booths facing paper targets twenty paces off.

locations.name: Gordeau Gypsum Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A white open-pit quarry cut in terraces into the desert floor, worked for gypsum until the price fell. A dragline and a few sheds still stand on the rim.

areas.name: Gypsum Quarry Dragline
areas.text: A huge rusting dragline left on the rim with its bucket on the ground.

areas.name: Gypsum Quarry Terraces
areas.text: Stepped white walls running down into the pit.

locations.name: Gordeau Highway Patrol Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A small police post where the airport highway leaves the city limits, with two patrol cars, a holding cell and officers who mostly hand out speeding tickets.

areas.name: Patrol Post Front Desk
areas.text: A counter, a phone and a board of wanted posters going yellow.

areas.name: Patrol Post Holding Cell
areas.text: One barred cell with one bunk and a bucket.

locations.name: Gordeau Line Terminus
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The last station on a subway line, built where the city's buildings give way to desert, so that the outskirts can ride into downtown. Its trains wait here with their doors open between runs.

areas.name: Terminus Platform
areas.text: A long tiled platform where the train sits at the buffers.

areas.name: Terminus Ticket Hall
areas.text: A dusty hall of turnstiles and ticket machines, with sand blown in at the doors.

locations.name: Gordeau Motor Court
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A one-storey motel built round its own car park, where travellers who missed the last coach to the city sleep on thin mattresses. The pool has been dry for years.

areas.name: Motor Court Dry Pool
areas.text: The cracked empty pool, half filled with drifted sand and a lost sandal.

areas.name: Motor Court Office
areas.text: A cramped reception with a key board, a bell and a fan turning slowly.

locations.name: Gordeau Night Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A doctor's surgery on the edge of the outskirts that keeps its doorbell lit all night. The day patients come with coughs; the night patients come through the back.

areas.name: Night Clinic Back Door
areas.text: A narrow alley door with a buzzer and a spyhole.

areas.name: Night Clinic Surgery
areas.text: A surgery under a strong lamp, a steel table and a tray of instruments.

locations.name: Gordeau Potter's Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A walled patch of desert where the city buries the people nobody claims: vagrants, the drowned and the unidentified, each under a numbered stake instead of a name.

areas.name: Potter's Field Digger's Shack
areas.text: A shack with spades, a lantern and a book of numbers and dates.

areas.name: Potter's Field Stake Rows
areas.text: Rows of short numbered stakes running off into the heat haze.

locations.name: Gordeau Pumping Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High]

The pumping station that pushes the city's water out of deep wells and into the mains. Without it, the outskirts would be dry in a week.

areas.name: Pumping Station Pump Hall
areas.text: A hall of green pumps and pipes the width of a man, roaring together.

areas.name: Pumping Station Reservoir Tank
areas.text: A steel tank on the hill above the station, with a ladder up its side.

locations.name: Gordeau Rock Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: Severe]

A field of tall rock spires in the desert where the wind moans through the stones and shadows fall long.

areas.name: Spire Maze
areas.text: The tangle of spires and the passages between them.

locations.name: Gordeau Scrapyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

A big scrapyard on the city's edge where cars and machinery are crushed into blocks and sold off by weight. The crusher runs from dawn till dark.

areas.name: Scrapyard Crusher
areas.text: The great hydraulic press, its bed stained dark, a cube of metal at its mouth.

areas.name: Scrapyard Scale House
areas.text: A hut by the gate where loads are weighed and paid for in cash.

locations.name: Gordeau Settlement School
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A small school for the children of the airport, the farms and the camp, run by one teacher who has stayed for twenty years. The bus comes when it can.

areas.name: Settlement School Classroom
areas.text: One room of battered desks and a blackboard with a map pinned beside it.

areas.name: Settlement School Yard
areas.text: A dusty yard with a flagpole and a single shade tree.

locations.name: Gordeau Wayside Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small whitewashed chapel on the airport road, built by a religious order for drivers and travellers. Its door is never locked and its candles are never quite out.

areas.name: Wayside Chapel Confessional
areas.text: A wooden booth in the corner with a lattice and a worn kneeler.

areas.name: Wayside Chapel Nave
areas.text: A short nave of six pews and a plain altar, bright with candles in jars.

locations.name: Gorteau Border Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: Deadly]

The border post on the road from West Gorteau, a wall, a gate and searchlights. Few foreigners are let through.

areas.name: Border Gate
areas.text: The gate in the wall.

locations.name: Gorteau National Gungi Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-34 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The home of Gungi, the strategy game East Gorteau invented and nearly everyone in the country plays. The national tournaments are fought here under a demonstration board the size of a wall, and East Gorteau has won every international tournament ever held. The reigning champion is a blind girl named Komugi.

areas.name: Gungi Hall Demonstration Wall
areas.text: The great wall board where a match is shown to the hall piece by piece.

areas.name: Gungi Hall Record Room
areas.text: A back room of bound game records, ordered by year and by player.

areas.name: Gungi Hall Tournament Floor
areas.text: Rows of low tables and cushions under the hall's tiers of seats.

locations.name: Greed Island Badlands
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

Badlands full of stone pillars and monsters on the way to Masadora: one-eyed giants, fire-breathing lizards and worse. Every monster turns into its card when beaten.

areas.name: Digging Ground
areas.text: The ground where tunnels have been dug through the pillars.

areas.name: Pillar Field
areas.text: The forest of stone pillars where the monsters live.

locations.name: Greed Island Hills
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

Rolling hills across the island where the bubble horses run, the one-eyed giants roam and the strange creatures of the game live.

areas.name: Bubble Horse Meadow
areas.text: The meadow where the bubble horses graze.

locations.name: Greed Island Port
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe]

The only port in the game, run by an unscrupulous harbourmaster. A player who wants to leave the game by its door must get past him.

areas.name: Harbourmaster's Office
areas.text: The office where the harbourmaster sits.

areas.name: Port Tower
areas.text: The tower from which players leave the game.

locations.name: Greed Island Sea Cliffs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-26 · Danger: High]

The high cliffs that ring most of the island, sheer to the surf with seabirds nesting on every ledge. On a clear day a player at the top can see nothing but sea in every direction, which some find comforting and some do not.

areas.name: Sea Cliffs Ladder Ledge
areas.text: A ledge halfway down with an old rope ladder hanging from it.

areas.name: Sea Cliffs Rim
areas.text: The grassy rim of the cliffs, the wind tearing at it.

locations.name: Greed Island Starting Point
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The tower where every player arrives on entering the game, its floor and walls covered in designs. A woman on a floating seat, Eta, greets each newcomer and explains the rules; a stair winds down to an endless grassy plain.

areas.name: Entry Chamber
areas.text: The small room where a new player first appears.

areas.name: Rules Hall
areas.text: The round hall where Eta explains the game.

areas.name: Starting Plain
areas.text: The grass plain at the tower's foot, stretching away in every direction.

locations.name: Green Creed Meeting House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A round meeting house built around a living tree, where villagers gather on rest days to hear the creed read: that humankind went wrong when it let machines think and work for it. Weddings and funerals are held here too.

areas.name: Green Creed Porch
areas.text: A deep porch where the elders sit after meetings and settle village business.

areas.name: Green Creed Ring Hall
areas.text: The round hall, its benches in a ring around the tree trunk at its centre.

locations.name: Greyback Hills
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-32 · Danger: Severe]

A range of grey wooded hills in the north of the country, marked forbidden to travellers. The country says it is a nature sanctuary; the villagers say the hills are where their sons go to work and come back rich and quiet.

areas.name: Greyback Forbidden Sign
areas.text: A carved post at the foot of the hills warning all travellers back.

areas.name: Greyback Goat Track
areas.text: A narrow track along the ridges, used by goats and by people who do not want to be seen.

locations.name: Gridline Internet Café
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An internet café near the central station, rented by the hour, open all night. Travellers check their mail, students play network games, and dealers look up prices before the auctions open.

areas.name: Gridline Booth Row
areas.text: A long row of partitioned booths, each with a monitor and a hard chair.

areas.name: Gridline Front Desk
areas.text: The desk where hours are paid for and cards are swiped.

locations.name: Grimes Auto Salvage
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

A scrapyard on the west edge where wrecks are stripped for parts and crushed into blocks. Mechanics buy here cheap, and a car that arrives on a tow is never asked where it came from.

areas.name: Grimes Crusher Pit
areas.text: The crusher in its concrete pit with a booth of levers.

areas.name: Grimes Wreck Rows
areas.text: Lanes of stripped cars stacked two high.

locations.name: Grindstone Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

A quarry cut into the hillside by hand, where millstones, whetstones and building stone are split with wedges and hauled away on sledges. Prisoners from the stockade work beside paid quarrymen.

areas.name: Grindstone Quarry Face
areas.text: The cut face of the hill, stepped like stairs and white with dust.

areas.name: Grindstone Quarry Sledge Track
areas.text: The worn track down which the stone goes on wooden sledges.

locations.name: Gullrest Hostel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-5 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A narrow hostel squeezed between two warehouses, all bunk rooms and steel lockers, run by a widow who has seen thirty winters of applicants pass through. She takes cash up front, bars weapons from the dormitories and does not ask what anyone is in town for.

areas.name: Gullrest Attic
areas.text: A low attic room under the eaves with one window and a desk covered in notes.

areas.name: Gullrest Bunk Rooms
areas.text: Rooms of iron bunks, six to a room, each guest with a locker and a key on a string.

areas.name: Gullrest Lobby
areas.text: A cramped lobby with a counter, a noticeboard of ferry times and a television on a bracket.

locations.name: Gullscrap Point
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A headland at the city's sea edge, built out of rubbish and loud with gulls. Fishermen cast from it and egg collectors climb it.

areas.name: Gullscrap Egg Ledges
areas.text: Ledges of packed rubbish thick with nesting gulls.

areas.name: Gullscrap Lookout Perch
areas.text: A seat of crates at the very tip, with a horn to blow.

locations.name: Gullwing Tavern
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The island's one bar, low-ceilinged and warm, with a whale's rib nailed over the door. Fishermen drink here after the catch, visiting crews spend their pay, and every tall story the island owns gets told at the counter at least once a week.

areas.name: Gullwing Counter
areas.text: The long counter, scarred with knife marks and bottle rings.

areas.name: Gullwing Stove Corner
areas.text: A corner by the iron stove where the old men sit with their cards.

locations.name: Gunshot Glade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

An open glade among the trees where the forest people once held midsummer dances.

areas.name: Gunshot Glade Dance Ring
areas.text: A ring of flat stones at the glade's centre, laid for dancing.

areas.name: Gunshot Glade Treeline
areas.text: The edge of the glade, where the trunks will one day carry bullet scars.

locations.name: Gyudondond Quarter
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A quarter of the city taken over by the last of the Gyudondond Tribe, who were given a place here when nowhere else would have them. On festival nights their Bap, the bandaged dancing warriors, play songs on their own bodies, and the sound carries across the heaps.

areas.name: Gyudondond Dance Court
areas.text: An open court under awnings where the Bap dance and play the songs of battle.

areas.name: Gyudondond Hut Lane
areas.text: A lane of low huts where bamboo and stones for the piercings dry on the roofs.

locations.name: Hacker's Loft
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

A loft over a closed garage, rented to a young man who works for whoever pays and works fast. The Mafia keeps his number for jobs that need records rather than guns.

areas.name: Loft Garage Below
areas.text: The empty garage under the loft, its shutter down.

areas.name: Loft Terminal Bank
areas.text: A wall of screens and towers on trestle tables.

locations.name: Halfway Diner
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A diner halfway along the highway between the town and Parasta. Truckers stop for coffee and the jukebox, and tourists stop because it is the only lit window for miles.

areas.name: Diner Counter
areas.text: A long counter of stools and a coffee urn.

areas.name: Diner Truck Park
areas.text: A gravel car park of trucks.

locations.name: Hall of the Burning Will
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A school on gym row that claims to teach the secret of the fighters above the 200th floor. Its master talks of inner fire and willpower, sells grades in coloured belts and makes his students hold their breath until they faint.

areas.name: Burning Will Master's Dais
areas.text: A raised dais with a cushion, incense and a box for fees.

areas.name: Burning Will Meditation Floor
areas.text: A polished floor where students sit in rows with their eyes shut.

locations.name: Handset Bazaar
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A covered arcade of stalls selling mobile phones, pagers, chargers and cards, new and secondhand and some with their last owner's numbers still in them. Nothing has a fixed price, and the loudest buyer wins.

areas.name: Bazaar Repair Benches
areas.text: Benches at the back where phones are opened, fixed and wiped.

areas.name: Bazaar Stall Rows
areas.text: Narrow aisles of glass-topped stalls under a tin roof.

locations.name: Harbour General Store
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The only shop on the island that sells anything not caught in the sea: tins, rope, batteries, school exercise books, tobacco, boots and sweets. What it lacks it orders from the mainland and you wait a month.

areas.name: General Store Back Room
areas.text: A storeroom of crates waiting for the next boat out or just come off one.

areas.name: General Store Counter
areas.text: The single counter with its till, its jars of sweets and its order book.

locations.name: Harbour Rest Guesthouse
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 1-4 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A narrow three-storey house on the harbour front that lets its upper rooms to whoever the ships bring and the weather keeps. A widow runs it and feeds her guests at her own table, whether they meant to eat or not.

areas.name: Harbour Rest Front Room
areas.text: A parlour and dining table where the guests are made to eat.

areas.name: Harbour Rest Top Room
areas.text: A locked room under the eaves, dusted weekly and never let.

locations.name: Haruna's Cottage
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small cottage at the edge of the village where a mother lives with her two children, a boy of nine and his little sister. The boy keeps a diary of everything his sister does, and the sister has announced she will marry him.

areas.name: Haruna's Cottage Garden Patch
areas.text: A fenced patch of beans and cabbages behind the house, with a gate to the river path.

areas.name: Haruna's Cottage Kitchen
areas.text: One warm room with a hearth, a table and three stools, a diary on the shelf.

locations.name: Hass Border Barracks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

An army barracks in the foothills of the Roto Mountains on the Hass side, built for a war that never came and now half empty. A skeleton company keeps the gate and the boilers; the rest of the huts stand shut.

areas.name: Hass Barracks Empty Huts
areas.text: Rows of shut wooden huts with stripped beds and cold stoves.

areas.name: Hass Barracks Gatehouse
areas.text: A barred gate and a sentry box with a field telephone.

locations.name: Hass Highland Dairy
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A dairy farm on the high pasture where the Roto Mountains run into Hass, its herd brought down to the barn every evening and its milk collected by lorry at a stand by the road.

areas.name: Hass Dairy Barn
areas.text: A long barn of stalls and steaming cattle, a radio playing for the cows.

areas.name: Hass Dairy Churn Stand
areas.text: A wooden platform by the road where the churns wait for the lorry.

locations.name: Hass Parish Church
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A stone church in a market town of the Republic of Hass, older than the republic itself, with a parish hall beside it where the town holds its dances, meetings and blood drives.

areas.name: Hass Parish Hall Stage
areas.text: A wooden stage in the hall, curtained, its boards hollow underfoot.

areas.name: Hass Parish Nave
areas.text: A cold stone nave with plain glass and the names of the dead on the walls.

locations.name: Hass Rail Junction
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The busiest rail junction in the Republic of Hass, where the line from Rokario meets the lines east to West Gorteau and south to the coast. Passengers change trains here and wait in its buffet.

areas.name: Hass Junction Buffet
areas.text: A steamy buffet of tea urns and buns, its windows running with water.

areas.name: Hass Junction Footbridge
areas.text: An iron footbridge over five platforms, painted many times in the same green.

areas.name: Hass Junction Lost Property
areas.text: A back room of shelves, umbrellas and labelled bags.

locations.name: Hass Vineyards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

Terraced vineyards on the south-facing slopes east of the Hass market towns, their rows tied to wires and their grapes pressed in a stone winery at the bottom of the hill.

areas.name: Hass Vine Terraces
areas.text: Steps of red soil held by dry stone walls, vines in rows on wires.

areas.name: Hass Wild Vine Terraces
areas.text: The abandoned top terraces where the vines have climbed the walls.

areas.name: Hass Winery Cellar
areas.text: A cool cellar of barrels under the stone winery, smelling of oak.

locations.name: Hass Wheat Cooperative
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A farmers' cooperative on the western plain of the Republic of Hass that owns the silos, the harvesters and the lorries its members share. Its noticeboard is the closest thing the plain has to a newspaper.

areas.name: Hass Cooperative Noticeboard
areas.text: A cork board under a little roof, layered with sale notices and grudges.

areas.name: Hass Cooperative Silos
areas.text: Tall concrete silos with a conveyor up the side, dust drifting off the top.

locations.name: Have-Not Day-Labour Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-24 · Danger: High]

An open yard at the back of the docks where Have-Nots wait each morning to be picked for a day's work. Foremen walk the line and point; the rest drink tea and wait for the second round.

areas.name: Labour Yard Hiring Line
areas.text: The chalk line where workers stand to be chosen.

areas.name: Labour Yard Tea Stall
areas.text: A stall of crates and a kettle under a tarpaulin, where the gossip of the docks is traded.

locations.name: Heap Generator Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A fenced yard of salvaged generators, coaxed back to life and run in turns, that feeds lamps, pumps and the church projector. Cables leave it in every direction like roots.

areas.name: Generator Yard Engine Row
areas.text: A line of rumbling generators on pallets, each patched in its own way.

areas.name: Generator Yard Fuel Store
areas.text: A pit lined with drums of fuel under a tarpaulin and a no-smoking sign.

locations.name: Heap Goat Folds
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Pens of pallet wood where the city's goats are kept, herded out each day to graze the heaps for anything green. They give milk and, now and then, a feast.

areas.name: Goat Folds Grazing Slope
areas.text: The heap slope the herd is driven up each morning, picked bare of green.

areas.name: Goat Folds Milking Pen
areas.text: A pen with a stool and a bucket, where the herders milk at dawn.

locations.name: Heap Radio Shack
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A shack with a tall aerial of welded bedframes, from which a resident broadcasts news, songs and lost-child notices across the city every evening.

areas.name: Radio Shack Aerial Yard
areas.text: The yard where the bedframe aerial stands, guyed with wire to stakes in the rubbish.

areas.name: Radio Shack Studio
areas.text: A cramped room with a mixing desk from a dump and egg boxes on the walls.

locations.name: Heap School
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A one-room school where an old resident teaches reading and sums from whatever schoolbooks the trucks bring. The books come in many languages, so the children learn several whether they mean to or not.

areas.name: Heap School Book Crate
areas.text: A crate of schoolbooks in many alphabets, their covers gone and their corners chewed.

areas.name: Heap School Tin Board
areas.text: A sheet of beaten tin painted black, chalk dust thick on the floor below it.

locations.name: Heavens Arena
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The world's most popular fighting site: a tower 991 metres tall with 251 floors, the fourth tallest building in the world, where about four thousand fighters a day climb by winning. More than a billion spectators come each year, and the building has its own restaurants and shops. Anyone may register; most go home sore.

areas.name: Arena Plaza
areas.text:
The plaza at the foot of the tower where airships, buses and taxis bring the crowds.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Dentora Region (about 15000 Jenny), Yorknew City (about 25000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Ground Floor Rings
areas.text: The ring-filled first floor where the newcomers are sorted by a single fight.

areas.name: Registration Desk
areas.text: The desk on the ground floor where a newcomer signs up and is sent to a first ring.

locations.name: Heil-Ly Brokerage House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

An old merchant house in the capital's gallery district, outwardly a dealer in antiques and fine art. Its clients come by appointment and leave by a side door.

areas.name: Heil-Ly Records Office
areas.text: A cramped room upstairs where two clerks keep the house's real accounts.

areas.name: Heil-Ly Viewing Salon
areas.text: A quiet room of silk screens where goods are shown one at a time on a velvet cloth.

locations.name: Hemlock Deep
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-34 · Danger: Severe]

Old hemlock forest near the heart of the country, so dark at noon that travellers light lamps.

areas.name: Hemlock Deep Fallen Giant
areas.text: A huge fallen hemlock lying across a hollow, a natural wall and a hiding place.

areas.name: Hemlock Deep Mist Floor
areas.text: The forest floor under the hemlocks, soft with needles and wrapped in mist.

locations.name: Hide-and-Seek Auction Club
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A nightclub somewhere in the city that the Mafia borrows for its conditional auctions, sales where the lot is not an object but a job. The address changes; the regulars always hear of it.

areas.name: Club Registration Booth
areas.text: A cloakroom window where the fee is paid and a number written down.

areas.name: Conditional Auction Stage
areas.text: A low stage under one hard spotlight, with a microphone and a rack of flyers.

locations.name: Hillside Dairy
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-8 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A family dairy farm on the slopes above the coast that sends milk to Beeskafmarro every morning.

areas.name: Dairy Farmhouse Kitchen
areas.text: The farmhouse kitchen with its big table.

areas.name: Dairy Milking Shed
areas.text: The shed where the cows are milked by machine.

locations.name: Hoihoi Hotel
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-32 · Danger: Severe]

A hotel in the Kakin Empire, one of the royal family's many, whose staff are discreet about who comes and goes and why.

areas.name: Hoihoi Meeting Room
areas.text: The guarded room where applicants are interviewed.

locations.name: Hollis Wholesale Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The wholesale food market under a long iron roof, where the city's restaurants buy their fish, meat and greens before the sun is up. By eight it is hosed down and empty.

areas.name: Hollis Cold Stores
areas.text: A corridor of steel cold-room doors.

areas.name: Hollis Fish Hall
areas.text: Rows of ice tables under hanging lamps.

locations.name: Hoofiron Forge
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A smithy that shoes the country's horses and mends its ploughs, all by hand and hammer. The smith may work only iron smelted inside the country, and the law inspects his scrap pile twice a year.

areas.name: Hoofiron Anvil Floor
areas.text: The front of the smithy, open to the road, where the anvil rings and horses wait to be shod.

areas.name: Hoofiron Scrap Pile
areas.text: A heap of bent iron behind the forge, the pile the law comes to count.

locations.name: Hotel Bayloke
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-24 · Danger: High]

A high-class hotel in Yorknew City, one name among many on the city's avenues.

areas.name: Bayloke Bar
areas.text: The hotel bar, dark and quiet.

locations.name: Hotel Beitacle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-26 · Danger: High]

A high-class hotel in Yorknew City where rich visitors stay during the auctions, with suites large enough for a whole household and its guards.

areas.name: Beitacle Lobby
areas.text: The marble lobby with its fountain and its concierge.

areas.name: Beitacle Suite
areas.text: The top-floor suite with its locked doors and its guards.

locations.name: Hotel Grandvale
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A grand old hotel off Auction Avenue with high ceilings and tired carpets, popular with visitors who want to look rich without paying what the new towers ask. Its suites sleep four and its bar never closes.

areas.name: Grandvale Long Bar
areas.text: A long polished bar in the lobby, under the chandelier.

areas.name: Grandvale Suite
areas.text: A suite of two rooms with a sofa, a minibar and a view of the avenue.

locations.name: Hotel Lavanda
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A business hotel with no sign over the door, used by firms that prefer their meetings unrecorded. Its staff do not remember guests, and its conference rooms have no windows.

areas.name: Lavanda Conference Room
areas.text: A windowless room with a long table and leather chairs.

areas.name: Lavanda Service Lift
areas.text: A lift that stops only at floors a key allows.

locations.name: Hotel Lingon Skyway
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A tall hotel joined to the terminal by a covered walkway, with rooms by the hour for crews and suites by the week for buyers who would rather stay out of the crush downtown.

areas.name: Skyway Lobby Bar
areas.text: A low bar off the lobby, where the windows look straight out at the airships.

areas.name: Skyway Sixth Floor
areas.text: A quiet corridor of identical doors and a single ice machine humming.

locations.name: Hotel Marro
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-8 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A business hotel across from the station with small rooms, a vending machine and a night clerk who reads comics. Salesmen use it; so do travellers who missed the last train.

areas.name: Hotel Marro Lobby
areas.text: The cramped lobby with its vending machine and the clerk's counter.

areas.name: Hotel Marro Single Rooms
areas.text: Narrow rooms with a bed, a phone and a window onto the tracks.

locations.name: Hotel Skyreach
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The town's grandest hotel, across the plaza from the tower, where rich spectators, sponsors and visiting promoters stay. The upper suites keep telescopes at the windows for watching the tower's lit floors at night.

areas.name: Skyreach Front Steps
areas.text: Marble steps and a doorman who knows who tips.

areas.name: Skyreach Lobby Bar
areas.text: A long bar in dark wood where business is done over whisky.

areas.name: Skyreach Telescope Suites
areas.text: Top-floor suites with brass telescopes trained on the tower.

locations.name: Hotel Starling
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A clean, middling tourist hotel two streets back from the station, the kind that fills with families and students in auction season. Its twin rooms have a desk, a television and a window over the rooftops.

areas.name: Starling Palm Lobby
areas.text: A small lobby of potted palms and a key rack.

areas.name: Starling Twin Room
areas.text: A twin room with two beds, a desk and a view of the rooftops.

locations.name: Hotel Sunwheel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A ten-storey hotel near the station with a sign like a sunburst on its roof, clean, plain and fully booked every January. Its bar is where applicants with money size each other up before the exam.

areas.name: Sunwheel Bar
areas.text: A dim bar off the lobby with leather booths and a television showing the weather.

areas.name: Sunwheel Roof
areas.text: The flat roof under the great wheel sign, humming with neon.

areas.name: Sunwheel Rooms
areas.text: Corridors of identical rooms, each with a narrow bed and a view of the street.

locations.name: Hui Guo Rou Palace
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 24-34 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The royal family's palace in the heart of the capital, its towers visible from the harbour. Tourists may cross the outer court on fixed days; past the second gate, nobody walks who is not expected.

areas.name: Palace Outer Court
areas.text: The public courtyard of white stone inside the first gate, where visitors are counted in and out.

areas.name: Palace Queens' Courts
areas.text: Eight walled gardens, one for each queen, with a household behind each wall.

areas.name: Palace Regalia Wing
areas.text: A windowless wing behind the throne hall, its doors under armed guard day and night.

locations.name: Hundreds Floor Gym
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A gym on the hundreds floors open only to fighters who hold a private room, with heavy bags, weights and a sauna. Fighters come to be seen training as much as to train.

areas.name: Hundreds Gym Bag Row
areas.text: A line of heavy bags, each with a regular's tape still on it.

areas.name: Hundreds Gym Sauna
areas.text: A cedar sauna where deals are made in towels.

locations.name: Hunter Association Headquarters
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 2-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The headquarters of the Hunter Association in Swardani City, where the chairman and the twelve Zodiacs meet, the exams are planned and the licences are issued. A licence opens its doors; without one a visitor waits in the lobby.

areas.name: Association Lobby
areas.text: The lobby with its reception desks and the card readers that admit Hunters.

areas.name: Records Floor
areas.text: The floors of files, bounty lists and exam records.

areas.name: Zodiac Chamber
areas.text: The council room where the chairman meets the Zodiacs.

locations.name: Hwaryu River
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-36 · Danger: Deadly]

The river that runs past the palace road and divides round the hotel island in the capital before it reaches the sea. Its banks are reed beds and allotments, and old men fish it from stools all day.

areas.name: Hwaryu River Rail Bridge
areas.text: An iron rail bridge with a sentry hut at each end.

areas.name: Hwaryu River Reed Banks
areas.text: Tall reeds on soft mud, cut through by fishermen's paths.

locations.name: Hybrid Pyre Ground
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-34 · Danger: Severe]

A scorched hollow outside the palace quarter where the city burns what must not be buried. Residents give it a wide berth.

areas.name: Pyre Ground Ash Bed
areas.text: A wide bed of grey ash, crusted where the rain has fallen on it.

areas.name: Pyre Ground Cart Road
areas.text: A rutted path from the palace quarter, wide enough for a handcart.

locations.name: Impaling Grove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

A grove of thorn trees near the hill villages, used by herders to shelter flocks.

areas.name: Impaling Grove Herders' Hollow
areas.text: A hollow among the roots where herders light fires.

areas.name: Impaling Grove Thorn Trees
areas.text: Thorn trees with long sharp branches, dense enough to keep the wind out.

locations.name: Ininge City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A city in the Republic of Rokario on the far side of the Miera Mountains from Pata.

areas.name: Ininge Junction
areas.text: The railway junction.

locations.name: Ininge Grain Exchange
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The grain exchange of Ininge City, a domed hall where the farmers of the northern plain sell their harvest to mills and shippers. Brokers shout and chalk, and buyers rub grain between their fingers before they bid.

areas.name: Ininge Exchange Gallery
areas.text: A railed gallery above the floor where the mill owners watch and send down runners.

areas.name: Ininge Exchange Trading Floor
areas.text: The floor under the dome, crowded with tables of sample sacks.

locations.name: Ininge Motor Works
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A factory on the edge of Ininge City that builds the buses and lorries which run the roads of Rokario. Its shifts change with a siren that can be heard across town.

areas.name: Ininge Works Assembly Shed
areas.text: A long shed of chassis on stands, welding light flaring along the line.

areas.name: Ininge Works Canteen
areas.text: A canteen across the road, loud with workers at every change of shift.

areas.name: Ininge Works Test Track
areas.text: An oval of cracked concrete behind the fence where new buses are run in.

locations.name: Inner Residential Zones
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The crowded heart of the city, where most of its millions live in shacks built on shacks. Every family here knows the next one, and strangers are noticed within a street.

areas.name: Inner Zones Corner Watch
areas.text: A crate seat at a crossing where one masked neighbour always sits.

areas.name: Inner Zones Water Queue
areas.text: A line of people with cans at a standpipe fed from a roof tank.

areas.name: Inner Zones Wire Lanes
areas.text: Narrow lanes under a web of washing lines and stolen power cables.

locations.name: Iron Mitt Boxing Gym
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: High]

A boxing gym in the basement under a laundry, warm with the dryers' heat coming through the ceiling. Boys train for neighbourhood bouts, old men sit on the bench and shout corrections, and the owner mentions his two champions to every visitor before he asks their name.

areas.name: Iron Mitt Bag Room
areas.text: A low room of heavy bags and speed balls that thud all day.

areas.name: Iron Mitt Ring
areas.text: A raised ring under one swinging lamp, its canvas stained.

locations.name: Ironweight Outfitters
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A metal workshop and outfitter at the edge of town that makes weighted clothing: vests, boots and wristbands sewn with iron plates. Visitors who want to try the gate for themselves buy here.

areas.name: Ironweight Fitting Room
areas.text: A room of vests on hooks and a scale to stand on.

areas.name: Ironweight Forge
areas.text: The workshop where iron plates are cut, drilled and heated in a gas forge.

locations.name: Juhan Coal Pits
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-36 · Danger: Deadly]

Coal mines in the hills west of Luonton City, worked by miners and by prisoners sent from the labour camp. The pithead wheels turn day and night, and the spoil heaps have buried a village.

areas.name: Coal Pits Deep Seam
areas.text: A low gallery far below, lit by cap lamps and propped with timber.

areas.name: Coal Pits Pithead
areas.text: The winding wheel and cage over the shaft, coal dust over everything.

areas.name: Coal Pits Sealed Gallery
areas.text: A fresh brick wall at the end of a tunnel, still damp.

locations.name: Junk Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A market where the residents trade what they have found, often by barter. Anything can turn up here, including things the rest of the world lost on purpose.

areas.name: Salvage Stalls
areas.text: The rows of stalls piled with found things.

locations.name: Kaedong Barrens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 34-40 · Danger: Deadly]

A stony plain in the wilderness beyond the palace, so poor that nobody has ever farmed it. There are no roads, no houses and no water, only rock and wind.

areas.name: Barrens Stone Flats
areas.text: Flat rock to the horizon, split by dry cracks.

areas.name: Barrens Wind Ridge
areas.text: A low ridge of broken stone, the only high ground for miles.

locations.name: Kakin Central Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The capital's main railway station, where the express lines from the interior end at the sea. Commuters pour through in the mornings, and the night trains leave for the provinces packed with workers going home.

areas.name: Central Station Night Platform
areas.text: The far platform where the slow trains to the interior wait after dark.

areas.name: Kakin Station Concourse
areas.text: The main hall under the iron roof, its floor worn smooth by a century of feet.

locations.name: Kakin Empire
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A country in the middle of the Azian Continent with more than a billion people, an economy that has grown fast for years and a king, Nasubi Hui Guo Rou, at the head of a parliamentary state. Thirty years ago it dropped its old socialist empire in a quiet revolution, but its caste system never changed: the Have-Nots at the bottom may hold no office and no military rank.

areas.name: Have-Not Quarter
areas.text: The crowded quarter where the lowest caste lives.

areas.name: Kakin Seaport
areas.text:
The vast harbour where ferries and airships carry people and cargo to the ships offshore.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Yorknew City (about 60000 Jenny); ferries sail to Black Whale 1 (about 1000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Royal Avenue
areas.text: The avenue of the capital lined with the dynasty's banners.

locations.name: Kakin Festival Quay
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The widest quay of the capital's harbour, kept clear of cargo so that the state has somewhere to hold its parades on the water. Ferry crews tie up here between runs, and on a holiday the crowds stand thirty deep behind the barriers.

areas.name: Festival Quay Ferry Ramps
areas.text: Three steel ramps where the harbour ferries load cars and foot passengers.

areas.name: Festival Quay Grandstand
areas.text: A tiered stand of painted timber that faces the harbour mouth on state days.

locations.name: Kakin International Airport
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The country's main airport, built on land reclaimed from the bay, where jet airliners and the big passenger airships share the field. Foreign arrivals queue at long immigration desks under portraits of the king.

areas.name: Kakin Airport Airship Masts
areas.text: A line of mooring masts on the far apron where airships swing with the wind.

areas.name: Kakin Airport Departure Hall
areas.text: A glass hall of check-in desks and duty-free shops, loud with announcements.

locations.name: Kakin Paddy Terraces
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

Hillsides east of the capital cut into rice terraces generations ago, still farmed by families who have worked them longer than anyone can say. Electric pumps lift the water now, but the walls are the old stone.

areas.name: Terrace Pump House
areas.text: A brick pump house at the foot of the slope, humming day and night.

areas.name: Terrace Village Granary
areas.text: A raised timber granary where the village stores its rice and holds its meetings.

locations.name: Kakin Parliament House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The seat of the parliament Kakin has had since its quiet revolution thirty years ago: a domed chamber, a warren of committee rooms and a press gallery that never empties during a budget week.

areas.name: Parliament Debating Chamber
areas.text: A horseshoe of green leather benches under the dome, with the speaker's chair at its head.

areas.name: Parliament Press Gallery
areas.text: A balcony crammed with reporters, cameras and the cables that feed them.

locations.name: Kakin Royal Military Academy
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 22-32 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The young state's officer school, which takes its pupils early and keeps them for years. Its cadets drill on the sand at dawn, strip rifles against the clock in the afternoon and march past their instructors at every prize-giving.

areas.name: Academy Armoury Hall
areas.text: A long hall of racks and benches where cadets strip and rebuild rifles on a stopwatch.

areas.name: Academy Cadet Dormitory
areas.text: Rows of iron cots made to the inch, with a footlocker at each.

areas.name: Academy Drill Field
areas.text: The raked sand square where companies form up under the clock tower.

locations.name: Kakin State Lottery Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The state lottery's main hall, where draws are made on a stage under television lights and winners collect at a row of glass windows. People of every caste queue here, the only building in the capital where they stand in one line.

areas.name: Lottery Hall Draw Stage
areas.text: The lit stage with its glass drum and a presenter's lectern.

areas.name: Lottery Hall Ticket Windows
areas.text: A row of barred windows where tickets are sold and prizes paid out.

locations.name: Kakin Survey Forest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

Wild forest in the Kakin Empire where new species still turn up, and a survey camp of tents.

areas.name: Survey Camp
areas.text: The camp of tents, cages and notebooks.

locations.name: Kakin Zoological Agency
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The government office that counts Kakin's animals, licenses its hunters and files away whatever the forests give up. Its corridors smell of formalin, and its staff are proud of collections that few outside the country have seen.

areas.name: Zoological Agency Quarantine Yard
areas.text: A fenced yard of cages where live finds are kept until someone decides what they are.

areas.name: Zoological Agency Specimen Hall
areas.text: A hall of glass cabinets and jars, each tagged in the agency's careful hand.

locations.name: Kelp Strand Saltworks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

A strip of coast where seawater is boiled down in wide pans over driftwood fires, and kelp is dried for fertiliser. The salt goes inland by cart, and the salt-boilers are the best-fed people on the coast.

areas.name: Kelp Strand Boiling Pans
areas.text: Wide pans steaming over fires on the shingle, tended by boilers with wooden rakes.

areas.name: Kelp Strand Drying Lines
areas.text: Lines of brown kelp strung on poles above the tide mark.

locations.name: Kessel Firearms
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

A licensed gun shop with a firing range downstairs, selling pistols, shotguns and hunting rifles to anyone with a permit. Bodyguards come in August to buy what their employers will not.

areas.name: Kessel Basement Range
areas.text: A narrow range of four lanes and paper targets.

areas.name: Kessel Shop Counter
areas.text: A glass counter of handguns and a wall rack of long guns.

locations.name: Kessel Road Truck Stop
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A forecourt, a diner and a car park full of lorries on the highway between the port and Zaban City. Drivers sleep in their cabs here, and the diner serves fried eggs at any hour to anyone with cash.

areas.name: Truck Stop Diner
areas.text: A long counter with stools, a griddle and a waitress who calls everyone love.

areas.name: Truck Stop Forecourt
areas.text: Diesel pumps under a canopy, an air hose and a payphone.

areas.name: Truck Stop Lorry Park
areas.text: Rows of parked lorries with their curtains drawn.

locations.name: King Beetle Tree
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

A single tree far taller than the rest of the wood around it, its bark alive with insects of every kind. Something large and white is sometimes seen in its crown at evening.

areas.name: Beetle Tree Crown
areas.text: The crown high above, where the white beetle rests.

areas.name: Beetle Tree Trunk
areas.text: The vast trunk, crawling with beetles and ants.

locations.name: King's Living Quarters
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The residence of Nasubi Hui Guo Rou on Tier 1, separated from the princes' rooms by the banquet hall, its floors patterned and its walls hung with paintings.

areas.name: King's Living Room
areas.text: The living room with its paintings and ornate furniture.

locations.name: Kirimori Embalming House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe]

A dark house where the bus road meets the valley, where Renko the embalmer receives the city's dead and sends them back looking as they did in life. Families ride out on the last bus to fetch them.

areas.name: Embalming House Laying-Out Room
areas.text: A cool room with a table, white cloths and jars of oil in rows.

areas.name: Embalming House Porch
areas.text: A porch facing the bus road, where a lamp burns for whoever comes late.

locations.name: Kirimori Valley
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-32 · Danger: Severe]

A valley in Meteor City away from the heaps.

areas.name: Valley Hut
areas.text: A small hut at the valley's head.

locations.name: Komugi's Family Home
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-28 · Danger: Severe]

A small, crowded house on the edge of a poor settlement, home to a family of twelve. One of them is Komugi, blind, clumsy and the national Gungi champion, whose winnings keep everyone fed.

areas.name: Komugi's Family Garden
areas.text: A vegetable plot where Komugi sits with her board in the sun.

areas.name: Komugi's Family Kitchen
areas.text: One room for cooking, eating and sleeping, full of children.

locations.name: Kon's Den
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A den under the roots in the deep forest where Kon, a foxbear Gon raised from a cub, makes his home. Kon is friendly to Gon and wary of everyone else, and a fox-bear's wariness is worth respecting.

areas.name: Fish Rock
areas.text: A flat stone near the den where fish are left as gifts.

areas.name: Root Hollow
areas.text: The den itself, dug under a great tree's roots and lined with dry leaves.

locations.name: Kuksan Labour Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-38 · Danger: Deadly]

A labour camp in the hills to the north-west, behind wire and watchtowers. People reported to the Peijin Informant Bureau come here, often with their families, and work the coal pits and the roads.

areas.name: Labour Camp Huts
areas.text: Rows of wooden huts behind wire, crowded and cold.

areas.name: Labour Camp Watchtowers
areas.text: Towers with searchlights at each corner of the wire.

locations.name: Kukuroo Bone Midden
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: High]

A gully just inside the wall where the remains of intruders end up once the hound has finished with them. Someone rakes it tidy, which somehow makes it worse.

areas.name: Bone Midden Pit
areas.text: The gully itself, white with old bones under a skin of leaves.

areas.name: Bone Midden Scrap Heap
areas.text: A pile of knives, pistols and belt buckles sorted out of the pit.

locations.name: Kukuroo Boundary Wall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-20 · Danger: High]

The wall of huge stones that rings the foot of Kukuroo Mountain and marks where the family's land begins. It runs out of sight in both directions from the Testing Gate, through jungle and over ravines.

areas.name: Boundary Wall Patrol Path
areas.text: The walkway along the wall's top, wide enough for one butler.

areas.name: Boundary Wall Ravine Span
areas.text: A stretch where the wall bridges a ravine on stone arches.

locations.name: Kukuroo Crash Cliff
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

A stretch of road on the way down from the mountain where it clings to a cliff above a dense forest. The guard rail has been mended more than once.

areas.name: Crash Cliff Guard Rail
areas.text: The bend where the rail buckles outward.

areas.name: Crash Cliff Wreck Ledge
areas.text: A ledge below the road where wreckage collects.

locations.name: Kukuroo Fumarole Gully
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A gully on the mountain's eastern flank where the old volcano still breathes, venting steam through cracks in the rock. Nothing grows in it, and the hounds will not go in.

areas.name: Fumarole Gully Mineral Pools
areas.text: Small pools tinted green and orange, too hot to touch.

areas.name: Fumarole Gully Vents
areas.text: A field of steaming cracks between dead trees.

locations.name: Kukuroo Lowland Forest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

A thick, low forest between the foot of the mountain and the highway to Parasta, with no road through it and few trails.

areas.name: Lowland Forest Fern Trail
areas.text: A trail half lost under ferns.

areas.name: Lowland Forest Hollow
areas.text: A hollow among tall trunks, where sound dies quickly.

locations.name: Kukuroo Mountain
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

A dormant volcano 3,722 metres high in the Dentora Region, wrapped in cloud, its foot hidden by jungle and ringed by huge stone walls. The Zoldyck Family owns all of it, and the estate runs from the gate to the summit.

areas.name: Cloud Slopes
areas.text: The upper slopes above the jungle, lost in cloud.

areas.name: Summit Road
areas.text: The road to the top, watched from somewhere above.

locations.name: Kukuroo Summit Crater
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

The dormant crater at the top of Kukuroo Mountain, above the mansion and above the clouds. From its rim on a clear day a person could see the whole Dentora Region, if anyone were ever allowed up to look.

areas.name: Summit Crater Floor
areas.text: The bowl of the crater, warm underfoot and streaked with sulphur.

areas.name: Summit Crater Rim
areas.text: A ridge of black rock around the crater, cold and windy.

locations.name: Kurta Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

The village of the Kurta Clan in the forests of the Lukso Province, a people whose eyes turned scarlet with strong feeling. The houses stand empty, and the village is spoken of as the site of a massacre.

areas.name: Elders' House
areas.text: The house where the elders set the test for any child who wished to leave.

areas.name: Village Graves
areas.text: The row of graves at the edge of the village.

locations.name: Kwanlo Ford
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-34 · Danger: Severe]

A shallow crossing of the border river south of the border post, beside the pillars of a bridge blown in an old war. It is the way people go when the border post will not let them through.

areas.name: Kwanlo Ford Reed Hide
areas.text: A hollow in the reeds where those crossing wait for dark.

areas.name: Kwanlo Ford Shallows
areas.text: Knee-deep water over gravel between the bridge pillars.

locations.name: Lamentation Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The road the daily Lamentation Tours bus takes up through Dentora's mountains to the foot of Kukuroo Mountain. The guide tells the tourists everything known about the family on the way up, which is not much, and turns the bus round at the gate.

areas.name: Lookout Bend
areas.text: The bend where the bus stops so the tourists can photograph the mountain.

areas.name: Tour Bus
areas.text: The bus with its microphone and its tourists pressed to the windows.

locations.name: Lamentation Tours Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The garage and booking office of Lamentation Tours, the company that runs the daily bus to the family's gate. The buses are washed every night and the guides rehearse their patter in the office.

areas.name: Tours Depot Booking Office
areas.text: A counter with a bell and a rack of souvenir leaflets.

areas.name: Tours Depot Bus Garage
areas.text: The garage of buses, one up on jacks.

locations.name: Lantern Alley Workshops
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

A crooked alley of small workshops behind the Bull Market, restorers and framers and carpenters, all with closed doors in auction season. The work is fine and nobody asks for a receipt.

areas.name: Lantern Alley Benches
areas.text: Workbenches under lanterns, covered in tools and half-made things.

areas.name: Lantern Alley Drying Shed
areas.text: A shed where aged pieces dry in rows.

locations.name: Lantern Noodle Row
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A lane of noodle shops and dumpling kitchens behind the royal avenue, open from noon until the last tram. Office workers, soldiers on leave and dock hands eat elbow to elbow on the pavement.

areas.name: Noodle Row Broth Counters
areas.text: Open counters where broth simmers in vats the size of barrels.

areas.name: Noodle Row Dumpling Kitchen
areas.text: A back kitchen where a family folds dumplings by the thousand.

locations.name: Lantern Shrine of All Faiths
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small shrine lit by hundreds of salvaged lamps, its walls carrying the symbols of every faith that has washed up in the city. Anyone may pray here, to whoever they choose.

areas.name: Lantern Shrine Lamp Wall
areas.text: A wall covered in oil lamps, candles and bulbs on wires.

areas.name: Lantern Shrine Oil Store
areas.text: A cupboard of oil cans and wicks that the keepers of the rota refill in turn.

locations.name: Leroute's Forfeit Cell
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small locked room off the platform on the Majority Path, with five hard bunks and a clock nobody can reach. Applicants who have lost hours on the platform sit here until those hours are spent.

areas.name: Forfeit Cell Bunks
areas.text: Five bunks bolted to the wall, close enough to hear every argument.

areas.name: Forfeit Cell Clock
areas.text: The clock behind its glass panel, counting off the hours that were lost.

locations.name: Lifeboat Launch Site
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The lifeboat station of Tier 1, behind an emergency door with a keypad lock and soldiers on watch. Closed lifeboats sit in a waterway and are launched from a control unit through an outlet just above the sea.

areas.name: Lifeboat Control Unit
areas.text: The panel that floods the channel and opens the outlet to the sea.

areas.name: Lifeboat Waterway
areas.text: A channel of water inside the hull where the sealed lifeboats wait in line.

locations.name: Limeiro
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-32 · Danger: Severe]

The capital of the game, a lively city round a great castle where the Game Masters are said to live. Players who clear the game arrive here for its ending.

areas.name: Limeiro Castle
areas.text: The great castle at the city's heart.

areas.name: Parade Street
areas.text: The street of the victory parade.

locations.name: Limeiro Grand Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A great market below the capital's castle, crowded and loud, where the townsfolk sell cloth, spices, sweets and toys under striped awnings and street players perform for coins.

areas.name: Grand Market Awnings
areas.text: Rows of stalls under red and white awnings.

areas.name: Grand Market Cloth Hall
areas.text: A hall of bolts and banners where the parade's flags are sewn.

locations.name: Limeiro Owlery
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A round stone tower on Limeiro's wall, full of perches and owls. The capital sends its letters by owl, and the birds come and go through the open windows at every hour.

areas.name: Owlery Letter Desk
areas.text: The keeper's desk at the foot of the tower, with sealed letter bags.

areas.name: Owlery Perch Hall
areas.text: The tall hall of perches rising to the roof.

locations.name: Lingon Airport
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A major airport in Yorknew City's suburbs, about ninety minutes by car from the city centre along a road across the desert. Airships from every continent land here, and the rich arrive for the auctions with their own households.

areas.name: Airship Hangars
areas.text: The hangars at the far end where private airships are kept.

areas.name: Lingon Concourse
areas.text: The shopping concourse of the terminal, crowded with travellers and their bags.

areas.name: Lingon Runways
areas.text:
The long runways and the airship stands where flights to every continent board.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Yorknew City (about 500 Jenny), Meteor City (about 4000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Lingon Arrivals Kerb
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The covered road outside the arrivals hall, where taxis queue, limousines idle and porters fight over the richest luggage. Everyone bound for the city by road leaves from here.

areas.name: Arrivals Kerb Limousine Bay
areas.text: A reserved bay of black cars with drivers leaning on the bonnets.

areas.name: Arrivals Kerb Taxi Rank
areas.text: The long rank where cabs wait in a line that reaches back past the car park.

locations.name: Lingon Cargo Terminal
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

The freight side of the airport: a row of sheds where airships unload crates, pallets and sealed cases for the city. Through the late summer it works around the clock, because half the auction city's goods arrive this way.

areas.name: Cargo Terminal Manifest Office
areas.text: A glassed office above the floor, its desks buried in waybills.

areas.name: Cargo Terminal Unloading Bay
areas.text: A broad shed door where an airship's hold opens straight onto pallets.

locations.name: Lingon Customs Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A bonded hall where goods for the auctions are opened, weighed, photographed and sealed again under official lead tags before they may leave the airport. The legal auctions lean on it heavily every autumn.

areas.name: Customs Hall Bonded Cage
areas.text: A locked wire cage of sealed goods waiting for their papers.

areas.name: Customs Hall Inspection Tables
areas.text: Long steel tables where crates are unpacked under bright strip lights.

locations.name: Lingon Departure Lounge
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The upper lounge where passengers wait to be called to their airships, with a wall of glass onto the runways, a newsstand and a coffee bar that never closes.

areas.name: Departure Lounge Newsstand
areas.text: A kiosk of papers, magazines and gum beside the boarding gates.

areas.name: Departure Lounge Window Wall
areas.text: A long line of seats facing the glass, the runways spread out below.

locations.name: Lingon Gas Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A fenced compound of white spheres and tanks at the far edge of the airport, holding the lifting gas and fuel the airships take on before every flight. Smoking within a mile of it can cost a worker his job.

areas.name: Gas Farm Sphere Yard
areas.text: The gravel yard among the spheres, each with its ladder and its gauge.

areas.name: Gas Farm Valve House
areas.text: A brick pump house where the main valves sit in a row under painted numbers.

locations.name: Lingon Ground Crew Village
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A grid of prefabricated houses behind the airport fence where mechanics, cleaners, porters and their families live. Everyone here works for the airport, and every conversation stops when an engine changes note.

areas.name: Crew Village Canteen
areas.text: A tin-roofed canteen where shifts change over cheap soup and the radio.

areas.name: Crew Village Main Row
areas.text: The one paved street, lined with identical houses and dusty cars.

locations.name: Lingon Private Apron
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A fenced stretch of tarmac at the quiet end of the airport, kept for private airships and the households that ride them. Cars may drive straight up to the gangway, and nobody here asks a passenger for a boarding pass.

areas.name: Private Apron Gangway
areas.text: The foot of a lowered gangway, a strip of red carpet laid on the tarmac below it.

areas.name: Private Apron Gatehouse
areas.text: A brick hut at the fence gate where a guard checks the cars in by their plates.

locations.name: Lingon Security Barracks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The airport police's barracks and motor pool, a long concrete block with a radio room, a dog run and a row of jeeps that patrol the perimeter fence day and night.

areas.name: Security Barracks Dog Run
areas.text: A fenced run where the patrol dogs bark at every engine.

areas.name: Security Barracks Radio Room
areas.text: A small room of radios and a map of the perimeter stuck with pins.

locations.name: Lingon Shopping Galleria
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Two storeys of boutiques, jewellers and perfume counters under a glass roof, built for travellers with an hour to kill and money to spend. The rich of every continent pass through here on their way to the autumn auctions.

areas.name: Galleria Boutique Row
areas.text: The upper gallery of designer shops, each window lit like a stage.

areas.name: Galleria Fountain Court
areas.text: The open floor under the skylights, with benches round a splashing fountain.

areas.name: Galleria Service Loop
areas.text: The plain corridor behind the shops that joins the restrooms to the loading bays.

locations.name: Lipa Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A train station in downtown Yorknew on the Castor Line, with exits into the Saloma Mall.

areas.name: Lipa Platform
areas.text: The platform under the downtown streets.

locations.name: Little Graves Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High]

A burial ground beside the big church where the city lays its children. Too many of the mounds are short, and the families leave a toy, a sweet or a picture on each.

areas.name: Little Graves Toy Wall
areas.text: The low tyre wall where the mourners line up the toys they bring.

areas.name: Sarasa's Grave
areas.text: A short mound under a hand-painted board, with a heart-shaped purse tied to it.

locations.name: Locust Grass Plain
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

A plain of waist-high grass in the island's south, running down to the sea. An old shepherd who keeps a hut on its edge says that in some years the whole plain rattles, and that you can hear it in Soufrabi.

areas.name: Locust Plain Grass Sea
areas.text: The open plain of grass rolling in the wind toward the coast.

areas.name: Locust Plain Shepherd's Hut
areas.text: A turf hut with a calendar of notches cut into its doorpost.

locations.name: Lone Pine Tree
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A huge pine standing alone on a hill in the forest outside Dolle Harbor, with a log cabin at its foot. The family who live there test the applicants who come asking the way, and a hard test it is.

areas.name: Kiriko Cabin
areas.text: The log cabin under the pine, its door broken and its lamps out.

areas.name: Pine Hill Path
areas.text: The path up through the forest to the hill, where something keeps pace in the trees.

locations.name: Longmane Stud
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

The stud that breeds the country's horses: heavy draught horses for the carts and the ploughs, light ones for the riders. Every horse that carries mail or pulls a cart in the country was foaled in these paddocks.

areas.name: Longmane Foaling Barn
areas.text: A warm barn of deep straw where the mares foal under a groom's lantern.

areas.name: Longmane Paddocks
areas.text: Rolling paddocks fenced with split rails, the horses grazing in their dozens.

locations.name: Lucky Ring Betting Parlour
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A betting shop off the plaza that takes bets the tower's windows will not: on rounds, on knockouts, on which fighter leaves on a stretcher. The odds are chalked up and wiped off all day.

areas.name: Lucky Ring Back Office
areas.text: A room of phones, a safe and a man who never smiles.

areas.name: Lucky Ring Odds Boards
areas.text: Chalkboards of names and numbers wiped and rewritten by the minute.

locations.name: Lukso Province
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A hidden forest province, hard to find even with directions, where the trees and plants grow with swirling patterns and big riding birds called Piko live. The Kurta Clan lived here for generations out of the world's sight.

areas.name: Piko Roost
areas.text: The tall trees where the riding birds nest.

areas.name: Swirl Wood
areas.text: The forest of swirl-barked trees where a path is easy to lose.

locations.name: Luonton Bus Depot
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The depot from which the buses of Luonton City run out to the villages. Most are old and patched; the timetable is written in chalk because it changes so often.

areas.name: Bus Depot Waiting Room
areas.text: Benches, a stove and a chalkboard timetable.

areas.name: Bus Depot Yard
areas.text: A yard of old buses in rows, some of them on blocks.

locations.name: Luonton City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: Deadly · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A provincial city of East Gorteau, with a highway running north-east into the forest.

areas.name: Luonton Square
areas.text: The central square where notices are read out.

locations.name: Luonton Highway Forest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The forest by the highway north-east of Luonton City.

areas.name: Ambush Hollow
areas.text: A hollow among the trees beside the road.

locations.name: Luonton Lumber Mill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-34 · Danger: Severe]

A sawmill at the edge of the forest on the highway out of Luonton City, cutting the logs that come out of the woods on lorries. The work is dangerous, and the men are proud of the fingers they still have.

areas.name: Lumber Mill Log Yard
areas.text: Stacks of logs as tall as houses, chained down against rolling.

areas.name: Lumber Mill Saw Shed
areas.text: An open shed where a great circular saw cuts logs into planks.

locations.name: Lurka Gate Village
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The village at the entrance to the ruins, which grew up to feed and house the visitors. It has guesthouses, a souvenir arcade and a square where the tour buses turn.

areas.name: Gate Village Guesthouse
areas.text: A family guesthouse with paper lanterns and a shared bath.

areas.name: Gate Village Souvenir Arcade
areas.text: A covered row of stalls selling postcards and clay copies of the tomb paintings.

areas.name: Gate Village Square
areas.text: The square where the buses park and the guides gather their groups.

locations.name: Lurka Restoration Trust
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The office of the nonprofit body that runs the ruins: a barn turned into a records room and a meeting table. It takes no profit and asks little of visitors.

areas.name: Trust Meeting Table
areas.text: The long table where the volunteers decide what may be done to the site.

areas.name: Trust Records Room
areas.text: Drawers of site plans and excavation diaries in Ging's careful hand.

locations.name: Lurka Royal Tomb
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The burial chamber under the ruins, opened by careful hands and now seen only in small guided groups. The paintings on its walls are behind glass and lit low.

areas.name: Tomb Painted Chamber
areas.text: The chamber itself, its walls painted and its floor kept bare.

areas.name: Tomb Passage
areas.text: The narrow stone passage that leads down into the chamber.

locations.name: Lurka Ruins
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The ruins of an ancient civilisation, excavated and restored by a single Hunter who paid for everything himself, including the public walkways that keep visitors from damaging it. His methods are now the textbook of the field.

areas.name: Ruin Walkways
areas.text: The raised walkways over the excavations.

areas.name: Visitors' Centre
areas.text: The hall at the entrance with its maps and plaques.

locations.name: Lurka Valley Woods
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-10 · Danger: Low]

The wooded valley around the ruins, never dug and protected by the trust. Mounds under the trees may be more of the old city or nothing at all.

areas.name: Valley Mounds
areas.text: The grassy mounds under the beeches that nobody has opened.

areas.name: Valley Stepping Stones
