areas.text: The stream crossing on flat stones below the ruins.

locations.name: Lurka Volunteers' Bunkhouse
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-8 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A plain timber bunkhouse where the ruins' volunteers sleep in the digging season. Anyone who turns up willing to sift soil all day is given a bunk.

areas.name: Bunkhouse Sleeping Loft
areas.text: The loft of bunks under the roof.

areas.name: Bunkhouse Tool Wall
areas.text: The wall of trowels, brushes and sieves.

locations.name: Mandai Black Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-32 · Danger: Severe]

A tangle of stalls in an alley behind the bus station, open only at dusk, selling what the shops do not: cigarettes, radios, medicine, foreign shoes. Money changes hands in every currency, and the moneychangers also deal in the Pail.

areas.name: Black Market Moneychangers' Corner
areas.text: A corner where men with fat wallets change money without a word.

areas.name: Black Market Stall Alley
areas.text: A narrow alley of tarpaulin stalls lit by paraffin lamps.

locations.name: Mandai City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: Deadly · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A city of East Gorteau where travellers can meet without attracting much notice.

areas.name: Mandai Hotel Room
areas.text: A rented room where plans are drawn.

locations.name: Mandai People's Hospital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The state hospital that serves Mandai and the country round it: a large building with too many patients and too little medicine. Treatment is free, so everyone brings the doctor a gift.

areas.name: People's Hospital Pharmacy
areas.text: A counter with bare shelves and a locked cupboard behind it.

areas.name: People's Hospital Ward
areas.text: A long ward of crowded beds and relatives sleeping on the floor.

locations.name: Mandai Sports Stadium
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-32 · Danger: Severe]

Mandai's stadium, used more for mass games than for sport: thousands of citizens in the stands turn coloured cards together to make the leader's face. Football is played here on the rare afternoons the rehearsals stop.

areas.name: Mandai Stadium Pitch
areas.text: A worn football pitch inside a running track.

areas.name: Mandai Stadium Stands
areas.text: Steep concrete stands where the card-turners sit in coloured blocks.

areas.name: Mandai Stadium Tunnel
areas.text: The players' tunnel, now used to store crates of cards and flags.

locations.name: Mandai Textile Mill
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A brick mill on the edge of Mandai that weaves the cloth for army uniforms. Its looms run in three shifts, and the workers live in dormitories beside it.

areas.name: Textile Mill Dormitories
areas.text: Brick dormitories where the workers sleep in rows.

areas.name: Textile Mill Loom Floor
areas.text: A deafening floor of shuttling looms and cotton dust.

locations.name: Mansion Lower Levels
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

The levels beneath the mansion where the family's children are trained and punished: cells, chains, and rooms where poisons are taken in small doses until the body stops caring.

areas.name: Poison Room
areas.text: A room of jars, vials and a chair.

areas.name: Punishment Cell
areas.text: A cell of bare rock with chains.

locations.name: Mansion Watch Room
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe]

A small room in the mansion where the pictures from the estate's cameras come together: the gate, the paths, the butlers' grounds and corridors that the family would rather nobody else saw.

areas.name: Watch Room Recorder Shelf
areas.text: Racks of tapes recording everything the cameras see.

areas.name: Watch Room Screens
areas.text: The wall of screens, each labelled in a careful hand.

locations.name: Masadora
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The magic city, a town of towers and spires that looks out of a storybook. Spell cards are sold here and nowhere else, and players who want to quit come here hunting a card to leave the game.

areas.name: Card Queue
areas.text: The line of players outside the shop.

areas.name: Spire Square
areas.text: The square of towers at the city's heart.

locations.name: Masadora Potion House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A crooked little shop on a Masadora side street that looks as if a witch built it out of a storybook. Coloured bottles fill its shelves to the roof, and its keeper talks about love and diets in the same breath.

areas.name: Potion House Cauldron
areas.text: A black cauldron over a low fire at the back of the shop.

areas.name: Potion House Shelves
areas.text: Floor-to-ceiling shelves of stoppered bottles with hand-written labels.

locations.name: Masadora Spire Inn
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An inn built into one of Masadora's spires, its rooms stacked up a spiral stair. Most of its guests are players who spend their days in the queue at the spell shop and their nights asleep in their boots.

areas.name: Spire Inn Bell Loft
areas.text: The room at the top, under the bell, that the innkeeper lets by the night.

areas.name: Spire Inn Notice Stair
areas.text: The bottom landing where guests pin up trade offers.

areas.name: Spire Inn Spiral Stair
areas.text: A narrow stone stair winding up the spire past numbered doors.

locations.name: Masadora Wolf Woods
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A pine wood on the road out of Masadora where the trees close over the path and a pack of upright, wolf-like beasts ambushes travellers. The shopkeepers warn about it; few players listen.

areas.name: Wolf Woods Chief's Rock
areas.text: A flat rock on a rise where the pack's leader stands to call.

areas.name: Wolf Woods Forked Path
areas.text: Where the road splits three ways among the pines and every branch looks the same.

locations.name: Mask Lane Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 12-18 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A clinic in a shipping container run by a resident who trained as a nurse somewhere else and never says where. Most of the medicine on the shelves is out of date; she knows which still works.

areas.name: Clinic Container Ward
areas.text: The inside of the container, three cots and a lamp, the walls painted white.

areas.name: Clinic Medicine Shelves
areas.text: Shelves of bottles and blister packs sorted by colour, dates scratched off.

locations.name: Mask Stitchers' Row
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A row of workshops where the wraps and masks the residents wear are stitched from salvaged cloth. The patterns differ by street and family, if you know how to read them.

areas.name: Stitchers' Drying Lines
areas.text: Lines strung across the row, hung with masks and wraps of every colour.

areas.name: Stitchers' Treadle Shop
areas.text: A shop of treadle sewing machines worked by women in a row.

locations.name: Masked Watch Barracks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Containers stacked by the road where the residents who keep the checkpoint sleep between watches. Every resident takes a turn sooner or later.

areas.name: Watch Barracks Bunk Rows
areas.text: Bunks three high inside a container, each with a mask hanging at its foot.

areas.name: Watch Barracks Radio Room
areas.text: A container corner with a radio set and a book of arrivals.

locations.name: Medical Ward
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 20-34 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The medical ward in the middle of Tier 3, with the central hospital and the tier's three clinics. Only a fraction of the planned doctors came aboard.

areas.name: Central Hospital
areas.text: The hospital at the heart of the ward.

locations.name: Melanin Lizard Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A stretch of baked mud and rock between the stone pillars where great spotted lizards lie in the sun. One can swallow a cow whole, and they kill by lying on their prey.

areas.name: Lizard Flats Bone Heap
areas.text: A heap of cattle bones where the lizards have fed.

areas.name: Lizard Flats Mud Pan
areas.text: The open pan of cracked mud where the lizards bask.

locations.name: Merchant Bell Square
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

A broad square in the old commercial quarter, ringed by banks and cafés and overlooked by a bell tower. Office workers eat on its benches; pigeons own the rest.

areas.name: Bell Square Benches
areas.text: Benches around a bronze statue of a founding banker.

areas.name: Bell Square Café Terrace
areas.text: A terrace of tables under awnings, facing the square.

areas.name: Bell Tower Gallery
areas.text: A narrow gallery below the bells, with a view of every bench.

locations.name: Mercy Street Free Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-16 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A shopfront clinic in the tenements kept open by one tired doctor, two nurses and whatever the cathedral sends. It treats the poor and the uninsured for nothing, and the queue starts before it opens.

areas.name: Mercy Street Back Surgery
areas.text: A small surgery behind a curtain, its steel table scrubbed raw.

areas.name: Mercy Street Waiting Room
areas.text: A room of plastic chairs and faded health posters.

locations.name: Meteor City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-34 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A junkyard city of eight to ten million people, about the size of the Lapet Republic, whose residents appear in no record anywhere. It is said to be fifteen hundred years old, first a dictator's internment camp, then the world's dumping ground. Every faith and every people seems to have washed up here, and they look after their own.

areas.name: Meteor City Road End
areas.text:
The end of the one road in, where trucks dump their loads and outsiders are met.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Lingon Airport (about 4000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Scavenger Lanes
areas.text: The lanes between the heaps where people sort the rubbish for anything of use.

areas.name: Shanty Rows
areas.text: The rows of shacks built from what others threw away.

locations.name: Meteor City Church
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

A church built from salvage, carrying the symbols of several religions at once, where the residents bring their dead and kneel to pray outside.

areas.name: Chapel of the Dead
areas.text: The room inside where the bodies are laid out.

areas.name: Church Steps
areas.text: The steps where the mourners kneel.

locations.name: Meteor City Last Bus Stand
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High]

The stand where the city's few buses leave on their rounds, the last of each day going furthest out, as far as the valleys. The drivers carry anyone, and take what the passenger can give.

areas.name: Last Bus Stand Repair Pit
areas.text: A pit dug under the parking place, where a driver lies working on an axle.

areas.name: Last Bus Stand Shelter
areas.text: A shelter of car doors bolted together, with the timetable painted on one.

locations.name: Meteor City Outskirts
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: Severe]

The thin edge of the city, where the heaps run out into waste ground and only a few hermits live. Parents warn their children never to come out here alone.

areas.name: Outskirts Bare Waste
areas.text: Flat grey ground between the last heaps and the horizon.

areas.name: Outskirts Hermit Shacks
areas.text: A few shacks standing far apart, each with a dog chained outside.

locations.name: Meteor Elder's House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

The hut of one of the elders who sit in the Assembly, swaddled in cloth like its owner. Residents who have been wronged by an outsider come here to tell him so.

areas.name: Elder's Rag Door
areas.text: The doorway hung with layers of cloth, where the petitioners wait on their heels.

areas.name: Elder's Smoke Room
areas.text: A dim inner room where the elder sits behind a haze of burning herbs and hears each case.

locations.name: Meteor Scrap Smelter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

A furnace yard where cans, wire and car parts are melted into ingots for the few traders the Assembly lets in. The smelters work stripped to the waist, masks soaked against the fumes.

areas.name: Smelter Furnace Pit
areas.text: A brick furnace sunk into the ground, fed through a hatch with a long shovel.

areas.name: Smelter Ingot Beds
areas.text: Trays of sand where the poured metal cools in rough bars.

locations.name: Miera Limestone Caves
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe]

A system of limestone caves high in the Miera Mountains, entered by a mouth in a cliff above the tree line. Cavers come from the cities to map them; shepherds keep away and say the deep passages flood without warning.

areas.name: Miera Cave Drip Gallery
areas.text: A long gallery of stalactites where every sound comes back twice.

areas.name: Miera Cave Mouth
areas.text: The wide arch in the cliff, its floor littered with old campfires.

areas.name: Miera Cave Sump
areas.text: A black pool at the bottom where the passage goes underwater.

locations.name: Miera Mountains
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe]

A range of mountains in the Republic of Rokario between the cities of Pata and Ininge.

areas.name: Miera Slopes
areas.text: The forested slopes.

locations.name: Miera Ranger Hut
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A log hut on the ridge path through the Miera Mountains, kept by the forestry service with a stove, bunks and a radio for walkers caught by the weather. A ranger comes up twice a week; the rest of the time the logbook keeps watch.

areas.name: Miera Hut Bunk Room
areas.text: Four bunks and a stove, with a sign asking guests to leave dry kindling.

areas.name: Miera Hut Radio Desk
areas.text: A desk under the window with a two-way radio and a chained logbook.

locations.name: Mile Forty Truck Stop
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A truck stop forty miles out on the airport road, with diesel pumps, a diner and a shower block for drivers who have come across the desert at night. The pie is famous for two hundred miles in both directions.

areas.name: Mile Forty Diner
areas.text: A chrome counter and booths, with a pie case lit up beside the till.

areas.name: Truck Stop Diesel Island
areas.text: The wide forecourt where the lorries pull in under floodlights.

locations.name: Milluki's Room
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

The second son's room, the brightest place in the mansion: computer screens from floor to ceiling, servers humming in a cupboard and glass cases of collectible figures he would kill to protect. He does most of his work for the family from this chair.

areas.name: Milluki's Figure Cases
areas.text: Glass cabinets of figurines, labelled and dusted daily by a nervous butler.

areas.name: Milluki's Monitor Wall
areas.text: The bank of screens and the reinforced chair in front of it.

locations.name: Milsy Field Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-9 · Danger: Low]

A research hut on stilts at the dry northern edge of the Milsy Wetlands, where a few biologists study the marsh's mimics: frogs that sound like crying children, flowers that smell of bread, and worse. They go out roped together and never after dark.

areas.name: Field Station Laboratory
areas.text: A cramped room of microscopes, specimen jars and a humming fridge.

areas.name: Field Station Rope Line
areas.text: A line of posts and rope leading out from the hut into the fog.

locations.name: Milsy Wetlands
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A marsh under constant fog, also called the swindlers' swamp, where the animals and even the plants live by deceiving prey. Creatures pass themselves off as people, and the fog swallows anyone who falls behind.

areas.name: Fog Banks
areas.text: The thick fog over the water where the path is lost a step at a time.

areas.name: Mimic Thicket
areas.text: A thicket where something calls out in a human voice.

areas.name: Tunnel Mouth
areas.text: The opening where the tunnel stair climbs into the marsh.

locations.name: Mito's House
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 1-4 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The house where Mito Freecss raises Gon with the help of his great-grandmother. Visitors who come home with Gon are fed first and questioned afterwards, and nobody leaves the table hungry.

areas.name: Gon's Room
areas.text: A small room under the roof with a fishing rod by the window and a bed by the wall.

areas.name: Mito's Kitchen
areas.text: The kitchen and its long table, where the meals are big and the questions bigger.

locations.name: Mossford
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A village built where the river is shallow enough to wade in summer, with a ferry raft on a rope for the rest of the year. The ferryman knows every face that crosses and charges strangers in gossip.

areas.name: Mossford Rope Ferry
areas.text: A flat raft hauled across the river on a rope by the ferryman and his son.

areas.name: Mossford Stepping Stones
areas.text: A line of mossy stones across the summer shallows, slick in the morning.

areas.name: Mossford Washing Rocks
areas.text: Flat rocks downstream where the village women wash and beat their linen.

locations.name: Motoba Building
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

An office building off Continental Street in Yorknew City.

areas.name: Motoba Lobby
areas.text: The lobby with a view of the street.

locations.name: Mountain God's Garden
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

An enormous forest on a high plateau, full of creatures of every kind, all of them friendly. Animals come up to strangers and follow them about, and nothing in the forest has ever been seen to bite.

areas.name: God's Garden Fern Floor
areas.text: The forest floor under ferns taller than a man.

areas.name: God's Garden Old Oak
areas.text: A huge old oak where the animals gather at dusk.

areas.name: God's Garden Plateau Edge
areas.text: The cliff at the plateau's edge, looking down over the island.

locations.name: Movie Theatre
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-32 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A cineplex of at least eight screens on Tier 3.

areas.name: Screen Eight
areas.text: One of the dark screening rooms.

locations.name: Nancha Bus Terminal
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The bus terminal on the west side of Nancha City, where coaches leave for the coast and the cities beyond. For the farm families of the region it is the door to the rest of the world, and on the platforms there is always someone crying.

areas.name: Bus Terminal Bays
areas.text: Concrete bays where the coaches idle and the luggage goes in underneath.

areas.name: Bus Terminal Ticket Hall
areas.text: A hall of benches, timetables on the walls and a single ticket window.

locations.name: Nancha City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The nearest city to the Lukso Province, six hours west of it by riding bird, with a large store and busy streets where country people stand out at once. Its shopkeepers are honest; some of its young men are not.

areas.name: Market Street
areas.text: The street of stalls where the hoodlums wait for marks.

areas.name: Nancha Store
areas.text: The big store with every floor full of goods.

locations.name: Nancha Old Quarter Inn
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An inn in the old quarter of Nancha City, older than anything around it, cheap and spotless, run by a landlady who rises at four. Country people stay here on market days, and she feeds them as if they were her own.

areas.name: Old Quarter Inn Courtyard
areas.text: A cobbled courtyard with a stone well and a bench under a vine.

areas.name: Old Quarter Inn Kitchen
areas.text: A low kitchen with a range, a long table and a pot always on.

locations.name: Nancha Piko Stable
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low]

A livery stable on the eastern edge of Nancha City where country people leave their animals while they shop. Tall, long-necked Piko stand in the stalls beside the horses and goats, and the stable boy knows which of them bite.

areas.name: Piko Stable Loft
areas.text: The loft above the yard, hay to the rafters and a cot where the boy sleeps.

areas.name: Piko Stable Yard
areas.text: The cobbled yard with its stalls of birds, horses and goats.

locations.name: Nebaska
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A place, probably a town, that most of the world knows only from a news report.

areas.name: Interview Spot
areas.text: The patch of ground where a reporter once set up her camera.

locations.name: Nest Woods
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-34 · Danger: Severe]

Dense forest in the NGL interior, old, unmapped and far from any village.

areas.name: Silent Clearing
areas.text: A clearing where nothing sings.

locations.name: Nettlecloth Weaving Sheds
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Open-sided sheds where the country's cloth is spun and woven by hand from flax and nettle. The rough tunics handed to visitors at the border are cut here, by the hundred, in three sizes that fit no one.

areas.name: Nettlecloth Dye Yard
areas.text: Iron-free wooden vats steaming over fire pits, the cloth inside going brown and dull green.

areas.name: Nettlecloth Loom Shed
areas.text: Forty hand looms in two rows under a thatched roof, clacking from dawn.

areas.name: Nettlecloth Retting Pond
areas.text: A green pond where flax stalks soak under stones until the fibre loosens.

locations.name: NGL
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A self-governed country of the Mitene Union, home to more than two million people who reject modern technology. Nothing made by machine or of synthetic stuff may enter; smuggling a machine, modern medicine or a weapon means prison or death. People write letters and ride horses, and the forests run to the sea.

areas.name: NGL Main Road
areas.text: The dirt road that runs from the border into the country.

areas.name: NGL Market Town
areas.text: A market town of wooden houses where the trade is by barter and coin.

locations.name: NGL Border Stop
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The checkpoint and embassy of the NGL Autonomous Region, built inside two huge hollowed trees. Everyone entering is examined head to foot, x-rayed and scanned, stripped of anything made by machine or of synthetic stuff, and given clothes of natural cloth. People with metal fillings or implants are turned away.

areas.name: Border Truck Road
areas.text:
The end of the road from Rokario, where trucks drop visitors and turn back.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Doli City (about 800 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

areas.name: Clothing Store
areas.text: The room where visitors' clothes are taken and natural cloth is handed out.

areas.name: Examination Trunk
areas.text: The inside of the first tree, with its scanners and its examination tables.

locations.name: NGL Horse Trail
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-32 · Danger: Severe]

A horse trail through the NGL's forests between the border and the villages, the only road most travellers use.

areas.name: Trail Rest Hut
areas.text: A hut where riders rest their horses.

locations.name: NGL Interpreters' Lodge
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A log house just inside the border, where the government's interpreters wait for visitors who have passed the examination. They speak the outside languages, lend horses, and ride along to translate for anyone who wants to talk with the villagers.

areas.name: Interpreters' Lodge Hitching Rail
areas.text: A rail along the front of the lodge where the guides' horses stand saddled and switching flies.

areas.name: Interpreters' Lodge Report Desk
areas.text: A plain back room with a writing desk, a lamp and a locked box of letters waiting for a rider.

locations.name: NGL Reserve Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-36 · Danger: Deadly]

A small post on the edge of the forests where travellers are logged.

areas.name: Ranger Hut
areas.text: The hut where the log is kept.

locations.name: NGL Shore
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-32 · Danger: Severe]

A lonely stretch of the NGL's coast with a fishing hamlet and a beach of driftwood.

areas.name: Driftwood Beach
areas.text: The beach of driftwood and wrack.

locations.name: NGL Stockade
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 22-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The country's prison, a palisade of logs on a low hill. Smugglers of machines, medicine or weapons end up here, breaking stone for the roads, and some do not leave at all.

areas.name: Stockade Cell Row
areas.text: A row of log cells with straw floors and doors barred with oak.

areas.name: Stockade Gallows Yard
areas.text: A small yard behind the cells, kept for the death sentences the law allows.

areas.name: Stockade Stone Yard
areas.text: The yard inside the palisade where prisoners break stone under the watchtower.

locations.name: NGL Village
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small village in the NGL, its houses thatched, its water from a well, its bread from a water mill.

areas.name: Riverbank
areas.text: The river below the village, where the children fish for supper.

areas.name: Village Mill
areas.text: The water mill on the stream.

locations.name: Ninth Avenue Pawnbrokers
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A pawnbroker that never closes during the auctions, buying anything from a wristwatch to a painting for cash on the counter. It sets its price by a phone call to a dealer, and its tickets run thirty days.

areas.name: Pawnbrokers' Grille
areas.text: The barred counter where goods are passed through a slot.

areas.name: Pawnbrokers' Strongroom
areas.text: A back room with the big safe and racks of ticketed goods.

locations.name: Northridge Coal Mine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-10 · Danger: Low]

A coal mine in the hills between the forest preserve and Split Mountain, its winding gear turning over the shaft and its spoil heaps black against the snow. The miners' town below is two streets and a bar.

areas.name: Northridge Deep Gallery
areas.text: The lowest working, low and hot, with a wall of fresh brick at its end.

areas.name: Northridge Miners' Bar
areas.text: A bar in the town with a stove, a dartboard and miners who will not talk.

areas.name: Northridge Pithead
areas.text: The winding gear and the cage that takes the miners down.

locations.name: Nostrade Lookout Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A low ridge of broken rock with a clear view across the flats below, the kind of place where someone could park behind cover and watch a fight without joining it.

areas.name: Lookout Ridge Car Hollow
areas.text: A hollow behind the ridge where cars can wait out of sight.

areas.name: Lookout Ridge Crest
areas.text: The broken crest, with flat rocks to lie behind and binoculars to spare.

locations.name: Nostrade's Mansion
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-26 · Danger: High]

The luxurious house of the Nostrade family, a Mafia family rising fast, where Light Nostrade lives with his daughter Neon and keeps her collection.

areas.name: Nostrade Test Room
areas.text: The room where applicants are tested with a list and an ambush.

areas.name: Trophy Hall
areas.text: The hall where Neon's collection of body parts and curios is shown.

locations.name: Observation Deck
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-32 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A sightseeing platform at the front of the Black Whale, full of outdoor lounge chairs, shops and bars.

areas.name: Bow Lounge
areas.text: The lounge chairs facing the sea at the bow.

locations.name: Old Gordeau Silver Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

The ruin of a mining camp from before the city grew, a single street of wooden fronts, a bank and a mine head fallen in on itself. Tourists come out sometimes; most turn back at the heat.

areas.name: Silver Camp Main Street
areas.text: The single street of leaning wooden shopfronts and a sun-bleached sign.

areas.name: Silver Camp Mine Head
areas.text: The fallen headframe and the black mouth of the shaft beneath it.

locations.name: Old Mafia Recruiting House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

The one concrete building near the road, put up long ago by the Mafia's families so their men had somewhere to sit while they picked recruits. A young man with no record was the best tool a family could buy.

areas.name: Recruiting House Back Office
areas.text: A desk, a dead telephone and a filing cabinet with every drawer emptied.

areas.name: Recruiting House Waiting Room
areas.text: A room of folding chairs where young residents once waited to be chosen.

locations.name: Ostmere Paddy Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-5 · Danger: Low]

A family rice farm on the lowland between the forest and the city, its paddies stepping down a gentle slope to an irrigation ditch. The family sell rice to the city's restaurants and spare rooms to walkers.

areas.name: Ostmere Farmhouse
areas.text: A low house with a tin roof, a porch and the scrapbook on a shelf inside.

areas.name: Ostmere Terraces
areas.text: Stepped paddies of standing water, green with young rice.

locations.name: Outer Gate Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-28 · Danger: Severe]

The road by which outsiders reach the city, watched by residents who say little and remember everything.

areas.name: Residents' Checkpoint
areas.text: The checkpoint where masked residents look at each arrival.

locations.name: Owl's Ambush Gully
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

A narrow gully where the desert road dips over a culvert between two long dunes, a natural trap for a car being chased and a good place to wait for one.

areas.name: Ambush Gully Culvert
areas.text: The concrete culvert where the road crosses the dry bed of the gully.

areas.name: Ambush Gully Dune Crest
areas.text: The crest of the dune above the road, with a clear line down onto it.

locations.name: Oxbow Felling Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-30 · Danger: Severe]

A logging camp at an oxbow bend of the river, where trees are felled with axes, sawn by hand in pits and dragged to the water by ox teams to be floated downstream.

areas.name: Oxbow Ox Lines
areas.text: A rope line where the ox teams are tethered and fed between hauls.

areas.name: Oxbow Sawpits
areas.text: Long pits where two men saw each trunk into planks, one above and one below.

locations.name: Paektae Hill Temple
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-32 · Danger: Severe]

An old temple on a pine-covered hill in the middle of the country, shut since the revolution and kept as a 'cultural site'. A caretaker lives in the gatehouse and sweeps the stair.

areas.name: Hill Temple Bell Court
areas.text: A courtyard with a great bronze bell and an empty altar.

areas.name: Hill Temple Stair
areas.text: A long stone stair through the pines up to the gate.

locations.name: Palace Guard Barracks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-38 · Danger: Deadly]

The barracks of the palace guard, a block of dormitories and a drill yard just outside the walls. The guard are the pick of the army, armed with assault rifles and drilled to stand still for hours in the sun.

areas.name: Guard Barracks Dormitory
areas.text: Long rooms of iron bunks, a rifle chained to each one.

areas.name: Guard Barracks Drill Yard
areas.text: A gravel yard where the guard practises standing still.

locations.name: Palm's Mansion
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A tall, gloomy house on the rise above Doli City, older than the flats around it and let out by the season to whoever can stand the draughts. The furniture comes with it, and so does the smell of damp in the upstairs hall.

areas.name: Palm's Dining Hall
areas.text: A long table under a dusty chandelier, chairs enough for a dozen and only one used.

areas.name: Palm's Doll Shelves
areas.text: Shelves along a back room crowded with home-made rag dolls and pincushions.

areas.name: Palm's Upstairs Hall
areas.text: A narrow hall of closed doors where the floorboards complain at every step.

locations.name: Panda Frog Ponds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low]

A frog farm on the edge of Zaban City, a grid of shallow ponds under bird netting where the city's famous panda frogs are raised for the grill stalls. Visitors can buy them live, cleaned or already skewered.

areas.name: Frog Farm Smoking Shed
areas.text: A shed where frogs are cleaned, skewered and boxed for the city stalls.

areas.name: Frog Pond Grid
areas.text: Rows of shallow ponds under netting, each one croaking.

locations.name: Paper Mound
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

A hill of tipped paper: books, magazines, books and comics, rotting at the bottom and readable at the top. Readers dig themselves hollows in it and stay for hours.

areas.name: Paper Mound Pulp Foot
areas.text: The sodden bottom of the hill, where old paper turns to grey mush.

areas.name: Paper Mound Reading Hollows
areas.text: Burrows dug into the drier upper paper, lined with sacking.

locations.name: Parasta
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 6-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A modest town with its own airport, the nearest place to the Dentora Region where an airship can be hired.

areas.name: Parasta Main Road
areas.text: The main road of shops and cafes.

areas.name: Parasta Taxi Rank
areas.text: The taxi rank by the town hall.

locations.name: Parasta Airport
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-20 · Danger: High]

The airport at Parasta, where blimps and airships can be booked or hired. It is busier than the town.

areas.name: Blimp Field
areas.text: The field where the blimps are moored.

areas.name: Departures Hall
areas.text: The hall of desks and boards.

locations.name: Parasta Back Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A narrow country road that leaves the highway and wanders through fields before rejoining it near Parasta. Locals use it to dodge roadworks.

areas.name: Back Road Farm Gate
areas.text: A farm gate where the road narrows to a single lane.

areas.name: Back Road Field Verge
areas.text: A grass verge between the road and the fields.

locations.name: Parasta Blimp Works
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A repair works near Parasta Airport where blimps are serviced, patched and chartered. Pilots wait here for parts and for clients.

areas.name: Blimp Works Charter Desk
areas.text: A desk with a list of pilots and their rates.

areas.name: Blimp Works Hangar
areas.text: The great hangar where blimps are repaired.

locations.name: Pata City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small city in the Republic of Rokario, one of the modern cities nearest the NGL border.

areas.name: Pata High Street
areas.text: The high street with its shops.

locations.name: Pata City Police Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The main police station of Pata City, a plain concrete block with a flag over the door and a yard of patrol cars behind. Its officers handle traffic, theft and drunks, and have not drawn their guns in years.

areas.name: Pata Police Cells
areas.text: Four barred cells along a tiled corridor that smells of bleach.

areas.name: Pata Police Front Desk
areas.text: A counter behind thick glass with a bell and a sergeant who answers it slowly.

areas.name: Pata Police Motor Yard
areas.text: The fenced yard where the patrol cars are washed and fuelled.

locations.name: Pata Freight Sidings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

A spread of sidings east of Pata City where goods trains are broken up and made again: grain north to Ininge, cement south to Doli City, livestock in slatted wagons that can be heard from the road.

areas.name: Pata Sidings Signal Box
areas.text: A brick box on stilts with a bank of levers and a kettle.

areas.name: Pata Sidings Weighbridge
areas.text: A steel plate set in the ground and the hut that reads it.

locations.name: Pata General Hospital
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The largest hospital between the border and the Miera Mountains, serving Pata City and the farms around it. Its emergency ramp is busy every night and its corridors are painted a calming green that calms nobody.

areas.name: Pata Hospital Ambulance Ramp
areas.text: A covered ramp where ambulances back up to swinging doors.

areas.name: Pata Hospital Green Ward
areas.text: A long ward of beds behind curtains on rails, painted a tired green.

locations.name: Peijin
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: Deadly · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The capital of the Republic of East Gorteau, in the south-east of the country: wide avenues built for parades, the Supreme Leader's portrait on every wall, soldiers at the crossings and poor streets behind the grand ones. The Supreme Leader's palace stands in the wilderness just outside the city.

areas.name: Parade Avenue
areas.text: The great avenue for the leader's parades, lined with his portraits.

areas.name: Peijin Back Quarters
areas.text: The poor streets behind the avenues.

areas.name: Peijin Highway Gate
areas.text:
The checkpoint on the highway into the city, where papers are read and bribes taken.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Doli City (about 6000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Peijin Armour Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-38 · Danger: Deadly]

The army depot on the palace side of the capital, where the tanks and armoured carriers for parades and for the border are kept, fuelled and painted. They come out for the leader's birthday and roll down the parade avenue in perfect lines.

areas.name: Armour Depot Fuel Dump
areas.text: Fenced tanks of diesel behind sandbags and a sentry.

areas.name: Armour Depot Repair Shed
areas.text: A long shed where engines hang from chains over open hulls.

areas.name: Armour Depot Tank Lines
areas.text: Rows of tanks under camouflage netting, numbered and polished.

locations.name: Peijin Assembly Grounds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The vast parade ground of the capital, where the nation is gathered to hear its leader.

areas.name: Parade Stand
areas.text: The stand from which the leader's voice is heard.

locations.name: Peijin Broadcasting House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 28-34 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The state broadcaster's building, the source of every speech the loudspeakers carry. A single radio and television service is made here, and the cables to the street speakers of the capital run out of its basement.

areas.name: Broadcasting House Studio
areas.text: A padded room with one microphone, a clock and a portrait.

areas.name: Broadcasting House Transmitter Room
areas.text: The humming room under the mast, guarded day and night.

locations.name: Peijin Central Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-32 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The terminus of the national railway, built to impress: a hall of marble and painted girders, a great clock that is never wrong, and a pair of soldiers at every platform gate reading passes. Few trains run, and every one runs on time.

areas.name: Central Station Goods Siding
areas.text: The freight yard behind the station, wagons sealed with lead and wire.

areas.name: Central Station Pass Gate
areas.text: The barrier where soldiers read travel passes before anyone reaches a train.

areas.name: Peijin Station Concourse
areas.text: The marble hall under the clock, quiet and swept, with a portrait over each arch.

locations.name: Peijin Foreigners' Hotel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 28-34 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The only hotel where foreigners may stay, a tall block on an island where the river divides. Guests are met by a minder, kept to approved tours and fed in the restaurant on the top floor, which turns slowly over the city.

areas.name: Foreigners' Hotel Lobby
areas.text: A marble lobby where minders wait in armchairs for their guests.

areas.name: Foreigners' Hotel Revolving Restaurant
areas.text: The turning restaurant on the roof, with the capital going by below.

areas.name: Foreigners' Hotel Seventh Floor
areas.text: A floor the lift does not stop at, where the listening equipment is kept.

locations.name: Peijin Go and Shogi Club
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A club on the first floor above a tea shop, where the capital's go and shogi players meet in the afternoons. It is less grand than the Gungi hall and likes itself better for it. The national champions of both games are members and come in to play the regulars.

areas.name: Go and Shogi Club Champions' Wall
areas.text: A wall of framed names, the two current champions at the top.

areas.name: Go and Shogi Club Room
areas.text: Tables of go and shogi boards under a cloud of tea steam and smoke.

locations.name: Peijin Informant Bureau
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 28-36 · Danger: Deadly · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A grey office block on a side street, its brass plate saying only that it serves the people. Citizens bring it names: a neighbour who listens to foreign radio, a cousin who complains. A good report earns rations or a better flat; a missed one, if someone else reports it first, costs the whole household.

areas.name: Informant Bureau Filing Hall
areas.text: Shelves of grey folders, one for every household in the capital.

areas.name: Informant Bureau Letter Slot
areas.text: A slot in the door where anyone may post a name without signing it.

areas.name: Informant Bureau Reward Window
areas.text: A counter where an accepted report is paid out in coupons and favours.

locations.name: Peijin Military Airfield
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-38 · Danger: Deadly]

The military airfield west of the capital, home of the air force's fighters and of the few flights that leave the country with permission. Officials and their families fly from a small terminal at the end of the apron.

areas.name: Airfield Officials' Terminal
areas.text: A small lounge for officials, with carpet, a bar and one window onto the apron.

areas.name: Airfield Revetments
areas.text: Earth walls round the parked fighters, each with a ground crew.

areas.name: Airfield Runway
areas.text: A long concrete runway running out into the grass.

locations.name: Peijin Model School
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The school that visitors are taken to see: clean classrooms, uniformed children who recite the leader's sayings together, and a playground where even the games are marched. The best pupils go on to the army, the state, or the Gungi hall.

areas.name: Model School Classroom
areas.text: A bright classroom of neat desks under a portrait and a slogan.

areas.name: Model School Playground
areas.text: A yard of painted lines where the children march between lessons.

locations.name: Peijin People's Cinema
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The capital's cinema, a big hall under a painted hoarding of the leader. It shows the state's films about his life and his victories, and workplaces send their staff by turns; a name missing from the register is noticed.

areas.name: People's Cinema Auditorium
areas.text: Rows of wooden seats facing a screen with the leader's face on it.

areas.name: People's Cinema Projection Booth
areas.text: A hot booth over the hall, cans of film stacked to the ceiling.

locations.name: Peijin Ration Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The hall where the back quarters of the capital draw their rations, coupon by coupon. The queue starts before dawn, and the clerks know every face in it.

areas.name: Ration Hall Counters
areas.text: A row of wire-fronted windows where coupons are torn and grain weighed out.

areas.name: Ration Hall Queue Yard
areas.text: A muddy yard where the queue waits in lines painted on the ground.

locations.name: Peijin Revolution Monument
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A bronze figure three storeys tall on a stone base: Ming Jol-ik as the young revolutionary who overthrew the old ruling class, rifle in one hand, the other pointing at the future. Citizens lay flowers on his birthday, and they lay them straight.

areas.name: Monument Plinth
areas.text: The base of the statue, its steps covered in rows of flowers and wreaths.

areas.name: Monument Square
areas.text: The wide paved square in front of the statue, where citizens must bow before crossing.

locations.name: Peijin Secretariat of State
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 30-38 · Danger: Deadly · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The ministry from which the country is administered day to day, a columned building on the avenue nearest the palace road. Its head is the Secretary of State, Bizeff, a smooth man in a pinstriped suit who is seen everywhere the leader is and speaks for him when he is not.

areas.name: Secretariat Minister's Office
areas.text: Bizeff's office, wood-panelled, with three telephones and a portrait behind the desk.

areas.name: Secretariat Steps
areas.text: Broad steps where the ministry's black cars wait with their engines running.

locations.name: Peijin State Dance Theatre
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-32 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The national theatre, gilded and red, where the state dance troupe rehearses the routines it performs for the leader and for foreign delegations. The dancers are chosen young, trained hard and sent wherever the palace wants a show, in costumes the palace designs.

areas.name: Dance Theatre Leader's Box
areas.text: A box draped in the national colours, always empty, always dusted.

areas.name: Dance Theatre Practice Room
areas.text: A mirrored room with a barre, where the troupe drills in the mornings.

areas.name: Dance Theatre Stage
areas.text: The raked stage behind the red curtain, marked with tape for the troupe's lines.

locations.name: Peijin State Department Store
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The capital's one department store, built for foreign visitors to see: the ground floor is stocked and lit, the upper floors are half empty, and the escalator stopped years ago. Citizens shop with coupons; foreigners are steered to a counter upstairs.

areas.name: Department Store Loading Yard
areas.text: The yard behind, where crates are counted twice and differently.

areas.name: Department Store Show Floor
areas.text: The bright ground floor, shelves full and staff smiling at the door.

areas.name: Department Store Upper Floors
areas.text: Dim floors of sparse racks, reached by a dead escalator.

locations.name: Peijin Underground Church
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-40 · Danger: Deadly]

A large old church dug beneath one of Peijin's quarters, from the years before the revolution closed the country's places of worship. The stair down is chained, the pews still stand in rows, and the only light falls through a grating in the street above.

areas.name: Underground Church Nave
areas.text: The long nave under its vault, rows of pews facing an empty altar.

areas.name: Underground Church Stair
areas.text: A narrow stair from a back lane, its iron gate chained and padlocked.

areas.name: Underground Church Vestry
areas.text: A low side room where the squatters keep a stove and bedding.

locations.name: Pell Street
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A street of shops selling old trading cards, coins and stamps, a few minutes from the Association's tower. Hunters come here to buy rare things, and other people come to buy something rarer.

areas.name: Pell Street Back Office
areas.text: An office behind one of the shops with a safe and a card reader.

areas.name: Pell Street Card Shops
areas.text: Small shops of glass cases full of cards and coins.

locations.name: Piko Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low]

A faint track running east out of Nancha City into the forests of the Lukso Province, six hours by riding bird and far longer on foot. It forks often, its markers are cut low on the trunks where a stranger would not look, and most who follow it end up back where they started.

areas.name: Piko Road Ford
areas.text: A shallow ford where the track crosses a cold river on flat stones.

areas.name: Piko Road Night Camp
areas.text: A clearing where riders once slept by turns with the birds tethered close.

locations.name: Plume Thicket
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

A thicket of hazel and holly so dense that a walker hears every twig he breaks.

areas.name: Plume Thicket Hazel Tangle
areas.text: A tangle of hazel stems where every step snaps a twig.

areas.name: Plume Thicket Holly Clearing
areas.text: A small clearing walled with holly, the only place to swing a fist.

locations.name: Political Ward
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe]

The ward in the middle of Tier 3 holding the ship's central police station and the Royal Army's office.

areas.name: Central Police Station
areas.text: The four-storey police building with its dorm.

areas.name: Community Safety Section
areas.text: The interview room for visitors who are not under arrest.

locations.name: Poster Press Printworks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low]

The print shop that makes the fight posters on every wall in town, running off thousands a week from photographs the arena sends down. The presses never fully stop.

areas.name: Printworks Drying Lines
areas.text: Lines of wet posters strung across a loft.

areas.name: Printworks Press Hall
areas.text: A hall of presses thumping in rhythm.

locations.name: Preview Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

A market where goods that missed the catalogues are shown before auction and merchants appraise them, run by a man named Taloon. It is the best place to let buyers know what is for sale and when, and full of traps for sellers.

areas.name: Appraisal Table
areas.text: The table where the market's appraisers name a price.

areas.name: Preview Floor
areas.text: The floor where lots are laid out for the merchants to see.

locations.name: Princes' Residential District
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The walled district on Tier 1 where each of the fourteen princes lives in one of fourteen identical rooms, numbered by birth order, set back to back in two rows with walkways between and walls round them all.

areas.name: District Gate
areas.text: The single guarded entrance opposite the banquet hall.

areas.name: Prince's Room Corridor
areas.text: The walkway between the rows of princes' rooms.

locations.name: Puffball Thicket
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A thicket of low bushes in the hills where small furry creatures dart about so fast they are only blurs. Chasing them is the favourite sport of new players, and the bushes are full of the hats they lost doing it.

areas.name: Puffball Thicket Burrows
areas.text: The tangle of bushes and hollows where the puffballs go to ground.

areas.name: Puffball Thicket Open Slope
areas.text: A grassy slope below the thicket where a chase always ends in a tumble.

locations.name: Quant City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A city in the Republic of Rokario, close to the Bilgai Desert.

areas.name: Quant Water Towers
areas.text: The water towers at the edge of town.

locations.name: Quant Motor Lodge
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-24 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A one-storey motel on the highway out of Quant City, rooms in a horseshoe round the car park and an office that smells of instant noodles. Its pool has been empty for years.

areas.name: Quant Lodge Empty Pool
areas.text: A dry pool full of leaves and a broken sun lounger.

areas.name: Quant Lodge Office
areas.text: A cramped office with a bell, a key board and a television on a bracket.

locations.name: Quant Pumping Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The pumping station that lifts water from deep wells and sends it up to the towers of Quant City. Without it the city would be another dry place on the edge of the Bilgai Desert, and every child in town knows it.

areas.name: Quant Pump Engine House
areas.text: A brick hall of pumps and pipes with gauges along one wall.

areas.name: Quant Wellheads
areas.text: Iron caps in the ground inside a fence, each over a shaft going deep.

locations.name: Queens' Living Quarters
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The suites of the king's eight queens on Tier 1, each with its own staff and its own royal guards, who serve the queen, not the prince she bore.

areas.name: First Queen's Drawing Room
areas.text: The first queen's sitting room, cold and formal, where her sons are received.

areas.name: Queens' Suite Corridor
areas.text: A hushed corridor of numbered doors, each with two soldiers outside.

locations.name: Quen City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A city in the Republic of Rokario, one of the three nearest the NGL border.

areas.name: Quen Depot
areas.text: The bus depot.

locations.name: Quen Fire Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The volunteer fire station of Quen City, one engine, one rescue lorry and a crew of shopkeepers who drop their tills when the siren goes. They also pull walkers out of the border woods, which is most of their work.

areas.name: Quen Fire Engine Bay
areas.text: The bay behind the red doors, the engine facing out, boots and coats on pegs.

areas.name: Quen Hose Tower
areas.text: A tall square tower where wet hoses hang to dry, with a ladder to a lookout.

locations.name: Quen Orchards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

Miles of orchard around Quen City, apple and pear in long rows with grass between. In autumn the pickers come from every town in Rokario, and the press in the big barn runs day and night.

areas.name: Quen Cider Barn
areas.text: A big barn with a press, vats and a smell that gets into clothes for days.

areas.name: Quen Orchard Rows
areas.text: Long rows of old trees, their trunks whitewashed against pests.

locations.name: Quiz Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A road through a small town on the way from the port to the pine, where a hunched old woman stops every applicant and asks a question that has no good answer. Those who answer are sent down the wrong road.

areas.name: Masked Square
areas.text: The town square, where the masked people watch the applicants squirm.

areas.name: Quiz Fork
areas.text: The fork where the old woman stands, one road to the pine and one back.

locations.name: Radio Rat Warren
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate]

Rubble and burrows in the hills where an empty suit of armour has been seen marching about and attacking travellers. It cannot be hurt, and it does not tire.

areas.name: Warren Armour Road
areas.text: The stretch of road where the empty armour patrols.

areas.name: Warren Rubble Heaps
areas.text: Heaps of broken stone riddled with fist-sized holes.

locations.name: Raiders' Clearing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

An overgrown clearing within sight of the wall where a large camp once stood. Rotted canvas and rusted gear still lie under the grass.

areas.name: Raiders' Clearing Fire Ring
areas.text: A ring of blackened stones, a rusted generator beside it.

areas.name: Raiders' Clearing Tent Lines
areas.text: The rows of rotted tents and collapsed poles.

locations.name: Rain Cistern Terraces
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Terraces of roofs and gutters built to catch every drop of rain and run it into big plastic tanks. The city has no river worth drinking from, so this is its water.

areas.name: Cistern Gutter Run
areas.text: Long gutters made of pipe split in half, leading in from the roofs.

areas.name: Cistern Tank Stilts
areas.text: A row of great plastic tanks raised on stilts of scaffolding pipe.

locations.name: Reedmouth
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

A village of reed-cutters on stilts at the edge of the Milsy Wetlands, the last place with people in it before the fog. Its families cut reeds for thatch and matting and do not go further in than they can see.

areas.name: Reedmouth Boardwalk
areas.text: A long boardwalk on stilts connecting the houses over the water.

areas.name: Reedmouth Drying Poles
areas.text: A bank of poles where the reeds and nets hang to dry.

locations.name: Reedwater Ford
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

A broad ford on the forest road toward the interior, its banks thick with reed and its shallows loud with frogs.

areas.name: Reedwater Reed Banks
areas.text: Dense reed beds on both banks, where anything could crouch unseen.

areas.name: Reedwater Shallows
areas.text: The ford itself, knee-deep and stony, where the road crosses the river.

locations.name: Relay Mast Mesa
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A flat-topped mesa rising out of the desert, crowned by a radio relay mast that carries the city's telephone and television signals to the towns beyond. A service track winds up its side.

areas.name: Mesa Relay Hut
areas.text: A concrete hut of humming equipment at the foot of the mast.

areas.name: Mesa Service Track
areas.text: The steep dirt track that switchbacks up to the top.

locations.name: Relief Sack Depot
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A shed by the road where food that comes in on the trucks is stored and shared out by the Assembly's tally. Every household gets the same, and arguing does not change it.

areas.name: Depot Sack Store
areas.text: A long shed with sacks stacked to the roof on pallets.

areas.name: Depot Tally Wall
areas.text: A wall chalked with marks for every household, rubbed out and redrawn each week.

locations.name: Republic of Hass
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A republic of the Mitene Union between Rokario to the west and West Gorteau to the east.

areas.name: Hass Border Post
areas.text: The post on the Rokario border.

areas.name: Hass Market Town
areas.text: A market town on the main road.

locations.name: Republic of West Gorteau
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A republic of the Mitene Union between Hass to the west and East Gorteau to the east, whose eastern border is shut.

areas.name: Eastern Border Fence
areas.text: The fence along the border with East Gorteau.

areas.name: West Gorteau Highway
areas.text: The highway through the towns.

locations.name: RG Foundation Tower
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The headquarters of the RG Foundation, a company that has grown fat on government contracts since Kakin's economy began to climb. Its boardroom has a view of the whole harbour, and its directors are invited to every royal function.

areas.name: RG Foundation Boardroom
areas.text: A glass-walled room at the top of the tower with a long table and a harbour view.

areas.name: RG Foundation Lobby
areas.text: A marble entrance hall where security men check every visitor against a list.

locations.name: Ringside Hostel
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A cheap hostel two streets from the tower where fighters on the lower floors sleep until they earn a room inside. The beds are rented by the night and the landlady takes payment before she gives a key.

areas.name: Ringside Hostel Bunk Room
areas.text: A long room of creaking bunks and taped-up posters.

areas.name: Ringside Hostel Kitchen
areas.text: A kitchen where twelve fighters cook rice at once.

areas.name: Ringside Hostel Records Desk
areas.text: The landlady's desk at the door with its book and its key board.

locations.name: Ringwear Outfitters
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A shop on gym row selling everything a fighter wears: uniforms in a dozen school styles, shoes, wraps, mouthguards and the tape that half the tower uses. Its owner was a fighter on the hundreds floors until a knee gave out.

areas.name: Ringwear Fitting Mirror
areas.text: A tall mirror and a bench at the back for trying on uniforms.

areas.name: Ringwear Wrap Counter
areas.text: A counter of rolled wraps, tape and mouthguards in jars.

locations.name: Road End Caravan Lot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

A patch of beaten ground by the road where newcomers who arrive with a vehicle are made to park and wait while the Assembly decides about them. Some wait for weeks.

areas.name: Caravan Lot Waiting Ring
areas.text: A rough ring of vehicles around a shared fire, each facing outward.

areas.name: Caravan Lot Water Barrel
areas.text: A barrel on a stand that the watch fills once a day, and no more.

locations.name: Rokario Border Guard Barracks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The barracks of the Rokario border guard on the road west of Quen City, a fenced compound of huts and garages. Its patrols ride the line with NGL in jeeps, since the other side will not let an engine past.

areas.name: Rokario Guard Mess
areas.text: A low hut of long tables and a hatch where the cook ladles soup.

areas.name: Rokario Guard Motor Pool
areas.text: A row of garages, jeeps and a mechanic who sleeps under one.

areas.name: Rokario Guard Parade Square
areas.text: A square of cracked tarmac where the morning roll is called.

locations.name: Roto Coal Mine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A deep coal mine on the Rokario side of the Roto Mountains, with a winding tower, a washing plant and a village of company houses down the valley. The seam is old and the shafts go further every year.

areas.name: Roto Company Row
areas.text: A row of identical grey houses with coal sacks at every door.

areas.name: Roto Mine Lamp Room
areas.text: A room of racks where each miner hands in his tally and takes his lamp.

areas.name: Roto Pithead
areas.text: The yard under the winding tower where the cage brings the miners up.

locations.name: Roto Mountains
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A range in the south-central Republic of Rokario that runs on into the Republic of Hass.

areas.name: Roto Pass
areas.text: A high pass between the two republics.

locations.name: Roto Pass Customs Post
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The customs post at the top of the road pass through the Roto Mountains, where Rokario ends and the Republic of Hass begins. A barrier, a hut, a stove and two officers who change every fortnight.

areas.name: Roto Pass Barrier
areas.text: A red-and-white pole across the road with a hut beside it.

areas.name: Roto Pass Stove Room
areas.text: A small warm room of forms, stamps and a stove that eats wood fast.

locations.name: Royal Palace of East Gorteau
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The Supreme Leader's residence, a great estate just outside Peijin, enclosed by tall stone walls round a wide courtyard. A central stair climbs to the throne room on the third floor. Nobody goes near it uninvited.

areas.name: Palace Courtyard
areas.text: The wide courtyard inside the walls.

areas.name: Palace Gate
areas.text: The main gate in the walls.

areas.name: Throne Room
areas.text: The throne room on the third floor at the top of the central stair.

locations.name: Rubicuta
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A town near the centre of the island with at least a hundred townsfolk, an alternative to Antokiba for a new player.

areas.name: Rubicuta Square
areas.text: The central square with its fountain.

locations.name: Rustline Factory Row
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A street of abandoned factories on the city's edge, closed since the plants moved somewhere cheaper. The roofs leak, the gates hang open and the squatters keep away after dark.

areas.name: Factory Row Loading Docks
areas.text: A row of dock doors with rusted shutters half rolled up.

areas.name: Factory Row Mill Floor
areas.text: A huge empty floor of bolt-holes where the machines were, under a shattered roof.

areas.name: Factory Row Service Tunnel
areas.text: A low brick tunnel joining the cellars of the mills.

locations.name: Sabazushi's Guard Barracks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A squat concrete block inside the castle walls that houses the armed force guarding the consoles. Its commander, Sabazushi, is a heavy man in a beret who runs his men like a business: shifts on a board, pay on the first of the month, nobody asking what the castle keeps downstairs.

areas.name: Guard Barracks Bunk Room
areas.text: Two rows of steel bunks, footlockers and a radio playing low.

areas.name: Guard Barracks Duty Office
areas.text: Sabazushi's office: a desk, a shift board in grease pencil and a coffee urn.

areas.name: Guard Barracks Motor Pool
areas.text: A concrete apron where two jeeps and a fuel bowser stand ready.

locations.name: Saddlebag Post House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The country has no telephone and no wire, so letters go by rider, and this stable is where the riders change horses and swap their bags. A bell over the gate is rung for an urgent bag, and the whole yard drops what it is doing.

areas.name: Saddlebag Post Sorting Loft
areas.text: A loft over the stalls, lined with pigeonholes for every village in the country.

areas.name: Saddlebag Post Stable Yard
areas.text: The cobbled yard where fresh ponies are saddled while the last rider eats standing up.

locations.name: Saherta Gallery of Modern Art
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A modern art museum of white walls and long galleries, its collection built from what rich patrons bought at the Yorknew auctions and later gave away for their taxes. Students sketch in its halls on free days.

areas.name: Gallery Long Hall
areas.text: A long white hall of canvases and benches.

areas.name: Gallery Sculpture Lawn
areas.text: A lawn of bronze and steel shapes behind the museum.

locations.name: Saloma Mall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A shopping mall in downtown Yorknew, connected to Lipa Station, busy with auction-season shoppers.

areas.name: Mall Atrium
areas.text: The glass atrium with its escalators.

locations.name: Saltgrass Oyster Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-10 · Danger: Low]

Wide tidal flats along the coast where oysters are farmed on stakes. At low tide the flats stretch out for miles; at high tide they are gone.

areas.name: Oyster Flat Channel
areas.text: A deep channel that fills first when the tide turns.

areas.name: Oyster Flat Stakes
areas.text: Rows of stakes with oyster bags tied to them.

locations.name: Sarohan Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-34 · Danger: Severe]

A farming village a short way inside the border, a few dozen houses round a square and a well. It holds festivals for the leader's anniversaries with bunting across the square.

areas.name: Sarohan Village Back Fields
areas.text: Fields behind the houses, rows of cabbages down to a ditch.

areas.name: Sarohan Village Square
areas.text: A dusty square with a well, bunting strung between the roofs.

locations.name: Sea God's Grotto
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

A cavern under the sea off Soufrabi, reached through no door anyone can find, where the walls glow blue and fish swim past windows of rock. Those who have been say it is never the same place twice.

areas.name: Grotto Blue Dome
areas.text: A great air pocket under a dome of glowing rock.

areas.name: Grotto Shifting Passages
areas.text: Tunnels that are never where they were the time before.

locations.name: Sedge Fen
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

Low fenland behind the coast, all reed and black water, crossed by a causeway of logs that rots and is relaid every summer. Reed-cutters and eel-trappers work it, and nobody else goes in.

areas.name: Sedge Fen Eel Traps
areas.text: Wicker traps staked in the channels, checked at dawn by trappers in flat boats.

areas.name: Sedge Fen Log Causeway
areas.text: A narrow causeway of logs sunk into the mud, bending under every step.

locations.name: Sengi Guild
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-28 · Danger: Severe]

A hidden hiring agency in a poor slum, where one agent offers shady jobs to people she judges capable. She turns away anyone who cannot see what she shows them.

areas.name: Agent's Office
areas.text: The small office with its desk and its one chair for visitors.

locations.name: Senior Butlers' House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High]

A quiet house uphill from the butlers' grounds where the oldest of the staff live. It is the tidiest building on the mountain, and younger butlers walk past it a little faster than they need to.

areas.name: Senior Butlers' Parlour
areas.text: A parlour of polished wood, a tea service laid out for guests who never come.

areas.name: Senior Butlers' Porch
areas.text: The deep porch with its rocking chair and its view down the mountain.

locations.name: Setl City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 14-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A city in the Republic of Rokario near the Bilgai Desert.

areas.name: Setl Caravan Market
areas.text: The market where the desert traders come.

locations.name: Setl Glassworks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A glassworks on the edge of Setl City that melts the desert's sand into bottles, jars and window glass. The furnace never goes out, and the men who work at it drink water by the bucket.

areas.name: Setl Furnace Hall
areas.text: A hall of roaring furnaces where blowers turn glowing gobs on long pipes.

areas.name: Setl Glass Packing Yard
areas.text: A yard of straw and crates where the bottles are packed for the railway.

locations.name: Setl Truck Stop
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-24 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A diner, fuel pumps and a car park on the desert road out of Setl City, open all night for the lorries crossing to Hass. The coffee is thin, the portions large, and the radio is always on the traffic.

areas.name: Setl Diner Counter
areas.text: A long counter of stools, pies under plastic domes and a coffee urn.

areas.name: Setl Lorry Park
areas.text: Rows of lorries with their engines ticking, drivers asleep in the cabs.

locations.name: Seventh Door Bar
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A bar near the station named for the gate's last door, where bounty hunters drink before they try the mountain and friends drink after. The back wall is painted with the seven doors, each one labelled with names.

areas.name: Seventh Door Back Booth
areas.text: A curtained booth where contracts are discussed.

areas.name: Seventh Door Taproom
areas.text: The long bar and its stools, under a lamp that swings in the draught.

locations.name: Shale Lookout Cliff
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-34 · Danger: Severe]

A cliff of loose grey shale with a ledge that looks over miles of forest. Hunters and trappers use it to spot game.

areas.name: Shale Lookout Ledge
areas.text: A flat ledge on the cliff's lip, a good place to watch the forest from.

areas.name: Shale Lookout Rock Face
areas.text: The sheer face of shale below the ledge, climbable by something with enough legs.

locations.name: Shingen-ryu Practice Room
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A bare room in the town where a Shingen-ryu pupil practises forms and meditation under a teacher's eye.

areas.name: Practice Mat
areas.text: The mat in the centre of the room.

locations.name: Signal Beacon Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-28 · Danger: Severe]

A bald hill above the forest where a bonfire is kept stacked and ready. With no radio in the country, a lit beacon is the fastest warning there is, and the next beacon along the hills answers it.

areas.name: Beacon Hill Bonfire
areas.text: The great stacked pile of dry wood and tar on the hilltop, ready for a torch.
