areas.name: Beacon Hill Watcher's Hut
areas.text: A turf hut where the watcher sleeps by day and watches by night.

locations.name: Silva's Chamber
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: Severe]

A wide, nearly empty room deep in the mansion where the head of the family receives his children. He sits on the floor among cushions, and the room is so dark the walls are a guess.

areas.name: Chamber Cushion Floor
areas.text: The open floor where Silva sits cross-legged in the dark.

areas.name: Chamber Transmitter Shelf
areas.text: A low shelf with a palm-sized transmitter.

locations.name: Skyfoot Bonesetter
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A bonesetter's clinic in the back streets that treats fighters who cannot afford the tower's doctors or do not want their injuries on file. The old man who runs it works fast and talks the whole time.

areas.name: Bonesetter Treatment Room
areas.text: A padded table, a chart of the skeleton and a smell of camphor.

areas.name: Bonesetter Waiting Bench
areas.text: A bench in the corridor where fighters sit with their arms in towels.

locations.name: Skyfoot Cemetery
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The town's cemetery on the slope that faces the tower, where fighters who died in the arena are buried with their floors carved under their names. The caretaker keeps the paths swept.

areas.name: Cemetery Caretaker's Lodge
areas.text: A small lodge with tools, a kettle and the burial register.

areas.name: Cemetery Fighters' Row
areas.text: A row of stones with fists, belts and floor numbers cut into them.

locations.name: Skyfoot Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-8 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small chapel in the tower's shadow where fighters light candles before a big bout and families light them after. A book by the door holds the names of those who never came down.

areas.name: Skyfoot Chapel Book of Names
areas.text: A lectern by the door with a heavy book of handwritten names.

areas.name: Skyfoot Chapel Candle Rack
areas.text: Racks of candles burning before a plain altar.

locations.name: Skyfoot Market Gardens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low]

Fields and greenhouses on the plain south of the town that grow the vegetables the tower's restaurants serve. The farmers set their working day by the tower's lights going off in the morning.

areas.name: Market Gardens Greenhouses
areas.text: Long glass houses of tomatoes and peppers.

areas.name: Market Gardens Packing Shed
areas.text: A shed of crates where the lorry is loaded for the tower.

locations.name: Skyfoot Night Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The street market that opens when the evening bouts end, filling three blocks behind the tower with food carts, cheap clothes and televisions on poles replaying the day's knockouts.

areas.name: Night Market Clothes Stalls
areas.text: Racks of knock-off fighter jackets and headbands.

areas.name: Night Market Food Lane
areas.text: A lane of grills, noodle carts and plastic stools.

areas.name: Night Market Replay Poles
areas.text: A small square of televisions on poles and a crowd arguing over every punch.

locations.name: Skyfoot Patisserie
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A cake and sweet shop on the plaza road whose window draws children like a magnet. Its owner keeps a framed photo of the best customer she ever had: a white-haired boy, years ago, who came in every day.

areas.name: Patisserie Back Bakery
areas.text: A hot bakery where the chocolate is tempered on marble.

areas.name: Patisserie Window Counter
areas.text: A counter of cakes under glass that the children press their noses to.

locations.name: Skyfoot Police Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-12 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The town's police station, where officers spend most of their time on pickpockets, drunk spectators and fights that start outside the tower without a referee.

areas.name: Police Station Cells
areas.text: Three cells, usually full of drunks on fight nights.

areas.name: Police Station Front Desk
areas.text: A high desk with a bell, a sergeant and a book.

locations.name: Skyfoot Primary School
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-6 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The town's primary school, where every child has an opinion on the week's fights and half of them want to register at the tower the day they are old enough. Their teachers try to keep them interested in arithmetic.

areas.name: Primary School Classroom
areas.text: A classroom of tower drawings and a blackboard of sums.

areas.name: Primary School Yard
areas.text: A tarmac yard with chalk rings and a climbing frame.

locations.name: Skyfoot Quarry Hills
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

Scrub hills north of the town, cut through by an old stone quarry that closed when the tower was finished. Nobody comes up here except hikers who want a photo of the tower and fighters who want to practise somewhere private.

areas.name: Quarry Hills Old Workings
areas.text: Rusted machinery and a collapsed shed by the quarry road.

areas.name: Quarry Hills Pit
areas.text: The deep stone pit of the old quarry, walls stepped and sheer.

areas.name: Quarry Hills Scrub Ridge
areas.text: A ridge of scrub and broken rock with a view of the tower.

locations.name: Skyfoot Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The railway station of the arena's town, built so the tower appears framed in its main doors as passengers walk out. Its walls carry a mural of fighters who climbed high, painted over and redone as they fall.

areas.name: Skyfoot Station Concourse
areas.text: The concourse with the mural and the doors framing the tower.

areas.name: Skyfoot Station Platforms
areas.text: Four platforms under a curved roof, trains in from across the continent.

locations.name: Slatehouse School
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A one-room school where the village children learn letters on slates, sums with pebbles, and the creed of living without machines. The teacher writes to every child's parents by hand each month.

areas.name: Slatehouse Classroom
areas.text: A single room of benches and slates, with a stove and the creed painted over the door.

areas.name: Slatehouse Dig Garden
areas.text: The garden the children dig and plant as part of their lessons.

locations.name: Smoulder Tyre Fields
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: Severe]

A field of tyres that caught fire long ago and has never quite gone out. The smoke lies low and black, and the ground is warm to stand on.

areas.name: Tyre Fields Glow Pits
areas.text: Hollows where the crust has fallen in on red embers below.

areas.name: Tyre Fields Wire Edge
areas.text: The cooled rim, where diggers pull steel wire from burnt casings.

locations.name: Snakebeech Charcoal Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A clearing on the forest's eastern edge where two brothers burn beech into charcoal in turf mounds. Their smoke goes up for days, and they sell the charcoal to the town's stoves and the smokehouse.

areas.name: Charcoal Camp Bark Hut
areas.text: A shelter of bark and tarpaulin with two cots and a stove.

areas.name: Charcoal Camp Kilns
areas.text: Low turf mounds that breathe smoke through holes in their sides.

locations.name: Snakebeech Denning Hollows
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low]

A tangle of gullies on the forest's northern edge where the foxbear mothers dig their dens. Every tree on the way in carries fresh claw marks, and the islanders give the whole slope a wide berth from late winter onward.

areas.name: Denning Hollows Clawed Trunks
areas.text: The ring of scored trees that marks the edge of a mother's ground.

areas.name: Denning Hollows Gully
areas.text: A narrow gully with dens dug into its banks under the roots.

locations.name: Snakebeech Fishing Bend
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A bend of the forest river where the water slows over a gravel bar and the fish rest in the shade of the roots. A boy and a foxbear used to fish here side by side and eat the catch on the stones, and the fire ring they left is still there.

areas.name: Fishing Bend Gravel Bar
areas.text: The bar of round stones that the river leaves dry in winter.

areas.name: Fishing Bend Root Shade
areas.text: The deep, cool water under the overhanging roots where the fish lie.

locations.name: Snakebeech Forest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

The forest of snakebeech trees that covers much of the island, home to the foxbears. The trees carry the foxbears' territory marks, and anyone who walks past them into a mother's ground learns why they are there.

areas.name: Marked Trees
areas.text: The trunks scored with the foxbears' claw marks, the border nobody should cross.

areas.name: Starlit Clearing
areas.text: A clearing in the trees where two boys can lie on their backs and see the whole sky.

locations.name: Snakebeech Sawpit
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

An old sawpit at the forest's northern edge where fallen snakebeech is cut into planks for the boatyard and the town. Two men work the long saw, one in the pit and one above, and the man below eats the sawdust.

areas.name: Sawpit Plank Stacks
areas.text: Planks stacked with spacers to dry in the wind under a roof of boards.

areas.name: Sawpit Trench
areas.text: The deep, sawdust-floored pit under the log trestles.

locations.name: Soeyang Fishing Harbour
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-34 · Danger: Severe]

A fishing harbour on the coast east of the capital, its boats numbered by the state and its catch weighed and taken at the quay. A coastguard launch keeps an eye on every boat that goes out.

areas.name: Soeyang Harbour Drying Yard
areas.text: Racks of split fish drying in the wind behind the harbour.

areas.name: Soeyang Harbour Quay
areas.text: A stone quay where the catch is weighed under a soldier's eye.

locations.name: Soldiers' and Associates' Quarters
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-38 · Danger: Deadly]

The living area on Tier 1 for the Royal Army's soldiers and the hundred and fifty provisional Hunters who passed the 289th Hunter Exam with licences good only for the voyage. It is reached from the heavily guarded left side of the princes' district.

areas.name: Associates' Bunk Rows
areas.text: Rows of steel bunks with a locker at each and a rota on the wall.

areas.name: Quarters Lower-Tier Passage
areas.text: The guarded stair and passage that runs from the barracks down through the ship.

locations.name: Soufrabi
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe]

The port city, on a line of beautiful cliffs, ruled by pirates. A team of exactly fifteen may challenge them; if they drive the pirates out, the town rewards them with a rare card.

areas.name: Cliff Streets
areas.text: The streets along the cliffs, full of pirates.

areas.name: Soufrabi Harbour
areas.text: The little harbour under the cliffs.

locations.name: Soufrabi Lighthouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: Severe]

The lighthouse on the headland of Soufrabi, the pirates' den.

areas.name: Lighthouse Gym
areas.text: The gym inside the lighthouse where the matches are played.

locations.name: Soufrabi Net Lofts
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A row of tarred lofts on stilts above the beach where Soufrabi's fishermen mend their nets and store their gear. Since the pirates came, the men work here in silence and keep their boats hauled up.

areas.name: Net Lofts Boat Chocks
areas.text: The shingle below the lofts where boats lie on chocks.

areas.name: Net Lofts Mending Floor
areas.text: The loft floor heaped with nets and floats.

locations.name: Soufrabi Pirate Tavern
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A harbour tavern in Soufrabi that the pirates have taken for their own, with a skull flag over the door and broken bottles in the street. Townsfolk cross the road rather than pass it.

areas.name: Pirate Tavern Fire Ring
areas.text: The yard behind the tavern, where a ring of burning oil marks out a sumo ring.

areas.name: Pirate Tavern Taproom
areas.text: A low taproom of kegs and rough tables, the pirates' cutlasses stuck in the wood.

locations.name: Sourapple Orchards
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High]

Old orchards on the slope above the border road, picked by hand and pressed by a horse walking in a circle. The apples are small and sharp, and the cider is the only drink in the country stronger than tea.

areas.name: Sourapple Press House
areas.text: A barn where a blindfolded horse turns the press beam and the juice runs into tubs.

areas.name: Sourapple Windfall Rows
areas.text: The low end of the orchard, where the fallen fruit rots sweet in the grass.

locations.name: Southernpiece Auction House
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-28 · Danger: Severe]

Yorknew's leading auction house and one of the most prestigious in the world, organiser of the Southernpiece Auction from the sixth to the tenth of September, the largest anywhere. Its catalogue is the admission ticket and costs a small fortune.

areas.name: Catalogue Desk
areas.text: The reception desk where the catalogue is sold and paid for by bank transfer.

areas.name: Southernpiece Saleroom
areas.text: The great saleroom where the lots are sold.

locations.name: Spear Clearing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A clearing in the woods of Zevil Island with a young tree cut through at the base and the grass sheared around it as if by one long swing.

areas.name: Spear Clearing Bushes
areas.text: The dense bushes at the clearing's edge, a good place to crouch and watch.

areas.name: Spear Clearing Stump
areas.text: The stump of the sapling, cut clean.

locations.name: Spell Card Shop
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The only place in the game where spell cards can be bought, three at random in each pack.

areas.name: Pack Counter
areas.text: The counter where the packs are sold.

locations.name: Spider Eagle Gatherers' Hut
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

A stone hut near the lip of Split Mountain where a few families of egg gatherers have lived for generations. They climb down into the gorge on ropes for the eggs of the Spider Eagle and sell them to the finest kitchens in the world.

areas.name: Gatherers' Hut Hearth
areas.text: The single room of the hut, warm around an iron stove.

areas.name: Gatherers' Rope Ledge
areas.text: A ledge where the ropes are anchored to iron rings over the gorge.

locations.name: Spirit Hollow Ravine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

A narrow ravine west of the starting plain where a dark hollow opens in the cliff. No birds sing in it. Players who step inside vanish from the ravine, and turn up days later saying they walked out somewhere nobody lives.

areas.name: Spirit Hollow Mouth
areas.text: The black mouth in the rock at the ravine's end, cold air breathing out.

areas.name: Spirit Hollow Ravine Floor
areas.text: The stony floor of the ravine between sheer walls.

locations.name: Split Mountain
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

A mountain split cleanly down the middle into two halves, with a strong wind rising through the cleft. Spider Eagles string their nests across the gap on webs.

areas.name: Chasm Edge
areas.text: The lip of the split, where the drop seems to have no bottom.

areas.name: Eagle Webs
areas.text: The webs strung across the chasm with the eagles' eggs hanging from them.

locations.name: Stillwater Bathing Pool
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High]

A small, still lake under a rocky ledge in the hills, deep at one end and reedy at the other. Travellers bathe here and leave their clothes folded on the flat stone, trusting the hills to be empty.

areas.name: Bathing Pool Ledge
areas.text: The rock ledge over the deep end, with a flat stone for clothes.

areas.name: Bathing Pool Reed Shallows
areas.text: The shallow end among the reeds, soft and muddy underfoot.

locations.name: Swardani Central Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The city's main station, a great shed of steel and glass where the high-speed lines meet. A desk on the main concourse is staffed for Hunters on their way to the Association's tower.

areas.name: Association Shuttle Desk
areas.text: A neat desk on the concourse with a banner of the Association.

areas.name: Swardani Concourse
areas.text: The huge concourse with its departures board and morning crowds.

locations.name: Swardani City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A sprawling metropolis best known as the seat of the Hunter Association. Hunters pass through on business with the Association, and the city's hospitals and offices serve them as readily as anyone.

areas.name: Swardani Avenue
areas.text: The broad avenue of offices that leads to the Association's tower.

areas.name: Swardani Station Square
areas.text: The square outside the main station, busy at all hours.

locations.name: Swardani Daily Courier
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The city's morning paper, eight floors of desks and telephones above a basement where the presses roll at midnight. Its reporters have covered the Hunter Association for decades and been granted a handful of interviews in all that time.

areas.name: Courier Morgue
areas.text: The clippings library, a warren of steel drawers labelled by name and year.

areas.name: Courier Newsroom
areas.text: An open floor of desks, ringing phones, overflowing ashtrays and a wall clock running five minutes fast.

areas.name: Courier Press Hall
areas.text: The basement where the rotary presses thunder through the night and the floor shakes.

locations.name: Swardani Hospital
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A large hospital in Swardani City that treats Hunters as well as citizens, with private rooms on its upper floors where a licence buys privacy and a guard at the door.

areas.name: Hospital Lobby
areas.text: The lobby where visitors wait for word.

areas.name: Private Ward
areas.text: The quiet upper floor of private rooms and guarded doors.

locations.name: Swardani Medical University
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

A medical university on the south side of Swardani City with its own teaching hospital, one of the best schools in the kingdom. Its entrance examination is notorious, and its fees are worse.

areas.name: Medical University Admissions
areas.text: A panelled office with a long queue outside it and a secretary who has heard every excuse.

areas.name: Medical University Lecture Theatre
areas.text: A steep wooden theatre of tiered benches looking down on a dissection table.

areas.name: Medical University Library
areas.text: Three floors of medical texts, journals and students asleep on them.

locations.name: Swardani Royal Barracks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

The barracks of an infantry regiment of the kingdom's army on Swardani City's eastern ring road, walled, gated and drilled from dawn. The soldiers stay out of the Association's affairs and the Association returns the courtesy.

areas.name: Barracks Armoury
areas.text: A locked brick armoury of rifle racks, watched by a sentry.

areas.name: Barracks Motor Pool
areas.text: Sheds of trucks and armoured cars, with mechanics under them.

areas.name: Barracks Parade Ground
areas.text: A wide square of tarmac with a flagpole and a reviewing stand.

locations.name: Taba City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: Deadly · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small city of East Gorteau on the highway, under the leader's loudspeakers like every other.

areas.name: Taba Main Road
areas.text: The main road through town.

locations.name: Taba Collective Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: Severe]

A collective farm outside Taba City, its quota painted on a board at the gate and its progress read out over the barn loudspeaker every morning. The farmers keep private plots behind their houses that the state pretends not to see.

areas.name: Collective Farm Fields
areas.text: Long fields of maize and potatoes worked by hand.

areas.name: Collective Farm Tractor Shed
areas.text: A shed with one working tractor and two that are cannibalised for it.

locations.name: Taba Road Inn
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 26-30 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An inn on the highway between Taba City and Luonton City, where lorry drivers eat noodles and sleep for a few hours. Every guest signs the book on the counter, and the book goes to the police every week.

areas.name: Road Inn Bunk Rooms
areas.text: Rooms of bunks rented by the night to drivers.

areas.name: Road Inn Noodle Room
areas.text: A steamy room of tables where drivers eat with their caps on.

locations.name: Tallow Cross Inn
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A coaching inn at the crossroads where the border road meets the roads to the coast and the hills. Carters sleep here, travellers eat here, and the landlord's candle-lit common room is where the country hears its gossip.

areas.name: Tallow Cross Carters' Yard
areas.text: The yard behind the inn where carts are parked in rows and the horses are watered.

areas.name: Tallow Cross Common Room
areas.text: A low-beamed hall of long tables, lit by tallow candles and loud with carters.

areas.name: Tallow Cross Guest Gallery
areas.text: A creaking upstairs gallery of small rooms with straw mattresses.

locations.name: Tarsetol Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High]

A train station in Yorknew City.

areas.name: Tarsetol Platform
areas.text: The platform where a private train can wait.

locations.name: Tenth Point Bar
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A smoky bar named for the point that ends a fight, where fighters drink after losing and spectators drink after betting. The big screen shows every televised bout, and the regulars score them aloud before the judges do.

areas.name: Tenth Point Back Booths
areas.text: Booths in the back where nobody watches the screen.

areas.name: Tenth Point Long Bar
areas.text: A scarred bar with a screen above it.

locations.name: Testing Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-20 · Danger: High]

The main gate of the Zoldyck estate: seven doors, each pair of panels twice as heavy as the last, the first panels weighing two tons each. It opens as far as the pusher's strength. Beside it is a small side door the tourists are told about with a wink.

areas.name: Gate Face
areas.text: The seven-door gate itself, its panels marked with their numbers.

areas.name: Guards' Door
areas.text: The small door beside the gate, the way intruders go in and do not come out.

locations.name: Thatchwright's Yard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A yard where reed is cut, bundled and dried, and where the country's thatchers and carpenters keep their tools. Every roof in the district was laid by a hand trained here.

areas.name: Thatchwright Practice Roof
areas.text: A half-finished roof on posts, where apprentices learn the craft.

areas.name: Thatchwright Reed Stacks
areas.text: Tall stacks of reed bundles drying under a lean-to.

locations.name: Tier 1
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-40 · Danger: Deadly]

A separate cruise ship floating in a great pool on top of the Black Whale, for the royal family, the V5's politicians, the great industrialists and the bosses of Kakin's three biggest Mafia families. Eight hundred guards and soldiers patrol its halls.

areas.name: Tier 1 General Store
areas.text: The store where rare items can be ordered and delivered by drone, blimp or fast boat.

areas.name: Tier 1 Pool Deck
areas.text: The deck round the great pool in which the cruise ship floats.

locations.name: Tier 1 Cell Block
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The ship's jail on Tier 1, where suspects wait in standard cells for a court-martial. One cell, furnished for royalty, is kept for prisoners who cannot be treated like anyone else.

areas.name: Cell Block First-Class Cell
areas.text: A cell with a soft bed, a rug and a writing desk behind its bars.

areas.name: Cell Block Standard Cells
areas.text: A row of narrow steel cells off a bare corridor.

locations.name: Tier 1 Supreme Court
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The highest court aboard the Black Whale, sitting on Tier 1 with the Supreme Magistrate Cleapatro on its bench. Even under martial law, the court hears cases that touch the royal family.

areas.name: Supreme Court Bench
areas.text: The raised bench where the magistrate sits, with a telephone at her elbow.

areas.name: Supreme Court Hearing Floor
areas.text: The floor below the bench where parties stand to be heard.

locations.name: Tier 1 VIP Casino
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-40 · Danger: Deadly]

A casino for the great of Tier 1, part of the deck's recreation area: slot machines in ranks, poker tables with dealers, and hostesses who carry drinks between them.

areas.name: Casino Card Room
areas.text: A quieter room of green baize tables where the stakes are high.

areas.name: Casino Slot Floor
areas.text: A bright floor of slot machines chiming under the chandeliers.

locations.name: Tier 2
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-36 · Danger: Deadly]

The highest tier inside the hull, for celebrities and the rich, with six hundred guards and soldiers. A thick bulkhead separates it from the lower tiers and opens only from this side.

areas.name: Ministry of Justice Headquarters
areas.text: The ministry's offices for legal matters on the upper tiers.

areas.name: Theater Venue
areas.text: A small auditorium with a big screen and loges.

areas.name: Tier Bulkhead
areas.text: The thick bulkhead between Tier 2 and Tier 3.

locations.name: Tier 3
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe]

The middle of the hull and the highest tier for ordinary passengers, with cabins of a bed, cupboards and a bathroom along corridors that open on assembly points. The wards for politics and medicine are here.

areas.name: Tier 3 Assembly Point
areas.text: An open assembly point where the cabin corridors meet.

areas.name: Tier 3 Cabins
areas.text: The corridors of passenger cabins.

locations.name: Tier 3 Central Court
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe]

The court for the lower tiers, in the middle of Tier 3, where passengers bring complaints and the accused are heard.

areas.name: Central Court Clerk's Window
areas.text: A window where complaints are filed on forms in triplicate.

areas.name: Central Court Public Benches
areas.text: Rows of benches full of passengers waiting for their case.

locations.name: Tier 3 First-Class Cabins
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe]

The first-class cabins of Tier 3, the best a general passenger can buy: suites with a sitting room, a bedroom and a bath, near the top of the tier.

areas.name: First-Class Cabin Corridor
areas.text: A carpeted corridor of brass-numbered doors.

areas.name: First-Class Cabin Suites
areas.text: Suites with a sofa, a bed behind a partition and a bath.

locations.name: Tier 4
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe]

The largest of the lower tiers, in the middle of the hull, with one medical clinic and the Royal Army's conference room.

areas.name: Royal Army Conference Room
areas.text: The room where the officers responsible for security meet.

areas.name: Tier 4 Halls
areas.text: The crowded passenger halls.

locations.name: Tier 4 Passenger Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 20-34 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

One of the clinics of Tier 4, set up in a hall meant for something else, with a handful of beds and a line of patients that never shortens.

areas.name: Passenger Clinic Triage Desk
areas.text: A desk at the door where a nurse sorts the queue.

areas.name: Passenger Clinic Ward
areas.text: A hall of folding beds behind curtains.

locations.name: Tier 5
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe]

The smallest and lowest tier, at the bottom of the hull beside the propeller and wholly below the sea, with one clinic and no doctor. Its one cafeteria is reached by a single passage.

areas.name: Assembly Point 37564
areas.text: An assembly point among the cabins of the lowest tier.

areas.name: Central Dining Hall
areas.text: The one cafeteria of Tier 5, at the end of a single passage.

locations.name: Tier 5 Sick Bay
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe]

The one clinic of Tier 5, with beds and shelves and no doctor of its own. Passengers who know some first aid take turns at the desk.

areas.name: Sick Bay Volunteer Desk
areas.text: A desk where a passenger with a first-aid kit does what can be done.

locations.name: Tin Roof Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-20 · Danger: High]

A squatters' camp of tin and plywood shacks where the city meets the desert, home to day labourers, runaways and families who lost a lease. Water comes from a standpipe the city forgot to close.

areas.name: Tin Roof Council Shack
areas.text: The biggest shack, where the old women sit on crates and hear complaints.

areas.name: Tin Roof Standpipe
areas.text: The single tap in the middle of the camp, with a queue of buckets beside it.

locations.name: Togari's Duel Chamber
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A round stone room somewhere in the upper half of the tower, bare but for a rack of knives and two doors. Whoever lands in it from the roof finds that the path below runs through it and through whoever is waiting there.

areas.name: Togari's Blade Rack
areas.text: The rack along the curved wall where the tower's spare knives hang beside Togari's whetstone.

areas.name: Togari's Lower Door
areas.text: The door on the far side of the chamber, which only opens once the room is settled.

locations.name: Tower Freight Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

The yard at the back of the tower where the lorries unload what a vertical city eats and wears in a day: crates of vegetables, sacks of rice, linen, beer and the arena's own merchandise.

areas.name: Freight Yard Loading Dock
areas.text: A long concrete dock with rubber bumpers and a goods lift.

areas.name: Tower Yard Foreman's Hut
areas.text: A hut with a kettle, a clipboard and a calendar of pin-ups.

locations.name: Tower Gondola Depot
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The depot of the crews who clean the tower's windows and repair its outside, working in gondolas hung from the roof. It takes them months to work from top to bottom, and then they start again.

areas.name: Gondola Depot Harness Room
areas.text: Rows of harnesses and a board of who is on which face of the tower.

areas.name: Gondola Depot Rack Hall
areas.text: A hall of gondolas, winches and cable drums.

locations.name: Tower Pawn and Loan
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A pawnshop on the poster street full of fighters' belongings: championship belts from small towns, gloves, watches and the occasional gold tooth. A fighter who loses a run of bouts usually ends up at its counter.

areas.name: Pawn and Loan Counter
areas.text: A counter behind a grille, with a bell and a magnifying glass.

areas.name: Pawn and Loan Trophy Shelves
areas.text: Shelves of dusty trophies from tournaments no one remembers.

locations.name: Tower River Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The flats of the river below the town, all reeds, gravel bars and slow water, where fighters do their roadwork along the banks and old men fish for carp with the tower reflected in the water.

areas.name: River Flats Footbridge
areas.text: An iron footbridge over the river, its rail scratched with names.

areas.name: River Flats Reed Beds
areas.text: Tall reeds full of birds and the hum of insects.

locations.name: Tower Shadow Park
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The park beside the tower, crossed each day by its long shadow. Fighters run laps here at dawn and spectators eat lunch here at noon, and a quiet corner of it is used by teachers who do not want to be watched.

areas.name: Tower Shadow Quiet Corner
areas.text: A ring of trees with a stone bench out of sight of the paths.

areas.name: Tower Shadow Running Track
areas.text: A gravel loop round the park where the shadow passes over the runners.

locations.name: Tower Strait Pier
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 5-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A fishing village built over the water on the strait facing Trick Tower, with boats, nets and a fish market under a tin roof.

areas.name: Strait Pier Fish Market
areas.text: The covered market where the catch is sold at dawn.

areas.name: Strait Pier Net Racks
areas.text: The racks where the nets dry in the wind.

locations.name: Tower Warders' Village
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 5-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A cluster of houses on the cliff path below the tower where the guards, cooks and clerks of the prison live with their families. It has a canteen, a small shop and a bus that runs the shifts up the hill.

areas.name: Warders' Bus Stop
areas.text: The stop by the gate where the shift bus waits.

areas.name: Warders' Canteen
areas.text: The canteen where the shifts eat and the radio plays the news.

areas.name: Warders' Row Houses
areas.text: The row of plain staff houses looking out over the strait.

locations.name: Tower Workers' Tenements
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 4-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The apartment blocks across the river road where the tower's cleaners, cooks, guards and lift attendants live. The children of the blocks play at being Floor Masters in the courtyards.

areas.name: Tenements Courtyard
areas.text: A paved yard of washing lines, bikes and chalked rings.

areas.name: Tenements Stairwell
areas.text: A concrete stairwell where the neighbours gossip on the landings.

locations.name: Trade Shops
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The card shops of the game, in Antokiba and Masadora, where players sell cards, buy information about cards and places, and bank their money, which in the game is itself a card.

areas.name: Card Bank
areas.text: The bank behind the counter.

areas.name: Card Counter
areas.text: The counter where cards are bought and sold.

locations.name: Traffickers' Track
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-32 · Danger: Severe]

An old track across the waste ground at the city's back, made by the vans of outsiders who came to take residents because the law did not count them as people. It is no longer used, and the residents want it remembered.

areas.name: Track Burned Van
areas.text: The shell of a van burned where it stopped, its doors still chained.

areas.name: Track Shoe Post
areas.text: A tall post at the track's end, heavy with small shoes on strings.

locations.name: Trappers' Longhut
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-30 · Danger: Severe]

A long hut where the country's fur trappers winter and trade, deep in the northern woods. Pelts are stretched on frames outside, and the trappers know every animal track for days around.

areas.name: Longhut Hearth End
areas.text: The far end of the hut, where the trappers sit around one fire and tell tales.

areas.name: Longhut Pelt Frames
areas.text: Rows of wooden frames outside the hut, each with a pelt stretched to dry.

locations.name: Trash Heaps
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-30 · Danger: Severe]

The hills of rubbish that make up most of the city, shifting underfoot and higher than houses. People live on them and dig in them, and some die in them.

areas.name: Heap Summit
areas.text: The top of a rubbish hill with a view over the city.

areas.name: Sinking Ground
areas.text: The soft, shifting lower slopes.

locations.name: Treefoot
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The town that has grown up at the foot of the World Tree, its streets of hotels, souvenir shops and cafés all turned towards the trunk. Guides in uniform wait at the coach stop to tell visitors the tree's history whether or not they want to hear it.

areas.name: Treefoot Coach Stop
areas.text: A wide lay-by where the tour coaches turn and unload.

areas.name: Treefoot Guides' Stand
areas.text: A kiosk by the coach stop where the uniformed guides wait with brochures.

areas.name: Treefoot Main Street
areas.text: A street of souvenir shops, cafés and postcards of the tree, every window facing it.

locations.name: Treefoot Climbers' Outfitter
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A climbing shop in a converted barn on the edge of Treefoot, selling ropes, harnesses, gloves and advice. The owner climbed to the crown twice when she was young and now spends her days talking customers out of trying.

areas.name: Outfitter Bouldering Wall
areas.text: A plywood wall studded with holds where customers prove they can hang on.

areas.name: Outfitter Shop Floor
areas.text: Racks of harnesses and boots, rope hanging from the beams.

locations.name: Tri-Orb Hotel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A hotel beside a train station in Doli City, cheap and plain.

areas.name: Tri-Orb Room
areas.text: A small room with two beds and a view of the tracks.

locations.name: Trick Tower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A huge cylindrical stone tower with no windows and no stairs on its outside, used as a prison, its inside a maze of traps and puzzle rooms. Applicants landed on its roof have seventy-two hours to reach the bottom alive.

areas.name: Majority Path
areas.text: The route where five must vote at every door, each with a wrist timer.

areas.name: Prisoners' Arena
areas.text: A stone platform over a drop where prisoners challenge the applicants.

areas.name: Tower Roof
areas.text: The flat roof where the airship sets the applicants down, with its hidden trapdoors.

areas.name: Warden's Control Room
areas.text: The room of screens where the warden watches every path.

locations.name: Trick Tower Cell Block
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The prison that fills most of the tower in the months without an exam: tiers of cells around a deep central well, built for the long sentences the courts of the region hand down to their worst.

areas.name: Cell Block Gantries
areas.text: The steel walkways the guards patrol above the well.

areas.name: Cell Block Lowest Tier
areas.text: The bottom tier, where the prisoners with no end to their sentences are kept.

areas.name: Cell Block Mess Hall
areas.text: The long hall where the prisoners eat in shifts under the guards' eyes.

locations.name: Trick Tower Cliffs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The sheer outer walls of Trick Tower and the air around them, where six-legged flying beasts nest and circle. Anyone outside the tower below its roof is prey.

areas.name: Beast Ledges
areas.text: The ledges where the flying beasts roost.

areas.name: Climbing Face
areas.text: The handholds down the outer wall, the climber's only path.

locations.name: Trick Tower Drop Shafts
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

The chutes under the tower's roof, each fed by one hidden trapdoor that takes one person and then locks. Every shaft ends in a different room, and no two of those rooms lead the same way down.

areas.name: Drop Shaft Landing Mats
areas.text: The rooms at the bottom of the chutes, padded with canvas.

areas.name: Drop Shaft Trapdoors
areas.text: The one-use trapdoors set flush in the roof stones.

locations.name: Trick Tower Fork Room
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Near the bottom of the Majority Path the route splits: a long way round that takes most of the time left, and a short way that opens only when two of the party have locked themselves to the wall in shackles.

areas.name: Fork Room Long Stair
areas.text: The winding stair of the long path, which drinks time.

areas.name: Fork Room Partition
areas.text: The stone partition between the two paths, thinner than it looks.

areas.name: Fork Room Shackle Wall
areas.text: The wall of manacles that the short door counts before it opens.

locations.name: Trick Tower Infirmary
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The prison's small ward, where guards and inmates alike are stitched up after a fight. During the exam it also takes in applicants pulled out of the tower before their time ran out.

areas.name: Infirmary Dispensary
areas.text: A locked cupboard of drugs and splints beside the medic's desk.

areas.name: Infirmary Ward Beds
areas.text: Six iron beds behind a curtain, two of them with restraints.

locations.name: Trick Tower Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The exit and jetty at the foot of Trick Tower, where those who make it down within the time are greeted, draw a card from a box and board a boat for the next phase.

areas.name: Island Boat Jetty
areas.text: The jetty where the boat waits for the two-hour crossing.

areas.name: Tower Exit
areas.text: The door at the bottom of the tower, the end of the seventy-two hours.

locations.name: Troupe Hideout
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

An abandoned, half-ruined building on the edge of Yorknew City, its windows broken and its floors open to the sky. Squatters avoid it.

areas.name: Rubble Hall
areas.text: The great broken hall where the Troupe sits on the debris.

areas.name: Upper Floors
areas.text: The half-collapsed upper floors, open to the sky.

locations.name: Tsezguerra's Hilltop Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-26 · Danger: High]

A tidy camp on a hilltop with four tents in a square and a lookout always posted. The team that keeps it is all professional Hunters and does not welcome visitors.

areas.name: Hilltop Camp Lookout
areas.text: A post with binoculars over the slope.

areas.name: Hilltop Camp Map Board
areas.text: A board with an island map and card lists.

locations.name: Tsubashi Street
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low]

A district of Zaban City where an applicant who knows the address is led past a grand building to the cheap restaurant beside it. Strangers who come looking for the exam without the address find only shops.

areas.name: Tsubashi Corner
areas.text: The corner at the address, where the great building stands beside the little restaurant.

locations.name: Tsubashi Tower
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

The tall office tower that stands beside the exam's address on Tsubashi Street, all glass and marble and corporate nameplates. Every January applicants march into its lobby sure that the exam must be here, and every January the guards march them out again.

areas.name: Tsubashi Tower Lift Shafts
areas.text: A bank of lifts and the dark service shafts behind them.

areas.name: Tsubashi Tower Lobby
areas.text: A marble lobby with a reception desk, turnstiles and two bored guards.

locations.name: Twin Ridges
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

The mountains that rise on either side of the island, forested to their tops, cut by streams and hard going for anyone without a guide. The island's children learn the paths by getting lost on them.

areas.name: Ridge Path
areas.text: The narrow path along the ridge top, slippery after rain.

areas.name: Stream Gully
areas.text: A cold stream that runs down a gully to the sea.

locations.name: Twin Ridges Falls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A waterfall where the stream off the western ridge drops into a fern-hung gorge. The plunge pool is deep and cold, and the young deckhands jump into it from the rocks at the top to prove they can.

areas.name: Falls Hidden Ledge
areas.text: A narrow dry ledge behind the falling water.

areas.name: Falls Plunge Pool
areas.text: The deep green pool at the foot of the falls, ringed with mossy boulders.

locations.name: Twin Ridges Radio Mast
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low]

A steel radio mast on the higher of the two ridges, put up so the island's radios could reach the mainland and the ships at sea. A hut at its foot holds the batteries and a weather recorder.

areas.name: Radio Mast Battery Hut
areas.text: A small hut of batteries, a charger and a weather recorder's paper drum.

areas.name: Radio Mast Foot
areas.text: The base of the steel mast, bolted to the rock, with the stays humming overhead.

locations.name: Uga Forest
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-32 · Danger: Severe]

A forest of large trees and short undergrowth within Meteor City.

areas.name: Uga Clearing
areas.text: The clearing among the great trees.

locations.name: Underground Clinic
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-36 · Danger: Deadly]

An illegal clinic somewhere in East Gorteau, filthy and decaying, run by a nurse who charges for everything, the telephone included.

areas.name: Clinic Bed
areas.text: The one bed in a dirty room.

locations.name: Underground Lake
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

A lake in a great cavern under East Gorteau, where trees grow under the water.

areas.name: Cavern Shore
areas.text: The stony shore round the lake.

areas.name: Drowned Trees
areas.text: The trees standing under the clear water.

locations.name: Upland Goat Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A hill farm north-west of the town where goats are kept for milk and cheese. Its cheese is sold in the market and served at the inn.

areas.name: Goat Farm Cheese Room
areas.text: A cool stone room of cheeses on shelves.

areas.name: Goat Farm Pasture
areas.text: Steep pasture fenced with wire.

locations.name: Uvogin's Old Territory
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

A ridge of crushed cars and tyres that one huge boy claimed as his own when he was still a child. Other children paid him in finds to cross it, and anything dumped on it was his.

areas.name: Old Territory Crush Ridge
areas.text: The spine of flattened cars, sharp-edged and slick when it rains.

areas.name: Old Territory Tyre Fort
areas.text: A ring of stacked tyres at the ridge top with a throne made of a car seat.

locations.name: Videotape Diggings
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-24 · Danger: High]

A stretch of heaps where electrical waste is tipped, rich in videotapes and cassettes. Children come here to dig for something to watch at the church.

areas.name: Diggings Ribbon Field
areas.text: A slope where unspooled tape lies in drifts and snaps underfoot.

areas.name: Diggings Sorting Rock
areas.text: A flat slab where the diggers lay out their finds and argue over them.

locations.name: Village of the Bandits from the Mountains
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

A poor village in the mountains where the bandits live, all of them ill with something no medicine cures. They ask everyone for help.

areas.name: Sick Huts
areas.text: The huts where the ill lie on mats.

areas.name: Village Well
areas.text: The well in the centre.

locations.name: VIP Witness Protection Area
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 28-38 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The witness area inside the Ministry of Justice building on Tier 2, furnished like a fine hotel and called by the ministry the safest place on the ship. The ministry has its own armed officers in their own uniform.

areas.name: Deputy Prosecutor's Office
areas.text: A small office lined with full bookcases, Kaiser's own.

areas.name: Witness Area Interrogation Rooms
areas.text: A row of plain rooms with a table, two chairs and a mirror.

areas.name: Witness Area Visiting Booth
areas.text: A booth divided by panels of glass, with a drawer on each side for papers.

locations.name: Visca Forest Preserve
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A forest preserve beyond the wetlands, its streams and lakes thick with fish and its clearings ruled by the Great Stamp, a pig with no equal for temper. Gourmet examiners hold their phase here.

areas.name: Cooking Ground
areas.text: The open ground with the examiners' kitchens and the judges' table.

areas.name: Fishing Stream
areas.text: A cold stream full of fish, crowded with applicants who have heard the word sushi.

areas.name: Stamp Grounds
areas.text: The clearings where the Great Stamps charge anything that moves.

locations.name: Visca Lakeside Lodge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

A timber lodge on the largest lake in the Visca Forest Preserve, built for anglers and naturalists who come with a permit. Its kitchen is good, its rooms are plain and its guestbook carries the names of Gourmet Hunters.

areas.name: Visca Lodge Great Room
areas.text: A beamed room with a fireplace, armchairs and the guestbook on a stand.

areas.name: Visca Lodge Jetty
areas.text: A wooden jetty with rowing boats and a view across the lake.

areas.name: Visca Lodge Kitchen
areas.text: A big kitchen with a wood stove, steel counters and a walk-in larder.

locations.name: Visca Ranger Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

The preserve's gate and ranger cabin, where permits are checked and visitors warned that the pigs here charge cars. The rangers drive the boundary in an old jeep and patch it after every storm.

areas.name: Ranger Post Cabin
areas.text: The cabin with its bunks, radio and maps of the preserve pinned to the walls.

areas.name: Ranger Post Gate
areas.text: A barrier pole across the track, a hut and the permit book.

locations.name: Visitors' Bunkhouse
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 14-22 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The only place an outsider may sleep in the city, and only with the Assembly's leave. The host feeds guests, watches them, and walks them back to the road when their time is up.

areas.name: Bunkhouse Cot Room
areas.text: A long room of cots, with a barred window and a stove at the end.

areas.name: Bunkhouse Host's Kitchen
areas.text: A kitchen by the only door, where the host cooks and sees everyone who passes.

locations.name: VVIP Living Quarters
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Deadly]

The residences on Tier 1 for the ship's most important guests from outside the royal family: politicians of the great powers, captains of industry and the bosses of Kakin's three great Mafia families, whose luggage allowance is second only to the king's.

areas.name: Onior's Cross-Bridge
areas.text: A private bridge from the Xi-Yu boss's residence to the tier below.

areas.name: VVIP Princes' Wall Corridor
areas.text: A long guarded corridor along the outer wall of the princes' district.

locations.name: VVIP Recreational Facilities
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-40 · Danger: Deadly]

Private leisure rooms on the odd-numbered side of the princes' district, reached only from inside the district's own entrance and set aside for the princes alone.

areas.name: Recreational Facilities Pool
areas.text: A tiled indoor pool, lit from below, with loungers along its edge.

areas.name: Recreational Facilities Screening Lounge
areas.text: A small cinema of deep armchairs and a private projector.

locations.name: Wallside Woods
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A strip of old woodland along the outside of the boundary wall, where tourists slip away from the bus to take photographs and pick mushrooms. It feels safe because it is outside the wall.

areas.name: Wallside Woods Mushroom Glade
areas.text: A clearing thick with pale mushrooms.

areas.name: Wallside Woods Photo Rock
areas.text: A boulder with a view of the wall, worn smooth by tourists.

locations.name: Waxlight Chandlery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-24 · Danger: High]

A chandler's house and its bee yard. With no electric light in the country, every lamp and candle burns tallow or beeswax, and the chandler's beeswax candles are the ones the longhouse buys.

areas.name: Waxlight Dipping Room
areas.text: A dark room where candles are dipped and hung from racks to harden.

areas.name: Waxlight Skep Row
areas.text: A line of straw beehives on a bench, humming in the sun.

locations.name: West Gorteau Army Garrison
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The main garrison of the West Gorteau army, a walled compound a few miles from the closed eastern border. Its soldiers patrol the fence and stare across it at a country that stares back.

areas.name: West Gorteau Garrison Interview Room
areas.text: A bare room with a table, two chairs and a mirror that is not a mirror.

areas.name: West Gorteau Garrison Vehicle Park
areas.text: A fenced park of armoured cars and fuel bowsers.

areas.name: West Gorteau Garrison Watchtower
areas.text: A concrete tower with binoculars on a stand pointed east.

locations.name: West Gorteau Customs Warehouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: Severe]

A bonded customs warehouse near the West Gorteau border where goods seized at the frontier are held until someone claims them or the state sells them off. It is full of things nobody admits to owning.

areas.name: West Gorteau Bonded Dock
areas.text: A dock of roller doors where the seized lorries back in.

areas.name: West Gorteau Bonded Racks
areas.text: High steel racks of sealed crates in rows, lit by strip lights.

locations.name: West Gorteau Highway Motel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 16-26 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A motel on the highway through West Gorteau, the last decent bed before the road reaches the shut border and turns south. Journalists and aid workers stay here when they come to look at the east.

areas.name: West Gorteau Motel Bar
areas.text: A dark bar off the lobby where the same few men are always drinking.

areas.name: West Gorteau Motel Restaurant
areas.text: A restaurant with a long window over the road and a menu in three languages.

locations.name: West Gorteau Radio Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The national radio station of West Gorteau, a squat building under a tall mast that carries its programmes far into the east. Its news is read twice an hour by announcers who know who is listening.

areas.name: West Gorteau Broadcast Studio
areas.text: A soundproofed studio of microphones and a red light over the door.

areas.name: West Gorteau Record Library
areas.text: Shelves of records in paper sleeves, catalogued by a librarian with a cough.

locations.name: West Gorteau Textile Mills
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A row of red-brick textile mills along a river in West Gorteau, spinning and weaving cotton for the whole Union. The looms run in three shifts, and the town on the hill lives by the mill whistle.

areas.name: West Gorteau Mill Riverside
areas.text: The mill race and the river bank where the workers eat at midday.

areas.name: West Gorteau Weaving Shed
areas.text: A shed of clattering looms under north-light roofs, fluff in the air.

locations.name: Whale Back Airship Pad
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-36 · Danger: Deadly]

The landing ground on the back of the Black Whale where airships set down, and the pontoon along its flank where ferries come alongside. Too big to dock anywhere, the ship takes on everything it needs here.

areas.name: Airship Pad Landing Circle
areas.text: A painted landing circle with wind socks and a ground crew.

areas.name: Whale Flank Ferry Pontoon
areas.text: A floating pontoon along the hull where ferries tie up to unload.

locations.name: Whale Island
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A small island port that fishing boats use more than anyone lives in it. A handful of families keep the town on the slope above the harbour, the forest covers most of the rest, and mountains rise on either side. Ging Freecss and his cousin Mito were born here, and Mito now raises Ging's son Gon, one of the only two children on the island.

areas.name: Harbour Street
areas.text: The one street that climbs from the quay past the chandler and the few shops to the houses.

areas.name: Upper Town
areas.text: The houses at the top of the slope, gardens and washing lines facing out to sea.

areas.name: Whale Island Harbour
areas.text:
The stone quay and its moorings, where the fishing boats tie up and the ships for the mainland call when the weather is fit.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: ferries sail to Dolle Harbor (about 3000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Whale Island Bakehouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A one-oven bakery up a lane off the harbour, lit before the boats go out so the crews can take a loaf with them. The baker is the first person awake on the island and the first to see who came home late.

areas.name: Bakehouse Lane Window
areas.text: The window onto the lane where the loaves are handed out to the crews.

areas.name: Bakehouse Oven Room
areas.text: A hot room around the brick oven, with long wooden peels on the wall.

locations.name: Whale Island Boatyard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A sloping yard at the harbour's western end where boats are hauled out on a cradle to be scraped, caulked and painted. The yard's shed smells of pitch and hot steel, and its owner builds a new dinghy each winter just to keep his hand in.

areas.name: Boatyard Dinghy Bench
areas.text: A bench at the back where the winter's new dinghy is taking shape plank by plank.

areas.name: Boatyard Shed
areas.text: The long shed of tools, with a welding set, a steam box for bending planks and a stove.

areas.name: Boatyard Slipway
areas.text: The greased timber rails that run from the yard into the harbour water.

locations.name: Whale Island Chapel
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 1-4 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small whitewashed chapel on the hill above the town, with a graveyard full of fishermen and their wives. Its bell rings for services, for funerals and for boats overdue in a storm.

areas.name: Chapel Bell Rope
areas.text: The rope that hangs in the porch, worn smooth by the hands that ring for the boats.

areas.name: Chapel Sailors' Graveyard
areas.text: Rows of headstones on the slope, many carved with a boat and no body beneath.

locations.name: Whale Island Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 1-4 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A converted cottage with a nurse in residence and a doctor who comes from the mainland every few weeks. Hooks in hands, rope burns and broken fingers are her daily work; anything worse goes out on the next boat, if there is one.

areas.name: Clinic Radio Corner
areas.text: The corner where the nurse talks the mainland doctor through what she sees.

areas.name: Clinic Treatment Room
areas.text: A clean room with a high bed, a lamp and a tray of instruments.

locations.name: Whale Island Constable's Post
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The island's one policeman lives and works in this cottage, with one cell that is mostly used for drunk visiting crewmen to sleep it off. He knows every islander by name and solves most trouble by talking to someone's mother.

areas.name: Constable's Cell
areas.text: A whitewashed cell with a cot and a bucket, its door rarely locked.

areas.name: Constable's Desk
areas.text: A desk under the blue lamp with a telephone, a typewriter and one open file.

locations.name: Whale Island Drying Racks
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Rows of wooden racks on the slope above the south shore where squid and small fish are hung to dry in the wind. Somebody has to stand guard with a stick, and the job goes to whoever is least busy.

areas.name: Drying Racks Gull Post
areas.text: A post at the top of the slope where the guard sits with a stick and a whistle.

areas.name: Drying Racks Squid Lines
areas.text: Lines strung between the racks, hung with pale squid.

locations.name: Whale Island Fish Market
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The covered market on the quay where the boats sell the morning catch. It is noisy before dawn and empty by noon, and everyone in it has a story about the swamp fish.

areas.name: Fish Stalls
areas.text: The long stone counters of the catch, with the scales and the ice.

areas.name: Net Loft
areas.text: The loft above the market where the nets are mended.

locations.name: Whale Island Fishing Grounds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low]

The sea east of the island where the boats go for the catch, out of sight of the town on a hazy day. Each family has its marks, lined up by the lighthouse and a ridge top, and nobody fishes another family's mark.

areas.name: Fishing Grounds Family Marks
areas.text: The fishing spots each family lines up by landmarks on the shore.

areas.name: Fishing Grounds Shoal Water
areas.text: Water boiling with a shoal, with the gulls diving.

locations.name: Whale Island Fuel Dock
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A floating pontoon off the end of the quay with a single diesel pump. Every boat on the island fills here, and the tanker that refills the tank comes twice a year if the sea allows.

areas.name: Fuel Dock Drum Store
areas.text: Steel drums under a tarp, lashed to rings in the quay.

areas.name: Fuel Dock Pump
areas.text: The pump on its pontoon, with a hose long enough to reach the outer berths.

locations.name: Whale Island Generator House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The diesel generators that light the town, the clinic and the ice house sit in a concrete block below the slope. Power is cut at midnight to save fuel, and the whole island knows to have its candles ready.

areas.name: Generator Engine Hall
areas.text: The loud hall of the two engines, oil on the floor and ear muffs on a nail.

areas.name: Generator Switch Panel
areas.text: A wall of switches and dials that sends power to each part of the town.

locations.name: Whale Island Goat Commons
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

Open grazing on the lower slopes of the western ridge, shared by every family that keeps a goat. The goats go where they like and come down for milking when they choose, and the boys of the island have spent whole days fetching them back.

areas.name: Goat Commons Rock Slope
areas.text: Steep rock and thin grass where the goats climb and people slip.

areas.name: Goat Commons Shelter
areas.text: A roofless stone pen where the goats are milked and kidded.

locations.name: Whale Island Harbourmaster's Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A white hut at the root of the quay with a marine radio, a barometer and the tide tables. The harbourmaster logs every boat out and back, sells passage on the mainland ship and rings the bell when the weather turns.

areas.name: Harbourmaster's Radio Desk
areas.text: A desk with the marine set, its handset hung on a hook.

areas.name: Harbourmaster's Ticket Window
areas.text: A hatch in the wall where passage is bought and the ship's times posted.

locations.name: Whale Island Ice House
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A squat concrete building by the quay where a compressor makes ice for the boats and the market. Its cold room keeps the island's catch fresh until the mainland buyer's boat comes, and the whole town stores its meat here in summer.

areas.name: Ice House Chute
areas.text: The chute that pours crushed ice straight into a boat's hold.

areas.name: Ice House Cold Room
areas.text: A cold, dim room of stacked fish boxes and hanging carcasses.

locations.name: Whale Island Lighthouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A small white lighthouse on the headland beside the harbour, kept lit for the boats coming in at night. From the lamp room the keeper can see every sail for miles.

areas.name: Headland Path
areas.text: The path along the headland from the harbour to the tower.

areas.name: Lamp Room
areas.text: The glass room at the top with the great lamp and its lens.

locations.name: Whale Island Net Works
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A long open shed on the town's western edge where nets are made new, tarred and hung to dry. Older women of the island sit here through the afternoons knotting mesh faster than you can follow and talking about everybody.

areas.name: Net Works Knotting Benches
areas.text: Benches along the shed wall where the mesh is knotted by hand.

areas.name: Net Works Tar Vat
areas.text: A blackened vat outside where finished nets are dipped against rot.

locations.name: Whale Island North Cove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A small cove on the island's north side, hidden from the town by the forest, where the storms pile up driftwood and whatever the sea has carried from the shipping lanes. The islanders come here to gather firewood and see what has washed in.

areas.name: North Cove Driftwood Line
areas.text: The heaped wrack of logs and wreckage along the top of the beach.

areas.name: North Cove Shallows
areas.text: The cold, clear shallows where the sand drops away suddenly.

locations.name: Whale Island Orchard
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A walled orchard on the sheltered side of the ridges where the island grows apples and plums. In autumn every family comes to pick, and the cider press runs for a week.

areas.name: Orchard Cider Press
areas.text: A wooden screw press under a lean-to, sticky with old juice.

areas.name: Orchard Wall Gap
areas.text: A gap in the orchard wall where the goats get in and the children climb out.

locations.name: Whale Island Outer Mole
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The breakwater on the harbour's seaward side, where boats from other ports tie up when they shelter from weather or put in for water. Their crews come ashore for a night, spend at the tavern and teach the local boys tricks nobody's mother approves of.

areas.name: Outer Mole Beacon
areas.text: The green light on a post at the breakwater's end.

areas.name: Outer Mole Berths
areas.text: The inner face of the breakwater, lined with bollards and the hulls of strangers.

locations.name: Whale Island Post Office
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

One room behind a blue door that is the post office, the telephone exchange and the place to pick up anything the mail boat brings. Postcards from far countries get pinned to the wall for a day before they go to whoever they are for, so the whole island can see them.

areas.name: Post Office Postcard Wall
areas.text: The wall by the door where cards from abroad are pinned for a day.

areas.name: Post Office Switchboard
areas.text: A wooden board of jacks and cords, with a stool and a headset.

locations.name: Whale Island Quarry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

An old quarry on the southwest slope where the stone for the quay, the chapel and the terrace walls was cut. Nobody works it now; rain has filled the bottom, and the young deckhands are forbidden to swim there and do anyway.

areas.name: Quarry Flooded Pit
areas.text: A deep, cold pool in the quarry floor, green and still.

areas.name: Quarry Rock Face
areas.text: The sheer cut wall, streaked with rust and seeping water.

locations.name: Whale Island Reef Wreck
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low]

The hull of a small cargo ship that ran onto the reef off the south-east coast years ago. The bow sticks up rusted and broken at low tide, and the fish that live in the hull make it the best fishing ground near shore.

areas.name: Reef Wreck Bow
areas.text: The rusted bow above water, where a person can stand and cast.

areas.name: Reef Wreck Flooded Hold
areas.text: The flooded cargo hold, full of fish and dim green light.

locations.name: Whale Island Rock Pools
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A stretch of rocky shore below the town where the tide leaves pools full of crabs, weed and small fish. Children fish here before they are allowed in boats.

areas.name: Tide Pools
areas.text: The pools among the rocks, clear and cold.

areas.name: Weed Shelf
areas.text: The flat shelf of rock covered with weed at the water's edge.

locations.name: Whale Island Sand Cove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A short sandy beach on the south shore, the only one on the island, where the rowing boats are pulled up and the few children learn to swim. On summer evenings the islanders light a fire here and cook whatever came in that day.

areas.name: Sand Cove Boat Line
areas.text: Rowing boats pulled above the tide on wooden rollers.

areas.name: Sand Cove Fire Ring
areas.text: A circle of blackened stones on the sand where summer fires are lit.

locations.name: Whale Island Schoolhouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A one-room school built when the island had thirty children. Now there are two, both taught at home, and the schoolroom doubles as the island's meeting hall, the polling station and the place the films are shown when the projector works.

areas.name: Schoolhouse Classroom
areas.text: Rows of old desks, two of them worn and the rest dusty, under a big world map.

areas.name: Schoolhouse Projector Booth
areas.text: A cupboard at the back with an old film projector and a stack of reels.

locations.name: Whale Island Sea Caves
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low]

A run of caves cut into the island's western cliffs, reachable by boat in calm weather or by a goat path at low tide. The sea fills the lower ones with noise; the higher ones are dry and have been used for things over the years that nobody wants to discuss.

areas.name: Sea Caves Booming Chamber
areas.text: A low cave the sea rushes into and out of with a sound like a gun.

areas.name: Sea Caves Dry Shelf
areas.text: A higher dry ledge at the back of the largest cave, with an old crate.

locations.name: Whale Island Seacliff
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A headland of short turf that ends in a drop to the sea, with a view along the coast to the lighthouse and the harbour. The island's two children walk up here to look at the ships, and the wind up top can knock a grown man off his feet.

areas.name: Seacliff Coast View
areas.text: A flat stone where you sit to see the coastline run away to the east.

areas.name: Seacliff Precipice
areas.text: The last yard of turf before the drop, with the surf far below.

locations.name: Whale Island Smokehouse
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A tarred shed below the town where the small fish the mainland buyers will not take are split, salted and smoked over beech. Smoked fish keeps through the winter storms, when the boats cannot go out for weeks.

areas.name: Smokehouse Hanging Rods
areas.text: Rows of rods under the roof, hung with split, gold-brown fish.

areas.name: Smokehouse Salting Trough
areas.text: A long wooden trough of brine where the fish soak before they go up.

locations.name: Whale Island Spring Cistern
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A walled spring at the foot of the western ridge feeds a stone tank, and a pipe carries the water down to the town's taps. In a dry summer the tank is the first thing the whole island watches.

areas.name: Spring Cistern Fern Head
areas.text: The spring itself, rising among ferns into a little stone basin.

areas.name: Spring Cistern Tank
areas.text: A covered stone tank, its lid heavy, a ladder inside.

locations.name: Whale Island Swamp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A marsh in the island's interior, where small odd creatures live in the mud and the reeds and the water is darker than it should be. It was the home of the Master of the Swamp, a whale-sized fish with a mouth of teeth and rows of thin legs, which five fishermen pulling together could not land.

areas.name: Black Water
areas.text: The deep pool at the marsh's heart where the great fish lived.

areas.name: Fishing Tree
areas.text: The high branch over the water where a patient angler can sit for days.

locations.name: Whale Island Terrace Gardens
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

Terraces of stony earth stepped up the hill behind the upper town, where each family keeps a plot of vegetables. The walls were built by hand, stone by stone, generations back, and still hold.

areas.name: Terrace Gardens Scarecrow Plot
areas.text: A top plot of onions guarded by a scarecrow in an old oilskin.

areas.name: Terrace Gardens Stone Steps
areas.text: Steep steps cut into the terrace walls from plot to plot.

locations.name: Whale Island Weighing Square
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The open square where the quay meets the town, with a big hanging scale for anything too heavy for the market counters. When Gon dragged the Master of the Swamp in from the marsh, half the island crowded in here to stare at it before Mito would even look at his application.

areas.name: Record Catch Board
areas.text: A painted board under a little tin roof, chalked with the island's biggest fish.

areas.name: Weighing Square Gantry
areas.text: The iron frame and hook of the big scale, rust-red, with a block and tackle.

locations.name: Whale's Back Headland
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-4 · Danger: Low]

A long humped headland on the island's north-east corner, shaped like a whale lying in the water. A blowhole in its back throws up a spout in heavy seas, and the older islanders say that is how the island got its name.

areas.name: Whale's Back Blowhole
areas.text: A hole in the rock where the sea booms and then shoots up as spray.

areas.name: Whale's Back Ridge
areas.text: The humped spine of the headland, bare rock and thrift.

locations.name: Wig & Pen
locations.info:
