[Town Core · Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A shop in Antokiba with posters all over its window.

areas.name: Wig & Pen Counter
areas.text: The counter behind the posters.

locations.name: Wild Hive Gully
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

A fern-choked gully on the old path from the northern woods toward the border, with a wild hive humming in a fallen log.

areas.name: Wild Hive Fallen Log
areas.text: A rotten log on the bank, humming with wild bees.

areas.name: Wild Hive Fern Bottom
areas.text: The gully floor, thick with ferns as high as a man's chest.

locations.name: Wine Spring Dell
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-22 · Danger: High]

A hidden dell where a clear spring fills a mossy pool. Visitors leave jugs on the stones around it, and the air smells faintly of wine.

areas.name: Wine Spring Jug Stones
areas.text: Flat stones round the pool, set with jugs and cups.

areas.name: Wine Spring Pool
areas.text: The mossy pool where the spring rises.

locations.name: Wing's Lodging
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 4-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small rented room in the arena's town where Wing, a teacher of the Shingen-ryu school, lives while his pupil Zushi fights. He serves tea and does not like to be lied to.

areas.name: Wing's Room
areas.text: The room with its table, its tea and its stack of books.

locations.name: Wire Burners' Hollow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-26 · Danger: High]

A hollow where cable is burned to strip off its coating and leave the copper behind. The smoke is poison and the burners wrap their faces twice.

areas.name: Burners' Copper Scales
areas.text: A beam scale under a sheet of tin, where bundles are weighed for the Assembly's share.

areas.name: Burners' Fire Rings
areas.text: Rings of stones where coils of wire burn down to bare copper.

locations.name: World Tree
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-10 · Danger: Low]

The only sapling of its kind in the known world, a tree 1,784 metres tall whose top stands above the clouds. Climbers sign a waiver at the gate; lifts and stairs carry them to the 500-metre point, and above that they climb with their own hands. Few reach the top.

areas.name: 500-Metre Platform
areas.text: The platform where the lifts stop and the bare climb begins.

areas.name: Crown Nest
areas.text: The top of the tree, a great nest above the clouds.

areas.name: Tree Gate
areas.text: The gate and booth at the foot where climbers pay, sign and get their warnings.

locations.name: World Tree Rescue Station
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-10 · Danger: Low]

The rescue station at the foot of the World Tree, its helicopter on a pad and its crews on call around the clock. Every climber who passes the 500-metre point wears one of its wristbands; when a wristband calls, a crew goes.

areas.name: Rescue Station Helipad
areas.text: A concrete pad with a red helicopter and a windsock straining.

areas.name: Rescue Station Signal Room
areas.text: A room of receivers and a board lit with the position of every wristband on the tree.

locations.name: Wrecked Car Valley
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-28 · Danger: Severe]

A hollow where whole cars are dumped, stacked and stripped down to the frame. Families live in some of the better ones.

areas.name: Car Valley Parts Pit
areas.text: A pit where engines, doors and wheels are sorted for the market.

areas.name: Car Valley Stacks
areas.text: Cars piled four high, with ladders between them and washing on the bonnets.

locations.name: Xi-Yu Shipping Office
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-32 · Danger: Severe]

A shipping agent's office above a ship's chandler near the old docks. It books passages, fills crews and finds berths for anyone who can pay, without asking the questions other agents ask.

areas.name: Xi-Yu Back Gate
areas.text: A gate from the yard straight onto the water, with a launch tied up beside it.

areas.name: Xi-Yu Manifest Room
areas.text: A back office with filing cabinets and a typewriter that never stops.

locations.name: Yaoshan Farmlands
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-34 · Danger: Severe]

The flat rice country of the interior, worked by collectives that answer to quotas from Peijin. A single bus comes down the dirt road twice a day, and anyone on foot is noticed.

areas.name: Yaoshan Collective Barns
areas.text: Long barns of the collective, one of them flooded on purpose.

areas.name: Yaoshan Paddies
areas.text: Flooded fields of rice with narrow dykes between them.

locations.name: YNB Broadcasting Tower
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The city's main television station, its mast the second-tallest thing on the skyline. Its news channel runs the auction results all September and anything with blood in it all year.

areas.name: YNB Mast Platform
areas.text: A maintenance platform halfway up the mast.

areas.name: YNB Newsroom
areas.text: An open floor of desks, monitors and a glass studio.

locations.name: Yorim Pine Ridges
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-38 · Danger: Deadly]

Forested ridges in the north of the country, dark with pine and cut by logging tracks. A fire lookout stands on the highest ridge, and hunters go after deer and boar in the valleys with old rifles.

areas.name: Pine Ridges Fire Lookout
areas.text: A wooden tower on the highest ridge with a view across the province.

areas.name: Pine Ridges Logging Track
areas.text: A rutted track up through the pines, littered with bark.

locations.name: Yorknew City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-28 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A sprawling metropolis in the United States of Saherta, famous for its auctions. From the first to the tenth of September thousands of licensed auction houses sell the rarest things on earth, black markets sell what the law forbids, and the money that changes hands in those ten days is beyond counting. A thing bought cheap one day can sell for a fortune the next.

areas.name: Auction Avenue
areas.text: The avenue of auction houses with banners hung between the street lamps.

areas.name: Downtown Crossing
areas.text: The crowded crossing of the downtown streets, where the giant screens show the news.

areas.name: Yorknew Central Station
areas.text:
The great station and its airship terminal on the roof, where every line in the country ends.

The airship, rail and sea lines serves this yard: coaches run to Lingon Airport (about 500 Jenny), Battera's Castle (about 2000 Jenny), Heavens Arena (about 25000 Jenny), Kakin Empire (about 60000 Jenny); ferries sail to Dolle Harbor (about 20000 Jenny), Doli City (about 20000 Jenny); ask at the yard or the pier, pay the fare, and the days of the road pass.

locations.name: Yorknew City Hall
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-22 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The seat of the mayor and the city council, a domed hall of grey stone on a plaza of fountains. Auction houses come here for their season licences, hawkers for their street permits, and reporters for the mayor's promises that the city is the safest place on the continent to spend a fortune.

areas.name: City Hall Permit Counter
areas.text: A row of glass windows where clerks sell auction and street-trading licences.

areas.name: City Hall Rotunda
areas.text: The marble rotunda under the dome, where petitioners wait on long benches.

areas.name: Mayor Jitonoda's Office
areas.text: A panelled corner office with a view of the plaza and a telephone that rings after hours.

locations.name: Yorknew Coach Terminal
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The long-distance coach terminal beside the freight yard, where the cheap coaches leave for every city on the continent. Students sleep on their rucksacks in the waiting hall, and the pickpockets know which ones are really asleep.

areas.name: Coach Terminal Bays
areas.text: Twenty numbered bays under a concrete canopy.

areas.name: Coach Terminal Waiting Hall
areas.text: A hall of plastic seats, a snack kiosk and a ticket window.

locations.name: Yorknew Freight Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: High]

The rail freight yard on the city's west side, where the trains from every coast are broken up and made up again. Containers stack three high and the cranes run all night in August, when the auction goods arrive.

areas.name: Freight Yard Crane Deck
areas.text: The cab and gantry of the big container crane.

areas.name: Freight Yard Foreman's Hut
areas.text: A tin hut of books and a kerosene heater.

areas.name: Freight Yard Sidings
areas.text: Rows of tracks and parked boxcars under floodlights.

locations.name: Yorknew Metropolitan Hospital
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 10-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The city's largest hospital, a white tower with an emergency ramp that is never empty in auction season. Its private floor takes rich patients and their guards without asking why they need guards.

areas.name: Metropolitan Emergency Ramp
areas.text: The ramp where ambulances unload under bright lights.

areas.name: Metropolitan Private Floor
areas.text: A carpeted floor of single rooms with guards' chairs outside the doors.

areas.name: Metropolitan Roof Helipad
areas.text: The helipad on the roof with its wind sock.

locations.name: Yorknew Metropolitan University
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The city's university, a campus of brick halls and lawns on the north side with a medical school, a law faculty and a library tower that stays lit until midnight. Its students cram under its trees in spring and in its cafés in winter.

areas.name: University Anatomy Theatre
areas.text: A steep lecture theatre round an anatomy table.

areas.name: University Library Tower
areas.text: A tower of stacks and reading desks with green lamps.

locations.name: Yorknew Police Headquarters
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

The headquarters of the city police, a squat block with a motor pool behind it and a holding wing below. In auction season half its officers are out on traffic duty, closing avenues and waving limousines through.

areas.name: Chief's Map Room
areas.text: An office with a city map pinned across one wall, roads marked in grease pencil.

areas.name: Police HQ Holding Wing
areas.text: Cells below the street, lit by caged bulbs.

areas.name: Police HQ Motor Pool
areas.text: A yard of patrol cars and stacked steel barriers behind the station.

locations.name: Yorknew Stadium
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A stadium for sixty thousand on the north side, home to the city's football club and to every touring band big enough to fill it. On match days the trains run packed and the bars around it open at breakfast.

areas.name: Stadium Concourse
areas.text: A curved concourse of food counters, programme stalls and bookmakers.

areas.name: Stadium Stands
areas.text: Steep tiers of seats around the pitch.

locations.name: Yorknew Stock Exchange
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The exchange where the continent's shares are traded, a columned hall of shouting brokers and flickering boards. In September the auction money passes through it twice: once on the way in, once on the way out.

areas.name: Exchange Trading Floor
areas.text: The pit under the boards, packed with brokers.

areas.name: Exchange Visitors' Gallery
areas.text: A gallery above the floor where the public can watch.

locations.name: Zaban Central Station
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The city's main railway station, a vaulted hall of glass and iron with lines to the coast and the inland cities. Commuters stream through it in their thousands, and in January it fills with applicants who got off at the wrong stop.

areas.name: Central Station Concourse
areas.text: The great hall under the glass roof, with the departures board and the crowds.

areas.name: Central Station Lost Property
areas.text: A counter and shelves of umbrellas, cases and things nobody came back for.

areas.name: Central Station Lower Concourse
areas.text: A lower level of left-luggage lockers and kiosks.

locations.name: Zaban City
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-10 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A prosperous city of busy streets, shady dealers and scam artists, famous for grilled panda frog on a stick and infamous as the home of Johness the Dissector, who killed a hundred and forty-six people with his bare hands. The exam's preliminary site is somewhere in its back streets, and nobody will say where.

areas.name: Back Lanes
areas.text: The narrow lanes behind the main street where the deals and the scams are made.

areas.name: Frog Stalls
areas.text: The row of grills where the city's panda frogs turn on sticks.

areas.name: Zaban Main Street
areas.text: The broad street of stalls, hawkers and pickpockets that every visitor walks first.

locations.name: Zaban City Police Headquarters
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The headquarters of the city police, a grey block with a yard of patrol cars and a lobby wall of wanted faces. In a city famous for its swindlers it is busy at every hour, and its detectives are tired men.

areas.name: Police Detectives' Room
areas.text: Desks pushed together, ashtrays and filing cabinets, a board of open cases.

areas.name: Police Front Desk
areas.text: A long counter with a duty sergeant and a queue of robbed tourists.

areas.name: Police Holding Cells
areas.text: A corridor of holding cells below the building.

locations.name: Zaban Free Clinic
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 1-6 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A charity clinic in a former shoe shop, run by a retired surgeon and two nurses, treating whoever walks in. In January the waiting room fills with applicants nursing the wounds of the road and the city.

areas.name: Free Clinic Treatment Room
areas.text: A single room with a couch, a lamp and a steel tray of instruments.

areas.name: Free Clinic Waiting Room
areas.text: Rows of plastic chairs, a water cooler and a noticeboard of free services.

locations.name: Zaban Technical High School
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-5 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A secondary school on the city's north side that teaches engineering trades alongside the usual lessons, its yard full of students in blue uniforms. The older boys talk about the Hunter Exam as if they could walk in and pass it.

areas.name: Technical School Running Track
areas.text: A cinder track round a football pitch, used for detention laps.

areas.name: Technical School Workshop
areas.text: A long workshop of lathes, drills and a smell of machine oil.

locations.name: Zaban Waterworks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-9 · Danger: Low]

The old pumping station and reservoir that keep the city's taps running, a brick hall of iron engines and a maze of mains beneath the streets. Maintenance crews go down in pairs and come up complaining of the depth.

areas.name: Waterworks Engine Hall
areas.text: A brick hall of great iron pumps, polished and thumping.

areas.name: Waterworks Mains
areas.text: The tunnels of water mains under the city, damp and echoing.

areas.name: Waterworks Sealed Door
areas.text: An iron door far below the lowest main, rusted shut.

locations.name: Zazan's Palace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-34 · Danger: Severe]

A palace-like building in Meteor City, grander than anything around it.

areas.name: Web Halls
areas.text: The halls hung with webs.

areas.name: Zazan's Throne Room
areas.text: The throne room at the palace's heart.

locations.name: Zebro's Cabin
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-20 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A small cabin near the Testing Gate where the gatekeeper lives. Everything in it is heavy on purpose: the chairs, the cups, the doors.

areas.name: Heavy Kitchen
areas.text: The kitchen where even a teacup weighs more than it should.

areas.name: Training Yard
areas.text: The yard behind the cabin, where visitors train with weights.

locations.name: Zepile's Workroom
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: High]

Two rented rooms over a frame shop, where an antiques trader with heavy eyebrows keeps his stock, his books on glazes and his opinions. He appraises for anyone who asks politely and charges people who do not.

areas.name: Zepile's Glazing Bench
areas.text: A bench of brushes, pigments and a small electric kiln.

areas.name: Zepile's Shelves
areas.text: Floor-to-ceiling shelves of pots and boxes, each tagged in a small neat hand.

locations.name: Zevil Butterfly Glade
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

A clearing of wild flowers in the island's forest where the crimson butterflies gather in clouds. When they leave all at once, they are flying toward blood.

areas.name: Glade Flower Bed
areas.text: The bed of low flowers where the butterflies rest.

areas.name: Glade Trickle
areas.text: A thin spring at the glade's edge that keeps the flowers wet.

locations.name: Zevil Crossing Launch
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-12 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

The boat that carries applicants from the foot of Trick Tower to Zevil Island, about two hours each way. Its loudspeaker can be heard across most of the island's shore.

areas.name: Launch Deck
areas.text: The open deck with its benches, where the applicants eye one another on the way over.

areas.name: Launch Wheelhouse
areas.text: The cabin with the wheel and the loudspeaker microphone.

locations.name: Zevil Grasslands
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Fields of grass taller than a man on Zevil Island, where a stalker can move without being seen and so can whatever lives in it.

areas.name: Dead Tree Mound
areas.text: A mound with one dead tree, the only high point in the fields.

areas.name: High Grass
areas.text: The tall grass itself, a sea of stalks.

locations.name: Zevil Hollow Oak
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-12 · Danger: Moderate]

An ancient oak on Zevil Island whose trunk has rotted out into a dry hollow. It is the best shelter in that part of the woods and the first place a searcher looks.

areas.name: Hollow Oak Crown
areas.text: The high branches, with a view across the island's middle.

areas.name: Hollow Oak Shelter
areas.text: The dry hollow inside the trunk, out of the wind.

locations.name: Zevil Island
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A remote island two hours by boat from Trick Tower, narrow at its middle where an isthmus joins two halves, with dense forest, fields of tall grass and crimson butterflies drawn to blood. Applicants spend a week here hunting one another's badges.

areas.name: Zevil Isthmus
areas.text: The narrow neck of land between the island's two halves.

areas.name: Zevil Landing Site
areas.text: The beach where the boat drops applicants and collects them a week later.

locations.name: Zevil Observers' Blind
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 6-14 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A hide built into a tree on Zevil Island, roofed with leaves and branches so it vanishes from the ground. It is not for applicants.

areas.name: Blind Platform
areas.text: The platform inside the hide with its radio and binoculars.

areas.name: Blind Rope Ladder
areas.text: The rope ladder that is pulled up behind whoever is inside.

locations.name: Zevil Shore Caves
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

Caves in the rocks along Zevil Island's shore, dry above the tide and good for an applicant who wants to sleep without being found.

areas.name: Dry Chamber
areas.text: The back of the cave, dry and dark.

areas.name: Tide Mouth
areas.text: The cave mouth over the narrow beach.

locations.name: Zevil Strait Lighthouse
locations.info:
[Safe Haven · Recommended Level: 5-10 · No hostile spawns · Downtime protected]

A lighthouse on a rock in the strait between the mainland and Zevil Island, kept by a family who live in its cottage.

areas.name: Lighthouse Keeper's Cottage
areas.text: The cottage at the base where the keeper's family live.

areas.name: Lighthouse Lamp Room
areas.text: The lamp room at the top, with its lens and a view of the island.

locations.name: Zevil Woods
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The dense forest on Zevil Island, where applicants hide, wait and stalk. The birds that skim the stream for fish are faster than most of the hunters.

areas.name: Fisher Stream
areas.text: The stream where the fish-hunting birds dive.

areas.name: Watch Tree
areas.text: A tall tree with a view of a clearing.

locations.name: Zoldyck Kennels
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-24 · Danger: High]

Mike's kennel, behind a stand of giant trees: a pen, a run and a meat store for the family's guard hound, who learns every stranger's face and scent and obeys nobody outside the family.

areas.name: Kennels Feeding Pens
areas.text: The great pen and its run, with a trough and a drain in the floor.

areas.name: Kennels Keepers' Shed
areas.text: The shed where the meat is cut and the rules are pinned to the wall.

locations.name: Zoldyck Mansion
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-30 · Danger: Severe]

The family's house high on Kukuroo Mountain, said to stand at the peak. Few people from outside the family have seen it, and fewer have left it. Silva, Kikyo, Zeno, Maha and the children live here.

areas.name: Japanese Room
areas.text: The family's sitting room of mats and paper screens, used for leisure.

areas.name: Mansion Halls
areas.text: The dim corridors and stairs that link the rooms.

locations.name: Zoldyck Proving Ground
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: Severe]

A clearing high on the mountain where the family's children are tested against each other and against things the family keeps for the purpose. The ground has been torn up and smoothed so many times it no longer grows grass.

areas.name: Proving Ground Rope Cliff
areas.text: A rock face scored by ropes and fingernails.

areas.name: Proving Ground Wired Posts
areas.text: A ring of posts strung with live cable that hums in damp weather.

factions.name: Amateur Hunters
factions.info: Six young people with no licence and no money who hunt, track and catalogue living things under a professional Hunter named Kite: Spinner Clow, Stick Dinner, Banana Kavaro, Lin Koshi, Monta Yuras and Podungo Lapoy. Kite was the first adult who listened to them, and he bought Spin and Stick a house so they could protect the small-billed swans nesting there. The Kakin Empire has hired the crew for a long biological survey of new species. A stranger meets them as campers with notebooks and good food; one who joins carries packs and learns to watch before touching.

factions.name: Battera's players
factions.info: The Hunters and adventurers hired by Battera, an old billionaire who has bought up every copy of the game Greed Island he can find and keeps the consoles in the basement of his castle. Since 1988 he has offered a famous reward to anyone who clears the game, and he uses his money to keep its details out of the press. Tsezguerra, a Jackpot Hunter, runs his tryouts and turns away nearly everyone. Of the more than a hundred Hunters he has sent in, few have come back. A stranger meets the company as an advertisement or a test in a hotel ballroom; one who joins signs a contract and is sent into the game.

factions.name: Cha-R Family
factions.info: One of the three great Mafia families of Kakin, led by Brocco Li, the king's half-brother, who rides as a guest on the first tier. About two hundred and fifty of its men are aboard the Black Whale, where they control the fifth tier and everything sold on it; their patron is the seventh prince, Luzurus. Ken'i Wang is the underboss. The family thanks the Phantom Troupe for Yorknew, which handed Kakin's families the new continent, and would still rather the Spiders left its deck. A stranger meets the Cha-R as the people who sell bread and beds on the bottom tier.

factions.name: Dark Continent Expedition Team
factions.info: The expedition announced on 10 August 2000 by Beyond Netero, son of the late chairman, under the patronage of Kakin's king: a voyage to the Dark Continent in open defiance of the treaty. Its members are about twenty-five Temp Hunters and the mercenaries of Stone Wall, a legendary unit of eleven that came out of the Lubo Civil War without a single loss; Muherr commands in the field. Beyond surrendered to the Zodiacs on the day of the announcement and sails under their guard. A stranger meets the team as men in uniform on the Black Whale and a face on every news channel.

factions.name: East Gorteau regime
factions.info: The dictatorship that rules the Republic of East Gorteau from Peijin, the capital, and from a palace in the wilderness outside it. Every power of state belongs to the Supreme Leader, Ming Jol-ik, born of a bloody revolt that made a new ruling class rich while most people stayed poor. Foreign aid goes on luxuries and weapons; rumour says the country cut every tie abroad to squeeze more aid, and that some of it pays for nuclear arms. A spy-catching system of informant groups rewards neighbours who report neighbours. A stranger meets the regime as a closed border and a portrait on every wall; one who serves it climbs by points earned informing.

factions.name: Floor Masters
factions.info: The twenty-one highest ranked fighters of Heavens Arena, each given a whole floor of the tower between the 230th and the 250th. To challenge one, a fighter on the 200th floor must win ten matches before losing four, and a master who loses the challenge loses the floor. Every second year the masters fight in Battle Olympia for the penthouse on the 251st. Crowds pay to see these bouts and swear the fighters up there use some trick that throws men across the ring without a touch. A stranger meets them as a name on a poster; one who joins climbs the tower match by match.

factions.name: Freelance Assassins
factions.info: Professional killers the Mafia hires for a single job when its own soldiers will not do. They meet in a hotel room, hear who the target is and how much the Dons will pay, and argue over whether to work together or alone; most work alone. None of them gives a real name. A stranger meets them as quiet men in good coats who leave town before the bodies are found.

factions.name: Have-Nots
factions.info: The lowest caste of the Kakin Empire, barred by an unchangeable caste law from public office and military rank. In ancient Kakin, princes who failed to become king were buried with afterlife companions to stop them turning into vengeful ghosts, and the companions were always chosen from the Have-Nots. The custom ended; the caste did not. Camilla, the second prince, has opened her private army to them, built them a ward on her land and given them a soldier's rights, and they now ask of their own accord to be her companions in death. A stranger meets them as servants who will not meet the eye.

factions.name: Heil-Ly Family
factions.info: The smallest and strangest of Kakin's three great Mafia families, led by Morena Prudo, the king's illegitimate daughter, who came up from a junior member to take the family in a coup. On the Black Whale the family is based on the third tier and earns its money by brokering secret deals with the upper decks; its patron is the fourth prince, Tserriednich. Its members are few, about twenty, and unusually loyal to their boss. A stranger meets them as polite young people who know a surprising amount about everyone.

factions.name: Hui Guo Rou royal house
factions.info: The ruling house of the Kakin Empire, a nation of over a billion people on the Azian Continent. Its king, Nasubi Hui Guo Rou, has eight queens and fourteen children, every one called a prince whatever their sex. Thirty years ago the country passed from empire to parliament in what is called the most silent revolution in history, and the economy has grown fast since. In 2000 the king announces that Kakin will lead a great voyage to the Dark Continent, open to all comers, on the Black Whale, and the whole royal family sails with it. A stranger meets the house as a parade, a portrait or a guard who says no.

factions.name: Hunter Association
factions.info: The body that tests and licenses Hunters, answerable to no single government. A licence is earned once, through the yearly Hunter Exam, and is never revoked and never reissued: it opens almost every border and public facility, lets its holder into restricted grounds and records, and is worth a fortune to collectors, so a careless Hunter loses it fast. Licensed Hunters chase rare beasts, lost ruins, treasures, criminals and cures, alone or for a client, and the Association ranks the best of them by stars. Its headquarters stands in Swardani City and its airships carry its people and cargo. A stranger meets it as a card shown at a gate; one who joins passes the exam and climbs by the work done.

factions.name: Hunter Exam Commission
factions.info: The people who run the Hunter Exam each year. Applications close on 31 December and the exam opens on 7 January at a site kept secret until the last day; only a candidate who finds the way, often through a navigator who tests them first, reaches it. Candidates wear numbered badges, the phases change every year and anyone may try as often as they live, but deaths and maimings are common and nobody is told how the scoring works. Examiners are elite Hunters who work unpaid; attacking one ends a candidate's year. A stranger meets the commission as a test they did not see coming.

factions.name: International Permit Agencies
factions.info: The agencies, working directly under the five great nations, that study travel risk everywhere, give each country a safety index and decide who may go to the Dark Continent. An applicant writes to the foreign minister of each of the five nations, waits half a year while the Restricted Voyage Agencies finish their contracts and briefings, then needs letters from three members of their own congress just to meet a section chief. Even then the answer is nearly always no. Steiner, the deputy secretary, is a careful, overworked official. A stranger meets the agencies as forms.

factions.name: Kakin Military
factions.info: The armed forces of the Kakin Empire, also called the Royal Army. Its officers come from the Royal Military Academy, which takes students young, and its soldiers wear pale combat gear whose headgear shows their rank: corporals in black round helmets, privates second class in berets. Benjamin, the first prince, holds the post of deputy military adviser. On the Black Whale the army enforces martial law from the army office on the third tier, with about two thousand guards and soldiers among two hundred thousand passengers. A stranger meets it as a checkpoint and a request for papers.

factions.name: Kazsule's Alliance
factions.info: Fifteen of the strongest card collectors in Greed Island, called together by a player named Kazsule when word spread that one group was only a few cards from clearing the game. Each had at least fifty specified cards, and each came to trade what they knew so that no one else would take the prize. Their first target is the card held by pirates in Soufrabi, where only fifteen players arriving together can even learn where it is kept. A stranger meets them as a council of rivals who distrust each other; one who joins proves what they can add.

factions.name: Mafia Community
factions.info: The crime syndicates, families and lone operators spread all over the world, ruled from the top by the Ten Dons with families ranked beneath them and lesser families beneath those. Their trade is commodity control, human trafficking, black market goods and smuggling, though some families keep their books clean. In Yorknew City they paid most of mayor Jitonoda's campaign, so the police close streets for them during the September auctions. Murder is a way of doing business, not the business itself. A stranger meets the Mafia as a man in a suit asking which family they belong to; one who joins starts as a soldier and rises by loyalty and profit.

factions.name: Meteor City Assembly
factions.info: The elders who rule Meteor City, a junkyard city of outcasts that appears in no official record and whose people are nowhere on paper. Residents wrap their bodies and faces in thick clothes, kneel at their churches for the dead and share a bond they call thinner than water and thicker than blood. The city takes whatever the world throws away, and the Mafia invests in it for a ready supply of killers who leave no trace. When the city is wronged it answers with suicide bombers walking into the offender's streets. A stranger meets the Assembly as silent figures in hoods who are already watching.

factions.name: Ministry of Justice
factions.info: The legal arm of the Kakin Empire, independent of the army and with its own uniformed officers. On the Black Whale its Justice Bureau occupies a five-storey building on the second tier and its Supreme Court sits on the first, under the Supreme Magistrate Cleapatro. Kaiser, the deputy chief prosecutor, calls the bureau the most neutral place on board, and its witness protection rooms the safest. Visits last ten minutes, every word is recorded, and a public defender sits in. A stranger meets the ministry as a summons or a refuge.

factions.name: Mitene Union
factions.info: A federation of five countries in the Balsa Islands, south of the Yorbian Continent: NGL, the Republic of Rokario, the Republic of Hass, the Republic of West Gorteau and the Republic of East Gorteau. Rokario's Doli City and its towns are the open, ordinary face of the Union; NGL and East Gorteau are closed to almost everyone. The members keep a common front abroad and quarrel at home. A stranger meets the Union as a border stamp and a crowded harbour; one who serves it carries papers between five capitals.

factions.name: NGL Autonomous Region
factions.info: A self-governing member of the Mitene Union whose two million people live without machines. Nothing made of synthetic material may cross its border, and anyone caught smuggling technology, modern medicine or weapons is jailed or executed. Visitors are stripped, x-rayed and scanned at the border stop and leave everything modern behind; inside, letters are the post and horses are the road. When an epidemic struck, the people refused foreign doctors so as to stay pure. A television crew that sneaked in years ago was caught, and one of them is still in prison. One who joins gives up the modern world and swears to the movement.

factions.name: Nickes' Alliance
factions.info: A great alliance of players inside Greed Island, sixty-three strong at its height, every one of them hired by Battera. Ten founders run it and split the largest share of the reward; the rest are paid by how long they have served and what they risked. Its plan is plain: corner the island's attack and defence spell cards so no one else can fight back, then collect the specified cards at leisure. New members are brought to a hidden base by a roundabout route and must learn every spell card by heart in an hour, or they are made errand runners. A stranger meets it as a recruiter with a pitch.

factions.name: Nostrade Family
factions.info: A provincial Mafia family under the Ritz Family, headed by Light Nostrade, that rose fast because his daughter Neon writes fortunes that come true; even the Dons ask for her verses. A dummy company, Polio & Co. Ltd., holds the property that should not carry the family's name. Neon collects human body parts and other morbid curiosities, and her father buys them for her. The family hires bodyguards through a test at its mansion: bring back one item from a list within a month. A stranger meets it as an employer paying well for dangerous work.

factions.name: Phantom Troupe
factions.info: A band of thieves and killers carrying a bounty of the highest class, known across the world by the twelve-legged spider each member wears tattooed with a number. Most of them grew up together in Meteor City. They take what their leader wants, let him enjoy it, then sell it all, and they kill whoever stands in the way; the extermination of the Kurta Clan for its scarlet eyes is laid at their door. There are never more than thirteen of them, a head and twelve legs. A new member is nominated by the others or takes a seat by killing the one who held it. A stranger meets them as a rumour, a ruin or a corpse; the city they came from still counts them as its own, at a distance.

factions.name: Pure Paladin Squad
factions.info: A team of versatile Hunters from long ago, so skilled that other Hunters still speak of them as legends. Netero, the chairman, belonged to it in his youth. Nobody can say what the squad did beyond its name or why it broke up, and that silence only feeds the stories told in Hunter bars. A stranger meets it as a toast or a boast; a Hunter who claims its name had better be able to prove it.

factions.name: Shingen-ryu
factions.info: A school of kung fu whose grandmaster is Isaac Netero, the Hunter Association's chairman, who took over a dojo when he came down from two years of training in the mountains. Its teachers drill etiquette, breathing and patience as hard as they drill strikes, and they will not hurry a student. Wing, an assistant master, keeps a small room near Heavens Arena where he trains Zushi; fighters there whisper that the school teaches some inner trick of the will that makes its pupils hard to read. One who joins bows, sweeps the floor and climbs by the teacher's word.

factions.name: Ten Dons
factions.info: The ten leaders of the Mafia, each ruling a territory on one of the six continents. Once a year, at the start of September, they gather in Yorknew City for the Underground Auction, where they settle their plans and give orders. Their combined wealth buys anything and anyone, and they hold Neon Nostrade's fortunes in high regard. Few families dare to cross them and fewer survive it. A stranger never meets a Don; a Mafia soldier hears their will through a boss.

factions.name: V5
factions.info: The leaders of the five great nations of the world, the United States of Saherta, the Federation of Ochima, the Mimbo Republic, the Kukan'yu Kingdom and the Begerossé Union, who meet in summits and decide what the world will do. About two hundred years ago they signed the Inviolability Treaty, which forbids any voyage to the Dark Continent; the world knows the Dark Continent is closed. When they want something done that armies cannot do, they hire the Hunter Association. A stranger meets them as the news; one who serves them carries a diplomatic passport.

factions.name: Xi-Yu Family
factions.info: The richest and most numerous of Kakin's three great Mafia families, led by Onior Longbao, the king's half-brother, who rides as a guest on the Black Whale's first tier. On the ship the Xi-Yu run the fourth tier and live off human trafficking and the exchange of goods, and they have a direct line to the third prince, Zhang Lei. Hinrigh Biganduffno, the underboss, is a huge man with a temper. Along with the other two families they want territory on the new continent. A stranger meets the Xi-Yu as the men who run the fourth tier's markets.

factions.name: Zodiacs
factions.info: The chairman's council: the vice chairman and eleven staff advisors, each a top Hunter whom Netero picked because their skill caught his interest. Each takes a codename from the zodiac and most dress or style themselves to match it, out of loyalty to the old man. They advise on anything the bylaws leave open, take the Association in hand in an emergency and spar with the chairman for his amusement. Hunters treat them with respect; outsiders rarely know their names. A seat is given by the chairman and nothing else, so a Hunter who wants one has to be noticed.

factions.name: Zoldyck butlers
factions.info: The servants of the Zoldyck estate, trained and schooled on the mountain itself, with headquarters so large they are taken for the family's house. Every call from outside goes through them before it reaches the main house, and every visitor meets them first. They train every day with weighted doors, slippers and cups, keep the family's secrets and turn away anyone who climbs past their posts, by force if needed. A butler may not take a lover and lives under strict orders. Gotoh is the head butler; Canary, an apprentice, guards a post near the headquarters. A stranger meets them as polite, frightening people in black suits.

factions.name: Zoldyck Family
factions.info: The deadliest house of assassins in the world, who live on Kukuroo Mountain, a dormant volcano in Padokea's Dentora region. Their name frightens the underworld more than the Phantom Troupe; their faces are almost unknown, and one photograph of a Zoldyck sells for a fortune. Tourist buses run to the Testing Gate, and its first door is too heavy for most men to move; beyond it a giant hound eats anyone who climbs the wall. The children are trained to kill from birth, grow used to poison, pain and current, and choose a speciality as they grow. The family takes contracts from anyone who can pay its very high fee, and no government in the world moves against it. A stranger meets the family as a closed gate; one who serves it starts as a butler and never speaks of what they see.

creatures.name: 200th floor fighter
creatures.info: A fighter on the floors above the two hundredth of Heavens Arena, where the prize money stops, weapons are allowed and every fight is for the record. Some welcome newcomers with a hard lesson the first day. Fights with a strange ability the crowd calls a trick, and keeps a count of wins and losses.

creatures.name: Amateur Hunter
creatures.info: One of the young, unlicensed field researchers who survey new species for a client, kids taken seriously by the Hunter who mentors them. Bright, loud and fiercely loyal to each other. Fights only to escape, and is better at spotting a new animal than at facing one.

creatures.name: Assistant Squadron Leader
creatures.info: An Officer raised to assistant leader or captain when a Squadron Leader reorganised its division after the Queen's death, one of a few trusted over many. Loyal to its leader, eager to prove the promotion right. Fights with a fresh ability and a squad at its back.

creatures.name: Beast Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who works with fauna: tracking rare species, guarding the endangered ones and studying what nobody has named yet. At ease in a forest, wary in a city, protective of the animals more than of people. Fights with the animal's own habits against it, and with a strong grip and a stronger stance.

creatures.name: Black Whale passenger
creatures.info: A lottery passenger on the lower tiers of the Black Whale, one of the many thousands sailing for the New Continent with a bag and a dream. Hopeful, crowded and nervous of the gangs. Does not fight unless cornered.

creatures.name: Blacklist Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who tracks wanted criminals for the bounty, with a list of names, a network of informants and the legal cover of the licence. Patient, cold and very good at waiting. Fights to capture or to kill, with blades, chains or traps, and walks in prepared for a gun.

creatures.name: Botanical Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who knows plants and goes to remote places to find and collect them, seeds and cuttings carried in careful cases. Patient, observant and quietly proud of a sharp nose. Fights rarely, and then with what grows around them.

creatures.name: Bubble Horse
creatures.info: A Bubble Horse of Greed Island's hills, which blows red and white bubbles that burst with a bang as it flees: the white burst at a touch of aura, the red at a touch of anything else. Skittish. Fights not at all; caught, it turns into its card (rank C).

creatures.name: Camp Tiger
creatures.info: A Camp Tiger of the Kakin Empire, a horned tiger that impales its prey and cooks it over a fire it knows how to make, found on a biological survey. Clever and patient. Fights with the horn, then roasts the meal.

creatures.name: Cha-R Family man
creatures.info: A member of the Cha-R Family, one of Kakin's three great Mafia families, which holds the fifth tier of the ship and everything sold on it. Polite until refused, then not polite at all. Fights with guns in a crowded hall.

creatures.name: Chief of the Wolf Pack
creatures.info: The chief of a Greed Island wolf pack, the strongest monster of its rank, whose wolves keep returning while it stands. Commanding and cautious. Fights behind its pack and then in front of it; beaten, it turns into its card (rank C).

creatures.name: Claymore Mushroom
creatures.info: A blotched fungus of the Milsy Wetlands that explodes when harmed, spraying spores that cling to the attacker and anything near. Inert and patient. Fights by bursting; the spores paralyse and take root.

creatures.name: Conjured Nen beast
creatures.info: A beast made of a user's aura, life-like or plainly mechanical, an animal or a figure, with as much will of its own as its maker gave it. Invisible to anyone who has not learned to see aura. Fights as its maker's ability decides, and fades when the aura behind it fails.

creatures.name: Construction Ant
creatures.info: A builder Ant the Queen hatches in a swarm once she finds a site, raising the nest out of mud and dung. Tireless, simple-minded and indifferent to intruders. Fights only by weight of numbers when the nest is breached.

creatures.name: Copycat King
creatures.info: A Chimera Ant that left the nest when the Queen died and set itself up as a king of its own territory, with a few followers as its guards. Swaggering, greedy and unsure what a king does. Fights to hold its ground and to breed.

creatures.name: Cyclops
creatures.info: A Cyclops of Greed Island's hills, a one-eyed giant with a club whose swings make a wind, moving in groups and shrugging off any blow but one to the eye. Dull and relentless. Fights with downward and sideways swings; struck in the eye, it falls and turns into its card (rank G).

creatures.name: Dark Continent calamity
creatures.info: A type kept only for a what-if Dark Continent mode: whatever lies past the waters of Lake Mobius, which a treaty forbids anyone to seek and only a few expeditions ever returned from. In the story it is talk on a ship's deck and a line in an old report, never a foe met in play.

creatures.name: Drudge Ant
creatures.info: A support soldier of a Chimera Ant colony, hauling fodder and carrying orders, a mix of insect and whatever beast the Queen ate. Obedient and expendable. Fights with claws or mandibles when cornered.

creatures.name: East Gorteau aura soldier
creatures.info: One of the few soldiers of East Gorteau who learned to use aura and was set to guard the dictator's palace. Muscular, quick to anger and confident of his fists. Fights barehanded, wrapped in an aura that a trained eye can see.

creatures.name: East Gorteau soldier
creatures.info: A soldier of the Republic of East Gorteau, a closed dictatorship, posted at the capital or the dictator's palace in a beret and plain kit. Obedient, afraid of the regime and more afraid of failing it. Fights with a rifle in a line and follows the last order given.

creatures.name: Eight-legged dog
creatures.info: An Eight-legged Dog of the forest outside Doli City in the Republic of Rokario, a small creature like a bear cub with a dog's head and too many legs. Timid. Does not fight; it bolts into the bushes.

creatures.name: Exam scout
creatures.info: One of the people the exam hires to cull applicants before the site: a ship's crew, a quiz on a hill road, a guide with a question nobody can answer well. Plain, patient and hard to read. Does not fight; sends the failures home and points the rest onward.

creatures.name: Exam veteran
creatures.info: An applicant on a fifth or tenth try, who no longer expects to pass and has made a hobby of breaking newcomers. Knows the old tricks, the laced drink and the false friend, and plays them in a team of brothers or partners. Fights in a pack and never alone, and stops the moment the odds turn.

creatures.name: Floor Master
creatures.info: One of the twenty-one fighters who hold a floor of their own near the top of Heavens Arena, won by beating the master before them. Bored by most challengers and choosy about the rest. Fights for their floor with a complete ability, and for little else.

creatures.name: Foxbear
creatures.info: A Foxbear of Whale Island's forests, a stocky bear with a fox's face and sharp claws, which marks its territory on the trees and attacks whoever ignores the marks. Fierce, above all a mother with cubs. Fights with claws and weight.

creatures.name: Freelance assassin
creatures.info: A professional killer hired by the job, an aura user of uneven skill working alone or with a few others on the same contract. Wary, competitive and quick to sneer at teamwork. Fights from the dark with a signature method, and dies when the target is better.

creatures.name: Gourmet Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who hunts rare ingredients and cooks them, a chef with a licence and a palate that judges before it compliments. Demanding, quick to anger and fond of eating. Fights with kitchen knives, speed and a temper.

creatures.name: Great Stamp
creatures.info: A Great Stamp, the world's fiercest pig, a fast pink brute with a snout like a battering ram and teeth that crush bone. Aggressive and herd-minded. Fights by charging, and drops at once to a blow on the soft spot its snout hides.

creatures.name: Greed Island Game Master
creatures.info: One of the people who run Greed Island from inside it: greeting players at the start, sending them home from the port, keeping the spells working and removing anyone who arrived by the wrong road. Cheerful or grave as the post demands, and absolutely in control. Fights only to enforce the game's rules, with the island's spells, which are their own work, at hand.

creatures.name: Greed Island guard
creatures.info: A guard character of Greed Island posted at a mansion or a gate, in a suit and tie, calm until a player takes what he guards. Professional, then belligerent. Fights with a clumsy rush; beaten, he turns into his card like everything else on the island.

creatures.name: Greed Island player
creatures.info: A player inside Greed Island, an aura user who came in through a console and can leave only through the port or by a spell card, with a binder at hand and an eye on other players' cards. Wary, greedy and often lonely. Fights with an ability and spell cards, and steals before it fights.

creatures.name: Greed Island villager
creatures.info: A villager of Greed Island who plays a part in one of its quests, such as the mountain folk who pose as bandits and beg for medicine. Frightened, poor and grateful to anyone kind without asking a price. Does not really fight.

creatures.name: Hacker Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who works the networks, following a crime through servers and records as other Hunters follow tracks. Pale, wry and online at every hour. Fights at a keyboard first, and in person only when the trace leads to a door.

creatures.name: Have-Not guard
creatures.info: A Have-Not of Kakin, the caste once barred from office and rank, given a soldier's standing by the prince who armed them and sworn to her past reason. Fierce, grateful and ready to die for the one who raised them. Fights with firearms and a loyalty that frightens the other camps.

creatures.name: Heavens Arena fighter
creatures.info: A fighter climbing the lower floors of Heavens Arena for prize money, ten floors a win, with no weapons allowed and a crowd that cheers the knockout. Tough, showy and sure the next floor is theirs. Fights barehanded in a ring, with a style learned in a gym or a street.

creatures.name: Heil-Ly Family man
creatures.info: A member of the Heil-Ly Family, the smallest of Kakin's three great Mafia families, based on the ship's third tier and living off secret deals made with the decks above. Close-mouthed and loyal to a boss who once purged her own family. Fights with whatever the boss allows.

creatures.name: Hemotropic Butterfly
creatures.info: A crimson butterfly of Zevil Island that smells blood from far off and gathers on wounds, more of them the more blood there is. Harmless but telling. Does not fight; it shows a hunter where the wounded lie.

creatures.name: Human-made Ant hybrid
creatures.info: A person turned into a Chimera Ant hybrid by another Ant's power rather than born from the Queen: a human shape with insect parts, pieces of the old life in memory, and sometimes an aura talent the person never had. Lost, obedient or broken, and some only want to die. Fights as it is told.

creatures.name: Hunter Exam applicant
creatures.info: One of the hopefuls who found the year's exam site, wearing a numbered badge and a look of having already lost something to get here. Fit, stubborn and sure the licence will change their life; few of them see the last phase. Fights with whatever the applicant brought: a sword, a bow, a trick, or fists.

creatures.name: Hunter Exam examiner
creatures.info: An elite Hunter running one phase of the exam for no pay, who sets the test, watches the applicants and keeps the score to themselves. Composed, a little bored, and far stronger than any applicant guesses. Striking an examiner disqualifies the applicant on the spot; few who try it land the blow.

creatures.name: Hyper Puffball
creatures.info: A Hyper Puffball of Greed Island's hills, a little black fluff ball on skinny legs that bounces too fast to see in straight lines with a hidden pattern. Weak blows, a tough body. Fights by ricochet; caught, it turns into its card (rank D).

creatures.name: Hypnosis Butterfly
creatures.info: A Hypnosis Butterfly of the Milsy Wetlands, ordinary to look at, whose flight pattern puts whoever watches it to sleep as live food for its larvae. Harmless alone and deadly in a swarm. Fights by flying.

creatures.name: Kakin military cadet
creatures.info: A student or recent graduate of Kakin's military academy, young, drilled on weapons against a stopwatch and placed in a prince's private army on graduating. Ambitious, competitive and eager to be noticed. Fights with rifle and knife as the field drills taught.

creatures.name: Kakin royal guard
creatures.info: A guard assigned to a prince or a queen of Kakin, picked for loyalty and skill, some of them aura users and some only well trained. Watchful, silent in the room and loud on the radio. Fights to keep their charge alive, and spies on the other camps when told to.

creatures.name: Kakin soldier
creatures.info: A soldier of the Kakin Military, the Royal Army that runs the ship's law from its office on the third tier, checking tickets and keeping the corridors. Disciplined, proud of the empire and wary of the princes' quarrels. Fights with rifles and numbers, and follows the chain of command.

creatures.name: King White Stag Beetle
creatures.info: A King White Stag Beetle of Greed Island, a rare white beetle that draws other insects into a vast colony in a giant tree and leaves it once a day. It falls only when the tree is struck hard enough. Does not fight; caught, it turns into its card (rank A, one of the cards a clear needs).

creatures.name: Kiriko
creatures.info: A Kiriko, a large fox-like magical beast that walks upright on three-clawed feet, sprouts wings to fly and can take a human shape well enough to live in a town. Clever, well read and fond of testing people. Fights with claws and deception, or carries a passenger off through the air.

creatures.name: Lingering spirit
creatures.info: A weak evil spirit that latches onto someone whose aura has nearly stopped, worsening the sickness until the end is days away. Unseen by non-users. Does not fight; an exorcist can drive it off, and it comes back until the sufferer recovers.

creatures.name: Mafia bodyguard
creatures.info: A hired protector of a Mafia boss or heir, picked by a test that weeds out the merely strong, with an ability of their own that the family's soldiers fear. Professional, unsentimental and paid well. Fights to keep one person alive, and to finish any threat to them.

creatures.name: Mafia soldier
creatures.info: A gunman of the Mafia Community, in a dark suit with a pistol and an earpiece, who guards a family's turf, its auctions and its bosses. Loyal to the family, brutal on orders, and frightened of what he does not understand. Fights with guns in numbers, and loses heart when bullets stop working.

creatures.name: Man-faced Ape
creatures.info: A Man-faced Ape of the Milsy Wetlands, a frail, long-clawed primate that can pass for a human and speak like one, and lures travellers into the fog by posing as someone they trust, even the exam's own examiner. Deceitful and cowardly. Fights hardly at all; it lets the swamp kill its prey and eats after.

creatures.name: Master of the Swamp
creatures.info: The Master of the Swamp, a whale-sized fish of Whale Island's swamp with sharp teeth and spindly insect legs along its belly, too strong for five fishermen to land at once. Wily and old. Fights on the line, and drags.

creatures.name: Melanin Lizard
creatures.info: A Melanin Lizard of Greed Island's hills, big enough to swallow a cow, that pins prey under its weight; one mole among the spots on its back is the weak point, and it guards that spot more than the rest. Persistent. Struck there, it turns into its card (rank E).

creatures.name: Meteor City resident
creatures.info: A resident of Meteor City, the junkyard city that is on no record, covered head to foot against the waste and the weather. Frank, close to their dead, and bound to their neighbours by ties thinner than water and thicker than blood. Fights by refusing to yield, and answers an insult to the city with a bomb.

creatures.name: Ministry of Justice officer
creatures.info: An armed officer of Kakin's Ministry of Justice, in a uniform unlike the army's, guarding the courts and interrogation rooms on the ship's second tier. Correct, neutral and proud of it. Fights by the book, with a sidearm and a cell door.

creatures.name: Needle person
creatures.info: A bystander with a Manipulator's needle driven into the head, eyes unfocused, obeying the needle's order until exhaustion kills them. Without will or fear, and once just a person in a park. Fights or chases without pain, and stops only when the needle comes out or the body gives up.

creatures.name: Nen exorcist
creatures.info: One of the rare aura users who can lift curses, fewer than ten in the world strong enough to undo what the dead leave behind. Grave, careful and paid in conditions the work lays on them. Does not fight; reads a curse, says what it would cost to remove, and sometimes says it cannot be done.

creatures.name: NGL border guard
creatures.info: A guard of the NGL checkpoint in the hollow trees on the border, who strips and searches every visitor for anything made by a machine. Proud of the natural life, thorough and suspicious. Fights only to turn a visitor back, and leans on the weight of the rule.

creatures.name: NGL villager
creatures.info: A villager of NGL living the natural life its founders chose: no machines, no engines, crops and horses and hand tools. Gentle, hard-working and sure the outside world is sick. Does not fight; runs, or hides the children.

creatures.name: Nickes' Alliance member
creatures.info: A member of the big player alliance that hoards spell cards so no one else can defend against it, hired into the game by a billionaire and promised a share. Organised, cautious and fond of numbers. Fights from a safe house with stored spells, and sends someone else out.

creatures.name: Noggin Lugging Tortoise
creatures.info: A giant man-eating tortoise of the Milsy Wetlands that moves only in thick fog, with tufts of human-looking strawberries on its shell to fool travellers into walking up to it. Slow, patient and greedy. Fights with a sudden bite from under the fog.

creatures.name: One-eyed box monster
creatures.info: A strange floating box of Greed Island with a single eye, quick in the air and hard to pin down. Curious. Fights by darting out of reach.

creatures.name: Pack wolf
creatures.info: A wolf of the pack that walks upright and ambushes travellers on the roads near Masadora, a fair fighter that seems to use aura. Cunning, many, and back again after every defeat. Fights in numbers, and keeps coming until its chief is beaten.

creatures.name: Parasitic Nen beast
creatures.info: A Nen beast that clings to one host and feeds on the host's aura, its shape and gifts drawn from the host's character and not always under the host's command. It fades while the host hides their aura or runs dry; otherwise it acts in its own way.

creatures.name: Phantom Troupe member
creatures.info: A Spider of the Phantom Troupe, a thief with a Class-A bounty and a numbered tattoo, one of thirteen at most who steal what they want and kill who is in the way. Loyal to the Spider over any one member, careless of anyone else. Fights with a fully trained ability and no mercy.

creatures.name: Piko
creatures.info: A Piko, the large ground-running bird the Kurta Clan of the Lukso Province rode and loaded with goods, long-necked and big-beaked. Steady and obedient to its rider. Does not fight; it carries.

creatures.name: Player killer
creatures.info: A Greed Island player who kills for cards, hiding behind a friendly face until a binder is worth taking. Patient, theatrical and unbothered by bodies. Fights with an ability that turns a touch into a death sentence, and with a partner who covers the escape.

creatures.name: Poacher Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who studies wild animals and protects them from the people who hunt them for money. Gruff with humans, gentle with beasts, and slow to forgive a snare. Fights hard and close when a poacher is caught in the act.

creatures.name: Professional Hunter
creatures.info: A working Hunter with a field, a reputation and the aura training every real Hunter must have, which they never explain to outsiders. Calm, self-interested and hard to surprise. Fights with a developed ability, a weapon of choice and the habit of reading an opponent before moving.

creatures.name: Provisional Hunter
creatures.info: A Kakin guard screened by the Association to serve during the voyage, given a licence that ends when the voyage does and no aura training to go with it. Disciplined, out of their depth around real Hunters, and aware of it. Fights with firearms and drill.

creatures.name: Radio Rat
creatures.info: A Radio Rat of Greed Island, a timid rodent that hides and works an empty suit of armour or other objects from a distance with aura to scare hunters off. Shy to the point of fainting. Fights through what it moves; seen, it faints and turns into its card (rank H).

creatures.name: Rookie Hunter
creatures.info: A newly licensed Hunter with no field yet, a card in the pocket worth more than a house and no idea how many people want to take it. Eager, careless with the licence, and still short of the art the Association quietly expects. Fights with raw talent and the training that got them through the exam.

creatures.name: Ruins Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who uncovers and restores ancient ruins so the people who built them can be understood again. Bookish, sunburnt and happiest in a trench. Fights reluctantly, with the strength of someone who lifts stone for a living.

creatures.name: Ruse Raven
creatures.info: A Ruse Raven, a raven with a split tongue that mimics voices and calls lies into the fog to lead prey into traps. Patient and scavenging. Fights by no means but the lie, and feeds on what the trap leaves.

creatures.name: Six-legged Flying Beast
creatures.info: A winged, six-limbed flying predator of the skies around Trick Tower, red or purple-skinned with razor teeth, that snatches anyone climbing down the outside wall. Swarming and ravenous. Fights in a flock, tearing prey apart in flight.

creatures.name: Slime monster
creatures.info: A slime of Greed Island with eyes and a mouth that sits still and does little, yet shrugs off a beginner's blows. Placid. Fights by being hard to hurt; the trick of beating it is one a teacher shows.

creatures.name: Spider Eagle
creatures.info: A Spider Eagle of Split Mountain, which strings its webbed nests deep in the canyon so no predator reaches its eggs. Watchful and territorial. Fights from the air and lets the drop do the rest.

creatures.name: Stone Wall mercenary
creatures.info: A mercenary of Stone Wall, the eleven-strong unit famous for coming through the Lubo Civil War without one death, scouts and artillery experts by their own account. Quiet, professional and careful with lives. Fights from cover with heavy guns and a map of every exit.

creatures.name: Stung hybrid
creatures.info: A human of Meteor City stung by a Chimera Ant Squadron Leader's tail and remade into a servant of her small queendom, with no Nen ability of its own. Mindless in loyalty, swears itself to her at once. Fights with a twisted body and no sense of danger.

creatures.name: Temp Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who takes government work subcontracted by the Association at a set fee, and so is mocked by Hunters who chase their own goals. Reliable, practical and tired of the jokes. Fights to finish the job and collect, without flourish.

creatures.name: Trade shop keeper
creatures.info: A shopkeeper of a Greed Island trade shop, who buys cards for the island's money, sells information and keeps a player's money if trusted with it. Monotone, patient and repetitive. Does not fight.

creatures.name: Treasure Hunter
creatures.info: A Hunter who goes after rare and valuable things, from lost gems to games no shop sells, for clients or for themselves. Shrewd, money-minded and good at deals. Fights when a rival reaches the prize first, with a team and a plan.

creatures.name: Two-headed Wolf
creatures.info: A Two-headed Wolf, an endangered species kept alive by a breeding programme a famous Hunter set up. Wary and protective. Fights with two jaws at once when the pack is threatened.

creatures.name: World Tree Bird
creatures.info: One of the huge birds that nest atop a World Tree, plumed in many colours, with ears like a cat's and a long beak to bring food back to the waiting chicks. Calm, and fierce only near the nest. Fights with the beak and wings.

creatures.name: Xi-Yu Family man
creatures.info: A member of the Xi-Yu Family, the largest of Kakin's three great Mafia families, which runs the fourth tier of the ship and its traffic in goods and people. Confident, numerous and backed by money. Fights with guns and many friends.

creatures.name: Yorknew police officer
creatures.info: An officer of the Yorknew City police, in a city whose mayor owes the Mafia most of his campaign, so the force looks away when the families ask. Tired, careful and outgunned during auction month. Fights with a sidearm and a radio, and calls for more cars.

creatures.name: Zodiac Hunter
creatures.info: One of the twelve Zodiacs, the chairman's advisors, picked by him for his own reasons rather than by star or rank, who decide whatever the Bylaws leave open. Eccentric, proud and much more dangerous than the costume suggests. Fights with a mature ability, and only when talk has failed.

creatures.name: Zoldyck apprentice butler
creatures.info: A young apprentice of the Zoldyck butlers, posted on the estate path with a staff and the order to drive back anyone who crosses a line drawn in the dirt. Polite, steady and quietly unhappy with the post. Fights with a staff, fast and without wasted motion.

creatures.name: Zoldyck assassin
creatures.info: A member of the Zoldyck Family, the world's most feared assassins, raised from birth to kill and to shrug off poison, pain and electric shock. Calm, polite and strict about the terms of a contract. Fights with a chosen tool, needles, paper, claws or a dragon of aura, and never wastes a blow.

creatures.name: Zoldyck butler
creatures.info: A butler of the Zoldyck Family on Kukuroo Mountain, trained on the estate with weighted cups, doors and slippers, and bound by rules that forbid lovers on pain of death. Formal, unsmiling and devoted to the family. Fights with speed, coins, a staff or bare hands, and treats an intruder as a chore.

creatures.name: Zoldyck groundskeeper
creatures.info: A groundskeeper of the Zoldyck estate who keeps a cabin by the Testing Gate, looks like its warden and is in truth the man who clears up after the guard dog. Courteous, weary and honest with visitors who mean no harm. Fights hardly at all; his strength is opening the gate's first door.

creatures.name: Zoldyck guard hound
creatures.info: A giant hound of the Zoldyck estate, near four metres tall, trained until it seems more machine than animal, obeying only the family and still keeping an old order to kill every intruder. Silent and unblinking. Fights with hand-like clawed forepaws, and eats what it kills.

items.name: 200th-Floor Registration Card
items.info: A fighter's card for the 200th floor, with the deadline to fight printed on it.

items.name: 3-D Camera
items.info: Specified card No. 097, rank A, limit 20 copies. A camera whose prints come out as solid objects, true to the touch, at any size wanted. Only the subject is made, never the background. Found, never sold: in-game.

items.name: Accompany
items.info: Spell card No. 1039, rank F, limit 130 copies. Flies the caster and every player within twenty metres to a town visited or a player met. A party travels on it together, and so does an enemy standing too close. Found, never sold: Spell Card Shop.

items.name: Accountant's Book
items.info: A book written in a code only the Dons' people read.

items.name: Adviser's Academy Ring
items.info: A class ring from the Royal Military Academy.

items.name: Advisor's Animal Mask
items.info: A mask shaped like a zodiac beast, worn by an advisor who chose to match the sign.

items.name: Aide's Seal Ring
items.info: A ring with a prince's personal seal.
items.where: Prince's Aide, Hui Guo Rou royal house

items.name: Aide's Summit Lanyard
items.info: A lanyard with the five nations' flags.

items.name: Aide's Zodiac Card
items.info: A card printed with one of the twelve beasts, carried by an advisor's aide.

items.name: Alternate's Contract
items.info: A contract for those kept in reserve.

items.name: Analysis
items.info: Spell card No. 1031, rank G, limit 400 copies. Reads out the text of any numbered card except the very last, which no spell can read. Found, never sold: Spell Card Shop.

items.name: Analyst's Risk Chart
items.info: A chart rating countries by danger and preservation level.

items.name: Angel's Breath
items.info: Specified card No. 017, rank SS, limit 3 copies. An angel who heals one person of every wound and sickness with a single breath, even at death's door. She comes only once, and the card is gone with her. Found, never sold: Masadora.

items.name: Angler's Fishing Rod
items.info: A long fishing rod with a strong line and a heavy float, as good for a fight as for a lake.

items.name: Antenna Needles
items.info: A pair of steel needles with a ball at one end, shaped like a small aerial. Shalnark kept his as the medium of his Manipulation, one for use and one in reserve. 3000 Jenny, sold at Saloma Mall.

items.name: Antivenom Ampoule
items.info: A sealed glass ampoule of serum against snake and insect venom, given by injection. A poison hunter never travels without two. 15000 Jenny, sold at Swardani City.

items.name: Apprentice's Guard Staff
items.info: A long staff used to drive trespassers from a butler's post.

items.name: Arena Bento Box
items.info: A lunch box of rice, fried chicken and pickles sold to the crowds between bouts. Fighters on the lower floors live on them until the prize money comes in. 900 Jenny, sold at Arena Concourse.

items.name: Army Ration Tin
items.info: A tin of army rations with the Royal Army's stamp.

items.name: Aromatherapy Girl
items.info: Specified card No. 048, rank A, limit 15 copies. A girl who gives off the scent the owner finds most soothing. Stress cannot touch anyone she sits beside. Found, never sold: in-game.

items.name: Assassin's Throwing Pins
items.info: A roll of long steel pins, weighted to fly straight and slim enough to vanish into a sleeve.

items.name: Assault Rifle
items.info: A soldier's automatic rifle with a curved magazine. The armies of East Gorteau and Kakin are armed with them, and they are not sold to the public. Found, never sold: Peijin.

items.name: Assembly Token
items.info: A stamped scrap of scrap metal that lets its holder speak before the elders.

items.name: Assistant Master's Glasses Case
items.info: A battered spectacle case that never leaves a teacher's pocket.

items.name: Assistant's Feather Fan
items.info: A fan of stiff feathers, a winged officer's keepsake.

items.name: Associate's Burger Receipt
items.info: A receipt from a burger bar on the third tier, with a number on the back.

items.name: Attaché's Diplomatic Pouch
items.info: A sealed leather pouch exempt from search.

items.name: Attendant's Coins
items.info: A handful of coins worn smooth from the coin game.

items.name: Bandage Roll
items.info: A roll of clean cotton bandage, the thing every arena fighter carries out of the ring. 500 Jenny, sold at Arena Town.

items.name: Bandit's Blade
items.info: Specified card No. 094, rank S, limit 10 copies. A blade that casts Mug, Pickpocket or Thief on whoever it wounds, though not on a player shielded by Fortress or the Paladin's Necklace. Found, never sold: in-game.

items.name: Battera's Rose
items.info: A dried rose like the one the old man always wears on his lapel.

items.name: Beatle-07
items.info: A mobile phone shaped like a rhinoceros beetle, its one horn the aerial and its wings opening on a screen and keypad. It is heavier and dearer than other models and worth it for its features, Leorio says; Gon and Killua each bought one on his word. 65000 Jenny, sold at Saloma Mall.

items.name: Beauty Magnet Emerald
items.info: Specified card No. 077, rank S, limit 10 copies. Experts in beauty seek out the emerald's owner on their own, and the owner shines with a loveliness nobody had noticed before. Found, never sold: in-game.

items.name: Ben's Knife
items.info: One of the numbered knives Benny Delon forged, a new one after each life he took, two hundred and eighty-eight in all. They are keen enough to open a Zoldyck's hardened skin, and the smith's aura still clings to them a century on, so a user who looks with aura in the eyes can pick one out of a junk stall. Collectors pay less than they are worth because of who made them, though even the cheapest fetches five million. 5000000 Jenny, sold at Bull Market.

items.name: Black Whale Boarding Pass
items.info: A pass to a numbered berth on the Black Whale 1, the great ship carrying two hundred thousand people to the new continent. The pass names the tier, and a passenger may not cross to another without leave. Found, never sold: Kakin Empire.

items.name: Blackout Curtain
items.info: Spell card No. 1025, rank F, limit 200 copies. Hides its holder from the next Peek or Fluoroscopy cast at them. Found, never sold: Spell Card Shop.

items.name: Blowgun
items.info: A long hollow cane that fires darts without a sound. Geretta preferred his to any gun and tested floors with it as well as men. 4000 Jenny, sold at Zaban City.

items.name: Blue Planet
items.info: Specified card No. 081, rank SS, limit 5 copies. A rare jewel with a beautiful blue shine. Its make-up matches no known mineral, so it was named a gift from space. Biscuit played the game for this stone alone. Found, never sold: in-game.

items.name: Bodyguard's Earpiece
items.info: A small radio earpiece for keeping in touch with the other guards.

items.name: Bodyguard's Royal Armband
items.info: A gold armband issued to those guarding a prince.
items.where: Royal Bodyguard, Hui Guo Rou royal house

items.name: Bodyguard's Shoulder Holster
items.info: A leather shoulder holster worn under a dark suit jacket, cut so the gun clears it in one pull.

items.name: Bomber's Spell Binder Page
items.info: A torn page of card notes in neat block capitals.

items.name: Book of Life
items.info: Specified card No. 093, rank B, limit 28 copies. A record of every person the owner has known since birth, with their talks and their memorable moments. It can run to tens of thousands of pages. Found, never sold: in-game.

items.name: Book of Tyson
items.info: Tyson Hui Guo Rou's book of peaceful teachings, promising world peace once everyone is her disciple. It is stitched together almost entirely from song lyrics, and some who read it find it strangely gripping all the same. Found, never sold: Princes' Residential District.

items.name: Book of V.I.P. Passes
items.info: Specified card No. 027, rank B, limit 25 copies. A book of a thousand passes, each one good for getting in anywhere at all. Found, never sold: in-game.

items.name: Border Guard's Search Gloves
items.info: Thick cotton gloves worn for searches at the border stop.

items.name: Border Officer's Cap
items.info: A peaked cap with a small brass badge.

items.name: Boss's Cigar Case
items.info: A silver cigar case that only the boss opens.

items.name: Bottle of Whisky
items.info: A bottle of aged whisky from the hotel bar, poured neat for men who would rather not talk about their day. 9000 Jenny, sold at Hotel Bayloke.

items.name: Bottled Water
items.info: A litre of water in a plastic bottle, the last that is sold before the desert road. 150 Jenny, sold at Desert Roadhouse.

items.name: Box of Pistol Rounds
items.info: A cardboard box of fifty pistol cartridges in one of the common calibres. It reloads a magazine four or five times. 3000 Jenny, sold at Yorknew City.

items.name: Braided Leather Whip
items.info: A long whip of braided leather with a weighted handle.

items.name: Broker's Contact Book
items.info: A tiny book of names from the upper decks.

items.name: Bubble Horse
