categories.name: The Last Vow
categories.info: Open only to one who has already staked their life, and only as their second vow: once, ever, everything for one fight.

skills.name: agility
skills.info:
Running, climbing, leaping, falling well and keeping balance on a wall, a rope or a moving roof. A basic success gets there; a great success gets there first, or where nobody thought a person could.

Covers: running, climbing, leaping, falling well and balance on a wall, a rope or a moving roof. Not: moving unseen, which is stealth, and holding on for hours, which is endurance. Easy: climb a ship's mast in a swell. Medium: climb down the outside of Trick Tower past the beasts that nest on it. Hard: jump into Split Mountain's canyon, take a Spider Eagle egg from its web and climb out. Very hard: climb a World Tree's trunk to the top. Extremely hard: dodge a hail of thrown cards in a corridor.

Primary Attribute: Speed

skills.name: appraisal
skills.info:
The Treasure Hunter's field: the worth of a thing, the forged and the real, auctions, collectors and the market. A basic success tells a fake from the real thing; a great success finds the treasure the seller does not know he holds.

Covers: the worth of goods, art and relics; forgeries; the auction floor, the collector and the Nen-made treasure that shows only to Gyo. Not: bargaining, which is negotiation, and the street's black market, which is streetwise. Easy: spot a cheap fake at a street stall. Medium: pick a Nen-made piece out of a bargain table at the Bull Market. Hard: value a lot in the Southernpiece Catalog. Very hard: value a pair of Scarlet Eyes before the bidding opens. Extremely hard: buy a treasure for a fraction of its worth because the seller did not know it.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: assassination
skills.info:
The killing arts of the Zoldyck Family: the silent step, the hand shaped into claws, the joint slipped from its socket, the afterimage, the mind that does not hesitate. A basic success kills or escapes quietly; a great success does it in a crowd and leaves nothing behind.

Covers: the Zoldyck arts: Silent Gaits, the claws, joints slipped to escape bonds, Rhythm Echo's afterimages, a mind that removes hesitation; taught only by a Zoldyck. Not: moving unseen with no killing in it, which is stealth, and a school's fight, which is shingen-ryu. Easy: walk across a floor without a sound. Medium: slip a joint and step out of handcuffs. Hard: pull a heart out with a hand shaped into claws, as Killua Zoldyck did in Trick Tower. Very hard: leave three afterimages with a shifting step. Extremely hard: kill a Mafia don in a guarded room and leave no witness.

Primary Attribute: Speed

skills.name: awareness
skills.info:
Noticing: the tail in a crowd, the trap in a floor, the lie in a smile, the shape that is wrong. A basic success spots the obvious; a great success spots what was hidden on purpose.

Covers: noticing: the tail in a crowd, the trap in a floor, the lie in a smile, the shape that is wrong. Not: reading aura, which is nen, and solving a whole crime, which is deduction. Easy: spot a pickpocket on a train. Medium: notice that the friendly veteran's juice was opened. Hard: spot the scout hidden among ordinary passengers. Very hard: spot the Kiriko wearing a human shape among the guides. Extremely hard: see the feint before the blow.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: beast-lore
skills.info:
The Beast Hunter's field: Magical Beasts, the rare and the undocumented, how they hunt, what they eat and where they break. A basic success names the creature and its danger; a great success finds the weak spot it hides.

Covers: Magical Beasts and wild fauna: Kiriko, the lure-beasts of Milsy Wetlands, the Great Stamp, the Spider Eagle, guard dogs and the undocumented. Not: a trail in the mud, which is tracking, and cooking what was caught, which is gourmet. Easy: tell a Foxbear's tracks from a bear's. Medium: tell the real examiner from the Man-faced Ape that wears his face. Hard: bring down a Great Stamp with a blow to the soft spot on its forehead. Very hard: walk past Mike's kennel and live. Extremely hard: find a creature no book has ever named.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: blades
skills.info:
Swords, knives and the hidden blade: the iaido draw, the umbrella sword, the knife from a sleeve. A basic success cuts true; a great success ends the exchange with one draw.

Covers: swords, knives and hidden blades: the iaido draw, the paired swords, the sword in an umbrella, the knife made by a famous killer. Not: a thrown blade, which is thrown-weapons, and a club or staff, which is weapons. Easy: cut a rope in one stroke. Medium: parry a knife with a wooden sword, as Kurapika did. Hard: cut down anyone who steps into your sword's reach before he finishes the step. Very hard: fight with a sword hidden in an umbrella, as Feitan Portor did. Extremely hard: cut a thrown blade out of the air with one draw.

Primary Attribute: Speed

skills.name: botany
skills.info:
The Botanical Hunter's field: plants, herbs, forests and trees, the useful, the poisonous and the rare. A basic success names a plant and its use; a great success finds one the world thought was gone.

Covers: plants, herbs, forests and trees: the useful, the poisonous, the rare and the ancient. Not: a toxin's effect, which is poisons, and living off the forest, which is wildcraft. Easy: name a medicinal herb by its leaf. Medium: find water in a forest by the plants that grow near it. Hard: find a rare flower in a swamp full of predators. Very hard: climb a World Tree and name what grows on its branches. Extremely hard: find a plant every botanist believed extinct.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: bounty-hunting
skills.info:
The Blacklist Hunter's field: wanted lists, bounties, the habits of fugitives and the law on taking them. A basic success finds where a wanted man was seen; a great success finds where he will be.

Covers: wanted lists, bounties, the habits of fugitives, the Association's rule on hunting a Hunter, and taking a quarry alive. Not: a trail on the ground, which is tracking, and solving a crime, which is deduction. Easy: read a wanted list for a name worth chasing. Medium: find where a wanted man slept last night. Hard: take a bounty alive and deliver him to the police. Very hard: track a member of the Phantom Troupe through Yorknew City. Extremely hard: take a top-class bounty that veteran hunters refused.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: command
skills.info:
Leading people: a guard team, a hunting party, a squad of soldiers, a crew in a crisis. A basic success is obeyed; a great success holds a team together when the plan has fallen apart.

Covers: leading people: a guard team, a hunting party, a squad, a crew in a crisis. Not: a deal across a table, which is negotiation, and a fight of your own, which is the fighting skills. Easy: get a ship's crew working together. Medium: run a night watch for a guard team. Hard: lead a bodyguard team through an attack on its charge. Very hard: hold a team together after its leader dies. Extremely hard: lead a royal guard on a ship of assassins and keep your charge alive.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: conjuration
skills.info:
Conjuration: an object made from aura, real enough to touch, bound by the conditions its maker set. A basic success calls the object up; a great success makes it do what its conditions promise against someone strong.

Covers: making a material object from aura, the only Nen a non-user can see and touch; the imagery training that makes it real; the conditions bound into the object. Not: aura given a property, which is transmutation, and an object already owned, which is manipulation. Easy: conjure a small object you have lived with for months. Medium: conjure a chain that answers your hand, as Kurapika did. Hard: conjure a vacuum cleaner that swallows only what its rules allow, as Shizuku Murasaki did. Very hard: conjure copies of the dead so true that the Mafia believes them, as Kortopi did. Extremely hard: conjure an object whose conditions hold against a stronger user who is trying to break them.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: deception
skills.info:
Lies, false names, disguises, a bluff at the table and a story that holds up under questions. A basic success is believed; a great success is believed by someone who was warned.

Covers: lies, false names, disguises, the bluff at a table and a story that holds under questions. Not: hiding aura, which is zetsu, and an honest deal, which is negotiation. Easy: lie to a ticket clerk about your age. Medium: pass a Navigator's question with a false answer and a straight face. Hard: bluff a Mafia guard into opening a door. Very hard: convince a whole city that you died. Extremely hard: lie to a user who can read memories and keep the truth.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: deduction
skills.info:
The Crime Hunter's field: reading a scene, a motive and a lie, the case that the police gave up. A basic success finds how it was done; a great success finds who did it and why.

Covers: reading a crime scene, a motive and an alibi; the case the police gave up; the logic behind a trap. Not: following a man, which is tracking, and noticing in the moment, which is awareness. Easy: tell how a door was forced. Medium: find the false wall in a Trick Tower room. Hard: work out who emptied the Underground Auction's vault before the sale. Very hard: find a killer among a ship's passengers by the timing of the deaths. Extremely hard: solve a case that two governments buried.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: emission
skills.info:
Emission: aura sent away from the body and kept alive at range, in shots, sent blows and the rare teleport. A basic success lands a shot; a great success keeps an emitted thing alive and working far from its maker.

Covers: aura sent away from the body: shots, sent blows, aura kept alive at range, the rare teleport between two marks. Not: the object a shot is made of, which is conjuration, and the throw of a real weapon, which is thrown-weapons. Easy: push a ball of aura a few metres across a room. Medium: send a punch through a portal to land far away, as Leorio Paradinight did. Hard: fire a stream of aura bullets from your fingers, as Franklin Bordeau did. Very hard: keep an emitted creature working while you sleep. Extremely hard: loose a rain of aura shots that wrecks a whole building from a hilltop away.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: endurance
skills.info:
Enduring: the long run, hunger, cold, pain and the fight that will not end. A basic success keeps going; a great success keeps going when everyone else has dropped.

Covers: enduring: the long run, hunger, cold, pain, poison and the fight that will not end. Not: strength, which is might, and fear, which is resolve. Easy: walk all day without a meal. Medium: follow an examiner through a tunnel for eighty kilometres. Hard: stay awake three nights on watch. Very hard: keep fighting with a broken arm. Extremely hard: keep fighting with an arm torn off, as Hisoka Morow did at Heavens Arena.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: enhancement
skills.info:
Enhancement: aura that makes the body or an object stronger, tougher and faster to heal. A basic success hits like a hammer; a great success breaks rock with a fist.

Covers: making the body or an object stronger, tougher and quicker to heal; the most balanced category in a fight, whose share runs through every clash. Not: pure strength with no aura, which is might, and aura shaped into another property, which is transmutation. Easy: break a rock that would bruise your hand. Medium: take a blade on the forearm and keep the arm. Hard: throw Gon Freecss's Rock, a fist with all the aura on it. Very hard: punch a crater metres wide into the desert floor, as Uvogin did. Extremely hard: stand in the blast of an anti-tank missile and walk out of the smoke, as Uvogin did.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: firearms
skills.info:
Pistols, rifles and the machine guns of the Mafia's soldiers and the royal armies. A basic success hits a target that is not moving; a great success hits one that is, from a moving car.

Covers: pistols, rifles, machine guns and the soldier's drill with them: the Mafia's hired guns, the royal armies, the guard at the door. Not: a thrown weapon, which is thrown-weapons, and aura bullets, which is emission. Easy: hit a bottle at twenty paces. Medium: hit a man running across a hotel lobby. Hard: keep a machine gun firing on a crowd of attackers from a moving car. Very hard: shoot the lock off a vault without hitting the lot inside. Extremely hard: hit a sniper's window from a moving airship.

Primary Attribute: Speed

skills.name: games
skills.info:
Games of every kind: Gungi, cards, dice, rock-paper-scissors, the rules of a game played for real and the trick hidden in them. A basic success wins a fair game; a great success wins one that was rigged against you.

Covers: Gungi, cards, dice, rock-paper-scissors, wagers, the rules of a game played for real, and the trap hidden in those rules. Not: a lie in the game, which is deception, and the Nen in a game, which is that user's category. Easy: win a hand of cards in a ferry bar. Medium: win a candle game in Trick Tower. Hard: win a dodgeball match against a team of Nen users on Greed Island. Very hard: beat a casino's dealer at his own table. Extremely hard: beat a national champion at Gungi.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: gourmet
skills.info:
The Gourmet Hunter's field: cooking, rare ingredients and where to find them, the palate that knows a dish at one taste. A basic success cooks a meal a traveller would pay for; a great success cooks one an examiner would pass.

Covers: cooking, rare ingredients and where they live, the palate, the dish that passes an examiner, and the poachers who steal them. Not: a poison in the food, which is poisons, and the beast itself, which is beast-lore. Easy: roast a whole pig over a fire on the trail. Medium: make a dish an examiner finishes, as the Great Stamp roast was finished. Hard: boil a Spider Eagle egg fetched from a canyon web. Very hard: make sushi for a Gourmet Hunter who knows it better than you. Extremely hard: find and cook an ingredient no menu in the world has served.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: hacking
skills.info:
The Hacker Hunter's field: computers, the networks of Cyberspace, the Hunters' Tavern site and the paths a file leaves. A basic success finds what is posted; a great success finds what was deleted.

Covers: computers, networks, Cyberspace, the Hunters' Tavern site, data recovery and the footprints a search leaves. Not: a cipher on paper, which is paleography, and a face-to-face source, which is streetwise. Easy: find a public record on the network. Medium: buy a name and an address from the Hunters' Tavern. Hard: pull a deleted file from a phone. Very hard: track a target's every move across the networks without leaving your room. Extremely hard: break into a government's sealed archive and leave no trace.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: hatsu
skills.info:
Building and keeping a personal ability: its idea, its conditions, its vows and limitations, and the Water Divination that names a user's category. A basic success keeps an ability's rules straight; a great success makes a vow that turns a modest ability into a deadly one.

Covers: the idea for a personal ability and its build; conditions that cannot be broken; vows and limitations that make an ability stronger and the toll for breaking them; Water Divination and the chart of the six categories; the Divine Script. Not: the strength of a category's effect, which is that category's skill, and the aura spent, which is ren. Easy: make the leaf move or the water change in Water Divination. Medium: name your ability and its first condition. Hard: draw a Divine Script and fight inside it as the Pirate boxer did. Very hard: make a vow that doubles an ability's power. Extremely hard: cut off your own fingers to make your shots stronger, as Franklin Bordeau did.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: lore
skills.info:
What the world knows: the nations and their laws, the Hunter Association's history and bylaws, the old peoples and the stories about the Dark Continent. A basic success recalls what any well-read traveller knows; a great success recalls what the records were meant to lose.

Covers: the nations and their laws, the Hunter Association's history and bylaws, the old peoples, the great families and the stories about the Dark Continent. Not: a cipher, which is paleography, and the street's rules, which is streetwise. Easy: name the great powers of the V5. Medium: recite the Hunter Bylaws from memory. Hard: tell the Kurta Clan's story and why their eyes are hunted. Very hard: know where Meteor City is said to have begun. Extremely hard: know what the oldest Hunters say about the voyages to the Dark Continent.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: manipulation
skills.info:
Manipulation: control of a living thing, an object or a construct through a medium the user has owned for years. A basic success moves the medium as the user wills; a great success takes a person over.

Covers: control through a medium the user has owned for years: needles, antennas, smoke, a phone, a puppet; control of a living thing by planting the medium; the harder the condition, the stronger the hold. Not: an object made from aura, which is conjuration, and a lie told to a person, which is deception. Easy: move a coin you have carried for years without touching it. Medium: throw a needle that makes a man take one step he did not choose. Hard: hold several people at once through a medium planted in each. Very hard: drive a stranger's body from a phone through a planted antenna, as Shalnark did. Extremely hard: work the bodies of the dead so well that their own guards are fooled.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: medicine
skills.info:
Doctoring: first aid, surgery, disease and the long care of the wounded, the field of the Disease Hunter and the would-be doctor. A basic success stabilises; a great success saves someone the other doctors had given up.

Covers: first aid, surgery, disease and long care; the doctor's licence and the Disease Hunter's search for cures. Not: a poison's chemistry, which is poisons, and healing by Nen, which is that user's category. Easy: bind a cut and set a sprain. Medium: treat a ship's crew through a storm's injuries. Hard: keep a man with a crushed chest alive until a hospital. Very hard: run a clinic for a whole ship's deck. Extremely hard: find the cure for a disease the world calls incurable.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: might
skills.info:
Raw strength: lifting, breaking, pushing, holding. A basic success moves what a strong man could; a great success moves a door built to keep strong men out.

Covers: raw strength: lifting, breaking, pushing, holding. Not: a fist in a fight, which is unarmed, and aura in the body, which is enhancement. Easy: carry a wounded friend down a mountain. Medium: force open a locked cell door. Hard: open the first door of the Testing Gate. Very hard: pull a car out of a ditch with your hands. Extremely hard: open the fifth door of the Testing Gate.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: music
skills.info:
The Music Hunter's field: instruments, songs, rare scores and the ear that hears more than notes. A basic success plays a piece that moves a room; a great success hears a lie in a heartbeat.

Covers: instruments, songs, rare scores, the Music Hunter's ear; hearing a heartbeat, a mood and a lie in a body's sound. Not: talk across a table, which is negotiation, and holding your own nerve, which is resolve. Easy: play a tune that quiets a room. Medium: hear a frightened heart in a calm face. Hard: calm an enraged comrade and an anxious team with a flute, as Melody did. Very hard: hear a lie in a speaker's heartbeat across a room. Extremely hard: find a score whose music, the stories say, is cursed.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: negotiation
skills.info:
Talk across a table: a deal, a contract, a bribe, a plea, a hostage exchange. A basic success gets a hearing and a fair price; a great success gets terms the other side swore they would never give.

Covers: deals, contracts, bargains, bribes, hostage exchanges, and an honest plea across a table. Not: a lie, which is deception, and an order, which is command. Easy: haggle a fare down in a port. Medium: sell a game at a better price than the dealer offered. Hard: win a rich collector's contract to clear a game. Very hard: talk a Mafia boss into hiring a stranger. Extremely hard: talk a hostage exchange into going your way.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: nen
skills.info:
Nen itself: opening the aura nodes, holding Ten, seeing aura, Gyo to the eyes, En spread around the body and Shu laid over a weapon. A basic success keeps the guard up and the eyes open; a great success feels everything in a room and reads another user's flow.

Covers: the aura nodes opened and closed at will; Ten held around the body, even in sleep; seeing aura; Gyo to the eyes; En spread around the body; Shu over a held object; reading another user's flow and the telltales of a Nen user. aura is invisible to anyone whose nodes are shut, and the world at large hears of it only as rumour. Not: aura pushed out to fight, which is ren, and the presence hidden, which is zetsu. Easy: hold Ten so another user's aura no longer chills you. Medium: use Gyo to read the number Biscuit wrote in hidden aura. Hard: spread En past two metres and hold it for a minute. Very hard: lay Shu over a shovel and dig through rock as Biscuit's students did. Extremely hard: spread En as wide as Zeno Zoldyck, three hundred metres around the body.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: ninja
skills.info:
The Cloud-Hidden Style of Jappon: shadowing, the hidden blade, the strike to a pressure point and the long patience of a spy. A basic success shadows a target or drops a guard; a great success does both and is gone before anyone turns.

Covers: the Cloud-Hidden Style of Jappon: shadowing, the hidden blade, pressure points, holding a man down and the spy's patience. Not: the Zoldyck arts, which is assassination, and a plain lie, which is deception. Easy: shadow a man through a market. Medium: hide a blade in a sleeve through a search. Hard: knock out a cell guard and reach the prisoner unseen, as Hanzo did. Very hard: pin a candidate and twist his arm until he submits. Extremely hard: guard a prince on a ship of assassins and never be seen at work.

Primary Attribute: Speed

skills.name: paleography
skills.info:
The Paleograph Hunter's field: dead languages, old scripts and ciphers, the Hunter Code among them. A basic success reads an old hand; a great success reads a tongue no one has spoken for a thousand years.

Covers: dead languages, old scripts, ciphers and codes: Ancient Kappe, the Hunter Code, the old alphabets. Not: the ruin the script is carved on, which is ruins, and a computer's code, which is hacking. Easy: read a Hunter Code message left on a wall. Medium: translate a page of an old script with a dictionary. Hard: read a letter written in Ancient Kappe. Very hard: break a cipher a king's court used for a century. Extremely hard: read a language no one has spoken in a thousand years.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: poisons
skills.info:
The Poison Hunter's field: venoms, toxins, paralytics and their cures, and the trained body that shrugs them off. A basic success names a poison by its signs; a great success makes or breaks one.

Covers: venoms, toxins, paralytics and their antidotes; the body trained against them; poisoning cases and their analysis. Not: medicine for the wounded, which is medicine, and plants in general, which is botany. Easy: smell a drugged drink. Medium: name the toxin from a victim's colour and breath. Hard: spot the laxative Tonpa slipped into a can of juice. Very hard: shrug off a poison that would kill an ordinary man, as a Zoldyck does. Extremely hard: make an antidote in the field for a toxin no doctor has seen.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: ren
skills.info:
Pushing aura out: Ren, Ken held as a guard, Ko poured into one fist, Ryu shifted in the middle of an exchange, and the bloodlust that freezes a room. A basic success hits harder and takes a hit better; a great success wins the exchange on aura alone.

Covers: Ren pushed out from the body; Ken held as an even guard; Ko poured into one point; Ryu shifting aura from guard to blow mid-exchange; the bloodlust that freezes an unguarded person; holding Ren for hours. Not: the shape a personal ability takes, which is hatsu, and the body's own strength, which is might. Easy: show your Ren to a teacher who asks for it. Medium: hold Ken for thirty minutes as Biscuit demands. Hard: freeze a room of thugs with bloodlust alone. Very hard: spar Flowing Dance and shift Ryu faster than your opponent can read it, as Biscuit Krueger's students did. Extremely hard: hold Ren for three hours without a break.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: resolve
skills.info:
Holding steady: fear, pain, grief, another user's bloodlust, a threat whispered in a dark room. A basic success holds; a great success holds and moves anyway.

Covers: holding steady: fear, pain, grief, another user's bloodlust, a threat in a dark room. Not: a body that will not quit, which is endurance, and the guard against aura, which is nen. Easy: keep your nerve on a stormy crossing. Medium: face an examiner's bloodlust and not run. Hard: sit through the Zoldyck torture room and keep your name. Very hard: stand before a Phantom Troupe member and say no. Extremely hard: walk toward an enemy whose aura alone has dropped stronger fighters.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: ruins
skills.info:
The Ruins Hunter's field: finding, reading, restoring and protecting the remains of lost peoples. A basic success dates a ruin and finds its door; a great success brings a dead city back to the light.

Covers: ruins and the peoples who left them: finding, dating, restoring and guarding a site; the Ruins Hunter's long work. Not: an old script on a wall, which is paleography, and the price a relic fetches, which is appraisal. Easy: find the hidden door of a tomb. Medium: date a ruin by its stonework. Hard: map a buried city through a jungle. Very hard: restore a ruin so well its old builders' purpose shows again, as Ging Freecss did at the Lurka Ruins. Extremely hard: find a site the world believed was a legend.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: seafaring
skills.info:
The Sea Hunter's field: ships, storms, tides and the creatures and wrecks under the water. A basic success keeps a boat on course; a great success brings it through a storm the crew swore would sink it.

Covers: ships, storms, tides and harbours; diving; the creatures and wrecks of the sea; the long voyage. Not: living off an island, which is wildcraft, and creatures on land, which is beast-lore. Easy: tie a ship's lines in a harbour. Medium: read the sky and call the storm before the Captain does. Hard: keep the exam ship afloat through a night storm. Very hard: dive a wreck for a sunken treasure. Extremely hard: bring a ship through waters no chart covers.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: shingen-ryu
skills.info:
The Shingen-ryu school of kung fu, which teaches the body and the aura together: the stance, the strike, the etiquette and the Nen of the Flame. A basic success lands a clean blow; a great success reads the opponent's aura and strikes where the guard is thin.

Covers: the Shingen-ryu school of kung fu: stance, strike, etiquette, Flowing Dance sparring, and Nen taught slowly through the Nen of the Flame. Not: a street brawl, which is unarmed, and aura pushed out in a fight, which is ren. Easy: bow and hold the opening stance through a full lesson. Medium: win your way to the fiftieth floor of Heavens Arena on Shingen-ryu form, as Zushi did. Hard: spar a round of Flowing Dance and keep your guard. Very hard: teach a student the Nen of the Flame, as Wing did. Extremely hard: fight as the school's grandmaster fought, with the speed won from ten thousand prayers and punches a day.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: specialization
skills.info:
Specialization: Nen that fits no other category, rare and all or nothing. A basic success makes the ability work at all; a great success makes it do something the world's rules said could not be done.

Covers: whatever fits no other category: prophecy, theft, memory, the abilities that break the world's rules; all or nothing, and open to a player only in what-if modes. Not: a Conjurer's or a Manipulator's ability with odd conditions, which is that category. Easy: feel that your Water Divination does something no chart names. Medium: write a fortune in verse that comes true, as Neon Nostrade did. Hard: read a memory from a man's body with one touch. Very hard: fire a memory into a friend's mind as a bullet. Extremely hard: keep a book of abilities taken from others, as Chrollo Lucilfer does.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: stealth
skills.info:
Moving unseen and unheard: the step that makes no sound, the shadow, the crowd, the empty corridor at night. A basic success passes the careless; a great success passes someone who is looking.

Covers: moving unseen and unheard: the step, the shadow, the crowd, the empty corridor, and sneaking past a guard dog. Not: hiding aura, which is zetsu, and the Zoldyck silent step, which is assassination. Easy: slip out of a hotel at night. Medium: pass a doorman unseen. Hard: cross a mansion's grounds past its guards. Very hard: walk into a Mafia auction hall with no ticket. Extremely hard: move through an assassin family's estate without the butlers knowing.

Primary Attribute: Speed

skills.name: streetwise
skills.info:
The underworld and the back street: the Mafia Community's rules, who sells what, which door is safe and which name not to say. A basic success finds the right contact; a great success gets a favour from someone who should have refused.

Covers: the underworld: the Mafia Community's rules, fences, hiring halls, black markets, and the city that keeps no records. Not: a court's law, which is lore, and the worth of a lot, which is appraisal. Easy: find a cheap room in Yorknew City. Medium: find the hidden hiring hall behind a slum doorway. Hard: buy a gun with no serial number. Very hard: get a meeting with a don's underboss. Extremely hard: walk out of Meteor City with a favour owed.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: thrown-weapons
skills.info:
Cards, needles, darts, tops and yo-yos: the throw that lands and the one that comes back. A basic success hits what was aimed at; a great success pins a sleeve across a room or bends a throw around a corner.

Covers: cards, needles, darts, tops, yo-yos and the blowgun: the throw that lands and the one that returns. Not: a firearm, which is firearms, and a weapon in the hand, which is weapons or blades. Easy: hit a can at twenty paces with a pebble. Medium: throw a playing card hard enough to cut, as Hisoka Morow does. Hard: paralyse a man with a blowgun dart, as Geretta did. Very hard: swing a fifty-kilogram yo-yo like a toy, as Killua Zoldyck does. Extremely hard: pin a man to a wall by throwing needles through his clothes from across a hall.

Primary Attribute: Speed

skills.name: tracking
skills.info:
Following a quarry by sign, scent, broken ground and the tail of a crowd. A basic success finds the trail; a great success follows a tail who knows he is followed.

Covers: following a quarry by sign, scent, broken ground, a car's route and the tail of a crowd. Not: noticing an ambush, which is awareness, and hunting a wanted man's record, which is bounty-hunting. Easy: follow footprints through a forest. Medium: follow a scent through Milsy Wetlands' fog to a friend, as Gon Freecss did. Hard: find your badge's target on Zevil Island. Very hard: tail half the Phantom Troupe through a city without being seen. Extremely hard: track a quarry who knows how to hide his aura.

Primary Attribute: Wit

skills.name: transmutation
skills.info:
Transmutation: aura given the properties of something else, such as electricity, rubber or gum. A basic success gives the aura a property and holds it; a great success turns that property into a weapon no one sees coming.

Covers: giving aura the properties of something else, such as electricity, rubber or gum, and keeping that property under control; pure aura, invisible to those who cannot see aura. Not: a material object made from aura, which is conjuration, and moving another thing by aura, which is manipulation. Easy: make your aura feel sticky or hot to the touch. Medium: stun a man with aura turned to electricity. Hard: stick a thread of elastic aura to a falling foe and pull him back. Very hard: stitch a severed arm back on with aura thread, as Machi Komacine did. Extremely hard: run as fast as a lightning bolt on electric aura, as Killua Zoldyck did.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

skills.name: unarmed
skills.info:
Fists, kicks, throws and holds: the ring, the street and the lower floors of Heavens Arena. A basic success lands or escapes; a great success knocks a trained fighter out of the ring.

Covers: fists, kicks, throws, holds and headbutts; the lower floors of Heavens Arena; the street fight and the prison yard. Not: a school's form, which is shingen-ryu, and the Zoldyck claws, which is assassination. Easy: win a scuffle on a ferry deck. Medium: climb the first fifty floors of Heavens Arena on your fists. Hard: push a man out of the ring with one shove. Very hard: beat a 200th-floor fighter without Nen. Extremely hard: win a fight to the death in a locked room.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: weapons
skills.info:
Clubs, staffs, poles and whatever reaches: a fishing rod, a pipe, a spear, a paper fan. A basic success keeps a foe at the length of the weapon; a great success turns a tool nobody feared into the thing that wins.

Covers: clubs, staffs, poles, spears and odd tools used as weapons: a fishing rod, a pipe, a paper fan, a spinning top. Not: a blade, which is blades, and a thrown weapon, which is thrown-weapons. Easy: fend off a dog with a fishing rod. Medium: snatch a badge off its owner with a fishing line, as Gon Freecss did on Zevil Island. Hard: beat a spearman with a staff. Very hard: fight with tops that spin around a ring, as Gido did. Extremely hard: cut a man down with a storm of paper from a fan, as Kalluto Zoldyck did.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: wildcraft
skills.info:
Living off the land: swamp, forest, desert and island; water, shelter, fire and food without a road. A basic success keeps a party fed and dry; a great success crosses the worst ground alive.

Covers: living off the land: swamp, forest, desert, island and mountain; fire, shelter, water and food without a road. Not: the creatures met on the way, which is beast-lore, and the plants by name, which is botany. Easy: fish your supper from a lake. Medium: find shelter in a forest storm. Hard: live a week on Zevil Island while others hunt you. Very hard: cross the Gordeau Desert on foot. Extremely hard: keep a party alive in a land where every creature hunts.

Primary Attribute: Body

skills.name: zetsu
skills.info:
Closing every node: the presence that vanishes, the In that hides a technique, the rest that refills the body. A basic success passes unnoticed by those who are not looking; a great success hides a technique from a master who is.

Covers: every node shut: presence gone, the body resting and recovering; In, the advanced Zetsu that hides a technique; slipping past En and past a tracker who reads aura. Not: seeing a hidden technique, which is nen, and moving without sound, which is stealth. Easy: sit in Zetsu until a sleeping dog no longer wakes. Medium: follow a target through a crowded street in Zetsu. Hard: hide a thrown thread from a user who is not using Gyo. Very hard: pass through a watcher's En without a ripple. Extremely hard: hide your presence from a Phantom Troupe member searching the room.

Primary Attribute: Spirit

lowText.body: A weak frame. An eighty-kilometre run behind an examiner is beyond you, a heavy door will not move for you, and a blow that a trained fighter shrugs off puts you down; the first Testing Gate stays shut.
lowText.speed: Slow hands and slow feet. A thrown card reaches you before you move, a pickpocket is gone before you turn, and on a narrow ledge or a falling floor you are always the last one off.
lowText.wit: A slow read. A trick question catches you, a forged map takes you the wrong way, a game's rules hide their trap from you, and a liar's story holds together until it is too late.
lowText.spirit: A thin will and a thin aura. Another fighter's bloodlust freezes you where you stand, fear and pain take the wheel, and whatever life force you carry leaks away faster than you can hold it.

lore.name: A Hunter's licence to kill
lore.info: A licence greatly reduces its holder's legal liability for killing. A Hunter who kills in the course of a hunt is rarely charged. The protection has limits: repeated killing without cause, or an attack on an envoy of a political authority, can still bring prosecution, and a Hunter who commits a heinous crime becomes fair game for other Hunters.

lore.name: A licence once lost
lore.info: The Association never revokes a licence and never reissues one. A Hunter who loses the card has lost it for life, and cannot sit the exam again. Thieves and swindlers know what a card is worth, and about one new Hunter in five loses theirs within the first year. The older Hunters keep the card on their body and tell rookies to do the same.

lore.name: Amateur Hunters
lore.info: Six young people with no licence and no money who hunt, track and catalogue living things under a professional Hunter named Kite: Spinner Clow, Stick Dinner, Banana Kavaro, Lin Koshi, Monta Yuras and Podungo Lapoy. Kite was the first adult who listened to them, and he bought Spin and Stick a house so they could protect the small-billed swans nesting there. The Kakin Empire has hired the crew for a long biological survey of new species. A stranger meets them as campers with notebooks and good food; one who joins carries packs and learns to watch before touching.

lore.name: Ancestors from the Dark Continent
lore.info: Scholars who read old myths and dig in ancient ruins have come to an awkward conclusion: humanity did not start here. The oldest stories and the oldest stones point to a migration from somewhere beyond the known seas, and many researchers think the Magical Beasts came the same way. The same artefacts carry a warning. Every time people went back, the records say, disaster followed them home. Nobody outside a few archives knows what kind of disaster, and the archives do not lend their books.

lore.name: Ancient Kappe
lore.info: Ancient Kappe is a dead language, a thicket of words beginning with N, that only a handful of scholars and Ruins Hunters can still speak. Specialists challenge one another to word contests in it, and few of them last long.

lore.name: Animals as weapons
lore.info: Not every fighter carries steel. Some keep bees under a hat, snakes in a basket or leeches in their own body, and train them to attack on command; some command flocks of birds. Hunters meeting a stranger with too many animals about them keep their distance until they know which kind of trainer it is.

lore.name: Aura
lore.info: Aura flows from every living thing and is tied to its stamina: a tired body makes less, a dying one almost none. It leaves the body through aura nodes all over the skin. In an untrained person the nodes stay nearly shut, and the aura seeps away a little at a time; a person whose nodes are thrown wide open without the skill to close them bleeds aura until they collapse. A lost limb or a deep wound can stop the flow in that part of the body.

lore.name: Battera
lore.info: Battera is a multi-billionaire who has spent much of his fortune buying copies of Greed Island and hiring people to beat it. He outbids everyone at every auction where a copy appears, rarely explains himself, and pays well. People who have worked for him say he is in a hurry.

lore.name: Battera's Castle
lore.info: Battera keeps his copies of Greed Island in the basement of an old castle on a cliff: thirty-two consoles in a row, each with a player's save. The upper floors are furnished like a museum and guarded like a bank, and its security system is known to kill people who wander off the path. Players he hires enter the game from there.

lore.name: Battera's players
lore.info: The Hunters and adventurers hired by Battera, an old billionaire who has bought up every copy of the game Greed Island he can find and keeps the consoles in the basement of his castle. Since 1988 he has offered a famous reward to anyone who clears the game, and he uses his money to keep its details out of the press. Tsezguerra, a Jackpot Hunter, runs his tryouts and turns away nearly everyone. Of the more than a hundred Hunters he has sent in, few have come back. A stranger meets the company as an advertisement or a test in a hotel ballroom; one who joins signs a contract and is sent into the game.

lore.name: Battera's search for Greed Island
lore.info: In 1988 a tycoon named Battera began buying every copy of an expensive, out-of-print game called Greed Island and offering rewards to anyone who would play it for him, with a fortune promised to whoever beat it. He has paid ever since. Strong people go to his castle, sit down at a console and vanish, and many never come back. The rewards keep rising, and the business pages call it a rich man's obsession. Hunters who know what the game is call it something worse.

lore.name: Battle Olympia
lore.info: Every two years Heavens Arena holds the Battle Olympia on its two hundred and fifty-first floor, a tournament open only to Floor Masters. The winner takes the penthouse on that floor. The arena uses it in every advertisement to tempt new fighters into the ground-floor queue.

lore.name: Ben's knives
lore.info: About a hundred years ago a blacksmith named Benny Delon forged a knife after each person he murdered, numbered it, and put it up for sale in his shop alongside ordinary blades. There are two hundred and eighty-eight. They are terribly sharp, collectors treat them as works of art, and those who handle them say the smith's presence still clings to the steel.

lore.name: Beyond's announcement
lore.info: On 10 August 2000 a man named Beyond Netero, the late Chairman's son, put a video on EyeTube announcing an expedition to the Dark Continent, in open defiance of the treaty, and asking anyone brave enough to join him. It passed a hundred million views in an hour. The same day Kakin's king declared his own voyage, and Beyond surrendered himself to the Hunter Association's Zodiacs to sail under their guard. Every government had to decide by nightfall what it thought of the idea.

lore.name: Biscuit Krueger
lore.info: Biscuit Krueger is a two-star Stone Hunter, a gem expert and a master of Shingen-ryu, who taught Wing among others. She looks like a little girl with ribbons and has looked like one for decades. She prefers to be called Bisky. People who underestimate her generally do it only once.

lore.name: Blacklist Hunters
lore.info: Blacklist Hunters track wanted criminals for bounties and for the law. Their quarry kills back, so they are among the toughest Hunters alive, and some of them are hardly better than the people they hunt. They read every bounty posted in the world and know which ones to leave alone: veterans let the Phantom Troupe's class A bounties pass, and the party of Blacklist Hunters that once went up Kukuroo Mountain after the Zoldycks is a story the family's tour guides still tell.

lore.name: Bloodlust
lore.info: Aura carries feeling. A trained user who directs real malice at someone pushes out a pressure that the target feels on the skin like cold, a wall in the air, an animal certainty of danger. Ordinary people freeze or faint under a strong user's bloodlust, and hostile aura can stop a non-user in their tracks as though they had walked into a wall. Hunters learn to read it the way sailors read the sky.

lore.name: Botobai Gigante
lore.info: Botobai Gigante is a three-star Terrorist Hunter and the eldest of the Zodiacs, a huge, grave man whose word carries weight in every Association quarrel. For the voyage he serves on its defence team.

lore.name: Bounties and classes
lore.info: Wanted criminals are posted with a bounty and a class, and the class tells Blacklist Hunters how dangerous the quarry is. A class A bounty marks the worst of the worst, people whom even veteran Hunters decline to chase. The Phantom Troupe all carry class A bounties. A political criminal can be posted class A too, if a government wants them badly enough.

lore.name: Camp Tiger
lore.info: The Camp Tiger is a horned tiger of Kakin's forests, found on a wildlife survey. It spears its prey on its horn and cooks it over a fire, which means it knows how to make one. Beast Hunters who hear of it want to see it; travellers who hear of it want to stay in the city.

lore.name: Cha-R Family
lore.info: One of the three great Mafia families of Kakin, led by Brocco Li, the king's half-brother, who rides as a guest on the first tier. About two hundred and fifty of its men are aboard the Black Whale, where they control the fifth tier and everything sold on it; their patron is the seventh prince, Luzurus. Ken'i Wang is the underboss. The family thanks the Phantom Troupe for Yorknew, which handed Kakin's families the new continent, and would still rather the Spiders left its deck. A stranger meets the Cha-R as the people who sell bread and beds on the bottom tier.

lore.name: Charities of the known world
lore.info: Not everything in the world is crime and war. The Norwell Fund supports the families of mercenaries killed in battle through a chain of trusted accounts, begun by a soldier who gave his pay to child soldiers and refugees. Mom's Help rescues poor children; its chairman, Risnorth, was murdered in 1991, and the case still makes the news on its anniversaries.

lore.name: Cheadle Yorkshire
lore.info: Cheadle Yorkshire is a three-star Disease Hunter and the Zodiac called Dog, a severe, precise woman who trusts rules more than people. After the thirteenth election she became the fourteenth Chairwoman of the Hunter Association, and she leads it aboard the Black Whale.

lore.name: Chimera Ants
lore.info: Chimera Ants are a giant breed whose queen grows her young from what she eats, so that each new soldier carries the traits of its food. Fed on beasts, they are beasts. In 2000 a queen washed up in NGL and fed on people, and her children came out smart, strong and able to use weapons. After the crisis the Hunter Association rated the species a threat of class B. Beast Hunters now watch every coast for the next one.

lore.name: Chrollo against Hisoka
lore.info: In the summer of 2001, between the 289th Hunter Exam and the Black Whale's departure, Heavens Arena hosted a fight that fans still argue about: a deathmatch on the top floors between two Floor Masters, the magician Hisoka and a man registered as Chrollo. The upper floors were wrecked and the result was murky. Rumour says the winner left the tower alive and the loser did not; other rumours say the reverse.

lore.name: Chrollo Lucilfer
lore.info: Chrollo Lucilfer is the founder and head of the Phantom Troupe, a quiet man who reads constantly and has a cross tattooed on his forehead. Very few people know his face, and those who do rarely live to describe it. He carries a class A bounty like every member of his Troupe.

lore.name: Clean Leaf
lore.info: Clean Leaf is a plant drug sold as the healthy alternative: less harmful than most, smoked by some to get off worse habits. Growing, holding or using it needs a licence, and its legal status changes from one border to the next. Bodyguards on long watches are said to like it.

lore.name: Conditional auctions
lore.info: Yorknew's stranger sales include the conditional auctions, where a seller asks not for money but for a deed: catch this, find that, bring proof of something. The first bidder to meet the condition takes the lot. They draw dreamers and fools, and now and then someone wins.

lore.name: Conditions and vows
lore.info: A Nen ability works by rules. Some are conditions, part of what the ability is, which cannot be broken at all. Others are limitations a user chooses to swear to, and the stricter the rule, the stronger the ability. A vow can be broken, and breaking it can take the ability away or wreck the user's whole Nen. Users who stake their own lives on a rule draw the most power of all. Teachers warn that vows are an unreliable source of strength and the price is always paid.

lore.name: Counting the years
lore.info: The known world keeps the ordinary calendar of twelve months, and its newspapers date things by the year. People date their lives by the big events: the year of the bumper exam, the year Yorknew burned, the year the Ants came, the year the old Chairman died, the year Kakin sailed. Hunters count by exams instead, the 287th, the 288th, the 289th, and ask a stranger which one they passed before they ask anything else.

lore.name: Dark Continent Expedition Team
lore.info: The expedition announced on 10 August 2000 by Beyond Netero, son of the late chairman, under the patronage of Kakin's king: a voyage to the Dark Continent in open defiance of the treaty. Its members are about twenty-five Temp Hunters and the mercenaries of Stone Wall, a legendary unit of eleven that came out of the Lubo Civil War without a single loss; Muherr commands in the field. Beyond surrendered to the Zodiacs on the day of the announcement and sails under their guard. A stranger meets the team as men in uniform on the Black Whale and a face on every news channel.

lore.name: Dino Hunter
lore.info: The Swashbuckling Adventures of Dino Hunter is a children's adventure book about a hero who goes everywhere no one has been. Copies turn up in the oddest places, Meteor City included, read to pieces by children who dream of being Hunters.

lore.name: District: East Gorteau
lore.info: East Gorteau is one of the parts of the known world as this map draws it. The Republic of East Gorteau at the Union's eastern end, a closed dictatorship under its Supreme Leader, whose palace stands in the wilderness outside the capital, Peijin. Informers are rewarded for denouncing neighbours, the rich live well and most people do not, and foreigners are rarely let in. lore.info: Gordeau Desert and the outskirts is one of the parts of the known world as this map draws it. The dry wasteland outside Yorknew City, crossed by the highway to Lingon Airport, and the empty buildings on the city's edge where nobody asks who is staying. Cars cross the desert in an hour and a half; anything that happens out among the rocks is seen by nobody. lore.info: Greed Island is one of the parts of the known world as this map draws it. The world of the game Greed Island and the castle where a billionaire keeps the consoles that open it. A player who enters wakes in a tower on a grassy plain and plays for the game's cards in towns of prizes, magic, love, gambling and pirates. Only those who can see a certain energy can play at all, and those who die in the game do not come back. Thousands of fighters climb its floors every day for prize money and fame, and the crowds who come to watch fill its hotels, shops and restaurants. The Kakin Empire in the middle of the Azian Continent, more than a billion people and growing richer every year, and the great ship Black Whale 1, built to carry the king's expedition to the New Continent. The kingdom north of the Yorbian Continent where the 287th Hunter Exam is held: the landing port where applicants gather, the forest of the navigators, the swindlers' streets of Zaban City, and the wetlands, forests and split mountain the exam runs through. A junkyard city that appears on no map and in no record: millions of people living on what the rest of the world throws away, ruled by an assembly of elders. Its people keep no papers, take care of their own and answer an insult with a bomb. Outsiders who come for recruits or salvage come by its one road. The Republic of Rokario in the Balsa Islands, the modern country on the Mitene Union's western side, with its small crowded cities close to the closed border of NGL, its mountains and its desert, and east of it the Republic of Hass and the Republic of West Gorteau. The remote sites the exam carries its applicants to by airship and boat: a prison tower with no door in its walls, an island where applicants hunt each other's badges for a week, a hall where the last phase is fought, and the small city where a later year's exam began behind a shop. Few people live there and fewer children; the town by the harbour, the swamp inland and the old forest behind it are the whole of it. Ships call when the weather allows, and the open sea lies between the island and everywhere else. lore.name: District: Yorknew City

Every September its auction houses sell the rarest things in the world, the street markets sell everything else, and the Mafia's own auction runs behind closed doors. lore.name: Divine Script
lore.info: There is an old writing that strengthens Nen. A user who draws it and charges it with aura through hours of fierce concentration can use an ability far beyond their level, but only within the ground where the script is drawn. It is rarely seen and less often understood.

lore.name: Dolle Harbor
lore.info: Dolle Harbor is a big port in the Kukan'yu Kingdom, and in the last weeks of every December it fills with would-be Hunters. They come off the ships asking for Zaban City, and the locals send them up the mountain road with a smile, because the road is a test and most never come back down it.

lore.name: East Gorteau
lore.info: East Gorteau was a closed dictatorship at the eastern end of the Mitene Union, ruled by its Supreme Leader Ming Jol-ik, who held the government, the law and the army in one hand. Informants were rewarded for denouncing their neighbours, and its counter-espionage system was famous enough that the Hunter website sold notes on it. Five million people lived there. It is gone now.

lore.name: East Gorteau regime
lore.info: The dictatorship that rules the Republic of East Gorteau from Peijin, the capital, and from a palace in the wilderness outside it. Every power of state belongs to the Supreme Leader, Ming Jol-ik, born of a bloody revolt that made a new ruling class rich while most people stayed poor. Foreign aid goes on luxuries and weapons; rumour says the country cut every tie abroad to squeeze more aid, and that some of it pays for nuclear arms. A spy-catching system of informant groups rewards neighbours who report neighbours. A stranger meets the regime as a closed border and a portrait on every wall; one who serves it climbs by points earned informing.

lore.name: Egypersia and Yul
lore.info: Some countries are known abroad mainly for what has been taken from them. Egypersia's old tombs supply collectors with relics that should not be on the market. Yul keeps a national treasury, and one of its treasures, a solid gold executioner's sword, turned up at the Mafia's auction in 1999.

lore.name: Eight-legged dog
lore.info: In the woods outside Doli City lives a small, timid, cub-sized beast with eight legs and the head of a dog. It runs from people, and a hiker who meets one usually sees only its back.

lore.name: Electing a Chairman
lore.info: The Bylaws say the Chairman must hold the confidence of a majority of the Hunters, and that a vote must follow at once whenever the chair falls empty. The thirteenth election set its own rules: every Hunter votes, signed ballots only, and any round with turnout under ninety-five percent is held again. Hunters who had not voted in years found Cluck's birds at their windows with ballots.

lore.name: En
lore.info: En is Ren spread wide and shaped with Ten into a field, usually a sphere, inside which the user feels every movement and every presence. It is very tiring. A user who can hold a radius of two metres for a minute is said to have En; a master's reaches about fifty. Stories of fields hundreds of metres across are told about only a handful of people in the world.

lore.name: Examiners
lore.info: Hunter Exam examiners are licensed Hunters, usually experienced ones, and they work unpaid; being asked is an honour, and the Chairman settles any dispute between them. Each designs a phase out of their own speciality, so a Gourmet Hunter's phase is a cooking test and a ruins expert's is a race through tunnels. A candidate who clears the third phase earns a free place in the next year's exam if they fail later.

lore.name: EyeTube and Facebox
lore.info: The known world shares its videos on EyeTube and its opinions on Facebox. Beyond Netero's call to the Dark Continent passed a hundred million views on EyeTube in its first hour, and Kakin's princes keep Facebox pages where they praise or snub one another in public.

lore.name: Families and hierarchies
lore.info: Below the Ten Dons, the Mafia is a ladder of families serving families: the Ritz Family under one Don, the Nostrade Family under the Ritz, and so on down to street crews. A family rises by money, favours and luck. Bosses hire bodyguards who fight above their weight, and the best of those are Nen users, whom the bosses neither understand nor ask about.

lore.name: Flesh collectors
lore.info: A certain kind of rich collector buys parts of people: eyes, hands, mummies, tattooed skin, the hair of a famous beauty. The trade is illegal nearly everywhere and flourishes anyway, through the Mafia's auctions and private dealers. Its customers are often perfectly charming. Hunters who chase stolen remains learn the collectors' names before they learn the thieves'.

lore.name: Floor Masters
lore.info: The twenty-one highest ranked fighters of Heavens Arena, each given a whole floor of the tower between the 230th and the 250th. To challenge one, a fighter on the 200th floor must win ten matches before losing four, and a master who loses the challenge loses the floor. Every second year the masters fight in Battle Olympia for the penthouse on the 251st. Crowds pay to see these bouts and swear the fighters up there use some trick that throws men across the ring without a touch. A stranger meets them as a name on a poster; one who joins climbs the tower match by match.

lore.name: Floor Masters of the arena
lore.info: The twenty-one strongest fighters in Heavens Arena hold a floor each between the two hundred and thirtieth and the two hundred and fiftieth, and are called Floor Masters. They defend their floors against challengers who have won ten bouts above the two hundredth, and every two years they compete in the Battle Olympia on the top floor, whose champion lives in the penthouse.

lore.name: Flowing Dance
lore.info: Shingen-ryu's advanced students spar slowly, so slowly that a watcher sees two people moving through water. The Flowing Dance lets each fighter feel exactly how much aura to send where to meet each blow, and it perfects Ryu. It only works between partners of similar strength; against a master, a weaker student cannot defend even at that speed.

lore.name: Founding of the Hunter Association
lore.info: The Hunter Association is old, older than most of the governments that now rely on it. The first Hunter Exam on record was held in 1713, and the numbering has run unbroken since: the exam of January 1999 is the 287th. The Association answers to no single state. It began, the old Hunters say, as a way to tell the real thing from the braggarts: a test anyone could take, which almost nobody passed, and a card that the whole world agreed to honour. Eleven chairmen led it before the present one, and their names mean little now outside its archives.

lore.name: Foxbear
lore.info: Foxbears are big brown beasts, half fox and half bear, with red eyes and claws like knives. They live in Whale Island's Snakebeech Forest and guard their cubs fiercely. Islanders do not go into the forest alone. One local boy is said to have raised a foxbear cub himself after its mother died.

lore.name: Freelance Assassins
lore.info: Professional killers the Mafia hires for a single job when its own soldiers will not do. They meet in a hotel room, hear who the target is and how much the Dons will pay, and argue over whether to work together or alone; most work alone. None of them gives a real name. A stranger meets them as quiet men in good coats who leave town before the bodies are found.

lore.name: Freelance assassins
lore.info: When the Mafia needs something killed that its own men cannot kill, it hires freelancers, and the world's best assassins sell to whoever pays. In Yorknew in 1999 the Ten Dons hired a whole squad of them against the Phantom Troupe, Zoldycks among them. Most of the freelancers died that week; the Zoldycks collected their fee.

lore.name: Geniuses
lore.info: A few people find Nen alone, with no teacher and no word for it: a craftsman whose blades come out better than they should, a game player who sees moves no one else can, a fortune-teller whose predictions keep coming true. Such geniuses usually use Nen in one craft only and without knowing it. Hunters spot them by results.

lore.name: Ging Freecss
lore.info: Ging Freecss is a two-star Ruins Hunter who passed the Hunter Exam before he turned twelve and became famous for digging out the Lurka Ruins and the Congo Gold Vein almost alone. He could have a third star for the asking and has not asked. He was the Zodiac called Boar until he quit. Nobody can find him when they want to, and he has a son on Whale Island he has not seen since the boy was a baby.

lore.name: Great Stamp
lore.info: The Great Stamp is the world's most ferocious pig, a pink beast with a huge snout and teeth that crush bone, found in the Visca Forest Preserve. It charges anything that moves. Its snout hides a soft spot on its forehead, and a single blow there drops it; finding the spot is the trick. Roasted whole, it is said to be very good.

lore.name: Great universities
lore.info: The known world's schools have their own fame. Miwal University is considered the most prestigious in the world, and a Kakin prince studied there. Varvard has professors who join expeditions. Fānlīn Medical College trains surgeons the Hunter Association itself recommends.

lore.name: Greed Island
lore.info: Greed Island is a game for the JoyStation, released in 1987 in a small print run and long out of print. Copies sell at auction for billions. It is a game only Nen users can play: a player who starts it is pulled bodily into its world and released only by winning, by leaving through the game's own exits, or by dying, and a death in the game is a death in fact. Rumours of who made it are many.

lore.name: Greed Island's cards
lore.info: Inside Greed Island everything a player picks up turns into a card, monsters included. Saying "Gain" turns a card back into the thing it shows, but only once, and a card not put in the binder within a minute turns back for good. Each card has a rank from H to SS and a limit on how many copies can exist at once. The rarer the card, the fewer there are.

lore.name: Greed Island's towns
lore.info: Players who come back from Greed Island describe its towns like a holiday they barely survived. Antokiba, the town of prizes, holds a contest on the fifteenth of every month. Masadora, the magic city, is the only place to buy spell cards. Aiai is a city of love scenes, Dorias a city of casinos where children may gamble, Soufrabi a port held by pirates, and Limeiro the capital, where the game ends for those who win.

lore.name: Gungi
lore.info: Gungi is a two-player strategy board game from East Gorteau, where nearly everyone plays it. Pieces stack in towers, and its players will tell you it is deeper than chess. In the fifteen years the world championship has been held, no other country has taken the title; through the late nineties it belonged to a blind girl from a poor family named Komugi.

lore.name: Gyo and In
lore.info: Gyo moves aura into one part of the body. In the eyes, it shows what a user has hidden with In, the art of making aura and its constructs invisible even to a trained eye. A fight between experienced users is often a contest of the two: one hides a trap, the other remembers to look. Teachers drill Gyo by writing numbers in hidden aura and making the student read them.

lore.name: Hass and West Gorteau
lore.info: The Republic of Hass and the Republic of West Gorteau sit in the middle of the Mitene Union, ordinary republics that history mostly passes over. Since the summer of 2000 they hold slices of what was East Gorteau.

lore.name: Hatsu
lore.info: Hatsu is the release of aura in a way that belongs to one user alone: a power, a weapon, a beast, a rule. Teachers will not design one for a student; they wait until the student has the idea, because an ability that does not fit its owner's nature never works well. A copied ability can function, but the old saying is that a user who only copies never truly masters Nen. Hunters guard the details of their Hatsu more closely than their bank accounts.

lore.name: Have-Nots
lore.info: The lowest caste of the Kakin Empire, barred by an unchangeable caste law from public office and military rank. In ancient Kakin, princes who failed to become king were buried with afterlife companions to stop them turning into vengeful ghosts, and the companions were always chosen from the Have-Nots. The custom ended; the caste did not. Camilla, the second prince, has opened her private army to them, built them a ward on her land and given them a soldier's rights, and they now ask of their own accord to be her companions in death. A stranger meets them as servants who will not meet the eye.

lore.name: Heavens Arena
lore.info: Heavens Arena is the fourth-tallest building in the world, 991 metres and 251 floors, and the most popular fighting venue on earth. It stands on the same continent as Padokea, on the far side. Thousands fight there every day for prize money and a higher floor, crowds fill the stands, and a town of hotels and souvenir stalls has grown up around its base. Children have climbed it. So have killers.

lore.name: Heavens Arena's ladder
lore.info: Heavens Arena takes about four thousand fighters a day. A newcomer fights on the ground floor and, by winning, is sent up in steps of ten floors at a time. Every floor below the two hundredth pays prize money, more at each level, and from the hundredth the fighter gets a private room. Weapons are banned below the two hundredth. A child who wins enough can climb to the hundred and ninety-ninth and walk away rich.

lore.name: Heil-Ly Family
lore.info: The smallest and strangest of Kakin's three great Mafia families, led by Morena Prudo, the king's illegitimate daughter, who came up from a junior member to take the family in a coup. On the Black Whale the family is based on the third tier and earns its money by brokering secret deals with the upper decks; its patron is the fourth prince, Tserriednich. Its members are few, about twenty, and unusually loyal to their boss. A stranger meets them as polite young people who know a surprising amount about everyone.

lore.name: Hemotropic Butterfly
lore.info: The Hemotropic Butterfly of Zevil Island is crimson from wingtip to body and smells blood from far off; swarms gather wherever it is spilled, more of them the more blood there is. They feed on nectar too, and at a quiet time they are beautiful. A cloud of them over the grass tells a hunter where someone has been hurt.

lore.name: Hisoka
lore.info: Hisoka is a fighter famous at Heavens Arena: a tall man in a clown's make-up with a deck of cards, a Floor Master in the later years, who fights for the fun of it and leaves opponents in pieces. He holds a Hunter licence, having passed the 287th Hunter Exam after being disqualified from the one before for nearly killing an examiner. Fans love him. Everyone else stands back.

lore.name: Hisoka's personality test
lore.info: Hunters pass round a joke about telling a user's Nen type by their character: Enhancers are simple and honest, Transmuters whimsical and deceitful, Emitters impatient and hot-headed, Conjurers nervous, Manipulators logical, Specialists individualists who keep their distance. The man who made it famous said himself it was about as reliable as fortune-telling by blood type. People still use it.

lore.name: How the exam is scored
lore.info: Candidates wear a numbered badge from the moment they arrive, and examiners follow them by it. The scoring is secret. Old examiners say it weighs three things, physical ability, mental acuity and an overall impression the examiners form over the whole exam, and that a candidate's attitude can sink them after the hardest phase is won. Attacking an examiner disqualifies the attacker for that year only.

lore.name: Hui Guo Rou royal house
lore.info: The ruling house of the Kakin Empire, a nation of over a billion people on the Azian Continent. Its king, Nasubi Hui Guo Rou, has eight queens and fourteen children, every one called a prince whatever their sex. Thirty years ago the country passed from empire to parliament in what is called the most silent revolution in history, and the economy has grown fast since. In 2000 the king announces that Kakin will lead a great voyage to the Dark Continent, open to all comers, on the Black Whale, and the whole royal family sails with it. A stranger meets the house as a parade, a portrait or a guard who says no.

lore.name: Hunter Association
lore.info: The body that tests and licenses Hunters, answerable to no single government. A licence is earned once, through the yearly Hunter Exam, and is never revoked and never reissued: it opens almost every border and public facility, lets its holder into restricted grounds and records, and is worth a fortune to collectors, so a careless Hunter loses it fast. Licensed Hunters chase rare beasts, lost ruins, treasures, criminals and cures, alone or for a client, and the Association ranks the best of them by stars. Its headquarters stands in Swardani City and its airships carry its people and cargo. A stranger meets it as a card shown at a gate; one who joins passes the exam and climbs by the work done.

lore.name: Hunter Exam Commission
lore.info: The people who run the Hunter Exam each year. Applications close on 31 December and the exam opens on 7 January at a site kept secret until the last day; only a candidate who finds the way, often through a navigator who tests them first, reaches it. Candidates wear numbered badges, the phases change every year and anyone may try as often as they live, but deaths and maimings are common and nobody is told how the scoring works. Examiners are elite Hunters who work unpaid; attacking one ends a candidate's year. A stranger meets the commission as a test they did not see coming.

lore.name: Hunters and governments
lore.info: Governments hire Hunters for what armies and police cannot do: find a lost heir, settle a plague, catch a killer who slips every border. Some Hunters take a salaried post with a state and are mocked for it by the rest. The Association itself sits beside the great powers rather than under them; when the V5 needed someone to keep Beyond Netero in custody, it was the Association they asked. Statesmen treat the Chairman as a peer, and Hunters treat statesmen as clients.

lore.name: Hunting Hunters
lore.info: The fourth Bylaw forbids Hunters to hunt each other, and makes one exception: a Hunter who commits a heinous crime may be hunted. The Bylaws never say what heinous means. In practice, a Hunter who kills civilians for sport soon finds a bounty posted and a Blacklist Hunter on the trail, and some serial killers hold licences anyway and are left alone until someone decides otherwise.

lore.name: Infamy in the Known World
lore.info: Every country keeps its own law, and the world agrees on this much: a killing that served nothing is remembered. Word travels faster than people, by phone, by the papers and by the Hunter website. A licensed Hunter is forgiven a great deal, but not killing after killing without cause. The police post notices, the Mafia families keep their own lists, and the Hunter Association's Blacklist Hunters read every bounty. A name that becomes notorious closes the respectable doors first, then the airports and the stations, and at the last brings Hunters who are paid to find it. The one way back anyone speaks of is old and quiet: penance on the steps of the church in Meteor City, which takes every faith and writes down no names.

lore.name: Initiation
lore.info: There is a faster way, and teachers frown on it. A trained user pushes their own aura into a student and forces the nodes open. Done carefully by an expert, it saves months. Done carelessly or in malice, it leaves the victim drained for a long time, crippled or dead. Shingen-ryu calls the forced opening Gehou. The fighters on Heavens Arena's two hundredth floor do it to newcomers with their fists, and those they initiate are often maimed for life or killed.

lore.name: International Permit Agencies
lore.info: The agencies, working directly under the five great nations, that study travel risk everywhere, give each country a safety index and decide who may go to the Dark Continent. An applicant writes to the foreign minister of each of the five nations, waits half a year while the Restricted Voyage Agencies finish their contracts and briefings, then needs letters from three members of their own congress just to meet a section chief. Even then the answer is nearly always no. Steiner, the deputy secretary, is a careful, overworked official. A stranger meets the agencies as forms.

lore.name: Jappon
lore.info: Jappon is an island country, the home of sushi, haiku, samurai and ninja. Its language and writing are its own. Its people turn up in the Hunter Exam, in Mafia bodyguard squads and among Kakin's royal guards.

lore.name: Kakin Military
lore.info: The armed forces of the Kakin Empire, also called the Royal Army. Its officers come from the Royal Military Academy, which takes students young, and its soldiers wear pale combat gear whose headgear shows their rank: corporals in black round helmets, privates second class in berets. Benjamin, the first prince, holds the post of deputy military adviser. On the Black Whale the army enforces martial law from the army office on the third tier, with about two thousand guards and soldiers among two hundred thousand passengers. A stranger meets it as a checkpoint and a request for papers.

lore.name: Kakin's castes
lore.info: Kakin keeps a caste system that its revolution never touched, and the bottom of it is the Have-Nots, barred from public office and from rank in the army. In the old days they were the ones sacrificed and buried with failed princes as afterlife companions. The custom is gone; the bar on office is not. Kakin's princess Camilla made a show of taking Have-Nots into her own army with full soldiers' rights.

lore.name: Kakin's great promise
lore.info: King Nasubi of Kakin promised the world twenty Black Whale ships in a year and a hundred million people sent to the new land within five. The first ship alone carries two hundred thousand. Lotteries filled the lower decks; the rich bought the upper ones. Whether the rest of the fleet will ever be built is a matter for the financial papers. For the people who won a ticket, the only question is what waits at the far end.

lore.name: Kakin's Mafia
lore.info: Kakin has its own Mafia, and its three great families, the Xi-Yu, the Heil-Ly and the Cha-R, have old ties to the royal house. Smaller families such as the Buor scramble for scraps. After Yorknew, Kakin's families gained more than anyone, and their bosses boarded the Black Whale as VIPs, housed as grandly as the senior queens.

lore.name: Kakin's princes
lore.info: Kakin's fourteen princes are a crowd the papers sort by mother and rank. Benjamin, the first prince, is a soldier and the Royal Army's deputy adviser. Camilla, the second, is proud and rich. Tserriednich, the fourth, is handsome and charming in public. Halkenburg, the ninth, studied at Miwal University. The youngest, Woble, is a baby.

lore.name: Kakin's regalia
lore.info: Kakin's crown has three regalia. One is the Sword of Good Omens, given to each new king on accession. The other two are older and stranger, kept by the royal house and shown to outsiders seldom, if ever. Kakin's people know of them mostly from coronation pictures.

lore.name: Kakin's royal children
lore.info: King Nasubi of Kakin has eight queens and fourteen children by them, and every one of the fourteen is called a prince, sons and daughters alike. Each queen keeps her own household and her own guards, and the princes are ranked from first to fourteenth by birth.

lore.name: Kakin's silent revolution
lore.info: In 1970 the Kakin Empire changed overnight. Seizing on a scandal called the Shinrinkan Incident, the country went from a socialist empire to a parliamentary democracy without a shot, in what its own historians call the most silent revolution in history. The dynasty's name came off the country's name, and every treaty the old empire had signed was declared void. The royal house kept its palaces and its king, and Kakin has grown richer every year since, until its population passed a billion.

lore.name: Kakin's survey forest
lore.info: Kakin's government hired an agency of Hunters to survey the wildlife of its forests over three years, and the survey turned up beasts few had seen, among them a horned tiger that cooks its prey with fire.

lore.name: Kastro
lore.info: Kastro was a celebrated fighter on Heavens Arena's two hundredth floor, a handsome master of the tiger-bite fist who had lost once, to Hisoka, and wanted a rematch more than a Floor Master's title. He got his rematch in 1999 and died in it.

lore.name: Kazsule's Alliance
lore.info: Fifteen of the strongest card collectors in Greed Island, called together by a player named Kazsule when word spread that one group was only a few cards from clearing the game. Each had at least fifty specified cards, and each came to trade what they knew so that no one else would take the prize. Their first target is the card held by pirates in Soufrabi, where only fifteen players arriving together can even learn where it is kept. A stranger meets them as a council of rivals who distrust each other; one who joins proves what they can add.

lore.name: Ken, Ko and Ryu
lore.info: Ken is Ren held evenly over the whole body, about ten times the guard of Ten, and it is the standard answer to an attack. Ko is the opposite: every drop of aura in one fist or one foot, devastating where it lands and leaving the rest of the body defenceless. Ryu is the art of moving aura between the two inside a fight, seventy to thirty, eighty to twenty, in time with each punch. A slow Ryu tells an opponent where the next blow is coming from.

lore.name: Kinds of Hunter
lore.info: Most of them specialise, and the Association names them by their quarry.
