Beast Hunters study and protect fauna; Botanical Hunters, plants; Ruins Hunters, lost sites; Treasure Hunters, riches; Gourmet Hunters, rare ingredients and recipes; Disease Hunters, plagues and cures; Blacklist Hunters, wanted criminals; Paleograph Hunters, dead languages. There are Sea Hunters, Music Hunters, Poison Hunters, Jackpot Hunters, Crime Hunters and Problem Hunters, and dozens of others. A Hunter with no field yet is called a rookie.

lore.name: King Nasubi
lore.info: Nasubi Hui Guo Rou is the king of Kakin, a man with eight queens and fourteen children, every one of them called a prince whatever their sex. He backed Beyond Netero's voyage, promised the world a fleet and a new land, and sailed with his whole family aboard the Black Whale.

lore.name: Kiriko
lore.info: Kiriko are Magical Beasts, tall and fox-like, with three long clawed fingers on each hand, who can take human shape so well that a family of them can live in a cabin and pass for farmers. They speak, read, sprout wings from their arms and carry a grown man through the air. Some of them work for the Hunter Association, guiding candidates to the exam and testing them on the way.

lore.name: Kite
lore.info: Hunters remember Kite as Ging Freecss's student, a tall, quiet Hunter with long white hair and a cap, who led a team of amateurs on biological surveys for governments. He found Ging, as his teacher demanded, before Ging found him. Kite went into NGL in 2000 and did not come out.

lore.name: Kukuroo Mountain
lore.info: Kukuroo Mountain is a dormant volcano 3,722 metres high in Padokea's Dentora Region, wrapped in jungle at its foot and cloud at its top. The Zoldyck family owns the mountain and all the land around it, and walls it with stone. The mansion is said to stand at the summit. Nobody outside the family and its butlers has seen it and talked about it afterwards.

lore.name: Kurapika
lore.info: Kurapika is a Blacklist Hunter of the 287th Hunter Exam, a slight, fair, serious young man, and, people say, the last of the Kurta. He works for the Mafia as a bodyguard and later as an underboss, and the underworld knows he hunts the Phantom Troupe and the Kurta eyes. Later he takes the Rat's seat among the Zodiacs.

lore.name: Kurta Clan
lore.info: The Kurta were a clan of a little over a hundred people who kept to a single village deep in the Lukso Province, ruled by an elder and seldom seen in any town. Not every Kurta's eyes turned, but those that did burned scarlet in anger or grief, and outsiders who saw it were frightened enough to turn violent while collectors offered fortunes. So the clan hid, rode its Piko birds to the nearest market and back, and let few of its young go out into the world. It is said a Kurta who wished to leave had to pass the elders' trials first, the last of them a day in town without once losing their temper. Nothing of the clan remains in the forest now but an empty village.

lore.name: Lamentation Tours
lore.info: Lamentation Tours runs a daily bus through Dentora's mountains to the Zoldyck gate. The guide tells the family's history on the way up: the killings, the fees, the photograph that sells for a fortune. At the gate the tourists take pictures. Now and then one tries the side door, and the bus leaves with an empty seat.

lore.name: Languages
lore.info: Some two hundred languages are spoken in the known world, though one common tongue, written in its own script, carries a traveller through most countries. Jappon has its own language and letters, Kakin another, and a second international language appears on signs from airports to the Black Whale. Scholars still argue over dead tongues such as Ancient Kappe and Nankul, and Paleograph Hunters make careers of them.

lore.name: Learning Nen the slow way
lore.info: The usual road is meditation under a teacher. A student learns to feel aura, then to open the nodes a little at a time, then to hold it in Ten. A promising student may open the nodes in three months and master Ten in six; most take far longer. Some teachers use an introductory exercise to gauge talent, and a few masters claim to judge it at a glance.

lore.name: Light Nostrade
lore.info: Light Nostrade is the head of the Nostrade Family, a modest Mafia house under the Ritz, who climbed by selling his daughter's fortunes to men above him. He hires bodyguards who can do things other men cannot, and does not ask how.

lore.name: Lingon Airport
lore.info: Lingon Airport serves Yorknew City from the suburbs, about an hour and a half by car through the desert from the downtown hotels. Its airships carry the auction crowds in and out every September.

lore.name: Lippo
lore.info: Lippo is a Blacklist Hunter and the warden of Trick Tower, who has been known to lend his prisoners to the Hunter Exam with a deal: a year off their sentence for every hour they hold a candidate up. Prisoners say he keeps his word to the minute.

lore.name: Lots of the 1999 auction
lore.info: The Mafia's catalogue for September 1999 is still passed round as a curiosity: the mummy of a princess named Corco, a tissue used by the film star Sonne Limarch with a certificate of his DNA, a solid gold execution sword from a national treasury, the last porcelain vase of the Lai dynasty, and a pair of Scarlet Eyes. None of them reached their buyers.

lore.name: Mafia Community
lore.info: The crime syndicates, families and lone operators spread all over the world, ruled from the top by the Ten Dons with families ranked beneath them and lesser families beneath those. Their trade is commodity control, human trafficking, black market goods and smuggling, though some families keep their books clean. In Yorknew City they paid most of mayor Jitonoda's campaign, so the police close streets for them during the September auctions. Murder is a way of doing business, not the business itself. A stranger meets the Mafia as a man in a suit asking which family they belong to; one who joins starts as a soldier and rises by loyalty and profit.

lore.name: Magical Beasts
lore.info: Hunters call some creatures Magical Beasts: animals with minds close to a human's, or bodies no ordinary animal has, or both. Some speak, some change shape, a few can open their aura nodes as humans do. Researchers suspect they came from beyond the known seas long ago, as humanity may have. Most live far from cities, and many live by rules of their own that the law of the nearest country does not reach.

lore.name: Man-faced Ape
lore.info: The Man-faced Ape of the Milsy Wetlands is weak in the body and makes up for it with a human face and a human voice. It approaches travellers as a person, talks them into following, and leads them to where it can kill them. One famously posed as a Hunter Exam examiner to steal a whole crowd of candidates.

lore.name: Martial law at sea
lore.info: The Black Whale sails under martial law kept by Kakin's Royal Army. Its five tiers divide the passengers by wealth and rank: royalty and the great powers' delegates on the first, the rich on the second, the lottery winners below. A bulkhead between the second and third tiers opens only from above. On the lower tiers the Mafia keeps its own order and sells its own tickets between decks.

lore.name: Master of the Swamp
lore.info: Whale Island's fishermen tell of the Master of the Swamp, a red fish many times the size of a man, with sharp teeth and spindly legs along its belly. For years no line could hold it. In late 1998 an island boy finally landed it with a fishing rod, and his guardian let him go to the Hunter Exam in return.

lore.name: Menchi and Buhara
lore.info: Menchi is a one-star Gourmet Hunter, said to be the finest in the world, whose work has changed what people cook. Her partner Buhara is a giant who can eat a herd of roast pig and ask for more. In 1999 they set the cooking test of the 287th Hunter Exam, and Menchi failed every candidate until the Chairman stepped in.

lore.name: Meteor City
lore.info: Meteor City is a junkyard city, a dumping ground that the rest of the world has been throwing its rubbish into for more than a thousand years. Eight to ten million people live there, and almost none of them have any record of existing: no birth, no papers, no name in any database. An assembly of elders rules it. Anything at all may be thrown away there, people included, and the residents take everything in.

lore.name: Meteor City and the Mafia
lore.info: For years outsiders treated Meteor City as a free supply of people: since its residents did not officially exist, some reasoned that hunting them could not be a crime, and hundreds were taken every year, most of them children. Then the city made an alliance with the Mafia, and the trafficking stopped. The arrangement has held ever since.

lore.name: Meteor City Assembly
lore.info: The elders who rule Meteor City, a junkyard city of outcasts that appears in no official record and whose people are nowhere on paper. Residents wrap their bodies and faces in thick clothes, kneel at their churches for the dead and share a bond they call thinner than water and thicker than blood. The city takes whatever the world throws away, and the Mafia invests in it for a ready supply of killers who leave no trace. When the city is wronged it answers with suicide bombers walking into the offender's streets. A stranger meets the Assembly as silent figures in hoods who are already watching.

lore.name: Meteor City's revenge
lore.info: Meteor City's people are untraceable, which makes them ideal hitmen, and the city defends its own. About a decade before the Yorknew massacre, a man with no papers was convicted of a murder and later proved innocent. Thirty-one residents killed everyone involved in his case by blowing themselves up beside them. Whatever the outside world does to Meteor City comes back to it.

lore.name: Mighty Sweepin' Power Cleaners
lore.info: Mighty Sweepin' Power Cleaners was a children's television show about a team of heroes in coloured suits who clean up the world's villains. Tapes of it travelled far, even to the dumps of Meteor City, where children who had no television of their own dubbed it into their own language for each other.

lore.name: Mike
lore.info: Mike is the Zoldyck family's guard hound, nearly four metres tall, who obeys no one but the family. Years ago he was told to kill every intruder, and he still does it without a sound and without a flicker of feeling. Tour guides describe him. Nobody who has seen him close describes anything.

lore.name: Ming Jol-ik
lore.info: Ming Jol-ik was the Supreme Leader of East Gorteau, the man on every banner and in every broadcast, who held all power in the country for decades. Abroad he was known only from those broadcasts. The news says he died in the summer of 2000.

lore.name: Ministry of Justice
lore.info: The legal arm of the Kakin Empire, independent of the army and with its own uniformed officers. On the Black Whale its Justice Bureau occupies a five-storey building on the second tier and its Supreme Court sits on the first, under the Supreme Magistrate Cleapatro. Kaiser, the deputy chief prosecutor, calls the bureau the most neutral place on board, and its witness protection rooms the safest. Visits last ten minutes, every word is recorded, and a public defender sits in. A stranger meets the ministry as a summons or a refuge.

lore.name: Mitene Union
lore.info: A federation of five countries in the Balsa Islands, south of the Yorbian Continent: NGL, the Republic of Rokario, the Republic of Hass, the Republic of West Gorteau and the Republic of East Gorteau. Rokario's Doli City and its towns are the open, ordinary face of the Union; NGL and East Gorteau are closed to almost everyone. The members keep a common front abroad and quarrel at home. A stranger meets the Union as a border stamp and a crowded harbour; one who serves it carries papers between five capitals.

lore.name: Mizaistom Nana
lore.info: Mizaistom Nana is a two-star Crime Hunter and the Zodiac called Ox, a calm man who believes in rules and procedure. He advises the new Chairwoman and sits on the Zodiacs' intelligence team for the voyage.

lore.name: Morel and Knov
lore.info: Morel Mackernasey is a Sea Hunter, a huge man with a giant smoking pipe, and the teacher of Knuckle Bine and Shoot McMahon. Knov, a neat, sharp-suited Hunter with a precise mind, taught Palm Siberia. Both are Netero's men, and both went to NGL in 2000 when the Chairman asked.

lore.name: Mukatolini's lithographs
lore.info: The lithographer Mukatolini signed only the prints he truly liked, with a sprawling signature that takes up almost as much paper as the image. A signed print from one of his limited series is worth a great deal; an unsigned one, much less. Dealers at Yorknew's Bull Market have been known to sell a signed one by mistake.

lore.name: Nen
lore.info: For Hunters, Nen is the art of controlling aura, the life energy every living body makes. Most people leak aura without ever knowing it and cannot see it in others. A trained user can hold it, hide it, harden it into armour or shape it into a power of their own. The Association treats Nen as the minimum martial skill a real Hunter needs, and it keeps the art out of public sight: a licensed Hunter may not teach it or show it to the uninformed except in an emergency. Courts do not accept it as evidence of anything.

lore.name: Nen after death
lore.info: Nen can outlive its user. A strong grudge, or some other overwhelming feeling, can leave an ability standing after the user dies, often stronger than before and fixed on a target. Hunters call such things curses. Lifting one is the work of an exorcist, and there are said to be fewer than ten in the world who can do it; the work often leaves a mark on the exorcist too.

lore.name: Nen and emotion
lore.info: Strong feeling feeds aura. Rage, grief and love can push a user past their usual ceiling for a while, at a cost the body pays afterwards. The same feeling can bend a user's judgement, and teachers spend as long on calm as on power. The old Hunters say the most dangerous user in a fight is the one who has decided something too firmly.

lore.name: Nen of the Flame
lore.info: Some kung fu schools teach a set of mental exercises they call Nen: Ten as focus, Zetsu as words, Ren as will, Hatsu as act, the four burning together like a flame. It is a real discipline of the mind, not the art of aura, and teachers sometimes give it to students they do not yet trust with the real thing. Those who later learn true Nen find the old exercise smooths their aura and lets them train while injured.

lore.name: Neon Nostrade
lore.info: Neon Nostrade is the daughter of the Mafia boss Light Nostrade, a cheerful, spoiled girl who collects human remains and writes fortunes for her father's friends. Her fortunes came true so reliably that the families paid fortunes for them, and the Nostrade rose on her talent.

lore.name: Netero's chairmanship
lore.info: Isaac Netero was elected the twelfth Chairman of the Hunter Association sometime between 1955 and 1965, and he has held the post ever since, well past his hundredth birthday. He is grandmaster of the Shingen-ryu school and, in his youth, was praised as the strongest Nen user in the world; Hunters say he still is. He runs the Association like a game he enjoys, sets impossible tasks with tight deadlines for the people he trusts, and turns up at the Hunter Exam to play with the candidates. Nobody has yet beaten him at his own ball game.

lore.name: Netero's death
lore.info: In August 2000 the Hunter Association announced that Chairman Isaac Netero had died during the Chimera Ant crisis. Hunters who had assumed he would outlive them all took it hard. He left a recorded message: he resigned the chairmanship, and he wanted every Hunter in the world to vote on his successor. His wishes started the Association's first chairman election in decades.

lore.name: Netero's ten thousand prayers
lore.info: Hunters tell a story about the Chairman's youth. Past forty, having reached the limit of his strength, he went into the mountains and set himself a single exercise: a prayer of thanks to martial arts, then one punch, perfect in form. Ten thousand a day. At first it took him all day and more; years later he finished before sunset, and then his punch was faster than sound. He came down from the mountain with nothing but that, and nobody in the world could touch him. The young Hunters tell it as a joke until they try it.

lore.name: NGL
lore.info: NGL, the Neo-Green Life autonomous region, is a country that rejected modern technology. Its two million people live without machines, synthetic fabric or modern medicine; they travel by horse and write letters. Visitors are strip-searched, x-rayed and scanned at the border, and anyone who smuggles in a phone or a pill goes to prison or to the gallows. A television crew that sneaked in during 1987 never came out.

lore.name: NGL after the Ants
lore.info: After the Chimera Ant crisis NGL ceased to exist. Its land passed first to an international security agency, which dismantled what was left of its government, then to the Hunter Association, which keeps it as an uninhabited nature reserve. No one lives there now, and Hunters who visit need the Association's leave.

lore.name: NGL Autonomous Region
lore.info: A self-governing member of the Mitene Union whose two million people live without machines. Nothing made of synthetic material may cross its border, and anyone caught smuggling technology, modern medicine or weapons is jailed or executed. Visitors are stripped, x-rayed and scanned at the border stop and leave everything modern behind; inside, letters are the post and horses are the road. When an epidemic struck, the people refused foreign doctors so as to stay pure. A television crew that sneaked in years ago was caught, and one of them is still in prison. One who joins gives up the modern world and swears to the movement.

lore.name: Nickes' Alliance
lore.info: A great alliance of players inside Greed Island, sixty-three strong at its height, every one of them hired by Battera. Ten founders run it and split the largest share of the reward; the rest are paid by how long they have served and what they risked. Its plan is plain: corner the island's attack and defence spell cards so no one else can fight back, then collect the specified cards at leisure. New members are brought to a hidden base by a roundabout route and must learn every spell card by heart in an hour, or they are made errand runners. A stranger meets it as a recruiter with a pitch.

lore.name: Nostrade Family
lore.info: A provincial Mafia family under the Ritz Family, headed by Light Nostrade, that rose fast because his daughter Neon writes fortunes that come true; even the Dons ask for her verses. A dummy company, Polio & Co. Ltd., holds the property that should not carry the family's name. Neon collects human body parts and other morbid curiosities, and her father buys them for her. The family hires bodyguards through a test at its mansion: bring back one item from a list within a month. A stranger meets it as an employer paying well for dangerous work.

lore.name: Ochima and Begerossé
lore.info: The Federation of Ochima, on a continent below the Azian, and the Begerossé Union, on one between the Yorbian and the Azian, round out the five great powers. Both sit at every summit and send delegates aboard the Black Whale.

lore.name: Other privileges of the licence
lore.info: The licence carries smaller gifts that Hunters use daily: free access to the network, entry to the website open only to Hunters where information is sold, the right to hire convicts who must obey absolutely, death-row prisoners among them, and exemption from many rules on degrees and age.

lore.name: Panda Frog
lore.info: The Panda Frog, a small mint-green frog with dark rings around its eyes and stripes down its back, is a famous treat of Zaban City's street stalls. Visitors buy one to say they did.

lore.name: Pariston Hill
lore.info: Pariston Hill is a three-star Hunter, the Vice Chairman under Netero, a cheerful young man with a perfect smile and a gift for making his opponents furious. He won the thirteenth election and resigned on the spot. Nobody knows what he wanted, and those who have asked him got a smile.

lore.name: Peijin
lore.info: Peijin was East Gorteau's capital, a city on the country's south-eastern end with the Supreme Leader's palace just outside it. In the summer of 2000 the entire population of the nation was ordered to assemble there, and what happened next is the part of the story nobody tells the same way twice.

lore.name: Phantom Troupe
lore.info: A band of thieves and killers carrying a bounty of the highest class, known across the world by the twelve-legged spider each member wears tattooed with a number. Most of them grew up together in Meteor City. They take what their leader wants, let him enjoy it, then sell it all, and they kill whoever stands in the way; the extermination of the Kurta Clan for its scarlet eyes is laid at their door. There are never more than thirteen of them, a head and twelve legs. A new member is nominated by the others or takes a seat by killing the one who held it. A stranger meets them as a rumour, a ruin or a corpse; the city they came from still counts them as its own, at a distance.

lore.name: Phones and the network
lore.info: The known world lives on its phones. Old wired sets still hang on walls at the Zoldyck gate, but most people carry a mobile, and the newer ones are touchscreens with more languages than their owners will ever need. Anyone can buy a line and a registration number and reach the whole network; a Hunter's licence gives access for free. Shops sell online, games are bought by post, and the Net Police patrol it all.

lore.name: Piko
lore.info: The Piko is a big flightless bird with a long neck, a large beak and a plume on its head, broken to the saddle and to the packframe. The Kurta clan rode them through the Lukso forest and used them to carry goods from the nearest city. Few have been seen since the clan was lost.

lore.name: Provisional Hunters
lore.info: For the Black Whale's voyage the Association made an exception to its own rules. About a hundred and fifty of Kakin's royal guards passed a special exam in 2001 and became Provisional Hunters, with the second Bylaw amended so that they need not know Nen. Their licences hold good only for the voyage and expire when it ends. The others treat them as soldiers with cards.

lore.name: Pure Paladin Squad
lore.info: A team of versatile Hunters from long ago, so skilled that other Hunters still speak of them as legends. Netero, the chairman, belonged to it in his youth. Nobody can say what the squad did beyond its name or why it broke up, and that silence only feeds the stories told in Hunter bars. A stranger meets it as a toast or a boast; a Hunter who claims its name had better be able to prove it.

lore.name: Q
lore.info: Hunters who need to talk without being overheard use Q, software run by a phone company the Association owns. A nine-digit code opens a line that leaves no log and no call history and that ordinary wiretaps cannot detect. Hunters under a non-disclosure contract are expected to use it.

lore.name: Rare beasts at auction
lore.info: Yorknew's sales trade in beasts as well as things: the fossil dung of a dinosaur goes under the hammer at the Southernpiece Auction, and its curators keep a standing request for anyone who finds an Albino Ponytail Cat. Beast Hunters who protect species and dealers who sell them end up in the same auction halls every September and do not shake hands.

lore.name: Reaching the exam
lore.info: Finding the Hunter Exam is the first test. The Association hires scouts who never say what they are: a ship's captain who puts the seasick ashore at the next port, a guide whose road is a trap. Then each candidate needs a Navigator, someone who knows where the site is this year and tests the candidate before leading them there. Only about one applicant in ten thousand ever stands in the hall where the first phase begins.

lore.name: Ren
lore.info: Ren pushes out more aura than the body normally makes and holds it there. It is the engine of every advanced technique and the measure Hunters use for one another: 'show me your Ren' means 'show me what you can do'. Holding it is exhausting. Teachers reckon a month of training for every ten extra minutes a student can keep it up.

lore.name: Ruse Raven
lore.info: The Ruse Raven of the Milsy Wetlands mimics voices and tells lies. It calls out in a friend's voice, or a child's, and draws prey into the swamp's deadliest corners, then waits to eat whatever the swamp leaves.

lore.name: Satotz
lore.info: Satotz is a Ruins Hunter, a tall gentleman with a curled moustache and no visible mouth, who led the first phase of the 287th Hunter Exam by simply walking, faster and faster, for eighty kilometres underground and then across the wetlands. He admires the Hunter Ging Freecss and says so.

lore.name: Scarlet Eyes
lore.info: The Kurta clan's eyes turned a brilliant scarlet when they felt strong emotion, and stayed that colour if they died in that state. Collectors of human remains count a pair among the most beautiful things in the world, and since the massacre the eyes have been sold, stolen and resold through the black market. A single pair can fetch billions at the Mafia's auction. Collectors keep them in jars of preserving fluid and show them only to friends.

lore.name: Sea Fireflies
lore.info: Sea fireflies look like any other firefly but live by brackish water, and in Rokario they light the shallows and the river mouths after dark. Travellers resting on that coast take them as a sign the land is still at peace.

lore.name: Shingen-ryu
lore.info: A school of kung fu whose grandmaster is Isaac Netero, the Hunter Association's chairman, who took over a dojo when he came down from two years of training in the mountains. Its teachers drill etiquette, breathing and patience as hard as they drill strikes, and they will not hurry a student. Wing, an assistant master, keeps a small room near Heavens Arena where he trains Zushi; fighters there whisper that the school teaches some inner trick of the will that makes its pupils hard to read. One who joins bows, sweeps the floor and climbs by the teacher's word.

lore.name: Silva and Zeno Zoldyck
lore.info: The underworld knows two Zoldyck names for certain. Silva Zoldyck, a giant with long silver hair, heads the family. His father Zeno, small and white-haired, still takes contracts and wears a shirt that reads 'lifelong service'. Either can be hired, and the family does not discuss its failures.

lore.name: Six continents
lore.info: Schoolbooks name six continents. The Yorbian Continent holds the United States of Saherta and Yorknew City, the richest city on it; the Azian Continent holds the Kakin Empire. The Kukan'yu Kingdom lies on a continent north of the Yorbian, the Federation of Ochima on one below the Azian, and the Begerossé Union on another between the two. Padokea, the Mimbo Republic and Heavens Arena share yet another. Island nations fill the gaps: the Balsa Islands south of the Yorbian, Jappon, and dozens of small states known abroad only for one export or one scandal.

lore.name: Six-legged Flying Beast
lore.info: The Six-legged Flying Beasts circle the outside of Trick Tower, huge winged things with red skin and teeth like saws. Anyone who tries to climb down the tower's outer wall instead of going through the traps inside is snatched off the stone and eaten in the air.

lore.name: Small-billed Swan
lore.info: The Small-billed Swan, a swan with a long narrow beak, lives only around certain mining areas, and nobody has worked out why. Its food, water and weather are no different there. Beast Hunters argue about it in journals.

lore.name: Snakebeech Forest
lore.info: The Snakebeech Forest covers much of Whale Island's interior, a tangle of old trees where foxbears den and children are told not to go. Islanders tell of a Hunter who passed through a few years ago and killed a foxbear there to save a local boy, and of the boy, who kept the orphaned cub and raised it.

lore.name: Specialists
lore.info: Specialization is the rarest type and the strangest. Its abilities fit no other category, which is why they are dreaded: prophecy, the reading of memories, powers nobody has a name for. One rough count puts Specialists at a few in every ten thousand users, and the person who made it admitted it might be wrong. Some say Conjurers and Manipulators are the likeliest to become Specialists later in life; nobody can say how.

lore.name: Spell cards
lore.info: Greed Island sells spell cards only in Masadora's shop, in random packs, and there are forty kinds: cards that track other players, move the user across the island in a breath, steal cards from another binder, or defend against those that do. A spell aimed at a player cannot be dodged, only blocked. The best players hoard defences.

lore.name: Spider Eagle
lore.info: The Spider Eagle builds webbed nests across the cleft of Split Mountain and hangs its eggs from them over a long fall. The eggs are a famous delicacy. Collectors jump into the gap, grab an egg on the way past and trust the updraft to carry them back up.

lore.name: Spirit echoes
lore.info: Some martial schools speak of a thing that happens when two truly great fighters meet. Each fighter's sense of time drifts out of step with the other's, and each hears the other's thoughts, secrets the opponent never said aloud. The schools call it spirit echoes. Few living people claim to have felt it.

lore.name: Split Mountain
lore.info: Split Mountain is cut down the middle into two equal halves, with a strong updraft rising through the gap. Spider Eagles hang their nests from webs between the cliffs, and their eggs are a delicacy worth the climb, if the climber is willing to jump.

lore.name: Spotted Leeches
lore.info: The Spotted Leech is a thin leech about three inches long that, in less than a day, lays its eggs in the bladder of a living host and dies. Travellers in leech country are told to keep their trousers tucked and their water boiled. Some people keep them for worse reasons.

lore.name: Stars
lore.info: The Association marks its best Hunters with stars on the licence. One star is earned for remarkable work in a field. Two stars need an official post, the first five Bylaws kept, and a junior one has mentored who earns a star of their own. Three stars need remarkable work in several fields and keeping the first six Bylaws. Among the six hundred or so active Hunters, only a handful hold three, and their names are known to all the rest.

lore.name: Swamp creatures of Milsy
lore.info: The Milsy Wetlands breed deceivers. The Noggin Lugging Tortoise moves only in the thickest fog and grows fake people on its shell to lure the curious. The Frog-In-Waiting lies under the mud and swallows whoever steps on it. The Hypnosis Butterfly's flight puts prey to sleep as food for its young, and the Claymore Mushroom bursts into paralysing spores when touched. Guides say the swamp's whole food chain runs on lies.

lore.name: Swardani City
lore.info: Swardani City is a sprawling metropolis and the home of the Hunter Association's headquarters. Hunters come there to vote, to report, to be honoured and to be patched up in its hospitals. The Association's airships moor over the city.

lore.name: Talent
lore.info: Talent for Nen is mostly inborn and changes little over a life. Quick learners usually rise higher, though not always. Hunters who teach for a living speak of a talent found in one person in ten million the way other people speak of comets. Some suspect it runs in families; the evidence is anecdote.

lore.name: Temp Hunters
lore.info: Some Hunters take salaried work with a government and are paid whether they hunt or not. The rest call them Temp Hunters and do not mean it kindly; a Hunter, they say, chooses the quarry. The Temps reply that wars, plagues and border disputes need professionals too.

lore.name: Ten
lore.info: Ten is the first lesson and the last thing a user stops doing. With the nodes open and the aura held close around the body instead of leaking away, the user is guarded against weak blows and against the ill will in other people's aura, and grows old more slowly. Experienced users keep it up in their sleep, and once learned it is never forgotten, like swimming.

lore.name: Ten Dons
lore.info: The ten leaders of the Mafia, each ruling a territory on one of the six continents. Once a year, at the start of September, they gather in Yorknew City for the Underground Auction, where they settle their plans and give orders. Their combined wealth buys anything and anyone, and they hold Neon Nostrade's fortunes in high regard. Few families dare to cross them and fewer survive it. A stranger never meets a Don; a Mafia soldier hears their will through a boss.

lore.name: Ten years without rookies
lore.info: For about ten years before 1999 no first-time candidate passed the Hunter Exam. The Association began to wonder aloud whether the exams had grown too hard or the young too soft. Then the 287th Hunter Exam, in January 1999, passed seven people, several of them first-timers and one of them a boy of twelve. The Chairman himself called that year's crop of rookies an anomaly. Examiners who were there speak of it the way sailors speak of a strange season.

lore.name: The 13th Chairman Election
lore.info: The election of the thirteenth Chairman ran over several rounds in August 2000, with every licensed Hunter bound to vote and a round thrown out whenever turnout fell under ninety-five percent. The Zodiacs set the rules and ran the count. Candidates won and lost votes on speeches, scandals and one famous punch in the hall. Vice Chairman Pariston Hill won in the end, and then, to general astonishment, resigned at once. Cheadle Yorkshire took up the office as the fourteenth Chairwoman.

lore.name: The 288th Hunter Exam
lore.info: The 288th Hunter Exam, in January 2000, was the shortest anyone remembers. Rumour says the first phase, held in the basement of a shop by the station in Beeskafmarro, was a free-for-all for badges, and that one twelve-year-old knocked out every other applicant, nearly fifteen hundred of them, while the examiner dozed on the stairs. The Chairman passed him by phone with no further phases. Only one licence was issued that year.

lore.name: The 289th Hunter Exam
lore.info: The 289th Hunter Exam ended in July 2001, far later in the year than usual, because the Association used it for a second purpose. Kakin's royal guards sat it together, screened by the new Chairwoman and a Blacklist Hunter, and about a hundred and fifty passed as Provisional Hunters whose licences end with the voyage. The older Hunters complained that the Bylaws had been bent; the new ones went aboard anyway.

lore.name: The advanced techniques
lore.info: Past the four principles lie the techniques that combine them. Gyo gathers aura in one part of the body, most often the eyes, to see what is hidden. In hides aura and constructs from every sense. En spreads aura out in a sphere to feel everything inside it. Shu wraps an object in aura so it acts as part of the body. Ken holds a full guard all over; Ko puts all of a user's aura into one point and leaves the rest bare; Ryu shifts the balance between them, blow by blow.

lore.name: The Balsa Islands
lore.info: The Balsa Islands lie south of the Yorbian Continent, a chain of jungle, mountain and coast. Most of their land belongs to the five states of the Mitene Union, which the rest of the world rarely thinks about unless something goes wrong there.

lore.name: The Beatle-07
lore.info: The Beatle-07 is a mobile phone shaped like a rhinoceros beetle, whose wings open on a screen and keypad. It is heavier and dearer than other models, and its fans list its features at length. Hunters who travel recommend it to friends.

lore.name: The binder
lore.info: Every Greed Island player carries a binder that appears at the word "Book". It has a hundred numbered slots for the specified cards and forty-five free slots for everything else. Fill all hundred, and the game is won. A winner, the rumour goes, may take three of the specified cards back to the real world; no one else takes anything.

lore.name: The Black Whale
lore.info: The Black Whale 1 is the largest ship ever built: one and a half kilometres long, eight hundred metres high and eight hundred wide, painted black with eyes that shine like searchlights. It was built quickly and simply for carrying people, two hundred thousand at a time, in five tiers sorted by wealth and rank. It is the first of a class Kakin promised to build by the dozen.

lore.name: The Black Whale sails
lore.info: At noon on 8 August 2001 the Black Whale 1 left Kakin's harbour for the New Continent with two hundred thousand passengers, the royal family, guards from every power and the Hunter Association's Zodiacs aboard. The voyage is meant to take about two months. Ashore, people followed the departure live on every channel. Aboard, the ship sealed its tiers, and the Royal Army declared martial law.

lore.name: The Book of Tyson
lore.info: Kakin's sixth prince, Tyson, wrote a book of gentle teachings that she promises will end all wars as soon as the whole world follows her. Critics point out that most of it is song lyrics. Readers who open it to laugh are sometimes surprised to finish it.

lore.name: The broadcast from Nebaska
lore.info: What turned the Chimera Ant rumours into a world story was a piece of television: a killing filmed in Nebaska, a lion-headed thing that walked and spoke like a man gave an independent reporter a rambling interview about ruling the world, and when she asked him to prove he was no man in a costume, he bit her in half on camera. Viewers who had laughed at the reports stopped laughing, and suddenly everyone had an opinion about giant insects.

lore.name: The Cemetery Building
lore.info: The Cemetery Building in Yorknew City is where the Mafia held its Underground Auction each September, a tall dark block with a hall inside it that could seat the Mafia's finest. On auction nights the police closed a kilometre around it. The building is better known now for the night of 1 September 1999.

lore.name: The Cloud-Hidden Style
lore.info: Jappon still has ninja, and the Cloud-Hidden Style is one of their schools: stealth, speed, endurance and the quiet kill, drilled from childhood. Its students take on secret jobs for hire and for their lords. Those who leave Jappon tend to talk about it too much for men trained in secrecy.

lore.name: The fall of East Gorteau
lore.info: East Gorteau, the closed dictatorship of the Mitene Union, collapsed in the summer of 2000. Its Supreme Leader was reported dead, its people became refugees, and its capital emptied. Afterwards the neighbouring republics of Rokario, Hass and West Gorteau divided its land among themselves, and the name East Gorteau came off the map. What exactly happened at the royal palace in Peijin is told a dozen different ways, and every official version leaves something out.

lore.name: The First King of Kakin
lore.info: Kakin's schoolchildren learn that their country was once a small kingdom in an age of warlords, forever about to be swallowed by its neighbours, and that its First King and his children unified the land and laid the ground for the power it is today. In old Kakin, a prince who never became king was buried with companions to keep his ghost from cursing the realm, and they were always chosen from the lowest caste. That custom is gone; the caste is not.

lore.name: The Four Major Principles
lore.info: Every Nen teacher starts from the same four principles, learned in order: Ten, holding the aura around the body; Zetsu, shutting it off; Ren, pushing out more of it; and Hatsu, using it in a personal way. Ten is the guard that keeps weak attacks and other people's emotions off the skin, and once learned it is never lost. Zetsu hides a person and lets the body rest, but leaves it bare. Ren raises strength and toughness and drives every other technique. Hatsu is the user's own ability, and no two are the same.

lore.name: The Gordeau Desert
lore.info: The Gordeau Desert begins at the edge of Yorknew's suburbs, a dry stony wasteland the airport road crosses. In September 1999 it was the scene of a fight between the Mafia's guards and a single thief that the Mafia lost badly, and of other things the police did not investigate.

lore.name: The Hunter Bylaws
lore.info: The Hunter Bylaws are ten articles every licensed Hunter is bound by. A Hunter must always be hunting something. A Hunter must know martial arts, Nen among them. A licence is never revoked and never reissued. A Hunter may not target another Hunter unless that Hunter has committed a heinous crime. Three articles set out the stars, and the rest cover the Chairman's election, how new members are chosen, and the cabinet that decides everything else.

lore.name: The Hunter code
lore.info: Hunters have an old trick for passing a secret message in plain sight. A sentence that begins with a number, such as a time of day, is read as a key: each figure picks out one part of the following sentences, and everything else is padding. A watcher reading over a Hunter's shoulder sees an ordinary report.

lore.name: The Hunter Exam
lore.info: Once a year, opening on the seventh of January, the Hunter Association holds its exam. Anyone may apply, at any age, with a guardian's signature for a minor; applications close at the end of December, and there is no limit on attempts. Nobody is told where the exam will be held. The phases, five or six on average, change every year along with the examiners, so a returning candidate has no advantage. Deaths and maimings are common, and the Association accepts no responsibility for them.

lore.name: The Hunter licence
lore.info: A Hunter licence is a thick card with a chip and a magnetic strip, the holder's name on the front, and the last three digits of its serial number showing the exam it came from. It opens about ninety percent of the world's closed countries and three quarters of its restricted areas, gives free first-class use of almost every public facility, and lets its holder into guarded records. Banks lend against it without interest. Collectors would buy it for enough to keep a family for seven generations.

lore.name: The Hunters' Tavern
lore.info: The Association runs a website open only to Hunters. A Hunter types the address, enters the code on their licence and swipes the card at any computer, and a saloon with wanted posters on its front opens on the screen. Inside, a bartender sells information that cannot be had anywhere else, about people, places, games and prices, and the rarer the answer, the higher the fee. The Association also posts its own news there.

lore.name: The International Human Databank
lore.info: Somewhere in the network sits the International Human Databank: medical files, military and school records, DNA, family registers, going back sixty years at least. People say a hacker could find a president's secret children in three hours with it. Tampering with it is a grave crime under international law. It finds nothing on anyone from Meteor City.

lore.name: The International Permit Agency
lore.info: The International Permit Agency works for the great powers. Its public job is to study travel all over the world, politics, wildlife and climate, and to give every country a safety index. Travel agents quote its ratings. It also has the last word on any voyage past the charts, which is why few people outside government have heard of it.

lore.name: The Inviolability Treaty
lore.info: About two hundred years ago the five great powers of the day signed a protocol forbidding any voyage to the Dark Continent, and every government since has upheld it. The treaty is the reason no shipping line sells a ticket past the edge of the charts and no expedition can raise money in the open. Most people know it the way they know the law of gravity: as a fact nobody questions. Hunters who chase the unknown grumble about it, and a few old ones go quiet when it comes up.

lore.name: The Jenny
lore.info: The Jenny is the common currency of the known world, used from Yorknew's auction halls to the vending machines of Heavens Arena. Most money moves by card and transfer. Prices run in the thousands for a meal, in the billions for the treasures Yorknew sells. A few closed places keep their own money: under East Gorteau, an underground clinic dealt in pail, five hundred to the Jenny.

lore.name: The JoyStation
lore.info: The JoyStation is an ordinary home game console sold in toy shops and online, and its memory cards save an ordinary game's progress. One game made for it is not ordinary at all, and owners who learn that tend to put the console in a cupboard.

lore.name: The Kakin Empire
lore.info: Kakin sits in the middle of the Azian Continent, a parliamentary democracy with a king, more than a billion people and one of the fastest-growing economies in the world. It is ruled in name by its royal house, the Hui Guo Rou, under King Nasubi. Its zoos, forests and ministries hire Hunters often, and it pays well.

lore.name: The Kakin Mafia bosses
lore.info: Kakin's three great Mafia families are led by people close to the throne: Onior Longbao of the Xi-Yu and Brocco Li of the Cha-R are both half-brothers of the king by women who were not queens, and Morena Prudo, the young and smiling boss of the Heil-Ly, keeps her own counsel about where she came from. They have rooms on the Black Whale's first tier.

lore.name: The known world
lore.info: People speak of the known world as if it were the whole of the map: six continents, a scatter of island nations, oceans crossed by liners and airships, and some two hundred languages, though one common tongue carries a traveller through most countries. Its great powers sit in summits, its cities run on phones, computers and the Jenny, and its wild corners still hide beasts, ruins and peoples no census has counted. Past the edge of the charts lies the Dark Continent, which the great powers have closed by treaty, and which most people think of the way they think of the bottom of the sea.

lore.name: The Kukan'yu Kingdom
lore.info: The Kukan'yu Kingdom, one of the five great powers, lies on a continent north of the Yorbian. Hunters know it for the exam: in January 1999 Dolle Harbor, Zaban City and the wild country around them hosted the 287th Hunter Exam. Its swamps, preserves and offshore islands are full of things that eat travellers, which is presumably why the examiners like it.

lore.name: The Kurta massacre
lore.info: In the forests of the Lukso Province lived the Kurta, a small clan whose eyes turned a brilliant scarlet when they felt strong emotion. Collectors coveted the eyes and outsiders feared them, so the clan hid itself away. About five years before the 287th Hunter Exam the Phantom Troupe found them. Of the clan's hundred and twenty-eight people almost all were killed and their eyes taken; the pairs have been surfacing in private collections and black-market auctions ever since. Rumour says one Kurta boy was away from the village that day.

lore.name: The Lone Pine Tree
lore.info: In the hills outside Dolle Harbor stands a single enormous pine with a cabin beneath it. Candidates who follow the hints that far meet a family there who are more than they look, and who choose who goes on to the exam. Locals know the tree. They also know to keep away from it in December.

lore.name: The Lubo Civil War
lore.info: Lubo's civil war is remembered abroad mostly for one thing: a mercenary unit called Stone Wall fought through the whole of it without losing a single man. Its members came out legends, and their price has never fallen. Militaries still study what they did there; most of what is written is guesswork.

lore.name: The Lukso Province
lore.info: The Lukso Province is deep forest full of trees with strange swirled bark, hard to find and harder to cross. The Kurta clan hid there for generations, riding great birds between their village and the nearest city. Since the massacre the forest has been empty of them.

lore.name: The Lurka Ruins
lore.info: The Lurka Ruins were a buried site until a young Hunter dug them out and restored them almost single-handed. Archaeologists still cite his work. The same Hunter excavated the Congo Gold Vein, and Ruins Hunters speak his name with a mixture of envy and exasperation: Ging Freecss.

lore.name: The Mafia after Yorknew
lore.info: With all Ten Dons dead in one week, the Mafia Community's map of territories had to be drawn again. Families that had kept quiet for decades grew bold, old alliances broke, and the great Underground Auction moved online. The biggest winners were Kakin's three families, whose influence grew so far that, when Kakin later sent ships across the sea, the Mafia granted them the rights to whatever lay at the far end. Yorknew still holds its auctions every September, but the old men who ran them are gone.

lore.name: The Mafia Community
lore.info: The Mafia Community is the world's web of crime families, old-fashioned in its structure and very modern in its business: trafficking, black-market goods, smuggling, control of whatever a city cannot do without. Murder is a tool for it, not a trade, so when it needs killing done it hires professionals. Most of its men have never heard of Nen; the few bosses who have treat it as a weapon best kept in balance and out of sight.

lore.name: The Milsy Wetlands
lore.info: The Milsy Wetlands, which travellers call the swindlers' swamp, lie at the far end of Zaban City's tunnel, a fog-bound marsh where almost every creature lives by deception: tortoises that carry fake people on their shells, frogs that wait under the mud, apes that speak and butterflies that put prey to sleep. The first phase of the 287th Hunter Exam ran straight through it, and a good many candidates are still there.

lore.name: The Mimbo Republic
lore.info: The Mimbo Republic lies south of Padokea and is one of the five great powers. Its leader sits at every summit of the V5, and its government has hired the Hunter Association before.

lore.name: The Ministry of Justice aboard
lore.info: For legal matters on the Black Whale's upper tiers, Kakin brought its Ministry of Justice: a neutral court with judges and prosecutors, sitting on the second tier. Passengers may bring complaints, and princes may be summoned. On the lower tiers, by most accounts, the law is whoever holds the corridor.

lore.name: The Mitene Union
lore.info: The Mitene Union is a federation of five states on the Balsa Islands, set west to east: NGL, Rokario, Hass, West Gorteau and East Gorteau. Its members share a flag at conferences and little else. NGL refuses the modern world, East Gorteau refuses everybody, and the three republics between them trade, quarrel and complain about both.

lore.name: The NGL crisis
lore.info: In the spring of 2000 news began to leak out of NGL, the technology-free country in the Mitene Union: villages silent, travellers missing, a smell of mud on the coast. The Hunter Association sent people in quietly. By summer the word was official: Chimera Ants, a giant breed with a taste for human beings, had nested in NGL and spread. NGL's government collapsed, its land was cleared, and the Association set its threat rating at B. The full story has never been told to the public.

lore.name: The permit agencies
lore.info: Officially anyone may apply to cross the sea to the Dark Continent. The application goes to the foreign ministers of the five great powers, then to their Restricted Voyage Agencies, which need half a year of contracts and briefings and letters from three members of the applicant's own congress, and only then to the International Permit Agency under the V5, and nobody anyone knows has ever been granted one.

lore.name: The Phantom Troupe's rise
lore.info: The Phantom Troupe appeared around 1986 or 1987, a band of thieves out of Meteor City with no records, no faces anyone could match to a file, and no limits. They steal what they want and kill whoever is in the room. Every member, rumour says, carries a twelve-legged spider tattoo with a number, and a new member joins by killing an old one. By the late nineties every one of them carries a class A bounty, and veteran Blacklist Hunters let those bounties pass.

lore.name: The Pure Paladin Squad
lore.info: Before he was Chairman, Netero belonged to a team of Hunters so skilled at everything that the rest of the Association still speaks of them as legends: the Pure Paladin Squad. What they did as a team, what benefit the name carried beyond prestige, and why they broke up, nobody now alive will say plainly. The name is enough to make a veteran stand straighter, and enough for any faction in Association politics to borrow when it wants to look like the old days.

lore.name: The Republic of Padokea
lore.info: The Republic of Padokea is a country anyone can enter, with no visa and no conditions, and its tourist trade lives on that. Its most famous attraction is in the Dentora Region: Kukuroo Mountain, home of the Zoldyck family, which foreigners ride out to see from the bus and then ride back from very quickly.

lore.name: The Republic of Rokario
lore.info: Rokario lies between NGL and Hass, a republic of small cities, mountains and desert. Doli City, one of the nearest modern towns to the NGL border, is where travellers buy supplies before going in and where they rest when they come out. Rokario's coast glows at night with sea fireflies.

lore.name: The Secret Hunter Exam
lore.info: Passing the Hunter Exam makes a person a licensed Hunter. It does not make them a Hunter in the eyes of other Hunters. There is an unspoken second exam every new Hunter must pass, however long it takes: learning Nen. Until then the newcomer is a rookie with a card, and most of the work a Hunter is hired for is closed to them. Most find a teacher within months of the exam; the Association does not say where to look.

lore.name: The Shingen-ryu school
lore.info: Shingen-ryu is a school of kung fu with Isaac Netero as its grandmaster. The story goes that when the young Netero came down from his mountain, a dojo master saw him fight and begged him to take over the hall and teach him. The school teaches its fighters to control aura alongside their forms and its etiquette, frowns on forcing nodes open, and never helps a student shape an ability until the student has the idea alone.

lore.name: The six categories
lore.info: Every person is born with one of six Nen types: Enhancement, Transmutation, Emission, Conjuration, Manipulation or Specialization. They sit in a ring, and a user works best in their own type, slightly worse in the types beside it, and worst in the one across from it. Enhancers strengthen the body; Transmuters give aura the qualities of other things; Emitters send it away from the body; Conjurers make objects of it; Manipulators control things through it. Specialists are whatever is left over.

lore.name: The Sonata of Darkness
lore.info: There is a piece of music for piano, violin, harp and flute that the legend says the devil himself composed. Whoever plays it or hears it is cursed: some die horribly, others are changed in body. Collectors pay fortunes for pages of it and keep them locked away. Musicians cross themselves at the name.

lore.name: The soul
lore.info: Hunters who have seen enough strange deaths argue about the soul: whether a person's memories and character outlast the body, whether they can come back in another one after a violent end. Some are sure it is real, perhaps even a thing with substance. The Association has no position, and the priests have several.

lore.name: The Southernpiece Auction
lore.info: Southernpiece, the most famous house in Yorknew and in the world, holds a sale from 6 to 10 September brings out the rarest lots of the year. Its catalogue is the ticket: buying one admits up to five people, and costs more than many people earn in a lifetime. Without it, a bidder does not even know which day the lot they want comes up.

lore.name: The Southernpiece catalogue
lore.info: The Southernpiece catalogue is a thick book listing every lot of the house's September sale with the day it comes up. Buying one costs more than most people's houses, and it is the admission ticket: no catalogue, no seat. Thieves steal them, of course.

lore.name: The steak set
lore.info: The story every Hunter of 1999 tells: in a cheap diner on Zaban City's Tsubashi Street, a candidate who asked for the steak set cooked over a low flame was shown to a back room where the meal was waiting. The room was a lift, and by the time the steak was eaten it had gone down a hundred floors. The diner still serves steak, they say, and nobody gets a second chance at the password.

lore.name: The Ten Dons
lore.info: Up to September 1999 the Mafia Community answered to the Ten Dons, ten bosses who each held a region, ten regions on six continents between them. Each September they gathered in Yorknew while the Underground Auction ran, settled their business, and gave orders their guards carried out. Few outside the families knew their faces. Every one of them died in Yorknew that September.

lore.name: The Testing Gate
lore.info: The Zoldyck estate's front entrance is the Testing Gate, seven doors in one. Each panel of the smallest door weighs two tons, and every larger door doubles the one before; the gate opens as far as the visitor can push. Those who can open it are guests. Those who climb the wall or slip in by the side door the guard uses are eaten. The guard himself tells visitors this, kindly, and suggests the bus home.

lore.name: The two hundredth floor
lore.info: Above the two hundredth floor Heavens Arena pays nothing; the fighters climb for glory. All weapons are allowed and every fighter uses Nen, which the crowds take for showmanship. A fighter has ninety days to prepare between bouts, is out after four losses, and after ten wins may challenge for a Floor Master's place. Newcomers who arrive without Nen are attacked by the regulars, and most are crippled.

lore.name: The Underground Auction
lore.info: Each September the Mafia held its own sale in Yorknew's Cemetery Building, alongside the city's legal auctions. Its lots were the things no auction house could list: a princess's mummy, a famous actor's used tissues, a golden executioner's sword lifted from a national treasury, the last vase of a lost dynasty, a pair of Kurta eyes. Guests came by invitation and bid in cash. After 1999 the sale moved online.

lore.name: The United States of Saherta
lore.info: The United States of Saherta, one of the five great powers, fills the middle of the Yorbian Continent. Its greatest city is Yorknew; beyond the suburbs lie deserts and wastelands. Saherta's leader sits at every V5 summit, and the country's money and laws shape half the known world.

lore.name: The V5
lore.info: The five great powers of the known world, the United States of Saherta, the Federation of Ochima, the Mimbo Republic, the Kukan'yu Kingdom and the Begerossé Union, meet as the V5 to decide what the world will do. Their leaders are two women and three men, and their summits are reported like weather. They upheld the treaty that closes the Dark Continent, and they hire the Hunter Association when armies are no use.

lore.name: The V5 becomes the V6
lore.info: The five great powers had opposed any voyage across the sea for two hundred years. When Kakin announced one anyway, they first tried to stop it and then, once Beyond was in custody, joined it, taking Kakin into their circle as the sixth member, and renamed the summit the V6, so that the voyage is now officially a joint enterprise of the six powers, with the Hunter Association aboard to keep order.

lore.name: The Vice Chairman
lore.info: The Vice Chairman is the second officer of the Hunter Association, chosen by the Chairman himself and ranking above the advisers. If the chair falls empty, the Vice Chairman holds its power until the election is over. For years the post has belonged to Pariston Hill, a smiling three-star Hunter whom Netero appointed, by his own account, because Pariston irritates him.

lore.name: The World Tree
lore.info: Somewhere in the known world stands a single World Tree, 1,784 metres tall, and the guides say it is only a sapling. Climbing it is legal for anyone who signs a waiver and pays the fee, which Hunters are spared. Lifts and stairs go to the five-hundred-metre mark; above that, climbers go by hand. Every year thousands try, and nearly all turn back before a thousand metres. A giant bird nests near the top.

lore.name: The Yorknew auction massacre
lore.info: On the night of 1 September 1999 the Mafia's Underground Auction in Yorknew City's Cemetery Building was emptied of its goods and its guests were killed. Over the following days gunfights, fires and bodies spread across the city, and on the third night roughly two thousand Mafia men died in and around the same building. The Ten Dons, gathered in the city for the auction, were found dead too. Underworld talk blames the Phantom Troupe, and adds that the Troupe died that week as well. Hunters are less sure.

lore.name: The Zodiacs
lore.info: The Chairman's twelve advisers are called the Zodiacs, each with the codename and the look of a sign of the old zodiac: Rat, Ox, Tiger, Rabbit, Dragon, Snake, Horse, Sheep, Monkey, Chicken, Dog and Boar. They are among the most accomplished Hunters alive, and they quarrel constantly. When the chair falls empty, they run the election to fill it.

lore.name: The Zoldyck legend
lore.info: Everyone in the underworld knows the name Zoldyck: a family of assassins on Kukuroo Mountain who take any contract for a high enough fee and do not fail. Very few know their faces; a single photograph of one sells for a fortune. The family is officially wanted, and no authority moves against it. Tour buses run to its front gate, the guide tells the history, and the tourists photograph the door.

lore.name: The Zoldyck training
lore.info: The underworld knows a little of how the Zoldyck family raises its children: killing taught from the cradle, poison in the food until it stops working, current and torture until pain means nothing. Each child picks a speciality as they grow. Whatever the details, the results are on record: a Zoldyck child of twelve is more than a match for most grown professionals.

lore.name: Trick Tower
lore.info: Trick Tower is a prison, a great stone cylinder on a plain with its cells hidden inside a maze of traps and puzzles. Its warden sometimes lends it to the Hunter Exam: candidates are dropped on the roof and told to reach the bottom alive within seventy-two hours, while the prisoners inside earn time off their sentences by stopping them. The outer walls are no shortcut; flying beasts hunt there.

lore.name: Tsezguerra
lore.info: Tsezguerra is a one-star Jackpot Hunter, a careful professional who leads a small team into Greed Island for Battera, and whose team knows the game better than almost anyone else on Battera's payroll.

lore.name: TSK-17
lore.info: TSK-17 is a biological weapon Kakin's army developed and then shelved: whoever catches it dies in about twelve hours as the organs fail one by one. The army called it a failure. Soldiers who know of it call it a perfect silent killer in the right hands.

lore.name: Two-headed Wolf
lore.info: The Two-headed Wolf is an endangered species, and it has survived this long mostly because one Hunter set up a breeding programme for it. Beast Hunters still cite that programme when they ask governments for money.

lore.name: V5
lore.info: The leaders of the five great nations of the world, the United States of Saherta, the Federation of Ochima, the Mimbo Republic, the Kukan'yu Kingdom and the Begerossé Union, who meet in summits and decide what the world will do. About two hundred years ago they signed the Inviolability Treaty, which forbids any voyage to the Dark Continent; the world knows the Dark Continent is closed. When they want something done that armies cannot do, they hire the Hunter Association. A stranger meets them as the news; one who serves them carries a diplomatic passport.

lore.name: Visca Forest Preserve
lore.info: Past the wetlands lies the Visca Forest Preserve, a forest of streams and lakes full of freshwater fish, and home to the Great Stamp, the world's most ferocious pig. In 1999 two Gourmet Hunters held their phase of the exam there and asked the candidates to cook.

lore.name: Water Divination
lore.info: Teachers find a student's type with a glass of water and a leaf. The student puts their hands around the glass and uses Ren. If the water rises, they are an Enhancer; if its taste changes, a Transmuter; if its colour changes, an Emitter; if impurities appear in it, a Conjurer; if the leaf moves, a Manipulator. Anything else marks a Specialist. Training a Hatsu often means repeating the test until a trickle becomes a flood.

lore.name: Whale Island
lore.info: Whale Island is a small fishing port far from anywhere that matters, visited mostly by fishing boats putting in for fuel and supplies. Few people actually live there, and the children can be counted on one hand. Its forests and swamps are wild enough to hide foxbears and a lake fish the size of a boat. The island is known to Hunters for one reason only: a Hunter named Ging Freecss was born there, and left.

lore.name: What the public believes about Nen
lore.info: Ask an ordinary person about Nen and they will tell you it is a mental trick, a kind of focus martial artists use to steady their nerves, or else a superstition from old kung fu films. Some fighting schools teach exactly that, a set of mental exercises they call Nen. The idea that a man could stop a bullet with his skin or kill with a look belongs, in the public mind, with ghost stories. Hunters do nothing to correct the impression.

lore.name: Wing
lore.info: Wing is an Assistant Master of Shingen-ryu, a mild young man in glasses with his shirt-tail always half out, who lives near Heavens Arena and trains his student Zushi there. He was trained himself by Biscuit Krueger. Fighters at the arena who want to learn properly sometimes find their way to his door.

lore.name: World Tree Birds
lore.info: The birds that nest at the top of the World Tree are enormous, with bright many-coloured feathers, ears like a cat's and long beaks for carrying food to their chicks. Hardly anyone has seen one up close, because hardly anyone reaches the top.

lore.name: Xi-Yu Family
lore.info: The richest and most numerous of Kakin's three great Mafia families, led by Onior Longbao, the king's half-brother, who rides as a guest on the Black Whale's first tier. On the ship the Xi-Yu run the fourth tier and live off human trafficking and the exchange of goods, and they have a direct line to the third prince, Zhang Lei. Hinrigh Biganduffno, the underboss, is a huge man with a temper. Along with the other two families they want territory on the new continent. A stranger meets the Xi-Yu as the men who run the fourth tier's markets.

lore.name: Yorknew City
lore.info: Yorknew City is a sprawling metropolis in the United States of Saherta, known everywhere for its September auctions. It is a city of towers, markets, hotels, stations and money, where the Mafia funded most of the mayor's last campaign and the police chief does what the mayor tells him. Visitors come for the sales. Locals stay out of the Mafia's way.

lore.name: Yorknew's auctions
lore.info: Every year from 1 to 10 September Yorknew City holds the biggest auctions in the world: thousands of licensed houses, hundreds of black-market sales, and tens of trillions changing hands in ten days. A thing bought cheap on the first day can sell at ten thousand times the price on the next. Dealers, collectors, swindlers and thieves fill the city.

lore.name: Yorknew's markets
lore.info: Around the big houses, Yorknew's September fills with smaller trade. The Bull Market's stalls sell anything with a price tag stuck on it, and buyers who know what to look for find real treasures among the junk. The Preview Market lets merchants appraise goods before they go under the hammer. Fortunes are made on bad appraisals.

lore.name: Zaban City
lore.info: Zaban City is a prosperous city in the Kukan'yu Kingdom whose streets are full of shady dealers and con men. In January 1999 it hid the opening of the Hunter Exam: beneath its streets, a hundred storeys down, a tunnel over eighty kilometres long runs to the wetlands. Candidates reached it through a small diner on Tsubashi Street by ordering the right meal.

lore.name: Zepile
lore.info: Zepile is an antiques dealer with an eye for value nobody can explain. In Yorknew he helped raise money for a Greed Island bid by buying underpriced goods and selling them on. Later he sat the 288th Hunter Exam.

lore.name: Zetsu
lore.info: Zetsu shuts every aura node at once. The user's presence fades until even a trained sense passes over them, which is why hunters of beasts and men alike learn it early. It also speeds recovery from fatigue and sharpens the user's sense of other people's aura. The price is total exposure: in Zetsu, even a weak Nen blow lands on bare flesh and does terrible damage.

lore.name: Zevil Island
lore.info: Zevil Island is a remote island of dense forest and tall grass with a narrow waist in its middle, home to blood-loving butterflies and fishing birds. In 1999 the exam left its candidates there for a week to hunt one another's badges, and the island's bushes hid as many traps as animals.

lore.name: Zodiacs
lore.info: The chairman's council: the vice chairman and eleven staff advisors, each a top Hunter whom Netero picked because their skill caught his interest. Each takes a codename from the zodiac and most dress or style themselves to match it, out of loyalty to the old man. They advise on anything the bylaws leave open, take the Association in hand in an emergency and spar with the chairman for his amusement. Hunters treat them with respect; outsiders rarely know their names. A seat is given by the chairman and nothing else, so a Hunter who wants one has to be noticed.

lore.name: Zoldyck butlers
lore.info: The servants of the Zoldyck estate, trained and schooled on the mountain itself, with headquarters so large they are taken for the family's house. Every call from outside goes through them before it reaches the main house, and every visitor meets them first. They train every day with weighted doors, slippers and cups, keep the family's secrets and turn away anyone who climbs past their posts, by force if needed. A butler may not take a lover and lives under strict orders. Gotoh is the head butler; Canary, an apprentice, guards a post near the headquarters. A stranger meets them as polite, frightening people in black suits.

lore.name: Zoldyck Family
lore.info: The deadliest house of assassins in the world, who live on Kukuroo Mountain, a dormant volcano in Padokea's Dentora region. Their name frightens the underworld more than the Phantom Troupe; their faces are almost unknown, and one photograph of a Zoldyck sells for a fortune. Tourist buses run to the Testing Gate, and its first door is too heavy for most men to move; beyond it a giant hound eats anyone who climbs the wall. The children are trained to kill from birth, grow used to poison, pain and current, and choose a speciality as they grow. The family takes contracts from anyone who can pay its very high fee, and no government in the world moves against it. A stranger meets the family as a closed gate; one who serves it starts as a butler and never speaks of what they see.

starts.name: (Party) Digging Drills
starts.info:
PARTY · Greed Island · 2-5 players · Gon, Killua and Biscuit · guided
📍 Greed Island Badlands, The known world. Badlands full of stone pillars and monsters on the way to Masadora: one-eyed giants, fire-breathing lizards and worse.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 14-26)

Inside the game, a little girl in a frilly dress has taken two boys under her wing and set them to dig holes in the badlands with their bare hands, all day, every day. She says it is training. They are starting to believe her.

starts.name: (Party) Fifteen at the Harbour
starts.info:
PARTY · Greed Island · 2-5 players · Gon, Killua, Biscuit, Goreinu and Tsezguerra · guided
📍 Soufrabi, The known world. The port city, on a line of beautiful cliffs, ruled by pirates.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 16-28)

The pirates of Soufrabi hold a rare card, and the town will only let a team of exactly fifteen challenge them for it. Two rival groups of players have agreed to put a team together, and they are still a few short.

starts.name: (Party) Heavy Cups and Heavy Doors
starts.info:
PARTY · Kukuroo Mountain and Heavens Arena · 2-5 players · Gon, Kurapika and Leorio · guided
📍 Zebro's Cabin, The known world. A small cabin near the Testing Gate where the gatekeeper lives.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟢 Low. Safe inside; the ground around it is not. (Recommended Level 6-20)

Killua went home after the exam, and his home is a mountain full of assassins. Three friends have come to fetch him, and the old man at the gate has offered them a bed while they get strong enough to knock.
🎭 Gon Freecss, Male, a boy from Whale Island. Large hazel-brown eyes, green high-collared jacket with orange-red trim. A small boy with spiky hair grinning in a crowd of hard-faced adults, a fishing rod on his shoulder.
🎭 Kurapika, Male, a slight. Grey-brown eyes. A slender blond youth in a blue tabard reading a stranger in silence, his eyes flickering red for an instant.
🎭 Leorio Paradinight, Male, a tall man in a dark suit and tinted glasses who looks ten years older than he is. White shirt. A tall man in a suit and tinted glasses bellowing at the top of a staircase, briefcase raised.
🎭 Zebro, Male, a balding. Narrow sleepy eyes, grey security guard uniform with pockets. A balding guard straining to push open a vast door while three visitors watch in disbelief.

starts.name: (Party) Money for the Catalogue
starts.info:
PARTY · Yorknew City · 2-5 players · Gon, Killua and Leorio · guided
📍 Bull Market, The known world. The cheap end of Yorknew's auction season: stalls where every lot carries a paper tag, and whoever has written the biggest number on it when time runs out takes it home, unless the seller likes an offer before then.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 10-22)

Two boys need to buy a game that sells for a fortune at the Southernpiece Auction, and they have nowhere near enough. Their friend Leorio has a plan, and the cheapest market in the city is where it starts.

starts.name: (Party) The Blimp Field
starts.info:
PARTY · the election and after · 2-5 players · Killua, Alluka, Tsubone and Amane · guided
📍 Parasta Airport, The known world. The airport at Parasta, where blimps and airships can be booked or hired.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 6-20)

The heir of the world's most famous assassins has walked out of his family's house with his little sister, and some of the family's butlers are going with them. They need to reach a hospital in Swardani City, and the family is following.

starts.name: (Party) The Bodyguard Test
starts.info:
PARTY · Yorknew City · 2-5 players · Kurapika, Melody and Basho · guided
📍 Nostrade's Mansion, The known world. The luxurious house of the Nostrade family, a Mafia family rising fast, where Light Nostrade lives with his daughter Neon and keeps her collection.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟠 High. Dangerous ground; a party that picks its fights survives it. (Recommended Level 12-26)

A Mafia boss is hiring Nen users to guard his daughter at the auctions, and the agency has sent its best applicants to his mansion. The interviewer has given them a list of items to fetch, and he has not said what comes after.
🎭 Kurapika, Male, a slight. Grey-brown eyes. A slender blond youth in a blue tabard reading a stranger in silence, his eyes flickering red for an instant.
🎭 Basho, Male, a Hunter from Jappon with a pompadour. A muscular man with a pompadour whistling as he writes a poem with a brush on a scrap of paper.
🎭 Dalzollene, Male, the head of Neon Nostrade's bodyguards and Light's right hand. Short messy black hair, tired heavy-lidded eyes, black v-neck sweater with olive and cream striped collar. A tattooed man on a mansion screen telling a room of applicants that the door is locked.
🎭 Melody, Female, a Music Hunter. Large round bulging eyes, long dark blue tunic. A small woman in a hat lowering her flute as a frightened room slowly goes calm.
🎭 Baise, Female, a Hunter with sharp green eyes. Sharp green eyes. A woman with an upright pink braid kissing a terrified man's cheek and smiling as his eyes go blank.
🎭 Shachmono Tocino, Male, a licensed Hunter and senior Nostrade bodyguard. Short cropped orange hair, wide pale eyes. A slender man with curled sideburns sitting among applicants, smiling as hooded gunmen burst in.

starts.name: (Party) The Climb
starts.info:
PARTY · Kukuroo Mountain and Heavens Arena · 2-5 players · Gon, Killua and Zushi · guided
📍 Arena Lower Floors, The known world. The floors from the first to the ninety-ninth, where a fighter climbs ten floors for a win and drops ten for a loss, fights with bare hands only, and is paid a little for every floor gained.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🟡 Moderate. Real fights at the edges; walk in with your eyes open. (Recommended Level 4-12)

Two boys walked into the tallest fighting tower in the world because they needed money, and their first bouts sent them straight to the fiftieth floor. A small boy in a white gi registered the same day and went up with them, and he is better than he looks.
🎭 Zushi, Male, a small, brown-haired, heavy-browed boy in a karate gi over a black turtleneck who climbs. Very short buzzed brown hair, big hazel-brown eyes. A small boy in a gi bowing deeply to his opponent before flooring a man four times his size.
🎭 Maita, Male, a large, bulky prizefighter with a bald head, narrow eyes and thick bushy eyebrows that. Narrow eyes. A huge bald fighter with bushy eyebrows eating a rice ball on the bench while his name crackles over the speaker.

starts.name: (Party) The Clinic on Tier 3
starts.info:
PARTY · the Black Whale · 2-5 players · Leorio · guided
📍 Tier 3, The known world. The middle of the hull and the highest tier for ordinary passengers, with cabins of a bed, cupboards and a bathroom along corridors that open on assembly points.
Pace: Guided. An authored opening plays out, then the world is yours.
Danger: 🔴 Severe. Deadly to the unready; the top of this band eats mid-level parties. (Recommended Level 20-34)
